title: FIBER EXTRACTION DEVICE FOR SISAL LEAVES
abstract: A fiber extraction device for sisal leaves, comprising a platform 101 configured to be positioned on a ground surface, a chamber 102 accessed by a user for placing multiple leaves of a sisal plant, a touch interactive display panel 103 enable user to provide input regarding the quantity of sisal fibers to be extracted from leaves, two robotic arms 104 grip a pre-defined quantity of leaves from chamber 102 and position leaves between two vertical blades 105, an imaging unit 106 determines thickness of leaves, two sliding units 107 translate blades 105, two telescopically operated grippers 108 grip sisal leaves and repeatedly pass leaves through blades 105 to obtain sisal fiber from leaves, a robotic gripper 109 grip and position obtained fibers on a motorized roller 114, which rotate to wind fibers on roller 114, an air blower 110 blows hot air towards fibers to facilitate proper drying of fibers.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves that is designed for the extraction of fibers from sisal leaves by extracting, handling, and processing the sisal leaves in an automated manner, thereby improve efficiency, accuracy, and ease of operation in fiber production. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	Sisal fibers, used for making ropes, textiles, and various products, are extracted from the tough, fibrous leaves of the sisal plant. Traditionally, this extraction process involved manual labour, where workers used simple tools like knives, spades, or hand-operated decorticators to separate the fiber from the pulp. This method was physically demanding, time-consuming, and required great skill to achieve consistent results. The process also led to high wear and tear on both the tools and the workers, as the rough nature of the plant material cause injuries. Additionally, the quality of the extracted fiber varied, often depending on the worker’s experience. Overall, traditional methods were inefficient and result in fatigue, inconsistent quality, and low productivity.

[0003]	Conventionally, the extraction of sisal fibers was a highly manual process. Workers use knives or machetes to cut the leaves from the plant and then scrape or peel the fibrous material from the inner pulp. This process was extremely labour-intensive and required significant skill to avoid damaging the fibers, which are critical for producing high-quality products. Early methods were limited to small-scale production, often done in rural communities or farms. So, people also use mechanical decorticators as these were developed to aid in the sisal extraction process. These machines were designed to automate the peeling of the fibers from the leaves by using rotating drums, knives, and rollers. The advent of such machines allowed for greater efficiency compared to manual methods and reduced some of the labour required. But these machines were more expensive than simple hand tools, making them inaccessible for smaller farms or rural areas. 

[0004]	CN104630903A discloses about an invention that includes a novel sisal fiber extraction method and device. The method comprises the steps that sisal leaves are crosswise fed into one hemp peeling mechanism from the middle of the sisal leaves, and fibers are obtained through direct reverse drawing. The device comprises a feeding mechanism, a sisal leaf clamping and delivery mechanism, a fiber clamping and delivery mechanism, a left hemp peeling mechanism and a right hemp peeling mechanism, sisal leaf base crushing mechanism, and a power and transmission device, wherein the sisal leaves and the fiber clamping and delivery mechanism are arranged in an inclined mode toward the hemp peeling mechanisms and perpendicular to the crushing mechanism, a chain and a belt are arranged in parallel and the delivery speeds are the same, and the linear speed of a crushing roller is 1.4 times those of the chain and the belt. Double-vane rolling cylinders with two vanes rotating in opposite directions serve as the hemp peeling mechanisms. The sisal leaves are crosswise fed into the left hemp peeling mechanism by the feeding mechanism, fibers are drawn out by the sisal leaf clamping chain and enter the fiber clamping belt, tip fibers are further drawn out, bases enter the right hemp peeling mechanism after winding around the shaft end of the crushing roller, and base fibers are reversely drawn out. By the adoption of the method and device in sisal fiber extraction, the per capita productivity of an existing device is improved by 2 to 3 times, and the productivity per kilowatt hour is improved by 1 to 2 times.

[0005]	CN101575741A discloses about an invention that includes a method for preparing viscose fiber by sisal leaves. The method comprises the following steps: sorting the sisal leaves; adopting mechanical knocking or roll compacting, carrying out devillication with a carding method so as to scrap off diachyma colloid of the sisal leaves, carrying out water washing, and obtaining sisal leaves cellulose base fiber; carrying out fermentation treatment in a microorganic mould solution and then peroxide treatment so as to remove residual colloid; preparing soda cellulose; etiolating and dissolving the soda cellulose to obtain filature serosity; defoaming the filature serosity; and wet spinning. The invention has the advantages that the method fully utilizes the waste sisal leaves to prepare the viscose fiber and improves the economic value of the sisal leaves; peroxide is used for replacing sodium sulfite, sodium bisulfite, ammonium oxalate, ammonium citrate in the ZL200510111703.2 biological-chemical method patent; and the discharged sewage contains no inorganic matters but polysaccharide compounds which are biologically degradable, and more conforms to the environment friendly requirement. 
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of performing fiber extraction from sisal leaves. However, these devices are incapable of carrying out the the extraction of fibers from sisal leaves within minimal manual effort. Additionally, these existing devices also lack in accurately determining and adjusting the amount of leaves required for extraction, which results in wastage of leaves. 

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of automating the extraction of fibers from sisal leaves, in view of reducing the need for manual labour and improving efficiency throughout the process. 

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automating the extraction of fibers from sisal leaves, in view of reducing the need for manual labour and improving efficiency throughout the process. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of accurately determining and adjusting the amount of leaves required for extraction, thereby ensuring optimal fiber yield and minimizing wastage.

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of handling and positioning sisal leaves based on their, in order to adjust the extraction parameters for more precise and effective processing. 
    	
[0012]	The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	The present invention relates to a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves that facilitates the automation of fiber extraction from sisal leaves, in view of aiming to reduce manual labour and enhance efficiency throughout the entire process. Additionally, the proposed device also efficiently dries the extracted fibers, for ensuring they are properly conditioned for subsequent use and enhancing the quality of the final product. 

[0014]	According to an embodiment of the present invention, a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves comprises of, a platform configured to be positioned on a ground surface, a chamber is positioned over the platform accessed by a user for placing multiple leaves of a sisal plant, a touch interactive display panel installed over the platform to enable the user to provide input regarding the quantity of sisal fibers to be extracted from the leaves, a pair of robotic arms configured on the platform to grip a pre-defined quantity of leaves from the chamber and position the leaves between a pair of vertical blades arranged in a tilted orientation on the platform, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the platform for determining thickness of the leaves, a pair of sliding units positioned in between the blades and platform to translate the blades for adjusting the gaps between the blades, a pair of telescopically operated grippers arranged on the platform, to grip the sisal leaves and repeatedly pass the leaves through the blades to obtain the sisal fiber from the leaves,  a robotic gripper is configured on the platform to grip and position the obtained fibers on a motorized roller installed on the platform, that rotate in order to wind the fibers on the roller.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of, an air blower mounted on the platform for blowing hot air towards the fibers to facilitate proper drying of the fibers, a suction unit is configured adjacent to the blades to generate a vacuum pressure for withdrawing residues coming out from the leaves during the fiber obtaining operation and collecting the residue in a receptacle paired with the suction unit, a weight sensor is installed in the chamber to monitor weight of the leaves stored in the chamber, a speaker installed over the platform to produce a voice command to notify the user regarding refilling of the chamber and a battery is associated with the device for supplying power to electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device. 

[0016]	While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of,  the like.

[0020]	As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves that automates the fiber extraction from sisal leaves, thereby significantly reducing manual labour and enhancing operational efficiency. Additionally, the device precisely calculates and adjusts the quantity of leaves needed for extraction, thereby ensuring maximum fiber yield while minimizing waste. 

[0022]	Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a fiber extraction device for sisal leaves is illustrated, respectively, comprising a platform 101 configured to be positioned on a ground surface, a chamber 102 is positioned over the platform 101, a touch interactive display panel 103 installed over the platform 101, a pair of robotic arms 104 configured on the platform 101, a pair of vertical blades 105 arranged in a tilted orientation on the platform 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 106 installed on the platform 101, a pair of sliding units 107 positioned in between the blades 105 and platform 101, a pair of telescopically operated grippers 108 arranged on the platform 101, a robotic gripper 109 is configured on the platform 101, an air blower 110 mounted on the platform 101, a suction unit 111 is configured adjacent to the blades 105, a receptacle 112 paired with the suction unit 111, a speaker 113 installed over the platform 101, a motorized roller 114 installed on the platform 101. 

[0023]	The device disclosed herein comprises a platform 101 designed to be positioned securely on a ground surface, with a chamber 102 mounted above the platform 101. This chamber 102 is structured to be accessed by a user for the purpose of placing multiple leaves of a sisal plant. The platform 101 serves as a stable base, while the chamber 102 provides an enclosed or semi-enclosed space where the leaves is positioned in a manner that facilitates subsequent processing or handling. The configuration of the platform 101 and chamber 102 is such that it optimizes the positioning and handling of the sisal leaves, ensuring efficient operation during the extraction of fiber, while maintaining accessibility for the user. 

[0024]	The platform 101 is installed with a touch interactive display panel 103 which facilitates a user in providing touch input command regarding the quantity of sisal fibers to be extracted from the leaves. The touch interactive display panel 103 as mentioned herein is typically an LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) screen that presents output in a visible form. The screen is equipped with touch-sensitive technology, allowing the user to interact directly with the display using their fingers. A touch controller IC (Integrated Circuit) is responsible for processing the analog signals generated when the user inputs details regarding the quantity of sisal fibers to be extracted from the leaves. A touch controller is typically connected to the microcontroller through various interfaces which may include but are not limited to SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) or I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit).

[0025]	An inbuilt microcontroller that is operatively linked to the display panel 103, is programmed to process input commands received from the user and subsequently determines the quantity of sisal leaves required for extraction. Upon receiving the relevant data, the microcontroller analyses the input and calculates the necessary amount of leaves to optimize the extraction process. 

[0026]	The information is then displayed on the panel 103, allowing the user to monitor and adjust the process as needed. This integration of the microcontroller ensures precise control over the operation, enhancing efficiency and accuracy in determining the appropriate quantity of leaves required for the extraction process.

[0027]	The platform 101 is installed with a pair of robotic arms 104 that is synchronously actuated by the microcontroller to grip a pre-defined quantity of leaves from the chamber 102. The robotic arms 104 used herein mainly comprises of motor controllers, arm, end effector and sensors. The arm is the essential part of the robotic arms 104 and it comprises of three parts the shoulder, elbow and wrist. All these components are connected through joints, with the shoulder resting at the base of the arm, typically connected to the microcontroller. The elbow is in the middle and allows the upper section of the arm to move forward or backward independently of the lower section. Finally, the wrist is at the very end of the upper arm and attaches to the end effector. The end effector connected to the arm acts as a hand and acquire a grip of the pre-defined quantity of leaves from the chamber 102 and position the leaves between a pair of vertical blades 105 arranged in a tilted orientation on the platform 101. 

[0028]	The microcontroller herein determines thickness of the leaves by means of an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 106 which is installed on the platform 101. The imaging unit 106 disclosed herein comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images of the leaves and the captured images are stored within memory of the imaging unit 106 in form of an optical data. The imaging unit 106 also comprises of the processor which processes the captured images. 

[0029]	This pre-processing involves tasks such as noise reduction, image stabilization, or color correction. The processed data is fed into AI protocols for analysis which utilizes machine learning techniques, such as deep learning neural networks, to extract meaningful information from the visual data which are processed by the microcontroller to determine thickness of the leaves.

[0030]	Based on the detected thickness the microcontroller actuates a pair of sliding units 107 that is positioned in between the blades 105 and platform 101. The sliding units 107 consists of a pair of sliding rails fabricated with grooves in which the wheel of a slider is positioned that is further connected with a bi-directional motor via a shaft. The microcontroller actuates the bi-directional motor to rotate in clockwise and anti-clockwise direction that aids in rotation of shaft, wherein the shaft converts the electrical energy into rotational energy for allowing movement of the wheel to translate over the sliding rail by a firm grip on the grooves. The movement of the slider results in translation of the blades 105 for adjusting the gaps between the blades 105. 

[0031]	The platform 101 is installed with a pair of telescopically operated grippers 108 which are pneumatically actuated to grip the sisal leaves and repeatedly pass the leaves through the blades 105 to obtain the sisal fiber from the leaves. The pneumatic arrangement of the grippers 108 comprises of a cylinder incorporated with an air piston and the air compressor, wherein the compressor controls discharging of compressed air into the cylinder via air valves which further leads to the extension/retraction of the piston. The piston is attached to the telescopic grippers 108, wherein the extension/retraction of the piston corresponds to the extension/retraction of the grippers 108. The actuated compressor allows extension of the grippers 108 to grip the sisal leaves and repeatedly pass the leaves through the blades 105 to obtain the sisal fiber from the leaves. 

[0032]	A suction unit 111 is configured adjacent to the blades 105 to generate a vacuum pressure during the fiber extraction process. This vacuum pressure effectively withdraws the residues that are released from the sisal leaves as they are processed by the blades 105. The residues, which may include unwanted plant material and by-products, are then directed into a receptacle 112 that is paired with the suction unit 111. 

[0033]	The receptacle 112 serves as a collection container for the withdrawn residues, ensuring that the extraction process remains clean and efficient. The suction unit 111 helps to maintain a tidy work environment while preventing the dispersion of waste material, thus enhancing operational efficiency and minimizing cleanup efforts.

[0034]	The suction unit 111 mentioned above comprises of a bowl-shaped cup alike entity having two openings in which one side of the opening has a larger diameter and another side has a smaller diameter wherein the smaller diameter of the cup is attached with a suction pump via conduit that is interlinked with the microcontroller. On actuation, the suction pump creates a negative pressure which in turn a vacuum that is created inside the cup in order to withdraw residues coming out from the leaves during the fiber obtaining operation and collecting the residue in the receptacle 112.

[0035]	The platform 101 is installed with a robotic gripper 109 which grip and position the obtained fibers on a motorized roller 114 installed on the platform 101. The robotic gripper 109 includes a link connected with multiple motorized ball and socket joints and a gripper for smooth and precise gripping of obtained fibers. The motorized ball and socket joint includes a motor powered by the microcontroller generating electrical current, a ball shaped element and a socket. The ball moves freely within the socket. The motor rotates the ball in various directions that is controlled by the microcontroller that further commands the motor to position the ball precisely. The microcontroller further actuates the motor to generate electrical current to rotate in the joint for providing movement to the gripper 109 for gripping and positioning the obtained fibers on the roller 114.

[0036]	The roller 114 is synchronously actuated by the microcontroller. The motorized roller 114 mentioned above is a mechanical unit designed to rotate on its axis with the help of an integrated electric motor. The cylindrical roller tube serves as a surface for supporting, and unwinding the positioned fibers. The motorized roller 114 is equipped with an electric motor that provides the rotational power necessary to turn the roller 114. The motor is connected to the roller tube through a drive mechanism, which involves gears, belts to transfer the motor’s rotational force to the roller 114, causing it to rotate in order to wind the fibres on the roller 114. 

[0037]	The platform 101 is installed with an air blower 110 which blows hot air towards the fibers. The air blower 110 consists of a motor-driven fan or impeller that generates a high-velocity stream of air.  The air blower 110 is typically designed to be compact and energy efficient. The air blower 110 is strategically positioned within the platform 101, so as to effectively dry out the fibers. The air blower 110 is positioned so that its airflow is directed toward the fibers and this is achieved by adjusting the louvers or ducts to focus the airflow. The microcontroller controls the speed and intensity of the air blower 110 and modulates the airflow based on their moisture level. The microcontroller monitors the drying process and once the fibers are dry, the microcontroller automatically turns off the air blower 110 to conserve energy.
 
[0038]	The chamber 102 is installed with a weight sensor which monitor weight of the leaves stored in the chamber 102. The weight sensor comprises of a convoluted diaphragm and a sensing module. Due to the weight of leaves in the chamber 102, the size of the diaphragm changes which is detected by the sensing module. The sensing module detects the weight of leaves in the chamber 102 and on the basis of the changes in sizes of the diaphragm, the acquired data is forwarded to the microcontroller in the form of a signal for further processing. The microcontroller after processing the data monitor weight of the leaves stored in the chamber 102.

[0039]	In the event, if the monitored weight recedes a threshold value, the microcontroller actuates a speaker 113 installed over the platform 101. The speaker 113 disclosed herein works by receiving signals from the microcontroller, converting them into sound waves through a diaphragm’s vibration, and producing audible sounds with the help of amplification and control circuitry in order to produce a voice command to notify the user regarding refilling of the chamber 102. 

[0040]	Moreover, a battery is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device and supplying a voltage to the components. The battery used herein is preferably a Lithium-ion battery which is a rechargeable unit that demands power supply after getting drained. The battery stores the electric current derived from an external source in the form of chemical energy, which when required by the electronic component of the device, derives the required power from the battery for proper functioning of the device. 

[0041]	The present invention works in the best manner, where the platform 101 configured to be positioned on the ground surface. The chamber 102 is positioned over the platform 101 accessed by the user for placing multiple leaves of the sisal plant. Thereafter the touch interactive display panel 103 enable the user to provide input regarding the quantity of sisal fibers to be extracted from the leaves. The inbuilt microcontroller linked to the display panel 103 processes the input commands and determines quantity of leaves required for extraction. The pair of robotic arms 104 grip the pre-defined quantity of leaves from the chamber 102 and position the leaves between the pair of vertical blades 105 arranged in the tilted orientation on the platform 101. Then the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 106 determines thickness of the leaves. Based on the detected thickness, the microcontroller actuates the pair of sliding units 107 to translate the blades 105 for adjusting the gaps between the blades 105. Upon actuation of the sliding unit 107, the microcontroller actuates the grippers 108 to work in coordination to grip the sisal leaves and repeatedly pass the leaves through the blades 105 to obtain the sisal fiber from the leaves. Synchronously, the suction unit 111 generate the vacuum pressure for withdrawing residues coming out from the leaves during the fiber obtaining operation and collecting the residue in the receptacle 112 paired with the suction unit 111.

[0042]	In continuation, the robotic gripper 109 grip and position the obtained fibers on the motorized roller 114 that rotate in order to wind the fibers on the roller 114. The air blower 110 blows hot air towards the fibers to facilitate proper drying of the fibers. Further the weight sensor monitors weight of the leaves stored in the chamber 102. And in case the monitored weight recedes the threshold value, the microcontroller actuates the speaker 113 installed over the platform 101 to produce the voice command to notify the user regarding refilling of the chamber 102. 

[0043]	Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: CHECK VALVE TESTING AND ANALYSIS DEVICE
abstract: A check valve testing and analysis device, comprising a platform 101 positioned on a fixed surface, plurality of supporting legs 102 for supporting platform 101, a holding unit 103 for engaging a check valve with holding unit 103, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 to detect dimensions of valve, plurality of motorized clippers 105 secures valve, plurality of water tubes 106 interconnected to holding unit 103 and a water chamber 107 integrated with a heating unit for generating steam that is transferred within conduits to test check valve, an electronically controlled valve 108 control flow of superheated steam, a flow meter measure flow rate of steam, enabling accurate monitoring of steam usage, a sound sensor measures sound generated by check valve under varying steam flow rates and temperatures, providing additional diagnostic information on valve performance and performance is displayed on a touch-interactive display unit 109.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a check valve testing and analysis device that is capably of automating the process of check valve testing under varying steam flow rates, to assess its effectiveness in controlling flow and accordingly displays the parameters.  

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	Testing check valves posses several challenges. Inaccurate flow measurement may occur due to improper sensor calibration, leading to unreliable data. Variability in steam pressure, temperature and flow complicate consistent testing conditions, affecting valve performance results. Leaks or malfunctions in the valve may not be easily detected under certain operating conditions. Additionally, improper sealing or valve seating could result in failure to close correctly, leading to inaccurate test outcomes. Safety risks also arise from the high-pressure steam used during testing, which can cause system failures or injuries if not properly managed. Furthermore, testing may be time-consuming and resource-intensive.

[0003]	Traditional check valve testing methods often involve visual inspection, manual flow testing, and pressure testing. In these methods, valves are subjected to steam, air, or water flow, and their response (e.g., closing time, sealing integrity, or leakage) is observed. However, these methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to human error. This method also fails to detect subtle leaks or performance issues, and controlling precise conditions like pressure and temperature can be challenging, leading to inconsistent results.

[0004]	CN101929923A provides a life testing device for a check valve. The device comprises a water tank, wherein the water tank is connected with an electric pump; the electric pump is connected in parallel with an overflow valve and connected in series with a cut-off valve I and then enters the lower part of a high-pressure tank; the middle part of the high-pressure tank is connected with a water pipe; the water pipe is sequentially connected with a cut-off valve II, the check valve, a cut-off valve III and the upper part of the water tank; the upper part of the high-pressure tank is also provided with an exhaust valve and a safety valve; the cut-off valve II is an electric cut-off valve; and a peeker is arranged between the check valve and the cut-off valve III. The device has the advantages of automatic mode, convenient and fast testing, time saving, labor saving and high testing efficiency. 

[0005]	GB2161903A discloses about a method of testing the operability of check valves having a pivotal closure disk wherein a check valve is provided having a valve body and first sealing member of nonmagnetic material and a pivotal closure disk and second sealing member of magnetic material, and a magnetic field is applied in a direction which causes the closure disk to move away from the first sealing member. The attraction between the magnetic field generator and the closure disk is measured to determine the relative position of the closure disk to the first sealing member and thus the operability of the valve. 
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed for testing the check valves but these all are operated manually and these al or labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to human error. 

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of testing performance and functionality of the check valve under varying steam flow rates, ensuring it operates efficiently and seals correctly and also in automated manner. 

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of testing performance and functionality of the check valve under varying steam flow rates, ensuring it operates efficiently and seals correctly. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of accurately measuring and comparing the steam flow rates at both the inlet and outlet of the check valve to assess its effectiveness in controlling flow and accordingly displays the parameters. 

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automating the valve testing process, allowing for consistent and repeatable testing with minimal manual intervention. 
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to a check valve testing and analysis device that capable of carrying out testing of check valves under varying steam flow rates, in an automated manner thereby saving the time needed assess its effectiveness in controlling flow and accordingly displays the parameters. 

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, a check valve testing and analysis device comprises of a platform positioned on a fixed surface and installed with plurality of supporting legs for supporting the platform at a height from ground surface, a holding unit is arranged on the platform that is accessed by a user for engaging a check valve with the holding unit, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the platform to detect dimensions of the valve, plurality of motorized clippers integrated within the holding unit for securing the valve with the holding unit, plurality of water tubes interconnected the holding unit a water chamber installed on the platform and integrated with a heating unit for heating water stored inside the chamber for generating steam that is transferred within the conduits to test the check valve, an electronically controlled valve integrated with each of the conduits to control flow of superheated steam.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of a flow meter is connected to both ends of holding unit to measure flow rate of steam during testing process, enabling accurate monitoring of steam usage, a sound sensor integrated with the flow meters to measure sound generated by check valve under varying steam flow rates and temperatures, providing additional diagnostic information on valve performance, a touch-interactive display unit attached to upper portion of the platform, providing real-time feedback on physical characteristics of valve for accurate performance analysis, a corrosion detection sensor provided with the platform to detect presence of corrosion over the check valve, a speaker mounted on the platform to produce audio alerts to notify the user regarding the detected corrosion, a temperature sensor is integrated within the chamber for measuring temperature of chamber and steam and if exceeding a threshold range then automatically heating unit is turned off for safety purposes, an ultrasonic sensor is integrated with the platform and synced with the imaging unit for detecting dimensions of the check valve during testing that is displayed on the display unit providing real-time measurements of valve's physical parameters. 

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a check valve testing and analysis device. 

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of,  the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to a check valve testing and analysis device that saves the time and effort required in carrying out testing of check valves under varying steam flow rates, by automating the testing process to assess its effectiveness in controlling flow. 

[0022]	Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a check valve testing and analysis device is illustrated, comprising a platform 101, installed with plurality of supporting legs 102, holding unit 103 is arranged on the platform 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101, plurality of motorized clippers 105 integrated within the holding unit 103, plurality of water tubes 106 interconnected the holding unit 103 and a water chamber 107 installed on the platform 101, an electronically controlled valve 108 integrated with each of the conduits, a touch-interactive display unit 109 attached to upper portion of the platform 101, and a speaker 110 mounted on the platform 101. 
 
[0023]	 The proposed device comprises of a platform 101 developed to be positioned on a fixed surface. The platform 101 that is developed a protective exterior of the device and the components associated with the device are mounted over the platform 101. The platform 101 is preferably rectangular in shape and made up of stainless steel that offers a corrosion resistant, strength and durability to the device and is easy to maintain. 

[0024]	Underneath the platform 101, plurality of supporting legs 102 are installed for supporting the platform 101 and capable of adjusting height of the platform 101 from ground surface. Initially the user is needed to access a push button integrated on the platform 101 to activate the device. The button used herein is a push button. Upon pressing of the button, the circuits get closed allowing conduction of electricity that leads to activation of the device and vice versa. Upon activation of the device by the user, an inbuilt microcontroller embedded within the device and linked to the switch generates relative command. 

[0025]	A holding unit 103 is arranged on the platform 101 that is accessed by the user for engaging a check valve with the holding unit 103. Based on the received command, the microcontroller actuates an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101 to detect dimensions of the valve. The imaging unit 104 comprises of a processor and a camera which on actuation capture the multiple image of the surroundings. The camera is comprised of a lens and a digital camera sensor, wherein the camera lens takes all the light rays rebounding around the surroundings and utilizes the lenses to transmit them to a single point for creating a sharp image. When all of those light rays rebound back and meet together on a digital camera sensor, create a digital image of the surroundings by performing various operations like pre-processing, feature extraction and classification which is transmitted to the processor. 

[0026]	The processor further extracts all the required information from the digital images and transmit to microcontroller which further processes the information shared by the processor in order to detect dimensions of the valve and based on which microcontroller actuates plurality of motorized clippers 105 integrated within the holding unit 103 for securing the valve with the holding unit 103. The motorized clippers 105 employed herein is comprises of an end effector which is made of a pair of jaws hinged with each other by means of motorized joint which is comprises of an embedded motor. 

[0027]	On getting the actuation command from the microcontroller, the motor is capable to rotate in clock as well as in counter clock wise direction for enabling the opening/closing of the jaws of the effector for holding the members. The motor is capable of converting electric current into mechanical work by following the principle of Lorentz Law which states that, the current carrying conduction when placed in magnetic or electrical field experiences a force known as Lorentz force. Such that the motor converts the electrical current derived from an external source into a mechanical torque for providing the required rotational power to the jaws along a single axis for opening/closing the jaws for clasping the valve. 

[0028]	 A water chamber 107 installed on the platform 101 and integrated with a heating unit that is activated by the microcontroller for generating heat for heating the water. The heating unit consists of multiple electrically active coils of high resistive material, which on actuation generates heat by means of heat effect of current. The generated heat is utilized for heating the water to generate steam and the generated steam is transferred in plurality of water tubes 106 connected the holding unit 103 in a manner that the steam is passed through check valve to test the check valve. A temperature sensor is integrated within the chamber 107 for measuring temperature of chamber 107 and steam. The temperature sensor consists a conductive sensing element. On varying the temperature, the resistance of conductive element deviates which results in fluctuation in voltage flow across the sensing element. The voltage fluctuation cause the current to flow across the sensing element is detected by the microcontroller in form of electric pulse. Further the microcontroller evaluate the amplitude of the electric pulse to determine the temperature of steam and in case the detected temperature exceeds a threshold temperature then the microcontroller actuates turns off the heating unit and notifies the user if temperature exceeds a threshold value for safety purposes. the microcontroller automatically turns off the heating unit and notifies the user if temperature exceeds a threshold value for safety purposes. 

[0029]	An electronically controlled valve 108 integrated with each of the conduits that is actuated by the microcontroller along with activation of the heating unit, to regulate flow of superheated steam in the tubes 106, to check the valve under varying condition. The electronically controlled valve 108 comprises of a gate and a magnetic coil which uses electricity from microcontroller to generate the force to control the opening/closing of gate to control the flow of steam through a small aperture of the electronically controlled valve 108, allowing for precise control of the flow of steam in the check valve to test the valve under varying conditions. 

[0030]	The check valve is held in the holding unit 103 in a manner that the inlet an outlet of the valve is engaged with ends of the holding unit 103. A flow meter is connected to ends of the holding unit 103, to measure the flow rate at inlet and outlet of the valve. The flow meter consists of a sensor, rotor, and magnetic or optical detection unit. As the steam flows through the ends of holding unit 103, it passes over a rotor or turbine inside the flow meter. The flow of chemical causes the rotor to spin at a rate proportional to the flow rate. The sensor detects the rotor’s rotation or displacement and converts it into an electrical signal. This signal is then processed by the microcontroller to accurately measure the flow rate and in case the detect flow rates fund to be mismatching then considered to be faulty valve, and if found to be matching then the existing valve is considered to be correct valve. 

[0031]	Also a sound sensor integrated with the flow meters to measure intensity sound generated by check valve by varying steam flow rates and temperatures, by the valve and heating unit. The sound sensors work by converting sound waves into electrical signals. The sensor is designed to detect variations in air pressure caused by sound in the surrounding and transform those pressure fluctuations into electrical signals that is further processed, stored, or transmitted to the microcontroller. During the flow of steam across the valve on varying flow rates creaking sounding is generated, and creates a series of compressions and rarefactions in the surrounding medium, which constitute sound waves. 

[0032]	The acoustic sensor typically consists of a diaphragm, a magnet, and a coil. The diaphragm is a thin, flexible membrane that vibrates in response to the changes in air pressure caused by sound waves in the housing due to creaking sound. When the diaphragm vibrates, it moves the coil relative to the magnet, inducing an electric current in the coil due to electromagnetic induction. As the coil moves within the magnetic field of the sensor, it generates a varying electrical voltage proportional to the diaphragm’s motion. This voltage represents the electrical analog of the sound waves and is often referred to as the audio signal. The electrical signal generated by the sensor is amplified and converted into an analog electrical signal that is providing additional diagnostic information on valve performance.

[0033]	The fetched data is displayed on a touch-interactive display unit 109 attached to upper portion of the platform 101 for displaying these data related to physical characteristics of valve on the display unit 109 for allowing the user to carry out accurate performance analysis. The display unit 109 consists liquid crystal that flows like a liquid that contains some tiny solid part. The display unit 109 sends lights and electric current through the liquid crystals and this electric current causes the solid part to move around the display panel and further they block of let the light through in a certain way that make the picture on the display unit 109 depicting the data regarding information on valve performance. The display unit 109 is illustrated with options related to mode to monitor the valve to enable the user to to select operating modes and monitor status of the check valve and accordingly the microcontroller commands the relative components. 

[0034]	Also a corrosion detection sensor provided with the platform 101 to detect presence of corrosion over the check valve. The corrosion sensor used herein is preferably ultrasonic corrosion sensor which consists of an ultrasonic wave emitter, receiver and a sensing module. Upon actuation, the emitter sends the ultrasonic waves on the valve and the waves which are reflect back is received by receiver. The sensing module analyze the reflected back waves and based on the reflected waves, the sensor determines the rust on valve. After that the sensing module converts the determined data into the form of electrical signal and transmits to the microcontroller. 

[0035]	Upon successful detection of the corrosion the microcontroller activates a speaker 110 mounted on the platform 101 to produce audio alerts to notify the user regarding the detected corrosion. 

[0036]	When the valve is being tested, then an ultrasonic sensor which is integrated with the platform 101 works in synced with the imaging unit 104, for continuously monitoring dimensions of the check valve during testing. The ultrasonic sensor determines the dimension of the of valve by utilizing sound waves and analyzing the reflection pattern. The sensor consists of a transmitter that emits high-frequency ultrasonic waves and a receiver that detects the reflected waves. When the sensor is positioned in front of the valve, the emitted sound waves travel through the air and hit the valve. The waves then bounce back, or reflect, towards the sensor. The time it takes for the waves to travel to the valve and back is measured by the sensor. Since the speed of sound is constant, this time delay is used to calculate the distance between the sensor and the valve. The height is then determined by using the distance from the sensor to the valve and by means of the visual captured by the imaging unit 104 and the acquired data is sent to the microcontroller and that is displayed on the display unit 109 for providing real-time measurements of valve's physical parameters.

[0037]	 A battery is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrode named as a cathode and an anode. The battery use a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device. 

[0038]	The present invention works well in the following manner where the platform 101 positioned on the surface and in the holding unit 103 the user positions the check valve. The imaging unit 104 initially detects dimensions of the valve, based on which the microcontroller actuates plurality of motorized clippers 105 for securing the valve with the holding unit 103. Further plurality of water tubes 106 connected the holding unit 103, the water tubes 106 are connected with the water chamber 107 installed on the platform 101, wherein the water chamber 107 is integrated with the heating unit that is actuated by the microcontroller for heating water stored inside the chamber 107 for generating steam that is transferred within the conduits to test the check valve. The electronically controlled valve 108 control flow of superheated steam in the valve and the flow meter measures flow rate of steam during testing process, enabling accurate monitoring of steam usage. The sound sensor measures sound generated by check valve under varying steam flow rates and temperatures, providing additional diagnostic information on valve performance, that is displayed on the touch-interactive display unit 109 for accurate performance analysis. The corrosion detection sensor detects presence of corrosion over the check valve and upon successful detection the microcontroller activates the speaker 110 produces audio alerts to notify the user regarding the detected corrosion. 

[0039]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: ASSISTIVE DEVICE FOR RELOCATION OF OIL TANKS
abstract: An assistive device for relocation of oil tanks, comprising a curved-shaped frame 101 positioned on a ground surface via multiple wheels 103 provided beneath frame 101 to maneuver platform over surface, an imaging unit 105 installed on frame 101 detect dimension of an oil tank, a pair of telescopically operated rods 102 installed with frame 101, a pair of C-shaped extendable member 106 attached with rods 102 extend/retract for clasping oil tank within member 106, an angle sensor detect angle of member 106 with respect to oil tank, a L-shaped pole 110 integrated with a hinge mechanism adjust members 106 angle for adjusting position of oil tank, a base supporting panel 111 attached to frame 101 via a telescopic link 112 and equipped with motorized pop-out balls 113, extend/retract for engaging panel 111 with oil tank and assist in lifting, rotating, and stabilizing oil tank.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an assistive device for relocation of oil tanks that allows a user to relocate oil tanks or cylinders to a user-desired location in an easy manner by securely gripping the oil tank and absorbing any sudden shock over the ground surface while relocation.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Cylinders and oil tanks are relocated to ensure safe storage, transport, or placement for operational use. This is due to maintenance needs, equipment setup, or replenishing supply. Proper relocation prevents damage, leaks, or accidents, maintaining safety standards and ensuring the cylinder’s function effectively in their intended applications. Cylinders that need relocation typically include compressed gas cylinders (e.g., oxygen, nitrogen, propane), hydraulic cylinders, and industrial cylinders used in various machinery. Proper relocation ensures the oil tanks are protected from damage, leaks, or accidental discharge, maintaining both operational safety and longevity while preventing injuries or equipment malfunctions.

[0003]	 Traditionally, people relocate oil tanks manually using tools like dollies, trolleys, or hand trucks. The oil tanks are secured with straps or chains to prevent tipping during transport. Workers often roll smaller oil tanks by tilting them onto their edges or manually lifting lightweight ones. For heavier or pressurized cylinders, teams use carts with protective rails or cradles. Traditional methods of relocating oil tanks have several drawbacks. Manual handling increases the risk of accidents, such as dropping or tipping oil tanks, which lead to leaks or explosions, especially with pressurized gas cylinders. These methods are labor-intensive, requiring significant physical effort and often multiple workers, leading to potential injuries like strains or back pain.

[0004]	CN102328678A discloses about a gas cylinder transporting trolley. The gas cylinder transporting trolley comprises two parallel upright posts. The bottom ends of the upright posts are provided with bearing plates. At least three circular arc back cushions are arranged between the two upright posts. A gas cylinder can be safely leaned against the back cushions. The upper ends of the upright posts extend to form handles convenient to hold by transporting personnel. The rear parts of the upright posts are provided with shifters and clamping devices. The gas cylinder transporting trolley has simple structure, is convenient to operate, can be subjected to multi-position regulation, is suitable for heights of different people and is convenient to use. Meanwhile, better fixation is provided and the safety is improved.

[0005]	CN203876785U discloses about a gas cylinder trolley. The gas cylinder trolley comprises a pushing frame and a trolley frame, wherein the pushing frame and the trolley frame are mutually assembled, and the lower part of the trolley frame is connected with a slipping unit which moves along the forward direction. The gas cylinder trolley is characterized in that the pushing frame is provided with two pushing arms, at least one supporting seat and a protecting cover, the supporting seat is bridged across the two opposite sides of the two pushing arms to be used for placing gas cylinders, and the protecting cover is assembled above the two pushing arms to be used for protecting the gas cylinders. The gas cylinder trolley has the beneficial effects that the structure of the gas cylinder trolley is simple and the manufacturing cost is low. When the gas cylinder trolley is used, the gas cylinders are required to be sleeved into a gas cylinder holding space of the gas cylinder trolley to be seated on the supporting seat. Because the protecting cover is arranged on the supporting seat, the gas cylinder trolley is very safe during transportation or stagnation. The gas cylinder trolley also has the characteristics of fast transportation and high efficiency.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of assisting a user in relocating oil tanks. However, these devices are incapable of relocating the oil tanks to the user-specified location in an easy and secured manner by securely gripping the oil tank, and fails in reducing manual efforts and consumption of time in the overall process. Additionally, these existing devices also lacks in absorbing any jerk produced during relocation of the cylinder.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of assisting a user in relocating oil tanks to a user-specified location in a secured manner by properly accommodating the oil tank as per their dimensions. In addition, the developed device also adjusts the angle of the accommodate oil tank to prevent tilting of the tank.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of monitoring the weight of the oil tank and accordingly notify the user in case the detected weight is determined to be overweight condition, thereby eliminating any harm cause due to overweight.

[0021]	The present invention relates to an assistive device for relocation of oil tanks that aids a user in relocation of cylinder to a user-specified location by automatically lifting and gripping the cylinder. Additionally, the proposed device is capable of detecting unevenness of the ground surface during relocation and accordingly absorbs any sudden jerk in order to maintain the stability of the device during relocation.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an assistive device for relocation of oil tanks is illustrated, comprising a curved-shaped frame 101 installed with a pair of telescopically operated rods 102, multiple wheels 103 are provided beneath the frame 101, a microphone 104 provided with the frame 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 installed on the frame 101, a pair of C-shaped extendable member 106 provided between the rods 102 and attached with the rods 102 via a motorized ball-and-socket joint 107, plurality of electromagnets 108 provided on an outer surface of the member 106, a pair of motorized sliding units 109 provided between the rods 102 and member 106, a L-shaped pole 110 configured between the sliding unit and member 106, a base supporting panel 111 attached to frame 101 via a telescopic link 112, plurality of motorized pop-out balls 113 located along inner periphery of panel 111, a damping unit 114 integrated between the frame 101 and wheels 103, a pair of handles 115 attached with the rods 102, a UV-sanitization unit 116 is arranged on the handle 115, and a speaker 117 embedded on the frame 101.

[0023]	 The device disclosed herein comprises of a curved-shaped frame 101 incorporating various components associated with the device and positioned on a ground surface by means of multiple wheels 103 (ranging from 3 to 4 in numbers) arranged underneath the frame 101. The frame 101 serves as the core component of the device and is made from strong, lightweight, and water proof materials which includes but not limited to hardened steel, aluminum alloy, hard fiber, and composite materials. These materials offer strength and rigidity to the frame 101 making it resistant to mechanical stress and pressure. Vibration-dampening materials are integrated into the frame 101 to minimize noise and shaking of the frame 101 during operations.

[0024]	 The frame 101 is arranged with a pair of telescopically operated rods 102 affixed perpendicularly over the frame 101 and configured with a pair of C-shaped extendable member 106 attached between the rods 102, each via a motorized ball-and-socket joint 107, wherein a user is required to activate the device manually by pressing a button installed on the frame 101 and linked with an inbuilt microcontroller associated with the device. The button is a type of switch that is internally connected with the device via multiple circuits that upon pressing by the user, the circuits get closed and starts conduction of electricity that tends to activate the device and vice versa.

[0025]	 After activation of the device, the user is required to access a microphone 104 integrated with the frame 101 for providing input voice commands regarding assisting in relocating an oil tank present in proximity, from one place to another. The microphone 104 receives the user voice commands and converts the sound energy emitted by the user into electrical energy. Inside the microphone 104, a diaphragm made of plastic is present that moves back and forth when the sound wave hits the diaphragm, which then moves a coil attached to the diaphragm in the same way in order to generate an electrical signal proportional to the sound. The electric signal from coil flows to an amplifier which amplifies the electrical signal. The amplified electrical signal is then sent to the microcontroller linked to the microphone 104.

[0026]	 Upon receiving and processing the signal from the microphone 104, the microcontroller recognizes the user input voice command, and accordingly actuates an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 installed on the frame 101 and integrated with a processor for capturing and processing multiple images in a vicinity of the frame 101. The artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 comprises of a high-resolution camera lens, digital camera sensor and a processor, wherein the lens captures multiple images from different angles and perspectives in vicinity of the frame 101 with the help of digital camera sensor for providing comprehensive coverage of the surroundings.

[0027]	 The captured images then go through pre-processing steps by the processor integrated with the camera. The processor carries out a sequence of image processing operation including pre-processing, feature extraction and classification in order to enhance the image quality, which includes adjusting brightness and contrast and removing any distortion or noise. The pre-processed images are transmitted to the microcontroller linked with the processor in the form of electrical signals.

[0028]	 The microcontroller continuously processes the received signals from the imaging unit 105 in order to determine the presence and dimension of an oil tank present in proximity to the frame 101. Based on the detected dimensions of the oil tank, the microcontroller actuates a pair of motorized sliding units 109 provided between the rods 102 and the member 106 to translate the member 106 over the sliding unit, in order to place the member 106 at an optimum position over the oil tank suitable for clasping the oil tank. 

[0029]	The sliding unit used herein consists of a sliding-rail and multiple rolling members 106 which are integrated with a step motor. On actuation, the step motor rotates the rolling members 106 in order to provide rolling motion to the members 106 which results in translation of the extendable member 106 for positioning the member 106 at an optimum height over the oil tank.

[0030]	Post positioning of the member 106, the microcontroller actuates the member 106 to extend and retract in a repetitive manner as per the dimension of the oil tank, in synchronization with actuation of the ball-and-socket joint 107 for gripping the oil tank within the member 106. The extension/retraction of the member 106 is powered by a drawer arrangement integrated in each of the member 106. The drawer arrangement consists of a motor, hollow compartment and multiple compartments that are connected with sliders.

[0031]	 Upon actuation by the microcontroller, an electric current pass through the motor of the drawer mechanism and energized the motor. The energized motor further actuates the compartments which are initially at the stowed condition to move in a successive manner within the hollow compartment and extends/ retracts length of the compartments. Simultaneously, each of the compartments having a fixed groove track, wherein upon actuation of the slider, the motor of the slider gets energized and provides a movement to the compartment to move in a linear direction on the groove track of the successive compartment as directed by the microcontroller to extend/retract the member 106 in a repetitive manner, for clasping the oil tank within the member 106.

[0032]	 Synchronously, the microcontroller actuates the motorized ball and socket joint 107 to provide required movement to the member 106 in order to enable the member 106 to properly position the member 106 in contact with the oil tank. The motorized ball and socket joint 107 used herein is a mechanical component that connects the member 106 to the rods 102. The ball and socket joint 107 permits rotational and tilting movements, enabling the members 106 to rotate on its axis.

[0033]	 The ball and socket joint 107 is a coupling consisting of a ball joint 107 securely locked within a socket joint 107, where the ball joint 107 is able to move in a 360-dgree rotation within the socket thus, providing the required movement to the members 106. The ball and socket joint 107 is powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller for providing required rotation to the members 106 in order to properly accommodating the oil tank within the member 106.

[0034]	Upon clasping of the oil tank within the member 106, the microcontroller energize multiple electromagnets 108 provided on an outer surface of the member 106 for facilitating secure attachment of the oil tank with the member 106. The electromagnets 108 used herein consist of a coil of wire wrapped around a core of ferromagnetic material, such as iron. On actuation by the microcontroller, an electric current flows through the coil, that generates a magnetic field around the coil, which magnetizes the core of the electromagnets 108 to act as a magnet for providing secure attachment of the oil tank with the member 106.

[0035]	 Upon securing the tank with the member 106, an angle sensor installed on the frame 101 works in collaboration with the imaging unit 105 to detect angle of the member 106 with respect to the oil tank. The angle sensor uses light beams and optical detectors for measuring changes in light reflection or transmission caused by the angle of inclination of the member 106 with respect to the oil tank. As the angle changes, the amount of light reflected or transmitted varies, allowing the sensor to calculate the angle. The angle sensor provides an output signal corresponding to the detected angle that is sent to the microcontroller in the form of electrical signals.
 
[0036]	 The microcontroller continuously processes the signals received from the angle sensor to monitor the angle of the member 106. Based on which the microcontroller regulates actuation of a L-shaped pole 110 integrated with a hinge mechanism and configured between the sliding unit and the member 106 to apply pressure over the oil tank in order correct tilt angle of the oil tank. The hinge mechanism integrates an electric motor with a traditional hinge mechanism to enable controlled, automated tilting movement of the pole 110 around a fixed axis.

[0037]	 The hinge mechanism comprises of a pair of leaf that are screwed with the surface of the pole 110 and frame 101. The leafs are connected with each other by means of a cylindrical member 106 integrated with a shaft coupled with a DC (Direct Current) motor to provide required movement to the hinge. The rotation of the shaft in clockwise and anti-clockwise direction provides required tilting movement to the hinge, that in turn tilt the pole 110 to adjust the angle of the members 106 for adjusting position of the oil tank.

[0038]	A base supporting panel 111 is attached to frame 101 via a telescopic link 112, wherein upon adjusting position of the oil tank, the microcontroller actuates the link 112 to extend and engage the supporting panel 111 with the bottom of the oil tank. The extension of the telescopic link 112 is powered by a pneumatic unit associated with device, that includes an air compressor, air cylinder, air valves and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the telescopic link 112.

[0039]	The air compressor used herein extract the air from surrounding and increases the pressure of the air by reducing the volume of the air. The air compressor is consisting of two main parts including a motor and a pump. The motor powers the compressor pump which uses the energy from the motor drive to draw in atmospheric air and compress to elevated pressure. The compressed air is then sent through a discharge tube into the cylinder across the valve. The compressed air in the cylinder tends to pushes out the piston to extend. The piston is attached to the rods 102, wherein the extension of the piston corresponds to the extension of the link 112 to extend and engage the supporting panel 111 with the bottom of the oil tank in order to assist the user in lifting the oil tank.

[0040]	Further, the microcontroller actuates multiple motorized pop-out balls 113 located along inner periphery of the supporting panel 111 for providing required rotation to the oil tank over the panel 111. The pop-out balls 113 used herein are equipped with small DC (direct current) motors that enable them to extend outward and retract as needed. Upon getting actuation command from the microcontroller, the motor starts rotating in clockwise and anticlockwise direction in a controlled manner for producing rotational motion. This force is then transmitted to the mechanism that forces the ball out of its compartment to rotate in clockwise and anticlockwise direction in order to provide required rotation to the oil tank over the panel 111 for stabilizing the oil tank for relocation.

[0041]	Upon stabilizing the oil tank over the panel 111, the microcontroller actuates the telescopically operated rods 102 to extend/retract as per the detected height of oil tank in order to position a pair of handles 115 attached with the rods 102 at an optimum height. The extension of the rods 102 is powered by the pneumatic unit in the same manner as described above. 

[0042]	Once the handles 115 are positioned, the user is required to access the handle 115 to maneuver the frame 101 in order to relocate the oil tank. During movement of the frame 101 over the surface, the microcontroller in association with an ultrasonic sensor mounted on the frame 101 and synced with the imaging unit 105, detect unevenness on ground surface. 

[0043]	The ultrasonic sensor consists of an emitter that emits high-frequency ultrasonic sound waves towards the ground surface. These sound waves strikes the ground surface and gets reflected back and received by a receiver inside the sensor. The sensor measures the time it takes for the waves to bounce back after hitting the ground surface. By calculating the round-trip time and applying the speed of sound, the sensor detects unevenness on ground surface and sends acquired data to the microcontroller in the form of electrical signal.

[0044]	The microcontroller processes the received signals from the ultrasonic sensor in order to detect unevenness on ground surface and accordingly actuates a damping unit 114 integrated between the frame 101 and wheels 103 to absorb sudden shock and ensure stability of the frame 101. The damping unit 114 comprises of a cylinder filled with hydraulic fluid or gas, a piston rod, and valves. When the wheel 103 encounters a bump, the piston inside the cylinder compresses, forcing the fluid or gas through small valves. This process converts kinetic energy into heat, dissipating the shock. The damping unit’s 114 springs or flexible mounts further assist in cushioning the impact, preventing abrupt jolts from transferring to the frame 101 during the relocation of the oil tank.

[0045]	After each use of the device, the microcontroller activates a UV (ultraviolet) -sanitization unit 116 arranged on the handle 115 for automatically sanitizing the frame 101. The sanitization unit comprises of UV-C light emitters, sensors, and a reflective chamber or enclosure. On actuation, the UV-C emitters activate and direct high-energy light onto the frame 101. The UV-C rays penetrate microorganisms, disrupting their DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) or RNA (ribonucleic acid), rendering them inactive, in order to sanitize the frame 101.

[0046]	The microcontroller in association with a weight sensor installed on the panel 111, monitor the weight of the oil tank. The weight sensor used herein is a particular kind of transducer, more especially a weight transducer, which transform a mechanical force that is applied as an input, by the weight of the oil tank, into a change in electrical resistance, which varies proportionally to the force being applied to the sensor. This change in electrical resistance is detected by the microcontroller linked with the sensor, in the form of an electrical signal.

[0047]	The microcontroller processes the received signals from the weight sensors in order to monitor weight of the oil tank over the panel 111 and when the weight of the tank exceeds a predefined threshold, the microcontroller generates an alert notification through a speaker 117 embedded on the frame 101. The speaker 117 used herein is capable of producing clear and natural sound and is capable of adjusting its volume based on ambient noise levels.

[0048]	The speaker 117 consists of audio information, which is in the form of recorded voice, synthesized voice, or other sounds, generated or stored as digital data. The digital audio data is converted into analog electrical signals. Further the analog signal is amplified by an amplifier and the amplified electrical audio signal is then sent to a diaphragm, which is typically made of a lightweight and rigid material like paper, plastic, or metal, and is designed to vibrate or move back and forth when electrical signals are fed to it. This movement creates pressure variations in the surrounding air, generating sound waves in order to generate the audible sound for notifying the user regarding the overweight.

[0049]	Lastly, a battery is installed within the device which is connected to the microcontroller that supplies current to all the electrically powered components that needs an amount of electric power to perform their functions and operation in an efficient manner. The battery utilized here, is generally a dry battery which is made up of Lithium-ion material that gives the device a long-lasting as well as an efficient DC (Direct Current) current which helps every component to function properly in an efficient manner. As the device is battery operated and do not need any electrical voltage for functioning. Hence the presence of battery leads to the portability of the device i.e., user is able to place as well as moves the device from one place to another as per the requirements.

[0050]	The proposed invention works best in the following manner, where the curved-shaped frame 101 is positioned on the ground surface via multiple wheels 103 for allowing the user to maneuver the platform over the surface as per preferences. The user access the microphone 104 to provide voice commands for assisting in relocating the oil tank present in proximity. Based on which the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 105 installed on the frame 101 and paired with the processor detect presence and dimension of the oil tank present in proximity. Based on the detected dimensions of oil tank the pair of C-shaped extendable member 106 extends and retract in the repetitive manner in view of clasping the oil tank within the member 106. Simultaneously, the pair of motorized sliding units 109 translate the member 106 over the sliding unit for positioning the member 106 at the optimum position. Followed by energization of plurality of electromagnets 108 for facilitating secure attachment of the oil tank with the member 106. Subsequently, the angle sensor works in collaboration of the imaging unit 105 to detect angle of the member 106 with respect to the oil tank. Accordingly, the L-shaped pole 110 adjusts position of the oil tank. Further, the telescopic link 112 extends and retract for enabling the base supporting panel 111 to engage with the oil tank and assist in lifting. Simultaneously, the motorized pop-out balls 113 rotate and stabilize the oil tank for further operations. Based on the detected height of object/ oil tank, the pair of telescopically operated rods 102 extends/ retracts for positioning the pair of handles 115 attached with the rods 102 at the optimum height and allowing the user to maneuver the frame 101 for relocation of the oil tank. Synchronously, the ultrasonic sensor synced with the imaging unit 105 detect unevenness on ground surface during movement of the frame 101 over the surface. Accordingly, the damping unit 114 absorb sudden shock and ensure stability of the frame 101.  The weight sensor detects the weight of the tank and when weight of the tank exceeds the predefined threshold. The speaker 117 generates the alert notification to notify the user.
