The determined speed of the vehicle is sent to the microcontroller where the determined speed is compared with a predefined threshold value saved in a database linked to the microcontroller.

[0036]	In case, the detected speed of the vehicle approaching from behind exceeds the predefined threshold, the microcontroller activates a speaker integrated into the infotainment unit. The speaker is triggered to generate an audible alert to notify the user of the potential risk. The speaker works by converting the electrical signal into the audio signal. The speaker consists of a cone known as a diaphragm attached to a coil-shaped wire placed between two magnets. When the electric signal is passed through the voice coil, a varying magnetic field is generated by the coil that interacts with the magnet causing the diaphragm to move back and forth. The movement of the diaphragm pushes and pulls air creating sound waves just like the electrical signal received and used to notify the user. The alert advises the driver to change lanes for safer driving and avoid being overtaken in hazardous conditions. 

[0037]	While changing the lanes as notified by the speaker, the microcontroller activates a turn signal indicating sensor within the body 101 that works in synchronization with the imaging unit 102 to detect the direction in which the vehicle is turning. The turn signal indicating sensor detects the vehicle's turning through motion, angular position, or signal input monitoring. The turn signal indicating sensor utilize gyroscopic sensors, accelerometers, or is directly linked to the vehicle's electronic turn signal unit. When the driver engages a turn signal, the sensor captures the activation data or senses changes in the vehicle's lateral motion and angular orientation. This data is processed to determine the vehicle's turning direction. 

[0038]	Based on the detected direction, the microcontroller activates a series of yellow LEDs (Light Emitting diodes) lights 109 attached to the cuboidal body 101, causing the LEDs (Light Emitting diode) 109 to blink and signal the vehicle's intended turn. LEDs (Light Emitting diodes) lights 109 (Light Emitting diodes) are made from semiconductor materials which have properties that allow them to emit light. The LEDs (Light Emitting diodes) 109 contains a p-n junction, where a p-type region is positively charged and an n-type region is negatively charged. When voltage is applied, electrons from the n-region move towards the p-region, and holes from the p-region move towards the n-region. As the electrons move across the p-n junction, they recombine with the holes. During this process, the electrons lose energy, and this energy is released in the form of photons (light).

[0039]	Moreover, a battery is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrodes known as a cathode and an anode. A voltage is generated between the anode and cathode via oxidation/reduction and thus produces the electrical energy to provide to the device.

[0040]	The present invention, works best in the following manner, where the hollow cuboidal body 101 is attached to the lower edge of the side-view mirror. The user-interface in the vehicle's infotainment unit wirelessly provides input commands for securing the body 101 over the side view mirror of the vehicle. Upon receiving commands, the artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102 captures and processes images of the side-view mirror to determine its lower edge dimensions. Motorized clamps 103 adjust accordingly to acquire the secure grip. The ultrasonic sensor measures the distance between the body 101 and the mirror's lower edge, prompting the telescopically operated rod 104 to extend or retract, ensuring optimal positioning. The blind spot mirror 105, mounted on the telescopically operated bar 106, extends outward to enhance visibility of blind spots during lane changes or turns. The motorized ball and socket joint 107 adjusts the mirror 105 angle as per user preference for better viewing. The radar gun 108 detects the speed of approaching vehicles, triggering the audio alert through the infotainment unit in case, the detected speed exceeds the threshold, prompting the user to change lanes. The turn signal indicating sensor, synchronized with the imaging unit 102, detects the vehicle's turning direction and activates yellow LED lights 109 attached to the body 101 to signal turning intentions clearly. 

[0041]	 Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: EXAMINATION MONITORING SYSTEM
abstract: An examination monitoring system, comprising of a plurality of bodies 101 adapted to be positioned inside a classroom, the bodies 101 are configured with multiple Omni-directional wheels 102 to maneuver the bodies 101 over the classroom, an imaging unit 103 to detect students entering inside the classroom, a laser emitter 104 installed over the body, to emit laser light onto the designated seat to guide the student to their assigned seat with the classroom, a holographic projection unit 105 installed over the bodies 101, to project holographic images of student’s roll number and desk location on an invigilator’s desk, multiple plates 201 to extend to create a physical barrier around the student’s desk, a motorized clamping unit 106 to grasp the answer sheet from the concerned student and provide a new sheet to the student from a chamber 107 stored with multiple sheets.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an examination monitoring system that is capable of managing and monitoring examination environments by automating seating arrangements, student monitoring, and cheating prevention during examinations, thus ensure an efficient and fair examination process.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Examination monitoring plays a crucial role in maintaining fairness and integrity during academic assessments ensuring that students follow the rules and that exams are conducted in a controlled environment. Effective monitoring helps prevent cheating and other unauthorized activities, thereby upholding the credibility of the examination process. Examination monitoring faces several challenges that compromise the fairness and integrity of the assessment process. One major issue is the difficulty in effectively supervising a large number of students, which increases the chances of undetected cheating. Human invigilators become fatigued or distracted, leading to lapses in observation. Verifying student identities and ensuring they are seated in their designated spots is time-consuming and prone to errors, especially in crowded exam halls. Additionally, subtle forms of cheating, such as hidden notes, unauthorized devices, or communication between students, are often hard to detect through manual monitoring. Invigilators also struggle to maintain consistent vigilance throughout the exam duration, increasing the risk of misconduct. In cases where cheating is suspected, to gather concrete evidence without disrupting the examination is a challenge. These issues highlight the need for more efficient, accurate, and reliable examination monitoring solutions.

[0003]	 Traditional examination monitoring primarily relies on human invigilators who supervise students during exams to ensure compliance with rules and prevent cheating. Invigilators manually verify student identities, often by checking admit cards or identification documents, and guide students to their assigned seats based on seating charts. Throughout the examination, they observe students’ behavior, looking for signs of misconduct such as copying, unauthorized communication, or the use of prohibited materials. In larger exam halls, multiple invigilators are positioned at different locations to cover the entire area effectively. Some institutions also use basic surveillance tools like CCTV cameras to assist invigilators in monitoring the room. However, these systems often require manual review and lack real-time intervention capabilities. Despite these efforts, traditional methods heavily depend on human vigilance, which is affected by fatigue or oversight, potentially allowing instances of cheating or rule violations to go unnoticed.

[0004]	EP1987505A2 disclose systems, methods and apparatuses for remotely monitoring examinations. Examinations are authored and rules are attributed to the exams that determine how the exams are to be administered. Exam proctors monitor exam takers from remote locations by receiving data indicative of the environment in which the exam takers are completing the exams.

[0005]	CN203397186U discloses an examination monitoring system, comprising a cloud computing platform, at least one monitoring terminal and at least one network matrix. The cloud computing platform is connected to the monitoring terminal via an IP network. The monitoring terminal, which is correspondingly connected to the network matrix one by one, comprises at least one carriage, on which a control mainboard, a microphone, a signal jammer, a touch display screen and at least one camera are arranged integrally. The microphone, the signal jammer, the touch display screen and the camera are connected with the control mainboard. The carriage can be disposed in an examination room, so that images on the inside of the examination room can be acquired in real time via the camera on the carriage, meanwhile audio about the inside of the examination room can be captured via the microphone, and then the acquired images and audio are transmitted to the cloud computing platform by the monitoring terminal, thereby realizing monitoring of the inside of the examination room.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many systems have been developed to facilitate examination monitoring, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to identifying students and guiding them to their designated seats is time-consuming and prone to errors. Additionally, detecting subtle forms of misconduct, such as hidden notes or unauthorized communication between students, is often difficult. Human invigilators miss instances of cheating due to fatigue, distraction, or the sheer number of students present.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a system that is capable of monitoring student behaviour during examinations to detect unauthorized activities, managing student seating arrangements, and providing real-time monitoring of student behaviour during the examination.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of monitoring student behavior during examinations to detect unauthorized activities, in view of ensuring integrity and preventing cheating, thus allows for real-time detection and intervention, thereby upholding the exam's security and fairness

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a system that is capable of automatically managing student seating arrangements by identifying students and guiding them to their assigned seats based on pre-configured seating charts, thereby eliminating confusion and improving the organization of the examination process.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an examination monitoring system that is capable of facilitating the observation of student actions throughout the examination process in order to enable the identification of improper conduct, thereby preserving the security and fairness of the assessment environment. 

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, an examination monitoring system comprises of a plurality of bodies adapted to be positioned inside a classroom at different locations, the bodies are configured with plurality of Omni-directional wheels to maneuver the bodies over the classroom as per requirement, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the bodies and integrated with a processor for capturing and processing images of the surroundings to detect students entering inside the classroom, an optical character recognition (OCR) module installed over one of the body to work in sync with the imaging unit to scans an admit card held by the students and cross-references the data with a predefined seating arrangement to fetch designated seat of the student within the classroom, a laser emitter installed over the body, to emit laser light onto the designated seat to guide the student to their assigned seat with the classroom.

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. [0021]	The present invention relates to an examination monitoring system that enable continuous supervision of student conduct during tests to identify and address any unauthorized actions, in view of ensuring the exam’s legitimacy and discouraging cheating, thus permits prompt identification and corrective measures, for guaranteeing that the examination remains secure and equitable for all participants. 

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, and 2 a perspective view of a body associated with an examination monitoring system and an inner view of a classroom that is associated with the proposed system is illustrated, respectively, comprising a plurality of bodies 101 adapted to be positioned inside a classroom at different locations, the bodies 101 are configured with plurality of Omni-directional wheels 102, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 103 installed on the bodies 101, a laser emitter 104 installed over the body, a holographic projection unit 105 installed over the bodies 101, Plurality of extendable plates 201 are installed on each of central and lateral side of student’s desk, a motorized clamping unit 106 is installed over each of the bodies 101, a chamber 107 installed over the bodies 101. 

[0023]	 The device disclosed herein comprising a plurality of bodies 101 are designed to be strategically placed at various locations within a classroom. Each body is equipped with a plurality of omni-directional wheels 102 (preferably 2 to 6in numbers), enabling it to maneuver effortlessly across the classroom floor in any direction as needed. This configuration allows for precise positioning and movement of the bodies 101, providing flexibility in their placement within the classroom environment to serve specific functions, such as monitoring, guiding, or interacting with students. The omni-directional wheels 102 ensure smooth and efficient movement, facilitating dynamic adjustments in response to classroom requirements or operational needs. 

[0024]	 The omnidirectional wheels 102 comprises a wheel coupled with a motor via a shaft that is designed to move the bodies 101 in any direction without changing the orientation of the bodies 101 offering exceptional maneuverability to the bodies 101. Upon actuation of the wheels 102 by the microcontroller, the motor starts to rotate in clockwise or anti-clockwise direction in order to provide movement to the wheels 102 via the shaft. The wheels 102 thus enables the bodies 101 to move seamlessly in any direction, making it valuable for moving and positioning bodies 101 over the classroom as per requirement.

[0025]	 The bodies 101 are installed with an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 103 which detect students entering inside the classroom. The imaging unit 103 disclosed herein comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images of the surroundings and the captured images are stored within memory of the imaging unit 103 in form of an optical data. 

[0026]	The imaging unit 103 also comprises of the processor which processes the captured images. This pre-processing involves tasks such as noise reduction, image stabilization, or color correction. The processed data is fed into AI protocols for analysis which utilizes machine learning techniques, such as deep learning neural networks, to extract meaningful information from the visual data which are processed by the microcontroller to detect students entering inside the classroom.

[0027]	 Synchronously, an optical character recognition (OCR) module which is installed on one of the bodies 101, functioning in coordination with the imaging unit 103 to scan the admit card presented by the students. The OCR module processes the data extracted from the admit card and cross-references it with a predefined seating arrangement stored in a database linked to the microcontroller. This enables the microcontroller to retrieve the specific, designated seat assigned to each student within the classroom, ensuring efficient and accurate seat assignment. The synchronized operation of the OCR and imaging unit 103 enhances the accuracy and speed of the seating process. 

[0028]	 The Optical Character Recognition (OCR) module works by using the imaging unit 103 to capture an image of the text on an object, such as an admit card. The captured image is then processed by the OCR module, which identifies and extracts the alphanumeric characters from the image. These characters are converted into machine-readable text. The OCR module compares this extracted text with data stored in a database to retrieve relevant information, such as the student's designated seat number. The data is then transmitted to the microcontroller for further processing and action, ensuring accurate seat assignment. 

[0029]	 Upon fetching the designated seat, the microcontroller actuates a laser emitter 104 installed over the body. The laser emitter 104 works by stimulating atoms or molecules to release photons in a specific direction, creating a coherent beam of light. This process involves the use of a gain medium, such as a crystal or gas, and mirrors to amplify and reflect the light back and forth to produce a powerful and focused beam on the designated seat to guide the student to their assigned seat with the classroom.

[0030]	The bodies 101 are installed with a holographic projection unit 105 which project holographic images of student’s roll number and desk location on an invigilator’s desk. The holographic projection unit 105 disclosed herein, comprises of multiple lens. After getting the actuation command from the microcontroller, a light source integrated in the projection unit 105 emits various combination of lights toward the lens which is further portrayed to project holographic images of student’s roll number and desk location on an invigilator’s desk and simultaneously reactivates the laser emitter 104 to project light on the concerned student’s seat to take necessary actions.

[0031]	 A plurality of extendable plates 201 (preferably 2 to 6 in numbers) is positioned on both the central and lateral sides of each student's desk. In the event that the microcontroller, through the imaging unit 103, detects repeated or continuous cheating attempts by a student, the microcontroller activates the extendable plates 201. These plates 201 extend outward to form a physical barrier around the student's desk. This serves to prevent any unauthorized interaction with other students, ensuring that the student remains isolated, thereby reducing the possibility of cheating and maintaining the integrity of the examination environment.

[0032]	 The plates 201 are embedded with a drawer arrangement, that consists of multiple plates 201 that are overlapped to each other with a sliding unit, wherein upon actuation of the multiple plates 201 and sliding unit by the microcontroller, the motor in the sliding unit starts rotating a wheels 102 coupled via a shaft in clockwise/anticlockwise direction providing a movement to the slider in the drawer arrangement to extend to create a physical barrier around the student’s desk, thereby preventing unauthorized interaction with other students.

[0033]	 A motorized clamping unit 106 is integrated into each of the bodies 101. If the microcontroller, using the imaging unit 103 in conjunction with the optical character recognition (OCR) module, detects the presence of hidden notes, unauthorized markings, or an attempt to swap answer sheets, the microcontroller triggers the clamping unit 106. This action causes the clamping unit 106 to grasp the answer sheet from the student in question. Simultaneously, a new answer sheet is provided to the student from a chamber 107 installed on the body, which contains multiple sheets. This ensures the prevention of cheating and maintains the integrity of the examination.

[0034]	The clamping unit 106 used herein has an open side and a curved side, forming a partial circle or a half-moon shape. At the open side of the clamping unit 106, there is a screw mechanism which includes a threaded screw or spindle and an electric motor.  As the motor rotates it causes the screw to move in or out, which in turn adjusts the width of the clamp opening and eventually applies the required force to grip the answer sheet from the concerned student and provide a new sheet to the student from the chamber 107. 

[0035]	 Moreover, a battery is associated with the system for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the system and supplying a voltage to the components. The battery used herein is preferably a Lithium-ion battery which is a rechargeable unit that demands power supply after getting drained. The battery stores the electric current derived from an external source in the form of chemical energy, which when required by the electronic component of the system, derives the required power from the battery for proper functioning of the system. 

[0036]	The present invention works in the best manner, where the plurality of bodies 101 adapted to be positioned inside the classroom at different locations. The bodies 101 are configured with plurality of Omni-directional wheels 102 to maneuver the bodies 101 over the classroom as per requirement. title: AUTOMATED DEVICE FOR WRAPPING PIPE BUNDLE
abstract: An automated device for wrapping pipe bundle comprises of a platform 101 positioned on a fixed surface having plurality of suction cups 102 to secure platform 101, a touch interactive display panel 103 to provide input command regarding wrapping of a bundle of pipes with protective sheet and notify user regarding weight of bundle, an imaging unit 104 to detect placement of a bundle of pipe, an inverted U-shaped frame 105 with a pair of robotic grippers 106 to grip bundle, a pair of holding unit 108 to secure an end of sheet on an end of bundle for covering bundle, a motorized roller 109 unwraps sheet in accordance to evaluated length, a RPM sensor monitors length of unwrapped sheet, a robotic link 111 cuts sheet via a motorized cutter 110, a chamber 112 to store plurality of adhesive patches to secure end of sheet, to prevent unraveling of sheet.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle that wraps a pipe bundle in an automated manner by using an appropriate length of wrapping sheet as per the dimension of the bundle and also secure the wrapped sheet over the bundle by automatically applying adhesive patches over the ends of the wrapped sheet to prevent unravelling of the sheet.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Wrapping pipe bundles securely is essential for ensuring their protection during storage, handling, and transportation. Proper wrapping safeguards the pipes from environmental factors such as moisture, dust, and physical damage, preserving their structural integrity and preventing corrosion or surface wear. Achieving a uniform and tightly wrapped covering is crucial for maintaining the stability of the bundle, reducing the risk of shifting or loosening during movement. Inconsistent or inadequate wrapping leads to exposure, increasing the likelihood of material degradation or damage. Ensuring that the wrapping process is carried out with precision, using an appropriate length of material tailored to the bundle's dimensions, enhances efficiency and minimises material wastage. Securing the ends of the wrapped covering prevents unravelling, maintaining the protective layer’s effectiveness throughout handling and transport. A well-executed wrapping process contributes to safer handling, reduced maintenance costs, and improved longevity of the pipes.

[0003]	 Traditional methods for wrapping pipe bundles often rely on manual labour and basic tools, requiring significant effort and time. These approaches present several drawbacks. For example, conventional wrapping techniques lack the precision needed to ensure uniform coverage, leading to inconsistencies that compromise the protection of the pipes. Furthermore, manual methods do not account for variations in bundle dimensions, resulting in excess material usage or insufficient coverage. The absence of automated adjustments for determining the appropriate length of wrapping material increases material wastage and the likelihood of inadequate protection. Additionally, securing the wrapped covering manually is prone to errors, leading to loose ends that may unravel during handling or transport. Ensuring a consistent and secure wrapping process requires an advanced approach that enhances precision, minimises waste, and maintains the integrity of the bundle throughout storage and transportation.

[0004]	CN105691721A discloses about an invention that relates to a full-automatic pipe packaging machine. The full-automatic pipe packaging machine comprises a pipe stacking machine used for stacking pipes, a bundling machine used for bundling the stacked pipes and a wrapping machine used for arranging packaging bags on the bundled pipes in a sleeving mode, wherein the input end of the bundling machine is connected to the output end of the pipe stacking machine in a butt joint mode, and the input end of the wrapping machine is connected to the output end of the bundling machine in a butt joint mode; the pipe stacking machine is provided with a pushing mechanism used for pushing the stacked pipes to a bundling station of the bundling machine, and the wrapping machine is provided with a clamping device used for clamping the bundled pipes and conveying the bundled pipes to a wrapping station of the wrapping machine. Through the pipe stacking machine, the bundling machine and the wrapping machine, full automation of the processes from forming to packaging of the pipes is realized, and the packaging efficiency of the pipes is greatly improved.

[0005]	CN216882366U discloses about a utility model belongs to the technical field of finished steel pipe packing, and particularly relates to automatic welding equipment for steel pipe straps; the steel pipe bundle wrapping and sealing device comprises a wrapping and packaging mechanism and a welding mechanism moving along the wrapping and packaging mechanism, wherein the wrapping and packaging mechanism comprises a plurality of packaging units arranged in an in-line mode, the packaging units are used for gathering a steel pipe bundle and pressing a wrapping tape to the surface of the steel pipe bundle, and a laser tracking sensor used for locking a welding position is arranged on the welding mechanism. The automatic welding equipment for the steel pipe wrapping tape, provided by the utility model, can automatically bundle steel pipes and automatically weld a plurality of wrapping tapes on the steel pipe bundle by the welding mechanism; degree of automation is high, has reduced the staff, has alleviated staff's working strength, has improved staff operational environment.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices are available for wrapping pipe bundles. However, the cited inventions lack the ability to precisely evaluate the required length of wrapping material based on bundle dimensions, leading to inefficiencies and material wastage. Additionally, these devices lack detecting the weight of the wrapped pipe, and preventing unintended unraveling during transportation which are essential for ensuring accuracy and reliability in the wrapping process.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that requires to be capable of accurately evaluating the required length of wrapping material based on bundle dimensions while ensuring uniform and secure coverage. In addition, the developed device also needs to be capable of detecting weight of wrapped pipe and preventing unintended unraveling during transportation in order to improve efficiency and reduce material wastage during the wrapping process.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of autonomously wrapping pipe bundles with a protective sheet of appropriate length as per the dimensions of the pipe bundle, thereby ensuring even and consistent wrapping without gaps or misalignments and eliminates manual handling.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of securing the wrapped sheet by applying adhesive patches over the entire length of the wrapped pipe bundle in an automated manner, thus preventing unintended unraveling during transportation and handling.

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting the weight of the wrapped pipe bundle for allowing the user to assess the total load of the pipe bundle for efficient logistics and resource planning.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle that is capable of wrapping a pipe bundle with a wrapping sheet in an automated manner without any gaps or misalignments. Further, the device is capable of reducing labor-intensive tasks by minimizing direct human involvement in the pipe bundle wrapping process.

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle comprises of a platform positioned on a fixed surface and configured with plurality of suction cups that get adhered with the surface, to secure the platform on the surface, a touch interactive display panel installed on the platform, that is accessed by a user to provide input command regarding wrapping of a bundle of pipes with protective sheet and to notify the user regarding weight of the bundle, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit having a processer, installed on the platform, to capture and process images of vicinity of the platform to detect placement of a bundle of the pipe, an inverted U-shaped frame installed on the platform and configured with a pair of robotic grippers to grip the bundle and engage with a pair of holding unit installed on the platform and to grip the sheet and secure an end of the sheet on an end of bundle for wrapping the sheet around the bundle for covering the bundle entirely, an ultrasonic sensor installed on the frame to detect dimension of the bundle and evaluates a length of the sheet required for wrapping the bundle of the pipes, a pair of motorized sliders arranged between the platform and frame to provide linear movement to the frame to travel along length of the bundle of pipes, facilitating process of wrapping, evenly over an entire length of the bundle.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of, plurality of load cells equipped in the holding unit, to detect weight of the bundle, for allowing the user to use appropriate resources for handling the bundle, a motorized roller wrapped with a sheet, installed on the platform to rotate in a pre-defined direction, to unwrap the sheet in accordance to evaluated length and a RPM (Revolutions per minute) sensor which is equipped with the roller, counts number of revolution made by the roller while unwrapping the sheet monitors length of the unwrapped sheet, a motorized cutter installed with the frame by means of a robotic link to cut the sheet via the cutter, a chamber arranged on the platform to store plurality of adhesive patches, that are accessed by the grippers, to grip and remove substrate of the patches and attach over end of the wrapped sheet in a successive manner, to secure the end of the sheet, to prevent unraveling of the sheet, during handling or transport and a battery is associated with the device for supplying power to electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle. 

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of, the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle that wrap the pipe bundle with a protective sheet evenly over an entire length of the bundle in a self-sufficient manner by automatically dispensing an appropriate length of the sheet suitable as per the dimensions of the bundle. Additionally, the proposed device is capable of securing the ends of the wrapped sheet by applying an adhesive patch over the wrapped sheet in order to prevent unraveling of the sheet.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an automated device for wrapping pipe bundle is illustrated, comprising a platform 101 configured with plurality of suction cups 102, a touch interactive display panel 103 installed on the platform 101, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101, an inverted U-shaped frame 105 installed on the platform 101 and configured with a pair of robotic grippers 106, a pair of motorized sliders 107 arranged between the platform 101 and frame 105, a pair of holding unit 108 installed on the platform 101, a motorized roller 109 installed on the platform 101, a motorized cutter 110 installed with the frame 105 by means of a robotic link 111, and a chamber 112 arranged on the platform 101.

[0023]	 The device disclosed herein comprises of a platform 101 incorporating various components associated with the device and developed to be positioned over a fixed surface. The platform 101 serves as the core structure and is made from strong and lightweight materials which includes but not limited to hardened steel, aluminum alloy, hard fiber, and composite materials. These materials offer strength and rigidity to the platform 101 making it resistant to mechanical stress and pressure. The surface of the platform 101 is coated with material like Teflon or other low-friction coatings to improve wear resistance and reduce friction.

[0024]	 The platform 101 is configured with multiple suction cups 102 (ranging from 4 to 6 in numbers) arranged underneath the platform 101 for affixing the platform 101 over the surface. The suction cups 102 are used to create a vacuum seal between the fixed surface and the platform 101. When the suction cups 102 are pressed against the fixed surface by a user, the initial contact creates a seal between the cup’s flexible rim and the surface. The suction cup 102 used herein are made up of silicone rubber that easily eliminates pressure inside the suction cup 102 for creating a vacuum between the cup and the fixed surface in order to affix the platform 101 firmly with the fixed surface to prevent undesired movement of the platform 101 on the surface.

[0025]	 The user is required to activate the device manually by pressing a button associated with the device and assembled with the platform 101. The button is a type of switch that is internally connected with the device via multiple circuits that upon pressing by the user, the circuits get closed and starts conduction of electricity that tends to activate the device and vice versa.

[0026]	 After activation of the device, the user is required to access a touch interactive display panel 103 installed on the platform 101 to provide input command regarding wrapping of a bundle of pipes with a protective sheet. The touch interactive display panel 103 used herein is a type of Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) that detect touch input from a user. It consists of both an input unit (preferably a capacitive touch panel) and an output unit (a visual display). The capacitive touch panel is layered on the top of the visual display. The touch panel consists of an insulator such as glass, coated with a transparent conductor, such as indium tin oxide (ITO).

[0027]	 When the user touches the surface of the display panel 103 for giving input commands, the electrostatic field of the screen gets distorted, that is measured as a change in capacitance. This change in capacitance is used to determine the location of the touch. The determined location of the touch is then sent in the form of electrical signals to an inbuilt microcontroller associated with the device and linked with the display panel 103.

[0028]	 The microcontroller processes the received signals in order to determine the user input and accordingly activates an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 integrated with a processor and installed on the platform 101, to capture and process multiple images of vicinity of the platform 101, respectively, to detect placement of a bundle of the pipe. The artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 comprises of a high-resolution camera lens, digital camera sensor and the processor, wherein the lens captures multiple images from different angles and perspectives in vicinity of the platform 101 with the help of digital camera sensor for providing comprehensive coverage of the platform 101.

[0029]	The captured images then go through pre-processing steps by the processor integrated with the imaging unit 104. The artificial intelligence protocols encrypted in the processor, including machine learning and computer vision protocols, optimize image processing by enhancing feature extraction and classification. The captured images undergo pre-processing steps such as adjusting brightness, contrast, and noise removal to enhance quality. These refined images are transmitted to the microcontroller linked with the processor, in the form of electrical signals.

[0030]	 The microcontroller processes the received signals from the imaging unit 104 in order to detect the placement of a bundle of the pipe over the platform 101. An inverted U-shaped frame 105 is installed on the platform 101 and configured with a pair of robotic grippers 106, wherein upon successful detection of the bundle, the microcontroller actuates the pair of robotic grippers 106 to grip the bundle and engage with a pair of holding units 108 installed on the platform 101. The robotic gripper mainly comprises of motor controllers, arm, end effector and sensors. The arm is the essential part of the robotic gripper and it comprises of three parts, the shoulder, elbow and wrist.

[0031]	 All these components are connected through joints, with the shoulder resting at the base of the arm, and connected to the microcontroller. The elbow is in the middle and allows the upper section of the gripper to move forward or backward independently of the lower section. Finally, the wrist is at the very end of the upper arm and attached to the end effector that is moved by the gripper to grip the bundle and engage with the pair of holding unit 108.

[0032]	 Upon engaging the bundle with the holding unit 108, the microcontroller by means of an ultrasonic sensor installed on the frame 105, detect dimension of the bundle. The ultrasonic sensor consists of an emitter that emits high-frequency ultrasonic sound waves towards the bundle. These sound waves strikes the bundle and gets reflected back and received by a receiver inside the sensor. The sensor measures the time it takes for the waves to bounce back after hitting the bundle. By calculating the round-trip time and applying the speed of sound, the sensor determines the dimensions of the bundle and sends acquired data to the microcontroller in the form of electrical signal.

[0033]	The microcontroller processes the received signals from the ultrasonic sensor in order to determine dimensions of the bundle. Based on the detected dimension, the microcontroller evaluates a length of the sheet required for wrapping the bundle of the pipes and accordingly actuates a motorized roller 109 installed on the platform 101 and wrapped with the sheet, to rotate in a pre-defined direction and unwrap the sheet in accordance to evaluated length. The motorized roller 109 used herein is a mechanical unit designed to rotate on its axis with the help of an integrated electric motor. The roller 109 consists of a cylindrical roller 109 tube that serves as a surface for accommodating the sheet.

[0034]	 The motorized roller 109 is equipped with an electric motor that provides the rotational power necessary to turn the roller 109. The motor is connected to the roller 109 tube through a drive mechanism, which involves gears, belts to transfer the motor’s rotational force to the roller 109, causing the roller 109 to spin and unwrap the sheet. Simultaneously, as the roller 109 starts to unwind the sheet, the microcontroller by means of a RPM (Revolutions per minute) sensor equipped with the roller 109, counts number of revolution made by the roller 109 while unwrapping the sheet.
 
[0035]	 The RPM sensor used herein is an optical RPM sensor that measures rotational speed using light and a rotating disc. The sensor consists of a light source (LED or laser) and a light detector (photodiode or phototransistor). The rotating disc, attached to the rotating component, has alternating opaque and transparent sections. As the disc spins, it periodically interrupts the light beam emitted by the light source. The detector converts these interruptions into electrical pulses. The frequency of these pulses correlates to the rotation speed, allowing the microcontroller to calculate RPM of the roller 109 while unwrapping the sheet in order to monitor the length of the unwrapped sheet.

[0036]	 Upon matching of the length of unwrapped sheet with the evaluated length, the microcontroller deactivate the roller 109 and subsequently actuates a robotic link 111 installed with the frame 105 to position a motorized cutter 110 configured with the link 111, over the sheet. The robotic link 111 used herein works in the same manner as described above for the robotic grippers 106 in order to position the cutter 110 over the sheet for cutting the sheet via the cutter 110. 

[0037]	Post positing of the cutter 110, the microcontroller actuates the cutter 110 in sync with the robotic link 111 to cut the sheet for separating the unwrapped sheet from the roller 109. The motorized cutter 110 used herein is coupled with a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller to rotate the cutter 110 with a specified speed and cut the sheet to separate the sheet from the roller 109.

[0038]	Upon cutting the sheet, the microcontroller reactivate the grippers 106 to grip the sheet and secure an end of the sheet on an end of the bundle and wrap the sheet around the bundle by coordinated movement of the grippers 106. Synchronously, the microcontroller actuates a pair of motorized sliders 107 arranged between the platform 101 and frame 105 to provide linear movement to the frame 105 for enabling the grippers 106 to travel along length of the bundle of pipes, for wrapping the sheet evenly over an entire length of the bundle.

[0039]	The slider used herein consists of a sliding-rail and multiple rolling members which are integrated with a step motor. On actuation, the step motor rotates the rolling members in order to provide rolling motion to the members which results in sliding of the frame 105 and provide translation to the frame 105 along the slider in order to allow the grippers 106 to wrap the sheet evenly over the entire length of the bundle.

[0040]	A chamber 112 is arranged on the platform 101 and stored with multiple adhesive patches, wherein upon completion of the wrapping of the sheet, the microcontroller directs the grippers 106 to grip the adhesive patches from the chamber 112 and remove substrate of the patches and attach over the end of the wrapped sheet in a successive manner to secure the end of the sheet in order to prevent unraveling of the sheet during handling or transportation.

[0041]	Further, the microcontroller by means of multiple load cells equipped in the holding unit 108, detect weight of the bundle. The load cells used herein contains a piezoelectric material, which generates a voltage in response to mechanical stress. When a pressure is applied by the bundle, it deforms the piezoelectric material, creating a strain. This strain results in the generation of an electric charge across the material, producing a voltage signal proportional to the applied pressure. The generated voltage is typically very small so the signal is amplified to make it suitable for further processing by the microcontroller.

[0042]	The microcontroller continuously processes the signals received from the load cells in order to detect the weight of the bundle. The detected weight is further sent to the display panel 103 by the microcontroller in the form of digital signal. The display panel 103 convert the received signals into visual output to notify the user regarding weight of the bundle, for allowing the user to use appropriate resources for handling the bundle as per the weight of the bundle.

[0043]	Lastly, a battery is installed within the device which is connected to the microcontroller that supplies current to all the electrically powered components that needs an amount of electric power to perform their functions and operation in an efficient manner. The battery utilized here, is generally a dry battery which is made up of Lithium-ion material that gives the device a long-lasting as well as an efficient DC (Direct Current) current which helps every component to function properly in an efficient manner. As the device is battery operated and do not need any electrical voltage for functioning. Hence the presence of battery leads to the portability of the device i.e. user is able to place as well as moves the device from one place to another as per the requirement.

[0044]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the platform 101 is positioned on the fixed surface via multiple suction cups 102. The user access the touch interactive display panel 103 to provide input command regarding wrapping of the bundle of pipes with protective sheet. Accordingly, the artificial intelligence based imaging unit 104 detect placement of the bundle of the pipe. Afterwards, the pair of robotic grippers 106 grip and engage the bundle with the pair of holding unit 108. Further, the ultrasonic sensor detects dimension of the bundle and accordingly the microcontroller evaluates the length of the sheet required for wrapping the bundle of the pipes. Based on which the motorized roller 109 rotates to unwrap the sheet in accordance to evaluated length and once the required length is unwrapped the motorized cutter 110 cut the sheet. The unwrapped sheet is further gripped by the grippes and wrapped around the bundle in synchronization with the movement of the pair of motorized sliders 107 to provide linear movement to the grippers 106 to travel along length of the bundle of pipes for evenly wrapping the sheet over entire length of the bundle. Afterwards, the grippers 106 grip and apply the adhesive patches over end of the wrapped sheet in successive manner to secure the end of the sheet to prevent unraveling of the sheet during handling or transportation.

title: AUTOMATED OPHTHALMIC EYELID STABILIZATION DEVICE
abstract: An automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device, comprising of a platform 101 positioned over a fixed surface, an inflatable member 102 linked with a motorized air compressor 103, to inflate the member for allowing the user to comfortably accommodate the head portion, an imaging unit 104 to determine positioning of the user’s eye, a sliding unit 105 installed on lateral ends of the platform 101 to translate a L-shape telescopic rod 106 mounted over each of the sliding units 105 in vicinity to the user’s eye portion, a C-shape link 107 to extend and position in proximity to the user’s eyelids, a curved silicone member 108 to detect upper and lower eyelid of the user, a pair of motorized hinges 109 integrated at mid-section of the C-shaped links, to adjust positioning of the links to gently secure and stabilize the eyelids in an open position.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to an automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device that is capable of automatically stabilizing the user’s eyelid by detecting the eyelid’s positioning for ensuring unobstructed access for ophthalmic procedures and monitoring the moisture level in the surrounding and taking the necessary steps for preventing eye dryness during the ophthalmic procedure.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Stabilizing a user’s eyelid while detecting its positioning for ensuring unobstructed access during ophthalmic procedures presents several challenges. Involuntary blinking and sudden eye movements interfere with accurate positioning, making it difficult to maintain a stable working area. Traditional manual methods, such as mechanical eyelid speculums, causes discomfort, irritation, or even minor injuries if excessive force is applied. Additionally, variations in eyelid size, muscle tension, and patient sensitivity require a highly adaptable stabilization approach to ensure comfort and efficiency. Another challenge is ensuring precise real-time detection of eyelid positioning, as minor misalignment obstructs the procedure and compromise accuracy. External factors such as ambient lighting, patient anxiety, and involuntary muscle reflexes further complicate stabilization. Ophthalmic procedures require precise stabilization of the eyelid to ensure unobstructed access to the eye while minimizing patient discomfort. Inadequate stabilization leads to involuntary blinking or movement, affecting the accuracy of procedures. Additionally, maintaining proper moisture levels is essential to prevent eye dryness, which causes irritation and complications during the process. Furthermore, excessive pressure on the eyelid results in discomfort, making it crucial to regulate the applied tension effectively.

[0003]	 Traditionally, ophthalmologists and medical practitioners use manual techniques or mechanical eyelid speculums to keep the eyelids open during procedures. These devices require careful placement and constant adjustments to ensure stability. In some cases, eye drops or lubricants are applied to prevent dryness, but they require frequent reapplication. Pressure control is generally managed manually, relying on the practitioner's expertise to avoid discomfort or excessive force. However, these methods are inconsistent and lead to patient discomfort, inefficiency, or procedural complications.

[0004]	US5433190A discloses an eyelid speculum device used to hold a person's eyelids open for ocular surgery, treatment, examination, or some other reason. The device has two elongated arms, each arm having one free end. The other ends of the arms are attached to a joining member. A person may grasp gripping portions at the free ends of the arms, and move the arms toward each other until the gripping portions contact one another. The device may then be inserted between the upper and lower eyelids of a person's eye. The elongated arms engage the eyelids after the gripping portions are released. A substantial length of each arm engages the eyelids, because the arms are contoured to generally conform to the curvature and/or length of the eyelids. As a result, reduced pressure is applied to the eyelids, which decreases the chances that post-operative ptosis or drooping of the eyelids will occur.

[0005]	US20150305732A1 discloses an eyelid speculum for retracting a pair of eyelids, comprises: a first arm having a first blade portion contoured to generally conform to an eyeball globe and one of the pair of eyelids; a second arm having a second blade portion contoured to generally conform to the eyeball globe an the other of the pair of eyelids; and a mechanism carrying the first arm and the second arm. The mechanism is operable to hold the first arm and the second arm parallel to and in proximity to each other so that the first blade portion and the second blade portion may be inserted between said eyelids to engage said eyelids. The mechanism is further operable to move the first arm and the second arm apart from each other while maintaining the first arm and the second arm in parallel such that the first blade portion and the second blade portion retract said pair of eyelids. The mechanism advantageously moves away from the surgical field of the eye when retracting the eyelids.

[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed to keep the eyelids open during procedures, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to constant adjustments to ensure stability and controlled tension, which leads to patient discomfort, inefficiency, or procedural complications.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of stabilizing the eyelid by detecting its position, ensuring uninterrupted access to the eye, and monitoring and maintaining optimal moisture levels to prevent dryness, thereby enhancing user’s comfort.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automatically stabilizing the user’s eyelid by detecting the eyelid’s positioning for ensuring unobstructed access for ophthalmic procedures.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of monitoring the moisture level in the surrounding and taking the necessary steps for preventing eye dryness during the ophthalmic procedure.

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of monitoring the pressure applied on the eyelids and accordingly maintaining the tension over the eyelids for preventing the user’s discomfort.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to an automated ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device that is capable of monitoring the pressure applied on the eyelids and accordingly maintaining the tension over the eyelids for preventing the user’s discomfort.

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device comprising of a platform positioned over a fixed surface, accessed by a user to rest the user’s head portion over the platform, wherein a touch sensor integrated on the platform is activated by an inbuilt microcontroller to detect accommodation of the user’s head portion over the platform, an inflatable member installed over the platform and linked with a motorized air compressor, wherein upon accommodation of the user’s head portion, the microcontroller actuates the air compressor to inflate the member for allowing the user to comfortably accommodate the head portion over the member, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the platform and integrated with a processor for capturing and processing images of the user’s eye to determine positioning of the user’s eye, based on which the microcontroller actuates a sliding unit installed on lateral ends of the platform to translate a L-shape telescopic rod mounted over each of the sliding units in vicinity to the user’s eye portion, a C-shape link is configured on free end of each of the rods, wherein upon positioning of the rods in vicinity to the user’s eye portion, the microcontroller actuates the rods to extend and position the links in proximity to the user’s eyelids, a curved silicone member attached with each end of the links, wherein an optical sensor integrated on the link is activated by the microcontroller to work in sync with the imaging unit to detect upper and lower eyelid of the user to allow the rods to precisely position the members over the upper and lower eyelids.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further includes a pair of motorized hinges integrated at mid-section of the C-shaped links, wherein upon detection of the user’s eyelids, the microcontroller actuates the hinges to adjust positioning of the links, enabling precise placement of the silicone members over the upper and lower eyelids to gently secure and stabilize the eyelids in an open position, ensuring unobstructed access to the user's eyes for ophthalmic procedures, such as laser treatments or eye surgeries as per requirements, a humidity sensor integrated within the platform to monitor moisture levels in air around the user’s eyes, and upon detecting a drop in humidity, the microcontroller actuates a humidification unit installed over the platform to release moisture, preventing eye dryness during the ophthalmic procedure, a pressure sensor integrated within the links to monitor force applied over the eyelids by the members, based on which the microcontroller regulates the hinges to ensure optimal tension maintained over the eyelids and to prevent user’s discomfort, and a battery unit is associated with the device for powering up electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of an automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of, the like.

[0021]	The present invention relates to an automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device that is capable of monitoring the moisture level in the surrounding and taking the necessary steps for preventing eye dryness during the ophthalmic procedure and monitoring the pressure applied on the eyelids and accordingly maintaining the tension over the eyelids for preventing the user’s discomfort.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an automated Ophthalmic eyelid stabilization device is illustrated, comprising a platform 101 positioned over a fixed surface, an inflatable member 102 installed over the platform 101 and linked with a motorized air compressor 103, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 installed on the platform 101, a sliding unit 105 installed on lateral ends of the platform 101 to translate a L-shape telescopic rod 106 mounted over each of the sliding units 105, a C-shape link 107 is configured on free end of each of the rods 106, a curved silicone member 108 attached with each end of the links 107, a pair of motorized hinges 109 integrated at mid-section of the C-shaped links 107, a humidification unit 110 installed over the platform 101.

[0023]	 The device disclosed herein employs a platform 101 that is positioned over a fixed surface. The platform 101 is accessed by a user to rest his head portion over the platform 101. The platform 101 is preferably made up of but not limited to stainless steel which provides stability and resistance to corrosion. 

[0024]	 For activating the device, the user need to press a push button which is arranged on the platform 101 which in turn activates all the related components for performing the desired task. After pressing the button, a closed electrical circuit is formed and current start to flow that powers an inbuilt microcontroller to allow all the linked components to perform their respective task upon actuation.

[0025]	 The microcontroller activates a touch sensor integrated on the platform 101 to detect the accommodation of the user’s head portion over the platform 101. The touch sensor detects the physical contact or pressure from the head portion of the user. It operates based on capacitive, resistive, or piezoelectric principles. The capacitive touch sensor work by detecting changes in an electrostatic field when the user’s head portion comes into the proximity. This change alters the capacitance at the touch point, which is then processed by the microcontroller to detect the accommodation of the user’s head portion over the platform 101.

[0026]	 Over the platform 101, an inflatable member 102 is arranged and linked with a motorized air compressor 103. Upon accommodation of the user’s head portion, the microcontroller actuates the air compressor 103 to inflate the member for allowing the user to comfortably accommodate the head portion over the member. The inflatable member 102 is a flexible structure that expands when filled with air allowing it to change shape and size as needed. It is typically made of elastic, durable materials like rubber, PVC, or fabric composites, which withstand internal pressure. The air compressor 103 is actuated to inflate the inflatable 102 member. The air compressor 103 inflates the member by converting power into pressurized air, which is then released in a controlled manner. It operates by drawing in ambient air and compressing it using a piston. The compressed air is stored in a tank and released through a hose when needed. The inflatable member 102 inflates for allowing the user to comfortably accommodate the head portion over the member.

[0027]	 For capturing and processing images of the user’s eye, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 is mounted on the platform 101 and integrated with a processor to determine the positioning of the user’s eye. The artificial intelligence (AI) based imaging unit 104 consists of a camera and a processor, where the camera comprises of a frame, electronic shutter, lens, lens aperture and image sensor, working in the sequential manner to capture the image of the user’s eye. The imaging unit 104 at the core comprises of deep learning architectures such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), trained on vast datasets to detect patterns and features of image. The data is processed using AI protocol to perform function of object detection, image enhancement, segmentation and classification to determine the positioning of the user’s eye.

[0028]	 Based on the positioning of the user’s eye, the microcontroller actuates a sliding unit 105 installed on lateral ends of the platform 101 to translate a L-shaped telescopic rod 106 mounted over each of the sliding units 105 in vicinity to the user’s eye portion. The sliding unit 105 for translation enables smooth and controlled linear movement along a fixed path. It consists of a guideway, a slider, and a drive mechanism such as a lead screw. The guideway ensures stability and precision, while the drive mechanism converts rotational motion into linear motion. Bearings or rollers within the unit minimize friction, allowing for efficient and accurate movement. The sliding unit 105 translates the telescopic rod. The telescopic rod 106 operates by extending and retracting in a controlled manner using a series of nested tubes that slide within one another. These tubes are designed with a precise fit to ensure smooth motion while maintaining structural stability. The extension and retraction is powered by pneumatic unit. The pneumatic unit for extension and retraction operates using compressed air to drive a piston inside a cylinder. When air is supplied to one side of the piston, it creates pressure that pushes the piston rod outward, causing extension. To retract, air is supplied to the opposite side while the initial chamber is vented, pulling the piston rod back. Hence, the telescopic rod 106 is placed in vicinity of the user’s eye portion.

[0029]	Within the platform 101, a humidity sensor is integrated to monitor the moisture levels in the air around the user’s eyes. The humidity sensor monitors the moisture levels by detecting changes in the surrounding air’s humidity and converting them into an electrical signal. It typically operates using capacitive, resistive, or thermal sensing principles. In capacitive humidity sensors, a hygroscopic material absorbs moisture, causing a change in capacitance that is measured and processed which is then converted into a readable output. The sensor’s data is processed by the microcontroller and displayed. So, the moisture level in the air around the user’s eye is monitored.

[0030]	Upon detecting a drop in humidity, the microcontroller actuates a humidification unit 110 installed over the platform 101 to release moisture for preventing eye dryness during the ophthalmic procedure. The humidification unit 110 increases air moisture levels by generating and dispersing water vapor into the surrounding environment. The humidification unit 110 operates by drawing in ambient air and passing it through an internal mechanism designed to generate and disperse water vapor. This process typically involves a water reservoir, a heating element and a fan. In steam-based humidification unit 110, the heating element heats the water, producing steam that is released into the air. The fan aids in distributing the generated moisture, ensuring even dispersion. As a result, the surrounding air's moisture levels increase, improving humidity and air quality.

[0031]	On the free end of the rods 106, a C-shape link 107 is attached. Upon positioning of the rods 106 in vicinity to the user’s eye portion, the microcontroller actuates the rods 106 to extend and position the links in proximity to the user’s eyelids. The C shape of the rod 106 enhances the stability.

[0032]	 A curved silicone member 108 is attached with each end of the link 107. The microcontroller activates an optical sensor that is integrated on the link 107 to work in sync with the imaging unit 104 to detect upper and lower eyelid of the user to allow the rods 106 to precisely position the members over the upper and lower eyelids. The optical sensor for detecting the upper and lower eyelids works by using infrared or visible light to track eye movements and blink patterns. The sensor consists of an infrared LED emitter and a photodetector that captures reflected light from the eye region. When the eyelids move, they partially or fully obstruct the reflection, causing changes in the received light intensity. The sensor processes these variations to determine the position of the upper and lower eyelids. 

[0033]	 At the mid-section of the C-shaped links, a pair of motorized hinges 109 integrated. Upon detection of the user’s eyelids, the microcontroller actuates the hinges 109 to adjust positioning of the links, thereby enabling precise placement of the silicone members 108 over the upper and lower eyelids to gently secure and stabilize the eyelids in an open position, ensuring unobstructed access to the user's eyes for ophthalmic procedures, such as laser treatments or eye surgeries as per requirements. The motorized hinge enables automated movement by integrating an electric motor with a hinge mechanism. It operates by converting electrical energy into mechanical motion, typically using a small motor connected to gears. When powered, the motor drives the hinge to rotate, allowing controlled opening and closing. The hinge adjusts the positioning of the links for precise placement of the member over the upper and lower eyelid.

[0034]	 Within the links, a pressure sensor is integrated to monitor force applied over the eyelids by the members. The pressure sensor measures pressure by converting applied force over the eyelids by the member into an electrical signal using a sensing element such as a strain gauge, piezoelectric crystal, or capacitive diaphragm. When pressure is applied, it causes deformation in the sensing element, altering its electrical properties like resistance. This change is then processed by an electronic circuit to produce a corresponding output, which is displayed or transmitted to monitor the force applied over the eyelids by the members. Based on the monitored force, the microcontroller regulates the hinges 109 to ensure optimal tension maintained over the eyelids and to prevent user’s discomfort.

[0035]	 For supplying power to electrical and electronically operated components, a battery is associated with the device. The battery powers electrical and electronic components by converting stored chemical energy into electrical energy. The battery’s terminals provide a voltage difference, allowing current to flow through circuits that supplies consistent energy to actuate and operate components like motors, sensors and microcontrollers, ensuring seamless functionality.
