title: FARM PRODUCES MANAGEMENT DEVICE
abstract: A farm produces management device, comprising of a cuboidal body 101 partitioned in plurality of compartments each designated for storing farm produce, positioned on a fixed surface, a display panel 102 to provide input command for sorting and storing farm produce, a speaker 103 to notify user to position farm produces on a tray 104 installed by means of a linkage 105, multiple load cells to detect accommodation of farm produces, an imaging unit 106 for detecting types of farm produce, a slider 107 to move tray 104, a gripper 108 to acquire a firm grip on farm produce, a chamber 109 to grip a covering sheet, multiple vibrating unit 110 for detaching dust particles, multiple iris lids 111 to allow detached dust particles to fall into a storage container 112, a receptacle 113 to store green and leafy farm produce, a sprayer 114 to preserve freshness of farm produce.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a farm produces management device that is capable in offering effective means for managing the farm produce by storing of different types of farm produce based on their characteristics, thereby ensuring that each type is placed in organized management and easy retrieval, thereby helps maintaining hygiene and extends the shelf life of the produce. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Farm produce management faces several challenges, including contamination, spoilage, inefficient handling, and storage limitations. Dust, dirt, and pathogens often accumulate on harvested produce, leading to hygiene concerns and increased risk of disease. Traditional cleaning methods are labor-intensive and ineffective in completely removing contaminants. Spoilage is another major issue, as improper storage conditions, temperature fluctuations, and humidity accelerate decay, resulting in significant post-harvest losses. Farmers and storage facilities often rely on manual inspection, which is prone to human error and delays in detecting spoilage. Additionally, unorganized storage systems lead to inefficient retrieval, causing damage to delicate produce and increasing waste. The lack of real-time monitoring and automated handling solutions further complicates management, making it difficult to maintain quality and extend shelf life. Without a solution to address these challenges, farm produce management remains inefficient, leading to economic losses and food security concerns.

[0003]	 Traditional farm produce management relied on manual labor and simple tools to ensure cleanliness, freshness, and proper storage. Cleaning methods included handwashing, winnowing, and sieving to remove dirt, dust, and impurities. Freshness monitoring was done through visual inspection, smell, and texture analysis, which were highly subjective and prone to errors. Farmers used natural preservatives such as ash, salt, and neem leaves to delay spoilage. Storage methods involved earthen pots, underground pits, granaries, and wooden or bamboo containers to protect produce from pests and environmental factors. Sun drying and smoking were common techniques to reduce moisture and extend shelf life. Retrieval of stored produce was manual, often leading to physical damage and inefficiencies. Over time, traditional knowledge and community practices played a crucial role in maintaining produce quality, but these methods lacked automation, consistency, and precision, leading to increased post-harvest losses and inefficiencies in large-scale farm management.

[0004]	EP2389060A2 discloses a storage device for agricultural products in particular vegetables of the long and flexible type such as leeks, for installation on a tractor, to fill said device and to cooperate with a picking device, characterised in comprising a storage strip and a first support comprising a hub, which can move in rotation about an axis, designed for rolling said storage strip and for the storage of said agricultural products between two layers of said strip. The invention further relates to a corresponding method.

[0005]	WO2012173314A1 The present invention relates to a container for storing agricultural products, wherein harvested agricultural products can be stored in a warehouse for a long time and the agricultural products can be easily transported and managed. According to the present invention, a container for storing agricultural products comprises: a body which has a storage space capable of storing agricultural products, and has one side on which an opening and closing door is formed; a ventilation unit which includes a ventilator installed in said body in order to allow the outside air to flow into the inside of said body; and first and second connection units, which are coupled with each other, are respectively formed on the upper part and the lower part of said body so as to vertically stack said body thereon. It is desirable that said ventilation unit comprises: a plurality of induction pipes which have air outlets such that said ventilator can send air along the bottom surface of an inner side of said body, and are installed on the bottom surface of said body so as to induce air discharged through said blast ports to a side portion of said body; a support plate, which is provided on the upper side of said induction pipes, forms a supporting surface to load the agricultural products thereon, and has a plurality of ventilation holes that penetrate upper and lower surfaces such that the air discharged from said ventilator is capable of moving to the upper side; and a sidewall guide pipe which is vertically extended along the side of said body, has an internal flow channel through which the air can move, and has a plurality of through holes that are communicated with said internal flow channel and are communicated toward the inside of said body so that the air, which is induced to the side portion of the body through said induction pipes, can move in an upper direction along said internal flow channel and be discharged to the inside of said body.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have been developed to address specific aspects of farm produce management, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to detecting and removing dust from farm produce before storage, careful handling to prevent damage, and detecting spoilage or changes in condition by providing real-time alerts.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that offers a solution for farm produce management which enhance storage operations, extend the usability of farm produce, and minimize losses due to contamination and spoilage.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	 The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]	 An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of offering effective means for managing the farm produce by detecting and removing dust from farm produce before storage, thereby ensuring cleanliness and preventing contamination, which helps maintain hygiene and extends the shelf life of the produce. 

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of offering effective means for managing the farm produce by monitoring the freshness of farm produce, thereby allowing the user to take necessary actions to prevent waste and ensure quality.

[0011]	 Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of offering effective means for managing the farm produce by facilitating controlled retrieval of stored farm produce upon user request, thereby ensuring careful handling to prevent damage and making the storage more efficient and user-friendly.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to a farm produces management device that is capable in offering an effective means for managing farm produce by detecting and removing dust from farm produce before storage, thereby ensuring cleanliness and preventing contamination, which helps maintain hygiene and extends the shelf life of the produce.

[0014]	 According to an embodiment of the present invention, a farm produces management device comprising of a cuboidal body partitioned in plurality of compartments each designated for storing a particular type of farm produce, positioned on a fixed surface, a touch interactive display panel installed on the body that is accessed by a user to provide input command for sorting and storing farm produce in designated compartments, a speaker installed on the body to generate audible instructions to notify the user to position the farm produces on a tray installed with the body by means of a linkage, plurality of load cells integrated in the tray to detect accommodation of farm produces on the tray, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit ]installed on the tray, to capture and process images of vicinity of the tray, in order to detect types of the farm produce placed on the tray, a motorized slider installed between the body and linkage, to move the tray towards the designated compartment, in order to align the tray with a compartment designated towards storage of the detected type of farm produce, a robotic gripper installed on the tray, to acquire a firm grip on the farm produce and store in the designated compartment, a chamber installed on the body to grip a covering sheet, and position over the cut farm produce, to preserve freshness and prevent spoilage of the farm produce.

[0015]	According to another embodiment of the present invention, the invention further includes a dust sensor installed on the tray and synced with the imaging unit, to detect presence of dust on the farm produce, plurality of vibrating unit installed in the tray, to generate vibration for detaching the dust particles from the farm produce, plurality of motorized iris lids installed in the tray to open and allow the detached dust particles to fall into a storage container installed underneath the tray, a receptacle installed on one of the compartment designated to store green and leafy farm produce, a timer module to keep track of time on storage of the leafy farm produce, an electronically controlled sprayer configured with the nozzle, to spray water on the farm produce to preserve freshness of the farm produce, a color sensor is installed on the tray to detect the farm produces to be rotten, a tactile sensor is integrated in the gripper to detect hardness of the farm produce, a compartment stored with the specified farm produce, to retrieve the farm produce from the compartment and place on the tray for user’s access, and a battery is associated with the device for supplying power to electrical and electronically operated components associated with the device.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a farm produces management device

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. [0021]	The present invention relates to a farm produces management device that is capable in offering an effective means for managing farm produce by monitoring the freshness of farm produce by detecting spoilage or changes in condition and providing timely alerts, thereby allowing the user to take necessary actions to prevent waste and ensure quality.

[0022]	Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a farm produces management device illustrated comprises of a cuboidal body 101, plurality of compartments partitioned on the body 101, a touch interactive display panel 102 installed on the  body 101, a speaker 103 installed on the  body 101, a tray 104 installed with the  body 101 by means of a linkage 105, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit 106, installed on the  tray, a motorized slider 107 installed between the  body 101 and linkage 105, a robotic gripper 108 installed on the  tray, a chamber 109 installed on the  body 101, plurality of vibrating unit 110 installed in the  tray plurality of motorized iris lids 111 installed in the  tray, a storage container 112 installed underneath the  tray, a receptacle 113 installed on one of the  compartment, an electronically controlled  sprayer 114 configured with the receptacle 113. 

[0001]	 The device disclosed herein comprises of a cuboidal body 101 partitioned in plurality of compartments each designated for storing a particular type of farm produce, positioned on a fixed surface. The user activates the device through a push button associated with the device. The push button has an outer casing and an inner mechanism, including a spring and metal contacts. When the button is pressed, it pushes down on the spring-loaded mechanism inside. In the default state, the internal contacts are apart, so the circuit is open and no electricity flows.

[0002]	 Pressing the button makes the contacts touch each other, closing the circuit and allowing electricity to flow and activate the device. The device in turn activates an inbuilt microcontroller that is pre-fed with a defined set of instructions to perform various functions. When the button is released, the spring pushes it back to its original position

[0003]	 Upon activation of the device the microcontroller activates a touch interactive display panel 102 installed on the body 101 that is accessed by a user to provide input command for sorting and storing farm produce in designated compartments. The touch interactive display panel 102 as mentioned herein is typically an LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) screen that presents output in a visible form. The screen is equipped with touch-sensitive technology, allowing the user to interact directly with the display using their fingers. 

[0004]	A touch controller IC (Integrated Circuit) is responsible for processing the analog signals generated when the user inputs details regarding sorting and storing farm produce in designated compartments. The touch controller is typically connected to the microcontroller through various interfaces which may include but are not limited to SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) or I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit).

[0005]	 After processing the input commands, the microcontroller and actuates a speaker 103 installed on the body 101 to generate audible instructions to notify the user to position the farm produces on a tray installed with the body 101 by means of a linkage 105. The speaker 103 used herein   works by converting the electrical signal into the audio signal, that consists of a cone known as a diaphragm attached to a coil-shaped wire placed between two magnets. 

[0006]	When the electric signal is passed through the voice coil, it generates a varying magnetic field that interacts with the magnet causing the diaphragm to move back and forth. This movement pushes and pulls air creating sound waves just like the electrical signal received and used to notify the user to position the farm produces on the tray 104.

[0007]	 Upon notifying the user regarding to position the farm produces on the tray 104 the microcontroller activates   plurality of load cells integrated in the tray 104 to detect accommodation of farm produces on the tray 104. The plurality of load cells used herein works by measuring the applied weight at multiple points. Each load cell consists of a strain gauge that deforms under load, altering its electrical resistance. The resistance change is converted into a voltage signal using a Wheatstone bridge circuit. These signals from multiple load cells are processed by an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and sent to the microcontroller. The microcontroller aggregates the data to determine the total weight and distribution of the produce.

[0008]	Post determining the total weight and distribution of the produce microcontroller activates the farm produces on the tray 104, the microcontroller activates an artificial intelligence based imaging unit 106 integrated with a processer, installed on the tray 104, to capture and process images of vicinity of the tray 104, in order to detect types of the farm produce placed on the tray 104. The imaging unit 106 used herein comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images of the vicinity of the tray 104 and the captured images are stored within a memory of the imaging unit 106 in form of an optical data. 

[0009]	The imaging unit 106 also comprises of a processor that is integrated with artificial intelligence protocols, such that the processor processes the optical data and extracts the required data from the captured images. The extracted data is further converted into digital pulses and bits and are further transmitted to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received data and to detects the types of the farm produce placed on the tray 104.

[0010]	Post detecting the types of the farm produce placed on the tray 104, the microcontroller actuates a motorized slider 107 installed between body 101 and linkage 105, to move the tray 104 towards the designated compartment, in order to align the tray 104 with a compartment designated towards storage of the detected type of farm produce. The motorized slider 107 used herein consist of a sliding rail and a motorized slid able member connected to the sliding rail. 

[0011]	The motorized slid able member is attached to the tray 104 and sliding rail on both sides to make the tray 104 slide.  The slid able member is attached to a motor which provides movement to the member in a bi-directional manner in order to align the tray 104 with the compartment designated towards storage of the detected type of farm produce.

[0012]	Upon aligning the tray 104 towards the designated storage, the microcontroller activates a robotic gripper 108 installed on the tray 104, that is actuated by to acquire a firm grip on the farm produce and store in the designated compartment. The robotic gripper 108 used herein includes a link connected with multiple motorized ball and socket joints and an end effector for smooth and precise gripping on the farm produce. 

[0013]	The motorized ball and socket joint includes a motor powered by the microcontroller generating electrical current, a ball shaped element and a socket. The ball moves freely within the socket. The motor rotates the ball in various directions that is controlled by the microcontroller that further commands the motor to position the ball precisely. The microcontroller further actuates the motor to generate electrical current to rotate in the joint for providing movement to the gripper 108 for gripping the farm produce and store in the designated compartment.

[0014]	Post gripping the farm produce, in case the imaging unit 106 detects placement of any partially cut farm produce, the microcontroller reactivates the gripper 108 to access a chamber 109 installed on the body 101 to grip a covering sheet, and position over the cut farm produce, to preserve freshness and prevent spoilage of the farm produce. The imaging unit 106 mention herein works same mentioned above and the gripper 108 mentioned herein works as mentioned above. 

[0015]	Subsequently the includes a tactile sensor is integrated in the gripper 108 to detect hardness of farm produce that is activated by the microcontroller to regulates functionality of the gripper 108 to grip the farm produce with an optimum pressure for preventing damage to the farm produce. The tactile sensor used herein is a piezo resistive tactile sensor detects the hardness of farm produce by measuring changes in electrical resistance due to applied force. The sensor consists of a flexible membrane with an embedded strain gauge that deforms when pressure is applied. 

[0016]	As the produce presses against the sensor, the strain gauge experiences mechanical deformation, altering its resistance. This change is converted into an electrical signal and processed by the microcontroller. The microcontroller compares the resistance values against predefined thresholds to determine the hardness level to regulates functionality of the gripper 108 to grip the farm produce with an optimum pressure for preventing damage to the farm produce

[0017]	The device includes a dust sensor installed on the tray 104 and synced with the imaging unit 106, to detect presence of dust on the farm produce. The dust sensor used herein is a laser-based dust sensor synced with the imaging unit 106 detects dust on farm produce using light scattering method. The sensor emits a focused laser beam, which interacts with dust particles on the produce. 

[0018]	When dust is present, it scatters the laser light, and a photodetector captures the scattered light intensity. The sensor converts this data into an electrical signal, which is processed by the microcontroller. Simultaneously, the imaging unit 106 captures images of the produce, and the processor analyzes variations in texture and color. The microcontroller cross-verifies the dust sensor readings with image data to confirm dust presence.

[0019]	On detection, the microcontroller actuates plurality of vibrating unit 110 installed in the tray 104, to generate vibration for detaching the dust particles from the farm produce. The vibrating unit 110 used herein produces an oscillating force across a single axis. The vibration unit relies on an AC voltage to drive a voice coil pressed against a moving mass connected to a spring. When the voice coil is driven at the resonant frequency of the spring, the entire actuator vibrates with a perceptible force. By driving the magnetic mass up and down against the spring, the LRA as a whole will be displaced and produce a vibration for detaching the dust particles from the farm produce.

[0020]	 Upon detaching dust particles   the microcontroller activates plurality of motorized iris lids 111 installed in the tray 104 that are actuated by the microcontroller to open and allow the detached dust particles to fall into a storage container 112 installed underneath the tray 104. The motorized iris lids 111 used herein functions as a controllable aperture for regulating removing dust particles, that comprises a series of overlapping blades that open or close around a central axis, adjusting the diameter of the aperture. 

[0021]	The unit is typically driven by a small electric motor, allowing for precise control via microcontroller. When the motor rotates, it adjusts the blades' position to open and allow the detached dust particles to fall into the storage container 112. Further the device includes a receptacle 113 installed on one of the compartment designated to store green and leafy farm produce. Herein the device includes a timer module integrated with the microcontroller to keep track of time on storage of the leafy farm produce and on completion of a pre-set duration. 

[0022]	The timer module works by using an internal clock and counting mechanism, that consists of a quartz crystal oscillator that generates stable clock pulses. These pulses are counted by an internal counter circuit, which increments time in predefined intervals (seconds, minutes, hours). The microcontroller reads the timer values and stores timestamps when the produce is placed in storage. It continuously updates the elapsed time by comparing the current time with the stored timestamp. 

[0023]	If the storage exceeds a preset duration actuates an electronically controlled sprayer 114 configured with the receptacle 113, to spray water on the farm produce to preserve freshness of the farm produce. The electrically controlled nozzle mentioned herein operates using a solenoid valve to regulate water flow. When an electric current is applied, the solenoid coil generates a magnetic field, pulling the valve open to allow water passage. The nozzle design controls flow rate and spray pattern based on applied voltage to dispense the appropriate amount of water on the farm produce to preserve freshness of the farm produce.

[0024]	 Additionally, the device includes a color sensor is installed on the tray 104 and synced with the imaging unit 106 to detect the farm produces to be rotten. in case of detection of rotten farm produce.  The color sensor synced with the imaging unit 106 detects rotten farm produce by analyzing color changes. The color sensor uses an RGB photodetector to measure the reflectance of red, green, and blue light from the produce, that converts detected color intensities into electrical signals, which are processed by the microcontroller. 

[0025]	Simultaneously, the imaging unit 106 captures high-resolution images, to analyze color variations, identifying discoloration patterns associated with rot. The microcontroller cross-verifies the sensor data with image analysis to confirm spoilage. In case of detection of rotten farm produce, the microcontroller directs speaker 103 to generate audible alert in order to notify the user to discard the rotten farm produce from the tray 104. The speaker 103 used herein works same mentioned above.

[0026]	 In case the user through the panel 102 provide command for retrieval of any of the farm produce, the microcontroller directs the slider 107 to align the tray 104 to align with the compartment stored with the specified farm produce. Upon aligning tray 104 the microcontroller reactivates the gripper 108 to retrieve the farm produce from the compartment and place on the tray 104 for user’s access.

[0027]	Lastly, a battery is installed within the device which is connected to the microcontroller that supplies current to all the electrically powered components that needs an amount of electric power to perform their functions and operation in an efficient manner. The battery utilized here, is generally a dry battery which is made up of Lithium-ion material that gives the device a long-lasting as well as an efficient DC (Direct Current) current which helps every component to function properly in an efficient manner. As the device is battery operated and do not need any electrical voltage for functioning. Hence the presence of battery leads to the portability of the device i.e., user is able to place as well as moves the device from one place to another as per the requirements.

[0028]	The proposed device works best in the following manner, the device disclosed herein comprises of the cuboidal body 101 partitioned into multiple compartments for storing different farm produce and is positioned on the fixed surface. The user activates the device through the push button, which completes an electrical circuit to power the microcontroller. The microcontroller activates the touch interactive display panel 102, allowing the user to input commands for sorting and storing farm produce. The touch controller processes input signals and sends them to the microcontroller, which then activates the speaker 103 to provide audible instructions for positioning farm produce on the tray 104. The plurality of load cells integrated into the tray 104 detects the weight and distribution of farm produce by measuring resistance changes using the Wheatstone bridge circuit. The artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 106, equipped with lenses and  processor, captures images of farm produce and processes them. The microcontroller, based on detected produce type, actuates the motorized slider 107 to align the tray 104 with the designated compartment. The robotic gripper 108, equipped with multiple motorized ball and socket joints, grips and stores farm produce. The tactile sensor in the gripper 108 regulates gripping pressure to prevent damage. The laser-based dust sensor, synced with the imaging unit 106, detects dust using a light scattering method, and upon detection, the vibrating unit 110 detaches dust particles. The motorized iris lids 111 then open to remove dust. The timer module tracks storage time using a quartz crystal oscillator, and upon exceeding preset time, the electrically controlled sprayer 114 sprays water. The color sensor, synced with the imaging unit 106, detects rotten produce, prompting the speaker 103 to generate an alert for the user to discard it.

The system comprises a control unit communicatively coupled to one or more sensors (21, 22, 31, 41), a spool unit (40), and an emergency control mechanism (70) associated with the crane (210). The control unit is configured to compute rate of spooling of the payload (50) during transport of the payload between a receiving station and a destination position. Further, the control unit being configured to compare the rate of spooling of the payload with at least one of an input value or a predefined threshold value to deduce an uncontrolled lowering condition of the payload by the crane. Following which, the system being configured to actuate the emergency control mechanism of the crane, to regulate at least one of the rate of spooling or movement of the payload towards the destination position

title: A SCOTT-CONNECTED TRANSFORMER SYSTEM FOR POWER CONVERSION FOR RAILWAY ELECTRIFICATION
abstract:
The present invention relates to a scott-connected transformer system (102) for efficiently converting three-phase power to two-phase power, particularly for railway electrification and industrial applications. The Scott-connected transformer system (102) includes a main transformer (104a) including a main primary winding (114a, 114b) having a first end connected to a three-phase power system and a second end in a series connection, and a main secondary winding (116a, 116b) configured to generate a first phase (O1) of a two-phase system. The Scott-connected transformer system (102) further includes a teaser transformer (104b) connected between the three-phase system and a center tap (M) of the main primary winding (114a, 114b) having a teaser primary winding (120a, 120b) having a first end and a second end, and a teaser secondary winding (122a, 122b), configured to generate a second phase (O2) of the two-phase system.
REF. TO FIGURE 1
specification:
“A SCOTT-CONNECTED TRANSFORMER SYSTEM FOR POWER CONVERSION FOR RAILWAY ELECTRIFICATION”
FIELD OF THE INVENTION    
[0001]	The present subject matter described herein relates to a Scott-connected transformer system. More specifically, the present invention relates to a Scott-connected transformer system to facilitate efficient conversion between three-phase and two-phase power systems, particularly for railway electrification.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[0002]	Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art.
[0003]	Scott-connected transformers are widely used for converting three-phase electrical power into two-phase power, A conventional Scott connection consists of a main transformer and a teaser transformer, where the main transformer is connected across two phases of a three-phase input, and the teaser transformer is connected between the center tap of the main transformer and the third phase. This arrangement facilitates balanced phase conversion, making it suitable for railway applications that require two-phase power distribution. 
[0004]	Over the years, several inventions have evolved in transformer technology to enhance efficiency, reduce losses, and improve load balancing. Existing art introduced the fundamental concept of scott-connected transformers, establishing their role in phase conversion. It describes the scott-connected transformer, which is used for converting three-phase electrical power to two-phase power and vice versa. This invention played a crucial role in the development of power distribution systems, especially in situations where both two-phase and three-phase systems were in use. The scott-connection uses two transformers: a "main" transformer and a "teaser" transformer. These transformers are interconnected in a specific way to achieve the phase conversion. The primary windings of the transformers are connected in such a manner that they receive power from a three-phase system, and the secondary windings output two-phase power. Despite its innovative approach, the original Scott-connected transformer was primarily designed for early power distribution needs and did not account for modern high-frequency applications, increased efficiency demands, or railway electrification challenges.
[0005]	A conventional solution discloses a design and application of transformers used for phase conversion and balancing in electrical power distribution networks. While not directly tied to the original Scott-connected transformer, it deals with similar objectives of optimizing power phase conversion and distribution. The conventional solution addresses methods and configurations for converting between different phase systems, specifically between two-phase, three-phase, or other polyphase systems. The transformer in the conventional solution is intended to provide balanced and efficient phase conversion, ensuring that power distribution remains stable and without significant losses or imbalances. The conventional solution introduces improvements in the winding and connection schemes of transformers used for phase conversion. However, the conventional solution focuses on load balancing and efficiency, it does not fully address issues related to compact design, reduced energy losses, and optimized performance for railway electrification, where power stability is crucial.
[0006]	Another conventional solution, describes transformer design, particularly aimed at improving efficiency and performance. This conventional solution likely discusses methods and configurations for reducing energy losses and enhancing the operational reliability of transformers in electrical power systems. One of the main focuses of conventional solution is on improving the design of the transformer core. Core design is critical in reducing losses (such as core losses due to hysteresis and eddy currents) and improving the overall efficiency of transformers. The conventional solution introduces changes to the material or geometry of the transformer core, which helps to minimize these losses and allow the transformer to operate more efficiently, especially under varying load conditions. Although improvements in core design and winding configurations were introduced, the transformer designs did not adequately cater to railway applications, where fluctuating loads and high voltage-to-low voltage conversion require specialized solutions.
[0007]	Another conventional solution addresses the need for reliable and efficient transformers in railway electrification systems. Railways, especially those using AC electric power, require transformers that can step down high-voltage electricity transmitted from power plants to a lower voltage suitable for use by electric trains. The transformer described in present conventional solution is designed to handle high-voltage input from power distribution networks and step it down to a voltage level that can be safely and efficiently used by railway systems. The system includes provisions for managing fluctuating loads, which is common in railway operations due to the varying power demands of trains at different points along the track. The transformers are designed to be installed along railway lines, ensuring efficient power delivery to locomotives and other railway equipment. While present conventional solution tackled some railway-specific power challenges, it lacked adaptability for modern, high-efficiency railway electrification schemes, especially with the shift toward more compact and energy-efficient designs.
[0008]	Another conventional solution discloses design of railway transformers for better integration with modern electric rail systems, with emphasis on cost efficiency and reliability. This conventional solution discusses a power converter utilizing a Scott-T transformer. The transformer is designed to operate in medium frequencies (hundreds of Hz to tens of kHz) rather than traditional low-frequency ranges, which reduces the transformer's size and weight. The conventional solution specifically mentions its use in European railway systems, where frequency requirements differ, such as 16⅔ Hz, 50 Hz, or 60 Hz.
[0009]	Despite these developments, conventional Scott-connected transformers still exhibit several limitations when deployed in railway electrification systems. One of the primary challenges is load imbalance, which arises due to variations in the electrical demand of railway networks. The uneven current distribution between the main and teaser transformers can lead to power inefficiencies and increased energy losses. Another challenge is impedance mismatch, which affects the stability and performance of the transformer, particularly under fluctuating load conditions. Existing Scott-connected transformers also suffer from high core and copper losses, reducing overall efficiency. The core design and winding configurations in prior art transformers often result in excessive heat generation, further impacting reliability and operational performance. Therefore, there is a need for high-efficiency railway electrification systems necessitating a transformer design that can effectively address the shortcomings of existing arts.
[0010]	Therefore, the said technical problem has also been well considered while developing the present Scott-connected transformer system that overcomes the limitations of prior art by offering enhanced impedance matching, better load balancing, and reduced energy losses. 
OBJECTS OF THE DISCLOSURE
[0011]	It is therefore the object of the present disclosure to overcome the aforementioned and other drawbacks in prior arts.
[0012]	It is a primary object of the present disclosure to provide a system for converting three-phase electrical power into two-phase power or vice versa, with enhanced efficiency, reduced energy loss, minimized harmonics, and optimized winding pair impedances.
[0013]	It is another object of the present invention to provide system for balancing power across the windings, improving voltage regulation, and ensuring optimal impedances between winding pairs for railway needs. 
[0014]	These and other objects and advantages of the present subject matter will be apparent to a person skilled in the art after consideration of the following detailed description taken into consideration with accompanying drawings in which preferred embodiments of the present subject matter are illustrated.

Additional features and advantages are realized through the technicalities of the present disclosure. The system includes a main transformer comprising a main primary winding distributed equally on a plurality of limbs of a main core, having a first end connected to a three-phase power system and a second end in a series connection. A main secondary winding distributed equally on the plurality of limbs of a main core, configured to generate a first phase of a two phase system. The main secondary winding is wound around a plurality of main core limbs of the main transformer. The present invention further includes a teaser transformer connected between the three phase system and a center tap of the main primary winding including a teaser primary winding distributed equally on the plurality of limbs having a first end and a second end. The first end is connected in a parallel connection to the three-phase power system and the second end is connected to a middle point of the main primary winding of and a teaser secondary winding distributed equally on the plurality of limbs, configured to generate a second phase of the two phase system. The first phase and the second phase is the two phase power converted from the three phase power of the three phase power system.

[0030]	While the embodiments of the disclosure are subject to various modifications and alternative forms, a specific embodiment thereof has been shown by way of example in the figures and will be described below. It should be understood, however, that it is not intended to limit the disclosure to the particular forms disclosed, but on the contrary, the disclosure is to cover all modifications, equivalents, and alternatives falling within the scope of the disclosure.

[0032]	The general existing transformer is a device used in the power transmission of electric energy. It is commonly used to increase or decrease the supply voltage without a change in the frequency of alternating current (AC) between circuits. A Scott-transformer (or Scott connection) is a specific type of transformer plays a crucial role in railway electrification, where it is used to convert three-phase power to two-phase power, or vice versa, by connecting two single-phase transformers in a specific configuration. The present invention optimizes the traditional scott connection by enhancing the winding arrangement, improving impedance characteristics, and ensuring stable operation for applications such as railway electrification. 
[0033]	Fig. 1 illustrates a diagram 100 depicting a core coil arrangement of a scott connection transformer system 102 in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention. The scott connection transformer system 102 may be configured to convert a three-phase power to a two-phase power, particularly in railway electrification. The three-phase power may be received from a three-phase power system. The three-phase power system (not shown in the figure) may include a number of phases connected to the scott connection transformer system 102. The number of phases may include a first phase U, a second phase V, and a third phase W.  The scott-connected transformer system 102 may include a number of transformers 104a, 104b, and a tap winding 110, a tap winding 124. The number of transformers 104a, 104b may be in connection with the number of phases of the three-phase power system and may further generate the two-phase power from the three-phase power of the three-phase power system. The number of transformers 104a, 104b may include a main transformer 104a and a teaser transformer 104b.  The main transformer 104a may include a number of main core limbs 112a, 112b, a main primary winding 114 (114a, 114b), and a main secondary winding 116 (116a, 116b).  The teaser transformer 104b may include a number of teaser core limbs 118a 118b, a teaser primary winding 120 (120a, 120b), and a teaser secondary winding 122 (122a, 122b). The tap winding 110 may correspond with the main transformer 104a and the tap winding 124 may correspond with the teaser transformer 104b. The main primary winding 114 and the teaser primary winding 120 may be three phase side windings and the main secondary winding 116 and the teaser secondary windings 122 may be two phase side winding. The main transformer 104a and the teaser transformer 104b may be wound with the two-phase side winding and the three-phase side winding.
[0034]	To that understanding, the main primary winding 114 may be formed from the windings 114a, 114b along the tap windings 110a, 110b from the tap winding 110. The main secondary winding 116 may be formed from the windings 116a, 116b. Further, the teaser primary winding 120 may be formed from windings 122a, 122b along with number of tap windings 124a, 124b from the tap winding 124. The teaser secondary winding 122 may be formed windings 122a, 122b as referred in figure 1.
[0035]	Continuing with the above embodiment, the main secondary winding 116 may be wound around the number of main core limbs 112a,112b, the main primary winding 114a, 114b with the tap windings 110a, 110b may be wound around the number of main core limbs 112. 
[0036]	The main primary winding 114 may be wound around equally on the main core limbs 112a, 112b.  The main primary winding 114 may include a number of ends. The number of ends may include a first end, and a second end. The first end of the main primary winding 114 may be connected to the three-phase power system and the second end may be in a series connection. title: WEATHER-TRIGGERED SMART CURTAINS
abstract: The present invention relates to a weather triggered smart curtain system designed to provide autonomous adjustment of curtains in response to real-time environmental conditions. The system comprises a microcontroller, a temperature sensor, a light dependent resistor (LDR) sensor, infrared (IR) sensors, a motor, and a motor driver. The microcontroller, preferably an ATMEGA328P mounted on an Arduino Uno development board, receives input from the temperature and LDR sensors to determine ambient conditions and from the IR sensors to detect the positional state of the curtain. Based on the processed data, the motor driver actuates the motor to open or close the curtains automatically. The invention eliminates the inconvenience of manual curtain operation, ensures optimum indoor lighting, thermal regulation, and privacy, and reduces reliance on artificial lighting and HVAC systems, thereby improving energy efficiency. The system is compact, cost-effective, universally compatible with different curtain types, and suitable for residential, commercial, and institutional applications.

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to the field of home automation technology, and more particularly to an automated curtain control system which operates based on real-time environmental triggers such as ambient temperature and light intensity. More specifically, the invention falls under the domain of smart home devices that enhance energy efficiency, user comfort, and convenience, while maintaining aesthetic compatibility and minimizing manual intervention.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
With rapid advancements in home automation, several domestic appliances have been automated to improve efficiency, energy savings, and convenience. While systems such as automated lighting, air-conditioning, and door-lock mechanisms have witnessed widespread adoption, curtain systems have remained largely manual or semi-automated. Traditional curtains require manual opening and closing, which is cumbersome for large windows, inaccessible areas, and for individuals with mobility impairments. This manual operation leads to irregular control of indoor lighting, poor thermal regulation, compromised privacy, and higher energy consumption due to increased dependence on artificial lighting and HVAC systems.
Several attempts have been made in the prior art to automate curtain control using timers, IR remotes, Bluetooth/mobile apps, or multi-sensor control modules. 
CN106647449A describes a curtain control system based on a 51 single-chip microcomputer (SCM) using light and temperature sensors. While it automates based on fixed threshold values, it relies on an IR remote controller for override and lacks true environmental adaptability.
CN106820916A incorporates a master control module with radar microwave induction, IR control, solar sensors, and scheduled timing chips. However, it is still dependent on time-based triggers and manual modules rather than autonomous, real-time weather responsiveness.
CN112160702 utilizes wind and sunlight sensors with a motor-driven system for automatic retraction. The setup involves mechanical components like telescopic rods and pressure buffers, making it bulky and overly specific to strong wind conditions.
CN205006586U features a dual-curtain system with solar panels, temperature and humidity sensors, and even heating wires. Although it promotes environmental protection, it is hardware-heavy and targets solar energy usage rather than direct climate control.
CN206769766U employs a variety of sensors including acoustic modules and timers to adjust curtain angles. Its complexity and reliance on sound and timing dilute the focus on core weather-triggered automation.
CN201621015804U based on Arduino Mega-SIM2560, it uses multiple modules including infrared sensors and GSM communication. Though advanced in connectivity, it lacks streamlined environmental logic and overcomplicates simple curtain automation.
CN201811295331A focuses on indoor light-based automation using illumination sensors and a central smart control platform. The curtain system is integrated with other smart devices but lacks dedicated weather sensitivity.
CN201910611222A combines multiple environmental sensors with wireless control through software modules. While robust, it requires high data processing and multiple external temperature/humidity sensors, which increases cost and complexity.
IN202341086001(A) Powered by Raspberry Pi with voice and gesture control, this system includes LDR, DHT11, rainfall sensors, and AI-based logic. However, its primary logic centers around rain and insect detection, and it sacrifices simplicity for multifactorial control.
However, most of these systems suffer from drawbacks such as:
•	reliance on manual or scheduled inputs rather than real-time weather responsiveness,
•	dependence on bulky or complex hardware,
•	over-integration with unrelated systems (e.g., fan or solar modules),
•	high cost of implementation,
•	and lack of universal compatibility with existing curtain types and aesthetics.
For instance, Chinese prior arts (e.g., CN106647449A, CN106820916A, CN112160702) disclose sensor-based curtain systems, but these are either dependent on IR/manual overrides, fixed thresholds, or complex telescopic mechanical assemblies, thereby limiting adaptability. Similarly, non-patent literature such as “Automatic Curtain Management” (Rucha Bagde et al.) and “Automatic Regulation and Control of Fan and Smart Curtain” (Raghu H. M. et al.) discuss Bluetooth/app-based systems or combined fan-curtain control mechanisms, which compromise curtain automation as a dedicated and independent function.
Thus, there exists a need for a simple, compact, and dedicated weather-triggered curtain system that:
•	operates autonomously in response to real-time environmental conditions,
•	minimizes energy usage by reducing HVAC dependence,
•	remains universally mountable without structural modifications,
•	and provides a cost-effective, aesthetically compatible solution for residential, commercial, and institutional use.
The present invention – Weather Triggered Smart Curtain System – addresses the above limitations by introducing a microcontroller-based adaptive control mechanism that seamlessly adjusts curtains based on ambient light and temperature, thereby improving energy efficiency, indoor comfort, and user convenience.
Therefore, to the best of our knowledge, none of the above-mentioned prior art attempts, individually or collectively propose the system and embodiment indicated and disclosed by the present invention 
OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION
The primary objective of the present invention is to provide a weather triggered smart curtain system capable of automatically adjusting curtains in response to real-time environmental conditions such as ambient temperature and light intensity, thereby eliminating the inconvenience and inefficiency associated with manual curtain operation.
Another objective of the invention is to integrate sensors and a control mechanism that analyze the environmental data and actuate the curtain movement smoothly and responsively, ensuring optimum indoor lighting, regulated temperature, and enhanced privacy.
Yet another objective of the invention is to promote energy efficiency by utilizing natural lighting and minimizing unnecessary dependence on artificial lighting and temperature-regulating systems such as air-conditioners or heaters, thereby contributing to a lower carbon footprint.
A further objective of the invention is to provide a curtain control system that is user-friendly, adaptive, and universally compatible with different types of curtains and existing infrastructure, without affecting the aesthetics of the room or requiring major structural modifications.
A still further objective of the invention is to design a compact and cost-effective system that is suitable for residential, commercial, institutional, and industrial applications, where autonomous curtain control based on weather conditions is desirable.
In essence, the objective of the present invention is to offer an innovative, automated, and sustainable curtain control solution, which enhances user comfort, operational convenience, energy savings, and overall quality of life.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to a weather triggered smart curtain system designed to provide autonomous adjustment of curtains based on real-time environmental conditions. The invention employs a set of integrated components including a microcontroller, temperature sensor, light dependent resistor (LDR) sensor, infrared (IR) sensor, motor, and motor driver, thereby enabling seamless automation of curtain operation.
In a preferred embodiment, the system is built around an ATMEGA328P microcontroller mounted on a development board (Arduino Uno). The IR sensor detects the positional state of the curtain, while the temperature and light sensors capture ambient conditions. Based on the sensor inputs, the control algorithm processes the data and actuates the motor via the motor driver circuit to open or close the curtain as required.
The invention thereby ensures optimum indoor lighting, improved thermal regulation, and enhanced privacy, while simultaneously reducing dependence on artificial lighting, air-conditioning, and heating systems. This results in significant energy savings and contributes to a lower carbon footprint.
The system is compact, cost-effective, and universally compatible with different curtain types and installations, without requiring major structural modifications. It is thus suitable for deployment in residential, commercial, institutional, and industrial environments, where automated environmental control is desirable.

ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION

Another advantage of the present invention is that the system improves energy efficiency by utilizing natural lighting and regulating indoor temperature, thus reducing dependence on artificial lighting, air-conditioning, and heating systems.

Another advantage of the present invention is that the compact and cost-effective microcontroller-based design makes the system easy to manufacture, install, and maintain compared to bulky or complex prior art solutions.
Another advantage of the present invention is that it enhances comfort and privacy by providing optimal lighting and thermal regulation while ensuring user independence, particularly for elderly or mobility-impaired individuals.
Another advantage of the present invention is that it contributes to sustainability by minimizing energy consumption and lowering the overall carbon footprint through efficient environmental control.

A SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR ENHANCING NATURAL CHILDBIRTH
The present invention relates to a system and methods for identifying a set of physical exercises for facilitating obstetrical care, which in particular enhances the chances of natural childbirth. More particularly, the invention provides a method for identifying a set of physical exercises for facilitating obstetrical care, the method comprising: receiving a user's responses to a specific set of questions; identifying suitable physical exercises based on the responses against the specific set of questions; and optimizing suitable timing, frequency, and duration for the identified physical exercises. FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[0001]	The present invention in general relates to the field of perinatal healthcare. Particularly, the present invention relates to systems, and methods for identifying physical exercises for facilitating obstetrical care. More particularly, the present invention relates to a system and method for identifying a set of physical exercises for facilitating natural childbirth.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[0002]	For women and families, the confirmation of pregnancy is often a source of immense joy and anticipation. The birthing process, physiologically begins with the onset of uterine contractions and is completed through the combined propulsive and expulsive efforts of the mother, ultimately resulting in the delivery of the baby through the birth canal. Psychologically, childbirth is a complex experience accompanied by sensory, emotional, and perceptual components that may significantly impact maternal well-being.
[0003]	A wide range of interventions are available in the art to help laboring women manage pain during labor. These interventions include both pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods. Pharmacological methods, while effective, may not always be affordable or cost-effective, and in some cases may pose risks to both mother and fetus, potentially increasing the complexity of the birthing process and the burden on caregivers. Non-pharmacological methods, by contrast, offer simplicity, effectiveness, affordability, acceptability, and applicability across various levels of healthcare systems, and are generally associated with minimal adverse effects.
[0004]	Various instruments and devices have been developed in the field of perinatal healthcare. For example, conception facilitating devices for achieving pregnancy through devices configured to increase the likelihood of conception. Devices for transferring preterm babies from a natural womb to an artificial womb to address the challenges associated with premature birth. Automatic bionic delivery assistants have further been developed to help pregnant women during childbirth. While these devices address various aspects of the perinatal care continuum, there remains a paucity of guidance in the art regarding identification of specific exercise protocols that may facilitate natural childbirth. In particular, existing approaches may lack detailed specifications regarding the timing, frequency, duration, and clinical criteria for physical exercises that could be performed during labor to potentially improve maternal outcomes. Therefore, improved systems and methods that identify specific physical exercises with optimized parameters for facilitating natural childbirth may be desirable.

EXAMPLES
[0093]	A Randomized Controlled Trial to assess the effectiveness of the set of identified physical exercises utilizing inflatable rubber ball during 1st stage of labor on selected maternal and fetal outcomes among laboring women, were conducted in selected hospitals in Uttarakhand. Additionally, the study was aimed at identifying the association of inflatable rubber ball usage on maternal and fetal outcomes with socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes. All hypotheses were tested at a 0.05 Level of Significance.
1 H0: There would be no significant difference in maternal and fetal outcomes between the experimental and the control groups.
2 H0: There would be no significant association between selected maternal and fetal outcomes and selected socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes of participants.
[0094]	The identified set of exercises were performed by the subject (during 1st stage of labor among laboring women) using a training device (inflatable rubber ball). This was followed by an evaluation of the subjects/users over selected maternal and fetal outcomes. Further, an association between the training device (inflatable rubber ball) based physical exercises and maternal, fetal outcomes with socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes was also studied.
[0095]	Materials and Methods: An experimental randomized controlled parallel group trial/ study was conducted on 74 research subjects/users, who were randomly assigned to the experimental and control groups. The current study was an open-blinded trial. 
This research study included independent and dependent variables, which are:
Independent variable: Exercise using the inflatable rubber ball.
Dependent variables: Maternal and fetal outcomes.
Selected maternal outcomes are, intensity of pain; mode of delivery; need for episiotomy; duration of the first stage; and duration of the second stage.
Selected fetal outcomes are, APGAR Scores (Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, and Respiration score) at 1 and 5 minutes; birth weight; immediate cry; need for resuscitation; and need for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) admission.
Population: All the laboring women in 1st stage of labor admitted at the selected settings.
Sampling: Purposive sampling technique was adopted with a sample size of 74 was adopted with below given sampling criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Consent to participate;
•	Age group between 18 to 45 years;
•	Third trimester with gestational age 29 to 42 weeks;
•	Cervical dilatation between 4 to 8 cm;
•	Primigravida or multigravida;
•	Singleton pregnancy;
•	Cephalic presentation; and
•	No contraindications for vaginal delivery.
Exclusion criteria:
•	Any Maternal or fetal complications;
•	Any medical or obstetrical complications; and
•	Being planned for an elective caesarean section.
Randomization: The block randomization (block size of 2) technique was used with the 1:1 allocation ratio of the treatment. Online software “Sealed Envelope” was used for the block randomization.
Concealment: The sequence of the treatment administration was created and enclosed in opaque envelopes.
Treatment allocation: With the entry of participants in the study, these sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes were provided randomly to the participants. After this, the participants were asked to pick one envelope, and it was opened in front of the participants after which their enrolment and treatment allocation was revealed subsequently.
Blinding: The study was conducted as  an open-blinded trial.
[0096]	Description of Intervention Schedule
Time:
•	Duration: 15 to 20 minutes of exercise schedule
•	Frequency: maximum 3 times
•	Interval between two exercise schedules: 2 hours
•	Onset of exercise: after the cervical dilatation reaches 5 cm.
•	End of exercise: after the cervical dilatation reaches 8 cm or 3 exercise schedules have been completed, whichever is first.
Position: All exercises were performed in sitting positions.
Type of exercises-
•	Rocking front rear and sideways (The participant would gently rock back and forth and side to side for 5 times each, duration: 3 to 5 minutes)
•	Circular movements and rotation of pelvis in clockwise and anti-clockwise direction (The participant would move her hips in a circular motion to “draw” small circles on the floor with the ball. The participant would do 5 movements clockwise, then repeat counter-clockwise, duration: 4 to 5 minutes)
•	Pelvic Floor Exercises (The participant would sit on the ball and contract her pelvic muscles, as would do to stop the flow of urine. The participant would hold for few seconds, and then release and repeated for 5 times, duration:4 to 5 minutes)
•	“Figure 8” Exercise (The participant would sit on the ball and move her hips as if drawing a figure of eight on the ball and repeat it 5 times, duration: 4 to 5 minutes)
•	Each exercise was performed for its stated base duration, and where two or three exercises were identified the duration of one or more exercises was extended, up to a maximum of 10 minutes per exercise, so that the total duration of the exercise schedule was 15 to 20 minutes.
Number of exercise schedules: A single day exercise schedule of maximum 3 exercises of duration up to 15 to 20 minutes in between or attaining a cervical dilatation of 4 to 8 cm, whichever happens first.
Ethical considerations:
•	Required Ethical clearance was taken.
•	Informed consent was obtained from participants after they provided a proper and complete explanation regarding the purpose and procedure of the study.
•	Privacy was provided to the participants before the commencement of the intervention.
•	Anonymity and confidentiality of participants and their data was maintained.
•	No invasive procedures were performed during the study.
•	The principles of autonomy, beneficence, and non-maleficence were followed throughout the study.
[0097]	The subjects/users in the experimental group were actively offered and demonstrated the identified physical exercises using the training device (inflatable rubber ball) for 15 to 20 minutes. Routine medical and obstetrical care was provided to the control groups. This was followed by an assessment of the maternal and fetal outcomes, and the resulting data was analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.
Data analysis:
[0098]	 Chi-square/ Fischer Exact Independent T-test was used for assessing the effects of inflatable rubber ball usage on maternal and fetal outcomes.
[0099]	ANOVA Correlation Chi-square tests were used to find out the association between inflatable rubber ball usage and maternal labor and fetal outcomes.

[0107]	Table 7 depicts the findings related to experience and recommendations of inflatable rubber ball usage in the experimental group. The majority of participants (46%) reported the use of an inflatable rubber ball as a great experience, followed by good (35%) and excellent experience (19%).
[0108]	By way of a first worked example, for a subject or user who is a primigravida, whose cervical dilatation is 5 cm (early category), whose membranes are not ruptured, for whom augmentation of labor has not been done, whose pain score is 8 (pain category of about 7 or more), who has attended 5 antenatal visits and for whom no analgesia has been used, the suitability scores are: rocking front, rear and sideways, 5 + 2 = 7; circular movement and rotation of pelvis, 2 + 3 + 3 - 1 = 7; pelvic floor exercises, 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 8; and figure of eight exercises, 3 - 1 - 1 = 1. Applying the threshold of 4 points, rocking front, rear and sideways, circular movement and rotation of pelvis, and pelvic floor exercises are identified as suitable, and figure of eight exercises is not. The base durations of 3, 4 and 4 minutes sum to 11 minutes, so the allocated durations are extended as described herein, the pelvic floor exercises having the highest suitability score being extended first, to give allocated durations of about 4 minutes, about 5 minutes and about 6 minutes respectively and a total of about 15 minutes for the exercise schedule.
[0109]	By way of a second worked example, for a subject or user who is a multigravida, whose cervical dilatation is 7 cm (late category), whose membranes have undergone spontaneous rupture, for whom augmentation of labor has been done with oxytocin, whose pain score is 5, who has attended 5 antenatal visits and for whom no analgesia has been used, the suitability scores are: rocking front, rear and sideways, 5; circular movement and rotation of pelvis, 2 - 1 - 1 = 0; pelvic floor exercises, 2 + 3 - 2 - 3 = 0; and figure of eight exercises, 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10. Rocking front, rear and sideways and figure of eight exercises are therefore identified as suitable, and the allocated durations are about 5 minutes and about 10 minutes respectively, giving a total of about 15 minutes.
[0110]	In certain embodiments, the suitability scores computed as described above reproduce, for each combination of the parity, dilatation and membrane categories tabulated in Table 1A, the set of physical exercises there identified, where augmentation of labor has not been done, the pain score is less than about 7, the number of antenatal visits is 4 or more and no analgesia has been used. Where any of those further response categories differs, the suitability scores are recomputed and the identified set of physical exercises may differ from the set tabulated in Table 1A, the tabulated set being superseded by the computed set.
[0111]	Major findings:
•	The participants in experimental and control groups were homogenous in socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes.
•	Statistically significant differences were found in maternal outcomes of participants between the experimental and control groups in terms of pain and duration of the first stage of labor. 
•	No statistically significant differences were found in the mode of delivery and need for episiotomy between the experimental and control groups. 
•	No statistically significant differences were found in the fetal outcomes of participants between the experimental and control groups. 
•	No statistically significant association was found between socio-demographic and maternal outcomes.
•	No statistically significant association was found between socio-demographic and fetal outcomes.
•	The majority of subjects/users (46%) reported the identified exercises using inflatable rubber ball of the present invention as a great experience, followed by good (35%) and excellent experience (19%).
[0112]	Comparison of maternal outcomes in experimental and control groups
The studies of present invention revealed that adoption of the identified exercises schedule using an inflatable rubber ball when performed by the participants (laboring women during the first stage of labor) resulted in a statistically significant difference in the reduction of pain. The results of the current study revealed a statistically significant reduced duration of the first stage of labor was attained upon adoption of the identified exercises schedule using an inflatable rubber ball. Concerning the duration of the second stage of labor, the findings of the current study demonstrate that the adoption of the identified exercises schedule using an inflatable rubber ball has no statistically significant effect on the duration of the second stage of labor.
[0113]	Comparison of fetal outcomes in experimental and control groups
The results of the current study infer that using the inflatable rubber ball based identified physical exercises among laboring women during the first stage of labor does not have any statistically significant effects on fetal outcomes between the experimental and the control groups.
[0114]	Association of socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes with maternal and fetal outcomes: The results of the present study showed that there was no statistically significant association between selected maternal and fetal outcomes and selected socio-demographic and obstetrical outcomes of subjects.
[0115]	ADVANTAGES:
•	Adequate and precise methodology in the intervention schedule was applied throughout the study for all participants.
•	The intervention can be applied to different settings thus increasing the scope of applicability.
•	Different perspectives of the research such as clinical, methodological, statistical, and 
•	ethical were tried to be covered during the study.
•	Clinically, participants’ threshold of pain was prioritized, which further led to either assistance or autonomy of participants during the intervention schedule.
•	Safety concerns of the participants were given due consideration.
•	Assistance and psychological support through the presence of a birth companion were encouraged for both experimental and control groups.
[0116]	The present study provides a method wherein a set of physical exercises are identified, which helps in alleviating maternal pain during periods of active contractions and aids in stretching pelvic muscles. In particular, the identified physical exercises when performed by a training device such as inflatable rubber ball, enhance the widening of the cervical canal and descent of the fetus, thus decreasing the duration of the labor. Also, it helps in improving the maternal satisfaction by encouraging their active participation in the labor process. In summary method described herein helps to select a set of physical exercises along with the timing, frequency, and duration that need to be adopted for the identified physical exercises, which collectively promotes physiological. psychological, emotional, and medical needs of the pregnant woman and to have enhanced chances of  natural childbirth.
