title: COMPACT AGRICULTURAL INTELLIGENCE WEATHER STATION SYSTEM
abstract: The present invention relates to a compact agricultural intelligence weather station system (100). The system comprises a wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102), a Stevenson screen (104), a rain gauge (106), a solar panel (108), a main enclosure (110), and a soil sensor module (114). The Stevenson screen (104) houses a temperature sensor (130), a humidity sensor (132), a pressure sensor (134), and an air-quality sensor assembly (136). The air-quality sensor assembly (136) comprises a particulate matter sensor (136a), a carbon dioxide sensor (136b), a nitrogen dioxide sensor (136c), and a volatile organic compound sensor (136d). The main enclosure (110) comprises a controller printed circuit board (144), a communication module (146), a battery pack (148), and a power management module (150). Sensor data are transmitted through a communication layer (170) to a cloud backend (172) comprising analytics and artificial intelligence advisory functions. The system enables hyperlocal environmental, air-quality, and soil monitoring and provides intelligent agricultural recommendations for crop management and decision support.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION 
The present invention relates generally to agricultural monitoring and decision-support systems and, more particularly, to a compact, solar-powered agricultural intelligence weather station configured to acquire atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition data and provide cloud-enabled analytics and artificial intelligence-assisted agricultural advisory services.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION 
Agricultural productivity is highly dependent upon local environmental conditions, weather variability, soil health, and air quality. Conventional agricultural weather stations generally provide limited meteorological measurements and are often expensive, bulky, and dependent upon fixed infrastructure. Furthermore, many existing systems monitor only isolated environmental parameters and fail to integrate atmospheric sensing, soil monitoring, air-quality assessment, cloud connectivity, and intelligent decision-support capabilities within a unified platform.
In many agricultural regions, farmers rely upon regional weather forecasts that may not accurately represent actual field conditions. Microclimatic variations across individual farms can significantly influence irrigation requirements, disease development, pest activity, nutrient availability, and crop growth. Existing monitoring solutions frequently require manual interpretation of sensor data and do not provide actionable recommendations tailored to field-specific conditions.
Accordingly, there exists a need for a compact, energy-autonomous, and intelligent agricultural monitoring platform capable of generating hyperlocal environmental information while integrating cloud-based analytics and artificial intelligence-assisted advisory functions to support precision agriculture and informed farm management decisions.
OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION
An object of the present invention is to provide a smart agricultural weather station system configured to acquire hyperlocal atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition data for supporting precision agriculture and informed agricultural decision-making.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a compact and field-deployable agricultural monitoring platform comprising atmospheric sensing, environmental sensing, air-quality monitoring, and soil-condition monitoring within a unified monitoring system.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a Stevenson screen-based environmental monitoring arrangement configured to house environmental and air-quality sensors while protecting the sensors from direct solar radiation, precipitation, and thermal disturbances and simultaneously permitting free circulation of ambient air.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a wind speed and direction sensing assembly incorporating contactless magnetic sensing technology, wear-resistant operation, continuous 360-degree directional measurement, and a precipitation monitoring arrangement capable of accurately measuring rainfall for long-duration field deployment.
Another object of the present invention is to provide an integrated soil-monitoring subsystem configured to measure soil moisture, soil temperature, and nutrient parameters associated with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a solar-powered and energy-autonomous agricultural monitoring platform capable of continuous operation in remote locations and configured to communicate sensor measurements to a cloud-based agricultural intelligence platform.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a cloud-enabled agricultural intelligence platform comprising secure Over-The-Air (OTA) firmware management, fail-safe operational architecture, data analytics, and remote monitoring capabilities for enhancing reliability, maintainability, and scalability of deployed weather station systems.
Another object of the present invention is to provide a Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) artificial intelligence advisory system configured to implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), sensor-data retrieval, predictive agricultural analytics, natural-language interaction, and intelligent recommendation generation for irrigation scheduling, spray timing optimization, disease-risk assessment, pest-risk assessment, environmental alerting, and agricultural decision support.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 
In the following detailed description, reference is made to the accompanying drawings, which form a part hereof, and in which is shown by way of illustration specific embodiments in which the invention may be practiced. These embodiments are described in sufficient detail to enable those skilled in the art to practice the invention, and it is to be understood that the embodiments may be combined, or that other embodiments may be utilized, and that structural and logical changes may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the present invention. The following detailed description is, therefore, not to be taken in a limiting sense, and the scope of the present invention is defined by the appended claims and their equivalents.
References will now be made in detail to the exemplary embodiment of the present disclosure. Before describing the detailed embodiments that are in accordance with the present disclosure, it should be observed that the embodiments reside primarily in a combination arrangement of the system according to an embodiment herein and as exemplified in FIG. 1 – FIG. 7.
The present invention provides a compact agricultural intelligence weather station system configured to acquire hyperlocal atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition data for supporting precision agriculture and intelligent farm management. The system integrates multiple sensing technologies, edge processing capabilities, cloud connectivity, and artificial intelligence-assisted advisory functions within a single field-deployable platform.
In an embodiment, the system comprises a wind speed and direction sensor assembly, a Stevenson screen, a rain gauge, a solar panel, a main enclosure, a mounting structure, and a soil sensor module. The wind speed and direction sensor assembly is configured to monitor local wind conditions, while the rain gauge measures precipitation. The soil sensor module is configured to monitor soil moisture, soil temperature, and nutrient parameters associated with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
The Stevenson screen comprises a ventilated protective enclosure configured to house environmental and air-quality sensors while shielding the sensors from direct solar radiation, precipitation, and external thermal disturbances. The Stevenson screen permits free circulation of ambient air through a louvered construction, thereby enabling accurate measurement of atmospheric conditions. In various embodiments, the Stevenson screen houses one or more sensors selected from a temperature sensor, humidity sensor, pressure sensor, particulate matter sensor, carbon dioxide sensor, nitrogen dioxide sensor, and volatile organic compound sensor.
The main enclosure houses electronic subsystems including a controller printed circuit board, a communication module, a battery pack, a power management module, and a sensor interface module. The controller receives sensor data from the atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-monitoring subsystems and performs local data acquisition, conditioning, processing, and management functions. The communication module enables transmission of sensor data to remote computing resources through one or more wired or wireless communication networks.
The system is configured for autonomous field deployment through the use of a solar-powered energy architecture comprising the solar panel, rechargeable battery system, and power management circuitry. The energy architecture enables long-duration operation in remote agricultural environments without dependence on external electrical infrastructure.
In another aspect, the invention provides a cloud-enabled agricultural intelligence platform configured to receive data from the weather station. The cloud platform comprises data storage, analytics, and advisory-generation capabilities. Sensor data collected from the field are transmitted to a cloud backend where historical information, environmental trends, and contextual agricultural information are processed to generate actionable insights.
In a further aspect, the cloud backend comprises a Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) artificial intelligence advisory engine configured to analyze atmospheric conditions, environmental parameters, air-quality measurements, and soil-condition data to generate intelligent recommendations. The advisory engine may provide irrigation recommendations, crop-management recommendations, disease-risk assessments, pest-risk assessments, environmental alerts, weather-based advisories, and conversational decision-support outputs.
Accordingly, the present invention provides a compact, solar-powered, and intelligent agricultural monitoring platform capable of integrating atmospheric sensing, environmental sensing, air-quality monitoring, soil-condition monitoring, cloud-based analytics, and artificial intelligence-assisted advisory generation within a unified system. The invention enables hyperlocal agricultural intelligence and supports data-driven decision-making for improved crop productivity, resource utilization, and farm management.

In an embodiment, the wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102) comprises a GS-303 wind sensing subsystem configured to provide accurate and continuous measurement of wind speed and wind direction while minimizing mechanical wear and maintenance requirements. The wind speed sensing portion of the assembly comprises a sealed magnetic reed-switch arrangement operatively associated with a multi-cup anemometer structure. Rotation of the anemometer in response to ambient wind conditions generates periodic magnetic switching events that are detected by the reed-switch arrangement and converted into wind speed measurements. The sealed configuration protects the sensing elements from dust, moisture, corrosion, and environmental contaminants, thereby enhancing operational reliability in agricultural environments. The wind direction sensing portion comprises a contactless magnetic sensing arrangement incorporating a 12-bit absolute magnetic encoder configured to determine angular orientation throughout a continuous 360-degree rotational range. Unlike conventional potentiometer-based wind direction sensors that are susceptible to mechanical wear, electrical noise, and directional dead zones, the magnetic encoder operates without physical contact between sensing elements, thereby providing wear-free operation and long-term measurement stability. The encoder is configured to generate high-resolution directional information corresponding to the angular position of a wind vane and is capable of dead-zone-free 360-degree directional measurement. In a preferred embodiment, the wind sensor assembly (102) provides simultaneous digital and analog output capabilities to maximize compatibility with different controller architectures and communication interfaces. The digital output may be transmitted through an Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C) communication protocol, while an analog voltage output corresponding to measured wind direction may be generated concurrently. The dual-output architecture enables integration with a wide variety of microcontroller platforms, data acquisition systems, agricultural monitoring devices, and edge-processing units without requiring additional signal-conversion circuitry. The GS-303 wind sensing subsystem thereby provides a compact, low-power, contactless, wear-resistant, and high-accuracy wind monitoring solution particularly suited for long-duration autonomous deployment in precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and hyperlocal weather sensing applications.

Over-The-Air (OTA) Firmware Update System
In an embodiment, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) comprises an Over-The-Air (OTA) firmware update system configured to enable remote software management, feature enhancement, calibration updates, security patch deployment, and firmware maintenance of deployed weather station units without requiring physical access to the installation site. The OTA firmware update system allows administrators and service operators to remotely monitor, manage, and upgrade field-deployed weather stations through a cloud-connected software infrastructure.
The communication module (146) is configured to establish communication with a cloud backend (172), wherein the cloud backend (172) maintains one or more version-controlled firmware packages associated with the weather station system (100). The controller printed circuit board (144) periodically communicates with the cloud backend (172) to determine the availability of updated firmware versions or may receive update instructions through remotely initiated commands. Upon identification of an available firmware package, the controller printed circuit board (144) downloads the firmware package through a secure communication channel and initiates a controlled update sequence.
In a preferred embodiment, the controller printed circuit board (144) implements a dual-partition firmware architecture comprising a first firmware partition and a second firmware partition. During normal operation, one partition operates as an active firmware partition while the other partition remains inactive. Upon receipt of a firmware update package, the updated firmware image is written to the inactive partition while the active firmware partition continues supporting uninterrupted operation of the weather station system (100). Following successful completion of the firmware transfer process, a boot management routine validates the newly installed firmware image and designates the updated partition for activation during a subsequent restart sequence.
The dual-partition architecture enables uninterrupted firmware deployment while minimizing operational downtime. Because the existing firmware remains preserved within the previously active partition until successful validation of the updated firmware image, the weather station system (100) maintains a reliable recovery path in the event of update failure, corruption, interruption, or communication loss during the update process.
In a further embodiment, the OTA firmware update system incorporates an automated rollback mechanism configured to restore a previously validated firmware version when a newly installed firmware image fails to satisfy one or more predefined operational criteria. Following activation of the updated firmware, the controller printed circuit board (144) executes a self-diagnostic validation sequence to verify successful boot completion, sensor communication functionality, memory integrity, communication subsystem operation, and application execution. If the validation sequence indicates a malfunction, instability condition, or startup failure, the boot management routine automatically reverts operation to the previously validated firmware partition, thereby preventing permanent system failure and ensuring continued field operation.
To prevent unauthorized firmware installation and malicious software injection, the OTA firmware update system further incorporates firmware authentication and verification mechanisms. Each firmware package is digitally signed prior to deployment, and the controller printed circuit board (144) verifies the authenticity and integrity of the downloaded firmware package before permitting installation. Cryptographic signature verification, integrity checking, and firmware validation procedures ensure that only authorized firmware images generated by approved sources can be executed by the weather station system (100).
Accordingly, the OTA firmware update system provides secure remote firmware management, continuous feature enhancement capability, reduced maintenance costs, improved fleet administration, minimized operational downtime, enhanced cybersecurity protection, and long-term scalability for large-scale deployment of autonomous agricultural weather station systems.
Fail-Safe Architecture and Autonomous Recovery System
In an embodiment, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) incorporates a fail-safe operational architecture configured to maintain continuous autonomous operation in remote agricultural environments where physical maintenance access may be limited, infrequent, or impractical. The fail-safe architecture is implemented through a combination of hardware-level monitoring mechanisms, fault-isolation procedures, autonomous recovery routines, communication resilience protocols, and fault-recording functionalities that collectively improve system reliability and operational uptime.
The controller printed circuit board (144) is configured to implement a hardware watchdog timer configured to continuously monitor execution of operational firmware. During normal operation, the firmware periodically transmits watchdog refresh signals within a predefined time interval. If a firmware malfunction, software deadlock, memory corruption event, communication failure, processor exception, infinite execution loop, or other abnormal operating condition prevents the watchdog refresh signal from being generated within the predefined interval, the hardware watchdog timer automatically initiates a processor reset sequence. Following reset, the controller printed circuit board (144) reloads operational firmware and resumes sensor acquisition, communication, and processing activities without requiring manual intervention. Accordingly, the watchdog mechanism enables automatic recovery from software and hardware fault conditions that would otherwise render the weather station non-operational.
In a further embodiment, the system implements sensor fault-isolation functionality configured to prevent failure of an individual sensing device from affecting operation of the remaining sensing subsystems. Sensor communication transactions associated with the temperature sensor (130), humidity sensor (132), pressure sensor (134), air-quality sensor assembly (136), particulate matter sensor (136a), carbon dioxide sensor (136b), nitrogen dioxide sensor (136c), volatile organic compound sensor (136d), and soil-monitoring sensors are individually monitored through timeout-controlled communication routines. When a particular sensor fails to respond within a predetermined communication interval, the controller printed circuit board (144) identifies the affected sensor, records the failure condition, isolates the faulty communication transaction, and continues acquisition of data from all remaining operational sensors. This architecture prevents a single sensor malfunction from causing complete system interruption.
In another embodiment, the communication module (146) incorporates network resilience and automatic reconnection functionality configured to maintain reliable communication with the cloud backend (172). Upon detection of communication loss, network interruption, signal degradation, cellular disconnection, wireless access point failure, or other connectivity abnormalities, the controller printed circuit board (144) initiates an autonomous reconnection sequence. The reconnection sequence may utilize a progressive retry mechanism, exponential back-off protocol, connection-state monitoring process, or equivalent recovery strategy to re-establish communication while minimizing power consumption and network congestion. During periods of communication unavailability, sensor data may be temporarily stored within local memory to prevent information loss.
In a preferred embodiment, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) further comprises a fault logging mechanism configured to maintain a persistent record of operational events and fault conditions. The fault logging mechanism stores diagnostic information including watchdog reset events, communication failures, sensor timeout events, power interruptions, firmware update outcomes, memory faults, and network connectivity interruptions. The recorded diagnostic information may be stored within non-volatile memory and subsequently transmitted to the cloud backend (172) for remote diagnostics, maintenance planning, performance evaluation, and reliability analysis.
The cloud backend (172) may further generate system-health notifications based on fault information received from deployed weather station systems. Such notifications may include low-battery alerts, sensor maintenance alerts, communication-failure alerts, firmware-update alerts, watchdog-reset alerts, and predictive maintenance recommendations. Accordingly, the fail-safe architecture provides enhanced reliability, autonomous fault recovery, improved operational continuity, reduced maintenance requirements, and long-term suitability for unattended deployment in remote agricultural environments.
Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) Artificial Intelligence Advisory System:
In an embodiment, the cloud backend (172) comprises a KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory system (172d), wherein KeSAN represents a Key Sensor Analytical Network configured to transform sensor-derived agricultural data into contextualized agronomic recommendations and natural-language advisory outputs. The KeSAN system is operatively coupled to atmospheric sensing, environmental sensing, air-quality monitoring, and soil-monitoring subsystems of the smart agricultural weather station system (100). The KeSAN system analyzes real-time sensor measurements, historical records, and contextual agricultural information to generate actionable recommendations relating to irrigation scheduling, crop management, disease prevention, fertilizer application, pest-risk assessment, environmental monitoring, and operational planning.
In a preferred embodiment, the KeSAN system implements a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture configured to combine artificial intelligence reasoning with real-time sensor data retrieval. Upon receiving a user query, the KeSAN system retrieves relevant environmental measurements, historical sensor records, weather information, agronomic datasets, and operational parameters from the cloud backend (172) and associated databases. The retrieved information is organized into contextual datasets and supplied to the artificial intelligence engine to generate context-aware and data-driven advisory outputs based on actual field conditions.
In a further embodiment, the KeSAN system incorporates a sensor retrieval framework and workflow orchestration mechanism configured to collect, correlate, and process sensor information originating from multiple sensing domains, including atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition monitoring. The system performs contextual reasoning using retrieved sensor data, historical trends, forecast information, and analytical results to generate task-specific recommendations and agricultural insights.
The KeSAN system further provides a natural-language interaction interface and sensor-to-language translation functionality. Users may submit queries relating to weather conditions, irrigation scheduling, nutrient management, crop protection, environmental quality, and operational planning using ordinary spoken or written language. The KeSAN system interprets the query, retrieves relevant contextual information, and converts sensor measurements, analytical outputs, and predictive results into human-readable recommendations, alerts, explanations, and decision-support guidance. Accordingly, the KeSAN system functions as an intelligent agricultural advisory layer between the sensing infrastructure and end-user agricultural operations.
Predictive Agricultural Analytics and Decision-Support Algorithms
In an embodiment, the KeSAN (Key Sensor Analytical Network) artificial intelligence advisory system (172d) comprises a predictive agricultural analytics engine configured to process atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition data obtained from the smart agricultural weather station system (100) and generate actionable agronomic recommendations. The predictive agricultural analytics engine utilizes real-time sensor measurements, historical environmental records, forecast information, crop-specific parameters, and analytical models to identify operational conditions that may affect crop growth, irrigation efficiency, nutrient utilization, disease development, pest activity, and environmental safety. The generated outputs may be communicated to users through the mobile application (174a), web dashboard (174b), conversational advisory interface (174c), and alert and notification engine (174d).
In one embodiment, the predictive agricultural analytics engine implements a spray timing prediction algorithm configured to determine optimal application windows for fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, growth regulators, or other agricultural treatments. The algorithm analyzes wind speed, wind direction, rainfall measurements, humidity levels, temperature conditions, environmental moisture conditions at the plant, and forecast data to identify application periods that minimize chemical drift, runoff losses, evaporation losses, and environmental contamination. Based on the analysis, the system generates recommendations indicating preferred treatment periods, unsuitable application windows, anticipated weather risks, and expected treatment effectiveness. The algorithm thereby assists users in improving chemical-use efficiency while reducing operational costs and environmental impact.
In another embodiment, the predictive agricultural analytics engine implements disease and pest prediction functionality configured to estimate the likelihood of crop disease outbreaks and pest infestations. The prediction process utilizes environmental variables including temperature, humidity, rainfall, environmental moisture conditions at the plant, wind conditions, air-quality parameters, and historical disease or pest occurrence information. The system applies predictive models to identify environmental conditions associated with pathogen development, fungal proliferation, insect activity, or crop stress. Based on the calculated risk levels, the system may generate preventive advisories, early-warning notifications, monitoring recommendations, treatment schedules, or intervention strategies. The disease and pest prediction functionality enables proactive crop protection measures before visible symptoms become widespread within the cultivation area.
In a further embodiment, the predictive agricultural analytics engine implements smart irrigation scheduling functionality configured to determine irrigation requirements based upon environmental conditions, soil measurements, and crop-specific water demand. The irrigation scheduling functionality utilizes soil moisture data, soil temperature data, ambient temperature measurements, humidity levels, wind conditions, light intensity measurements, rainfall information, and evapotranspiration calculations to estimate water availability within the crop root zone. Based on these calculations, the system generates irrigation recommendations including irrigation timing, irrigation duration, irrigation frequency, watering windows, and water-conservation strategies. The smart irrigation scheduling functionality improves water-use efficiency, reduces unnecessary irrigation events, and promotes optimal crop growth conditions.
In another embodiment, the predictive agricultural analytics engine implements air-quality threshold monitoring and alerting functionality configured to continuously evaluate air-quality measurements obtained from particulate matter sensors, carbon dioxide sensors, nitrogen dioxide sensors, volatile organic compound sensors, and related environmental monitoring devices. The system compares measured values against predefined thresholds, regulatory standards, crop-specific tolerance limits, or user-configurable safety parameters. When one or more monitored values exceed the applicable thresholds, the system automatically generates alerts, warnings, notifications, and recommended corrective actions. The alerting functionality may be implemented through push notifications, text messages, electronic mail communications, dashboard alerts, or conversational advisory responses. The air-quality threshold monitoring functionality thereby enables rapid identification of environmental hazards that may affect crop health, worker safety, equipment operation, or surrounding ecosystems.
Accordingly, the predictive agricultural analytics engine transforms raw sensor measurements into actionable agricultural intelligence by integrating environmental sensing, predictive modeling, contextual analysis, and artificial intelligence-assisted decision support. The engine enables users to proactively manage irrigation operations, crop protection activities, fertilizer applications, environmental risks, and overall farm productivity based upon continuously updated field-level information.

The method (700) begins at step (702), wherein atmospheric data are acquired using the wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102) and the rain gauge (106). At step (708), the acquired atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition measurements are transmitted to the sensor interface module (152). The sensor interface module (152) receives and organizes sensor inputs originating from multiple sensing subsystems and provides the measurements to the controller printed circuit board (144) for further processing.
At step (710), the controller printed circuit board (144) processes, validates, filters, calibrates, and aggregates the received sensor measurements. Processing operations may include signal conditioning, noise reduction, sensor validation, data normalization, anomaly detection, timestamp generation, and preparation of structured datasets suitable for transmission and analysis.
At step (712), locally generated operational data are stored and edge-level analytics are performed. In certain embodiments, the controller printed circuit board (144) performs preliminary trend analysis, threshold evaluation, sensor-health monitoring, fault detection, and temporary data buffering prior to communication with remote computing resources.
At step (714), the processed sensor information is transmitted through the communication module (146) and communication layer (170). The communication layer (170) may utilize one or more wired or wireless communication technologies including cellular communication networks, Wi-Fi networks, long-range communication protocols, satellite communication systems, or equivalent communication infrastructures.
At step (716), the transmitted sensor data are received by the cloud backend (172). The cloud backend (172) provides centralized storage, processing, analytics, and artificial intelligence services for a plurality of deployed weather station systems.
At step (718), the received sensor information is stored within the database (172b). The database (172b) maintains real-time measurements, historical records, environmental trends, operational logs, and contextual agricultural information for subsequent analysis.
At step (720), environmental analytics and predictive agricultural analyses are performed using the analytics engine (172c). The analytics engine (172c) evaluates sensor-derived information to identify environmental trends, forecast conditions, irrigation requirements, crop-health indicators, disease risks, pest risks, and other agronomically relevant conditions.
At step (722), relevant sensor records, historical measurements, weather information, agronomic datasets, crop-specific information, and contextual environmental data are retrieved through a KeSAN retrieval framework. The retrieval process identifies information relevant to a particular analytical task or user inquiry and prepares structured contextual data for artificial intelligence processing.
At step (724), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) processing and workflow orchestration are executed using the Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d). The KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) combines retrieved contextual information with real-time sensor measurements and artificial intelligence reasoning processes to generate context-aware agricultural intelligence and decision-support outputs.
At decision step (726), the system determines whether sufficient information is available for generation of agricultural recommendations and predictive advisories. If additional information, validation, or analytical processing is required, the method may return to one or more preceding processing stages. If the recommendation criteria are satisfied, the method proceeds to advisory-generation operations.
At step (728), irrigation scheduling recommendations are generated based upon soil moisture measurements, environmental conditions, weather information, crop requirements, and predictive analytics. The generated recommendations may identify irrigation timing, irrigation duration, irrigation frequency, and water-conservation opportunities.
At step (730), spray timing recommendations are generated. The spray timing recommendations are determined using environmental parameters including wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rainfall conditions, forecast information, and crop-specific treatment requirements to identify preferred application windows for pesticides, fertilizers, fungicides, herbicides, and related agricultural inputs.
At step (732), disease and pest risk predictions are generated. The predictions may be based upon environmental conditions, historical observations, crop characteristics, air-quality parameters, weather forecasts, and predictive disease or pest models. The generated outputs may include risk scores, warning notifications, and preventive management recommendations.
At step (734), air-quality threshold alerts and environmental warnings are generated. Measurements obtained from the air-quality sensor assembly (136), including data from the particulate matter sensor (136a), carbon dioxide sensor (136b), nitrogen dioxide sensor (136c), and volatile organic compound sensor (136d), are compared against predefined threshold values or crop-specific limits. Upon detection of threshold exceedance conditions, the system generates corresponding alerts and corrective-action recommendations.
At step (736), the generated agricultural intelligence is converted into natural-language advisory outputs through a sensor-to-language translation process performed by the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d). The sensor-to-language translation process converts sensor measurements, analytical results, predictive outputs, and environmental observations into human-readable recommendations and explanations.
The generated advisories are subsequently delivered through the application layer (174) comprising the mobile application (174a), web dashboard (174b), conversational advisory interface (174c), and alert and notification engine (174d). The advisories may include irrigation guidance, disease-prevention recommendations, pest-management strategies, fertilizer application recommendations, environmental alerts, crop-health insights, and operational planning assistance.
The method concludes at step (740), wherein the generated recommendations and advisory outputs are made available to users for supporting precision agriculture, resource optimization, crop management, and data-driven agricultural decision-making.

EXAMPLE: Hyperlocal Agricultural Monitoring and Intelligent Advisory Generation
In an exemplary embodiment, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) is deployed in a cotton cultivation field covering approximately 5 hectares. The weather station system (100) comprises a wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102), a Stevenson screen (104), a rain gauge (106), a solar panel (108), a main enclosure (110), and a soil sensor module (114).
The Stevenson screen (104) houses a temperature sensor (130), a humidity sensor (132), a pressure sensor (134), and an air-quality sensor assembly (136). The air-quality sensor assembly (136) comprises a particulate matter sensor (136a), a carbon dioxide sensor (136b), a nitrogen dioxide sensor (136c), and a volatile organic compound sensor (136d). The soil sensor module (114) comprises a soil moisture probe (160), a soil temperature probe (162), and an NPK probe (164).
During operation, the system continuously acquires atmospheric, environmental, air-quality, and soil-condition data at predetermined intervals. In an exemplary monitoring cycle, the temperature sensor (130) records an ambient temperature of approximately 34°C, the humidity sensor (132) records a relative humidity of approximately 78%, and the pressure sensor (134) records an atmospheric pressure of approximately 1008 hPa. The soil moisture probe (160) detects a reduction in available soil moisture below a predefined irrigation threshold, while the NPK probe (164) indicates declining nitrogen availability within the monitored cultivation zone.
The acquired sensor data are processed by the controller printed circuit board (144) and transmitted through the communication module (146) and communication layer (170) to the cloud backend (172). The analytics engine (172c) evaluates current measurements together with historical environmental records and forecast information. The Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) retrieves relevant sensor records, crop-specific information, weather forecasts, and agronomic datasets for contextual analysis.
Based on the observed combination of elevated temperature, high humidity, declining soil moisture, and forecasted absence of rainfall, the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) generates an irrigation scheduling recommendation advising irrigation within a predefined time window to prevent crop water stress and maintain optimal growth conditions.
In a subsequent monitoring period, the system identifies a combination of elevated humidity, increasing temperature, rainfall history, and environmental conditions associated with development of fungal disease. The analytics engine (172c) determines an increased disease-risk condition, and the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) generates a disease-risk advisory recommending preventive crop protection measures and enhanced field monitoring.
In another instance, the wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102) records low wind speed conditions and favorable wind direction characteristics, while forecast data predict no precipitation during the next several hours. Based on these conditions, the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) generates a spray timing recommendation identifying a preferred application window for pesticides or fertilizers to reduce drift and improve application effectiveness.
The generated recommendations are delivered through the mobile application (174a), web dashboard (174b), conversational advisory interface (174c), and alert and notification engine (174d). Accordingly, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) enables real-time environmental monitoring, predictive agricultural analytics, and intelligent decision support for precision farming operations.
EXAMPLE: Predictive Agricultural Analytics Using Hyperlocal Environmental Data
In an exemplary deployment, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) was installed within an agricultural field and operated continuously for approximately 150 days. During operation, the system acquired environmental measurements at predetermined intervals through the temperature sensor (130), humidity sensor (132), pressure sensor (134), air-quality sensor assembly (136), wind speed and direction sensor assembly (102), rain gauge (106), and soil sensor module (114). The collected environmental dataset comprised hourly records of temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, rainfall, soil moisture, soil temperature, nutrient measurements, and air-quality parameters.
The acquired sensor data were processed by the controller printed circuit board (144) and transmitted through the communication module (146) and communication layer (170) to the cloud backend (172). The database (172b) accumulated historical environmental records for subsequent analysis by the analytics engine (172c) and the Key Sensor Analytical Network (KeSAN) artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d).
In one embodiment, the analytics engine (172c) generated predictive environmental forecasts using a machine-learning model trained on historical environmental observations. In an embodiment, the analytics engine employs a neural-network model comprising an input layer receiving environmental parameters, one or more hidden layers comprising processing nodes, and an output layer configured to generate forecast values. The neural network may be implemented as a feed-forward neural network, recurrent neural network, long short-term memory network, gated recurrent unit network, convolutional neural network, transformer-based model, or combinations thereof. The predictive model utilized environmental variables including temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, rainfall, and temporal information. In an exemplary implementation, the model analyzed approximately 3,562 hours of environmental observations collected during the deployment period and generated short-term temperature forecasts. A forecasting architecture utilizing a three-hour historical observation window and a hidden processing layer comprising sixteen processing units was found to provide an effective balance between prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Experimental evaluation demonstrated temperature forecasting performance corresponding to a root mean squared error (RMSE) of approximately 1.245°C and a mean absolute error (MAE) of approximately 0.920°C, thereby enabling accurate prediction of localized environmental conditions.
In another embodiment, the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) generated crop-specific recommendations based on environmental measurements and historical climatic trends. Environmental variables including temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, light intensity, rainfall, soil moisture, soil temperature, nutrient levels, and temporal agricultural information were analyzed to identify crop suitability under prevailing environmental conditions. In an exemplary evaluation, environmental records were aggregated into approximately 158 daily climatic profiles, and the advisory engine generated crop recommendations based on observed environmental patterns. Under predominantly dry environmental conditions, recommendations favored drought-tolerant crops, whereas elevated moisture conditions resulted in recommendations suitable for water-intensive crops. The advisory engine compares environmental measurements with stored crop-specific environmental profiles and ranks candidate crops according to similarity scores.
In a further embodiment, the KeSAN artificial intelligence advisory engine (172d) combined real-time sensor measurements with historical environmental records, forecast information, and contextual agricultural datasets through a retrieval-based analytical framework. For example, when the soil moisture probe (160) detected moisture levels below a predetermined threshold and forecast information indicated absence of significant rainfall, the system automatically generated irrigation scheduling recommendations. Similarly, when humidity levels increased, rainfall history indicated prolonged environmental moisture conditions, and temperature measurements entered disease-favorable ranges, the system generated disease-risk advisories and preventive crop-management recommendations.
The generated recommendations, predictive forecasts, and environmental alerts were delivered through the mobile application (174a), web dashboard (174b), conversational advisory interface (174c), and alert and notification engine (174d). Accordingly, the smart agricultural weather station system (100) demonstrated the ability to transform continuously acquired hyperlocal environmental information into actionable agricultural intelligence supporting irrigation management, crop planning, disease prevention, nutrient management, and precision agriculture decision-making.

title: AI-Based Safe UPI Payment Verification
abstract: The present invention relates to an AI-Based Safe UPI Payment Verification System, which aims to improve the security and reliability of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. The system comprises Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine learning and transaction analytics to analyse the payment request prior to execution. It evaluates recipient data, transaction history, user behaviour, transaction amount and indicators of fraud to create an adaptive safety score and danger evaluation. Before completing a transaction, the system offers real-time warning, recommendation and verification alerts to the users. The invention protects against financial losses, accidental transfers, and enhances user trust in digital payment systems by identifying suspicious recipients and unusual transaction patterns, which helps to prevent potential fraud attempts.
specification:
Field of the Invention
The present invention relates to a a smart verification system for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions including an AI solution or behavioural analytics solution that determines the safety of the transaction and alerts to the risk in real time before the transaction is executed. 
Background
Digital payment systems and UPI transactions have revolutionized the financial sector, providing instant money transfers. But the incidents of payment fraud, phishing scams, fake UPI IDs and accidental transfer has also surged with the use of the service.
There are many instances when users receive funds from the wrong recipient or they are victim to requests for payment from fraudsters. Current UPI systems allow the process of transactions to go through after basic authentication, but pre-execution intelligent safety verification is lacking.
The current systems do not include facilities to:
•	Evaluate recipient trustworthiness.
•	Detect suspicious payment behaviour.
•	Notify users of possible fraud concerns.
•	Do analyse & understand transaction patterns before payments are made.
•	Give tips on payment safety when starting a payment.
Thus, an intelligent UPI verification system that can process information and determine safety scores prior to payment is required. The proposed invention tackles these drawbacks with the aid of AI payment verification and risk analysis.
Summary
The present invention provides an AI-Based Safe UPI Payment Verification System, which aims to improve the security and reliability of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. The system features Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine learning and transaction analytics to analyse the payment request prior to execution. It evaluates recipient data, transaction history, user behaviour, transaction amount and indicators of fraud to create an adaptive safety score and danger evaluation. Before completing a transaction, the system offers real-time warning, recommendation and verification alerts to the users. The invention protects against financial losses, accidental transfers, and enhances user trust in digital payment systems by identifying suspicious recipients and unusual transaction patterns, which helps to prevent potential fraud attempts.

The following detailed description illustrates the principles of the invention by way of example and not by way of limitation. Embodiments of the present invention are directed to a smart verification system for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions including an AI solution or behavioural analytics solution that determines the safety of the transaction and alerts to the risk in real time before the transaction is executed.  The invention can be used in banking applications, UPI platforms, digital wallets, mobile payment systems, ecommerce platforms, and more digital financial applications that need a secure payment process.
The invention provides a payment orchestration framework based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) designed specifically for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. It is a complete system that integrates recipient trust verification, predictive transaction success analysis, intelligent fraud detection, behavioural analytics, and smart payment routing in a single architecture. A dynamic trust and risk score is created ahead of the transaction, continuously adjusted based on the pattern of transactions, device attributes, user actions, and context. The predictive analytics engine predicts whether transactions will be successful or not and suggests the best payment paths. The invention greatly improves the security of payments, reduces the number of failed transactions, avoids fraudulent transactions, boosts customer trust, and contributes to the development of a safe and intelligent, scalable digital payments system. The AI-Based Safe UPI Payment Verification System has been designed to check each and every UPI transaction before processing. The system will gather the information on the transactions, analyse the payment behaviour, verify the credibility of the recipient, and produce a safety score that will help the users make safe payment choices. The invention uses machine learning models which are constantly learning based on transactional data, fraud reports, user behaviour, and payment history to enhance the accuracy of the verification over time.
5.1. System Architecture and Components
The proposed AI-Based Safe UPI Payment Verification System is an intelligent security system which would run before the initiation of the UPI payment. The system consists of several functional components, which interact with each other to verify the user, check authenticity of recipients, analyse the features of transactions, determine the possibility of fraud and generate instructions for the safety of transactions. The architecture's design also makes sure that all payment requests are thoroughly verified before approval, which increases the security of transactions and lowers the risk of financial fraud.
The first level of the security that the system ensures is the User Authentication Module. This module verifies the user's identity using methods of authentication like UPI PIN verification, biometric authentication and multi-factor authentication. The restriction of the functionality of the module prevents its users from accessing the accounts and making transactions without authorization, thus protecting the accounts and transactions of these users from misuse.
Upon successful authentication, details of the transaction are passed to the Recipient Verification Module that rates the credibility and trustworthiness of the beneficiary account. This module examines the recipient's UPI ID, past transactions, account activity and trust factors that are available. The system will identify the authenticity of the recipient which will keep transfers from being mistaken and even prevent any kind of fraudulent or suspicious accounts.
The Transaction Analysis Module then looks at the different parameters of the transaction such as the amount, the frequency, when it occurs, and behaviour in the past. The module will use an analysis of the characteristics of the transaction with previous user activity to identify unusual patterns or anomalies that may indicate suspicious activity. This analysis can help determine whether the transaction is in line with the user's normal finances.
The analysed transaction data enables the AI Risk Assessment Engine to function, which is the key intellectual part of the invention. The AI and machine learning engine analyzes transaction details, user behavior, recipient profiles, and fraud patterns to generate a real-time risk score. The engine is constantly learning from new data on transactions and fraud patterns, improving its ability to detect potential threats and suspicious activities over time.
The Safety Score Generator generates an easy to understand, numerical safety score for the transaction based on the results of the AI Risk Assessment Engine. The score indicates the risk level of the payment, and will help users determine whether the transaction is safe, moderately risky, or highly suspicious. This functionality helps in better understanding of the risks and helps users to make sound payment decisions.
With the help of the Alert and Recommendation Module, User is alerted and recommended with the created safety score. This module will provide you with live notifications, warnings and recommendations prior to completing transactions. In case of any possible threats, the system can suggest the recipient verification, take the transaction with a pinch of salt or even terminate the transaction. These alerts are additional safeguards against fraud and unintended payments.
The system includes a Fraud Detection Database that captures details of existing fraud accounts and fraud patterns or suspicious transaction activity, as well as historical fraud cases, to facilitate ongoing fraud detection and learning. This database acts as a repository of knowledge, helping the AI engine to detect potential threats and enhance prediction accuracy.
In addition, the system also includes a Reporting and Analytics Dashboard that provides an overview of transactions, Risk Report, Fraud Stats, payment Analytics and more. The dashboard allows users, financial institutions, and payment service providers to monitor the trends of transactions, analyze the security performance of the payment system and understand the payment behaviour.
The general use of the system architecture is a sequence in which the user's authentication is performed, followed by the recipient's verification, transaction analysis, risk assessment, the generation of the safety score, and finally the sending of the alert. This integrated design ensures a secure, intelligent, and user-friendly UPI payment verification process that can help mitigate fraud risks and boost trust in digital payments. Workflow of the system
a. Transaction Initiation: User provides address details of the recipient and amount to pay using a UPI app.
b. User Authentication: Securely authenticates customer by using secure authentication methods like UPI PIN verification.
c. Transaction Data Collection: The system stores the information about transactions, recipient details, transaction amount, device details and transaction records.
d. Recipient Verification: The Recipient Verification Module does an analysis of the Recipient account and verifies past interactions.
e. The Transaction Analysis Module assesses transactions in terms of amount, timing, frequency and payment behaviour.
f. Risk Assessment: Information collected is analysed and a risk score is calculated by the AI Risk Assessment Engine.
g. The Safety Score Generator generates a safety rating from 0 to 100.
h. Alert Generation: Warning messages and recommendations are shown to the user when suspicious activity is detected.
i. User Decision: User conducts safety evaluation and then decides to continue or cancel transaction.
j. Payment Execution: Once approved, the transaction is safely executed on the UPI network.
k. Data Storage and Learning: The results of transactions are not stored, but they are used to adjust the performance of the AI models to detect fraud.
Advantages
•	Enhanced Fraud Prevention through AI-based transaction analysis.
•	Reduces accidental money transfers to incorrect recipients.
•	Provides real-time transaction safety alerts and recommendations.
•	Improves user confidence in UPI-based digital payments.
•	Generates easy-to-understand safety scores for transactions.
•	Continuously learns from new transaction patterns and fraud cases.
•	Supports secure and reliable growth of digital payment ecosystems.
