title: CONTEXT-AWARE INFRASTRUCTURE-TO-VEHICLE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION SYSTEM WITH SELF-DIAGNOSTIC SAFETY EVALUATION
abstract: A context-aware infrastructure-to-vehicle communication system is disclosed for improving transportation safety through continuous infrastructure health monitoring and intelligent vehicle-specific safety evaluation. The system comprises an Infrastructure Monitoring System configured to acquire structural parameters of transportation infrastructure, a Roadside Unit configured to determine an Infrastructure Health Percentage and broadcast infrastructure health information through a Universal Optical Broadcast protocol, and a Vehicle Unit configured to receive the transmitted information and perform context-aware evaluation using real-time vehicle operating parameters. The Roadside Unit incorporates an optical backscatter sensing mechanism for determining a Contamination Index and one or more piezoelectric actuators configured to autonomously clean an optical transmission window, thereby maintaining communication reliability. A redundant radio frequency communication subsystem provides uninterrupted transmission during optical communication failure. A Smart Evaluation and Contextual Modulation algorithm determines a Safety Margin and generates individualized vehicle safety responses, thereby improving infrastructure management, communication reliability, and road safety.
specification:
The present invention provides a context-aware infrastructure-to-vehicle communication system and method for real-time structural health monitoring and intelligent safety management of transportation infrastructure. The invention integrates continuous infrastructure condition monitoring, Universal Optical Broadcast-based communication, autonomous self-diagnostic and self-cleaning of the optical communication subsystem, and vehicle-specific context-aware safety evaluation to facilitate reliable dissemination of infrastructure health information and generation of appropriate safety responses for approaching vehicles. The invention will now be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings and exemplary embodiments, which are illustrative in nature and are not intended to limit the scope of the invention.
In an embodiment, the system comprises an Infrastructure Monitoring System (IMS), a Roadside Unit (RSU), a Vehicle Unit (VU), a communication network, and a context-aware evaluation mechanism configured to generate vehicle-specific safety instructions. The Infrastructure Monitoring System continuously monitors structural characteristics of the infrastructure, the Roadside Unit processes and broadcasts infrastructure health information, the Vehicle Unit receives and interprets the transmitted information together with vehicle operating parameters, and the context-aware evaluation mechanism determines an appropriate safety response according to the instantaneous condition of both the infrastructure and the vehicle. 
In an embodiment, the Infrastructure Monitoring System forms the sensing layer of the overall architecture and continuously acquires structural parameters from one or more sensors installed on the infrastructure. The monitored parameters include, but are not limited to, structural strain, displacement, vibration characteristics, inclination, settlement, stiffness, deformation, dynamic response, fatigue-related parameters, and other indicators representing the structural condition of the monitored asset. The Infrastructure Monitoring System may comprise one or more strain gauges, accelerometers, displacement sensors, vibration sensors, fiber optic sensors, tilt sensors, load sensors, environmental sensors, or equivalent sensing devices depending upon the infrastructure under observation. The present invention is independent of the particular sensing technology employed, provided that structural condition data is continuously available for processing. 
In another embodiment, the Infrastructure Monitoring System continuously transmits the acquired structural information to the Roadside Unit through a secure wired or wireless communication interface. The communication interface may employ Ethernet, serial communication, optical communication, industrial communication protocols, or any equivalent data transfer mechanism suitable for reliable exchange of infrastructure health information. The Infrastructure Monitoring System therefore functions as a data acquisition platform, whereas the computational intelligence associated with infrastructure-to-vehicle communication is implemented within the Roadside Unit.
In an embodiment, the Roadside Unit receives the structural parameters from the Infrastructure Monitoring System and performs computational processing to determine the structural condition of the monitored infrastructure. The received measurements are compared with corresponding reference values established during commissioning or obtained from baseline structural characteristics. Based on the comparison, the Roadside Unit determines a normalized Infrastructure Health Percentage (HP) or Health Index representing the current structural condition of the infrastructure. The Health Percentage provides a quantitative representation of structural integrity that may continuously vary according to changes in structural behaviour, thereby enabling real-time assessment of infrastructure degradation and fatigue progression. 
In an embodiment, the computed Health Percentage is further classified into predetermined structural health categories representing different operational conditions of the infrastructure. The structural health categories may comprise an excellent condition, a satisfactory condition, a degraded condition, and a critical condition corresponding to predefined Health Percentage ranges. Such classification enables simplified interpretation of infrastructure health while supporting rapid communication of safety information to approaching vehicles. The classification thresholds may be modified according to infrastructure type, operational requirements, regulatory guidelines, environmental conditions, or maintenance policies without departing from the scope of the invention. 
In another embodiment, the Roadside Unit converts the computed Health Percentage into a structured infrastructure safety message. The infrastructure safety message includes the calculated Health Percentage together with associated structural hazard information, infrastructure identification information, zone identification, time information, integrity verification data, and other communication parameters necessary for reliable transmission. The infrastructure safety message is subsequently encoded into a transmission format suitable for optical broadcasting using a Universal Optical Broadcast protocol.
Unlike conventional infrastructure communication systems requiring establishment of individual communication sessions with every approaching vehicle, the present invention employs a stateless Universal Optical Broadcast protocol in which the Roadside Unit continuously broadcasts infrastructure health information throughout its coverage region. Since the communication remains independent of individual vehicle addressing and session establishment, communication latency is substantially reduced while communication scalability is significantly improved under dense traffic conditions. The broadcast architecture enables simultaneous dissemination of identical infrastructure health information to multiple vehicles without increasing computational load on the Roadside Unit or generating communication congestion typically associated with conventional RF-based communication systems. 
In an embodiment of the present invention, the Roadside Unit further comprises an optical communication subsystem configured to transmit infrastructure health information to approaching vehicles using a Universal Optical Broadcast (UOB) protocol. The optical communication subsystem comprises one or more infrared emitters, an optical transmission window, a signal encoding module, a modulation controller, an optical monitoring arrangement, a self-diagnostic module, and a communication controller operatively coupled to the processing unit. The processing unit converts the computed Infrastructure Health Percentage and associated infrastructure status information into a modulated optical signal suitable for transmission through the infrared emitters. The optical communication subsystem operates as the primary infrastructure-to-vehicle communication channel and continuously broadcasts infrastructure information throughout the defined coverage region without establishing individual communication sessions with approaching vehicles. This stateless communication architecture substantially minimizes communication latency while permitting simultaneous communication with multiple vehicles irrespective of traffic density. 
In an embodiment, the Roadside Unit employs one or more infrared light emitting devices operating within the near infrared wavelength range to generate a directional optical communication beam. The transmitted optical signal is modulated according to a predefined communication protocol such that infrastructure health information, hazard information, infrastructure identification, zone identification, integrity verification information and synchronization information are encoded into the optical transmission. The modulation scheme enables reliable reception of the transmitted signal while substantially reducing susceptibility to ambient light, electromagnetic interference, spectrum congestion and radio frequency collisions. The optical transmission therefore provides a dedicated communication channel for safety-critical infrastructure information while remaining independent of conventional radio frequency communication networks. 
In another embodiment, the Universal Optical Broadcast protocol continuously transmits infrastructure health information at predetermined transmission intervals irrespective of the number of vehicles present within the communication zone. Since the transmitted information is universally broadcast rather than individually addressed, additional vehicles entering the communication region do not increase computational overhead or communication delay at the Roadside Unit. The same infrastructure health information is therefore simultaneously available to all approaching vehicles, wherein subsequent interpretation and safety evaluation are performed locally within the respective Vehicle Units according to their individual operating conditions. This distributed decision-making architecture significantly improves communication scalability while reducing processing requirements at the infrastructure side. 
In an embodiment of the present invention, reliable operation of the optical communication subsystem is maintained through an autonomous self-diagnostic mechanism configured to continuously monitor the optical transmission path. Since contamination of the optical transmission window by dust, mud, rainwater, insects, oil deposits or other environmental contaminants may reduce transmission efficiency, the Roadside Unit continuously evaluates the condition of the optical transmission window and initiates corrective action whenever deterioration of optical performance is detected. The self-diagnostic mechanism therefore enables long-term autonomous operation with substantially reduced dependence upon manual inspection and maintenance. 
In an embodiment, the self-diagnostic mechanism employs an optical backscatter sensing arrangement positioned within the Roadside Unit enclosure. The optical backscatter sensing arrangement comprises a diagnostic optical sensor disposed adjacent to the infrared emitter and configured to detect infrared radiation reflected from the inner surface of the optical transmission window. Under normal operating conditions, a clean optical window permits transmission of the majority of emitted infrared energy with minimal internal reflection. However, accumulation of contaminants upon the external surface of the optical window causes scattering and reflection of a portion of the emitted infrared radiation back toward the diagnostic optical sensor. The detected reflected optical energy is continuously monitored by the processing unit to determine the optical condition of the transmission window. 
In another embodiment, the processing unit computes a Contamination Index (CI) representative of the degree of optical contamination present on the transmission window. The Contamination Index is determined by comparing one or more optical feedback parameters obtained from the diagnostic sensor with corresponding reference values established during system calibration. The Contamination Index therefore represents the optical transmission efficiency of the communication subsystem and provides a quantitative indication of contamination severity. The processing unit continuously updates the Contamination Index during operation, thereby enabling real-time assessment of optical communication quality. 
In an embodiment, the processing unit compares the calculated Contamination Index with one or more predetermined threshold values to determine an appropriate corrective action. When the Contamination Index exceeds a first threshold corresponding to minor contamination, the Roadside Unit increases optical transmission intensity to compensate for moderate signal attenuation while continuing normal communication. When the Contamination Index exceeds a second threshold corresponding to significant contamination, the processing unit activates an autonomous cleaning mechanism configured to restore optical transmission efficiency. Such multi-level response enables reliable communication while minimizing unnecessary cleaning cycles and reducing overall energy consumption. 
In another embodiment of the present invention, the autonomous cleaning mechanism comprises one or more piezoelectric actuators mechanically coupled to the optical transmission window. The piezoelectric actuators are configured to generate ultrasonic mechanical vibrations that propagate across the optical surface for removal of accumulated contaminants. The ultrasonic vibration produces atomization of liquid contaminants including rainwater, condensed moisture and water droplets while simultaneously generating sufficient mechanical excitation to dislodge solid contaminants including dust particles, mud deposits and other foreign materials adhering to the optical surface. Consequently, the optical transmission window is restored to an operational condition without requiring manual cleaning. 
In an embodiment, the autonomous cleaning mechanism further comprises a resonance controller and a driver circuit configured to excite the piezoelectric actuator substantially at its resonant operating frequency. The resonance controller continuously monitors the dynamic response of the optical assembly and adjusts the excitation frequency to maintain efficient transfer of vibrational energy to the optical window. Maintaining resonance substantially improves contaminant removal efficiency while reducing electrical power consumption and mechanical stress upon the optical assembly. Accordingly, the cleaning mechanism remains effective under varying environmental conditions and contamination levels. 
In another embodiment, completion of the cleaning cycle is followed by re-evaluation of the optical transmission path through the optical backscatter sensing arrangement. The processing unit recalculates the Contamination Index and determines whether the optical transmission quality has been restored. If the recalculated Contamination Index falls below the predefined operating threshold, normal optical communication resumes. Conversely, if the Contamination Index continues to indicate unacceptable optical degradation after one or more cleaning cycles, the Roadside Unit identifies the existence of persistent optical obstruction or component malfunction and initiates an alternative communication mode. This closed-loop self-diagnostic architecture enables continuous monitoring, autonomous maintenance and verification of communication integrity throughout system operation. 
In an embodiment, the Roadside Unit further comprises a redundant radio frequency communication module configured to operate as a fail-safe communication channel. Upon detection of prolonged optical communication failure, persistent contamination, adverse weather conditions, obstruction of the optical transmission path or malfunction of the optical communication subsystem, the processing unit automatically transfers safety-critical infrastructure information to the radio frequency communication module. The radio frequency communication module thereafter broadcasts high-priority infrastructure alerts to approaching vehicles until satisfactory restoration of optical communication is achieved. The automatic transition between optical communication and radio frequency communication ensures uninterrupted delivery of safety-related information while maintaining operational reliability under adverse environmental conditions. 
In an embodiment of the present invention, the system further comprises a Vehicle Unit (VU) configured to receive infrastructure health information transmitted by the Roadside Unit and to generate vehicle-specific safety decisions based on the received infrastructure information together with the instantaneous operating condition of the vehicle. The Vehicle Unit functions as an intelligent edge-processing platform capable of locally interpreting infrastructure health information without requiring continuous communication with a centralized processing server. Consequently, each vehicle independently determines an appropriate safety response while utilizing a common infrastructure broadcast transmitted by the Roadside Unit. 
In an embodiment, the Vehicle Unit is mounted at a suitable location on the vehicle to provide an unobstructed optical reception path toward the Roadside Unit. The Vehicle Unit comprises an optical receiving module, a communication interface, a processing unit, a vehicle data acquisition module, a context-aware evaluation module, a memory, an alert generation module, and one or more human-machine interface devices. The optical receiving module continuously monitors the optical communication channel for incoming infrastructure health messages transmitted by the Roadside Unit.
In an embodiment, the optical receiving module comprises one or more infrared receiving elements configured to detect the modulated optical signal transmitted through the Universal Optical Broadcast protocol. The received optical signal is converted into corresponding electrical signals, conditioned to suppress environmental noise and unwanted interference, and supplied to the processing unit for demodulation and decoding. The processing unit extracts infrastructure-related information including the Infrastructure Health Percentage, structural hazard information, infrastructure identification, communication integrity information, and associated metadata required for subsequent safety evaluation. 
In another embodiment, the Vehicle Unit continuously evaluates the quality of the received communication signal prior to utilizing the received information for safety analysis. The processing unit determines one or more communication quality parameters representing reception reliability, signal strength, transmission integrity, packet validity and communication confidence. The communication quality parameters enable the Vehicle Unit to distinguish valid infrastructure information from corrupted or incomplete transmissions, thereby improving reliability of subsequent decision making. When optical communication quality satisfies predetermined acceptance criteria, the received optical data is accepted for context-aware evaluation. Conversely, when optical communication quality deteriorates below acceptable limits, the Vehicle Unit automatically switches to the redundant radio frequency communication channel for continued reception of infrastructure information. 
In an embodiment, the Vehicle Unit further comprises a vehicle communication interface configured to acquire real-time operating parameters from one or more electronic systems within the vehicle. The communication interface is operatively connected to a Controller Area Network (CAN) bus, On-Board Diagnostic interface, vehicle electronic control units, or equivalent communication network capable of providing operational information associated with the vehicle. Through the communication interface, the Vehicle Unit continuously receives vehicle operating parameters including vehicle velocity, vehicle mass, axle configuration, axle loading, braking characteristics, braking efficiency, engine operating condition, and other dynamic parameters representing the current operating state of the vehicle. 
In another embodiment, vehicle-specific information including vehicle classification, permissible loading capacity, or measured vehicle mass may additionally be obtained from toll infrastructure, weigh-in-motion systems, fleet management systems or equivalent external information sources. Such information may be periodically synchronized with the Vehicle Unit and combined with real-time vehicle operating parameters to improve the accuracy of context-aware safety evaluation. Since vehicle characteristics remain available locally within the Vehicle Unit, sensitive operational information need not be transmitted back to the infrastructure, thereby preserving privacy while reducing communication bandwidth requirements. 
In an embodiment of the present invention, the processing unit executes a Smart Evaluation and Contextual Modulation (SECM) algorithm configured to evaluate infrastructure health in relation to the instantaneous operating condition of the receiving vehicle. Unlike conventional infrastructure warning systems that generate identical alerts for all vehicles, the SECM algorithm performs individualized safety analysis by jointly considering infrastructure condition and vehicle dynamics before generating a safety decision. Consequently, vehicles having different masses, speeds, braking capabilities or loading conditions may receive different operational instructions despite receiving the same infrastructure health information. 
In an embodiment, the SECM algorithm determines the stopping capability of the vehicle using one or more operating parameters including vehicle speed, braking efficiency, reaction time, road friction characteristics, vehicle loading condition, and gravitational effects. Simultaneously, the algorithm determines a safe traversable distance corresponding to the current structural condition of the monitored infrastructure based upon the Infrastructure Health Percentage received from the Roadside Unit. The algorithm subsequently compares the vehicle stopping capability with the permissible traversable distance to determine whether the vehicle can safely negotiate the monitored infrastructure under its present operating condition. 
In another embodiment, the processing unit computes a Safety Margin representing the relationship between infrastructure capability and vehicle operating capability. The Safety Margin is continuously updated as vehicle speed, loading condition, braking performance and infrastructure health change during vehicle movement. A positive Safety Margin indicates that the vehicle can safely traverse the infrastructure under prevailing operating conditions, whereas a Safety Margin approaching zero indicates a boundary operating condition requiring increased caution. A negative Safety Margin indicates that the vehicle is unlikely to safely negotiate the monitored infrastructure without corrective action, thereby requiring immediate intervention. The continuously varying Safety Margin therefore enables dynamic risk evaluation rather than reliance upon fixed threshold warnings. 
In an embodiment, the Vehicle Unit generates a proportional safety response according to the calculated Safety Margin. When the calculated Safety Margin indicates satisfactory operating conditions, the Vehicle Unit provides a normal operating indication permitting continued vehicle movement. When the calculated Safety Margin approaches a cautionary region, the Vehicle Unit generates one or more visual, audible or tactile warnings advising the driver to reduce vehicle speed or exercise increased caution. When the calculated Safety Margin indicates an unsafe operating condition, the Vehicle Unit generates a critical warning and may initiate one or more vehicle intervention measures including speed limitation, torque reduction, braking assistance, autonomous braking or equivalent protective actions through the vehicle electronic control system. The generated response therefore remains proportional to the actual risk associated with the combined infrastructure and vehicle operating conditions rather than depending solely upon infrastructure health. 
In another embodiment, the alert generation module comprises one or more display devices, audible warning devices, visual indicators, tactile feedback devices or combinations thereof for communicating safety information to the vehicle operator. The alert generation module may further interface with one or more advanced driver assistance systems or autonomous driving systems to facilitate automated implementation of the recommended safety action. Accordingly, the Vehicle Unit not only informs the driver regarding infrastructure condition but also supports timely execution of appropriate safety measures according to the prevailing operating environment. 
In an embodiment, the context-aware evaluation mechanism ensures that infrastructure information received from the Roadside Unit is interpreted independently by every receiving vehicle according to its own operating characteristics. For example, a lightly loaded passenger vehicle travelling at a moderate speed may safely traverse a bridge having a moderate Infrastructure Health Percentage, whereas a heavily loaded commercial vehicle travelling at a higher speed may receive a cautionary or critical instruction for the same bridge. Similarly, vehicles approaching the infrastructure under adverse road conditions or reduced braking capability may receive more conservative safety instructions than vehicles operating under favourable conditions. Consequently, the invention eliminates the limitations of conventional uniform warning systems by providing individualized safety recommendations derived from real-time infrastructure condition and real-time vehicle dynamics. 
In an embodiment of the present invention, the context-aware infrastructure-to-vehicle communication system operates through a coordinated sequence of infrastructure health acquisition, infrastructure health evaluation, optical communication, vehicle-specific interpretation, and safety response generation. The coordinated operation enables continuous monitoring of structural health while simultaneously providing approaching vehicles with real-time infrastructure information for dynamic safety assessment. The entire operational sequence is performed substantially in real time, thereby enabling predictive infrastructure health management and reducing the likelihood of accidents caused by undetected structural deterioration. 
In an embodiment, the operational sequence commences with continuous acquisition of structural parameters by the Infrastructure Monitoring System installed on the monitored infrastructure. The Infrastructure Monitoring System continuously measures one or more structural characteristics including strain, vibration, displacement, inclination, stiffness, deformation, fatigue behaviour, settlement, and equivalent structural parameters indicative of infrastructure condition. The measured parameters are processed to determine the structural condition of the infrastructure and are subsequently transmitted to the Roadside Unit through a communication interface for further processing. The Roadside Unit therefore receives updated structural information throughout the operational life of the infrastructure, thereby enabling continuous monitoring rather than periodic manual inspection. 
In another embodiment, the Roadside Unit processes the received structural information to determine a normalized Infrastructure Health Percentage representative of the present structural condition of the monitored infrastructure. The Health Percentage may further be categorized into predefined structural health classes to simplify interpretation of infrastructure condition while supporting rapid dissemination of safety information. Following computation of the Health Percentage, the Roadside Unit prepares an infrastructure communication frame comprising infrastructure identification information, infrastructure health information, hazard classification, communication synchronization information, message integrity information, and additional communication parameters required for reliable transmission. 
In an embodiment, the prepared communication frame is encoded and continuously transmitted through the Universal Optical Broadcast protocol using the optical communication subsystem. Since the Universal Optical Broadcast protocol operates in a stateless broadcast configuration, the Roadside Unit transmits the same infrastructure health information to every vehicle present within the communication region without establishing dedicated communication sessions. The transmitted information therefore remains available simultaneously to multiple vehicles while substantially reducing communication latency and computational overhead. 
Simultaneously with optical transmission, the Roadside Unit continuously evaluates the operational condition of the optical communication subsystem through the self-diagnostic mechanism. The optical backscatter sensing arrangement periodically determines the Contamination Index by monitoring optical feedback generated from the transmission window. When the calculated Contamination Index exceeds a predefined threshold corresponding to contamination of the optical surface, the processing unit activates the piezoelectric cleaning mechanism to restore optical transmission efficiency. Following completion of the cleaning operation, the Roadside Unit again determines the Contamination Index to verify restoration of normal communication quality. This closed-loop operational methodology enables autonomous maintenance of the communication subsystem without interruption of system operation. 
In another embodiment, when repeated cleaning operations fail to restore satisfactory optical communication quality or when environmental conditions prevent reliable optical transmission, the Roadside Unit automatically transfers safety-critical infrastructure information to the redundant radio frequency communication subsystem. The redundant communication subsystem thereafter transmits critical infrastructure alerts until restoration of normal optical communication. Consequently, uninterrupted delivery of infrastructure safety information is maintained even under adverse environmental conditions including heavy rainfall, dense fog, dust storms, optical obstruction or partial failure of the optical communication subsystem. 
In an embodiment, the Vehicle Unit continuously monitors both the optical communication channel and the redundant radio frequency communication channel for incoming infrastructure information. Upon successful reception of a communication frame, the Vehicle Unit verifies message integrity and communication quality prior to processing the received information. The Vehicle Unit further acquires real-time vehicle operating parameters from the Controller Area Network interface and combines the infrastructure information with the vehicle operating information to perform context-aware safety evaluation. Such localized processing enables every vehicle to independently determine its own operational safety without transmitting confidential vehicle information to the infrastructure. 
In another embodiment, the Smart Evaluation and Contextual Modulation algorithm computes a Safety Margin by evaluating infrastructure health together with vehicle-specific operating parameters including vehicle mass, velocity, braking capability, load distribution, reaction characteristics and prevailing road conditions. Based upon the calculated Safety Margin, the Vehicle Unit determines whether the vehicle may safely traverse the monitored infrastructure, whether cautionary action is required, or whether immediate intervention should be initiated. Since identical infrastructure information may result in different Safety Margin values for different vehicles, individualized safety decisions are generated without increasing computational requirements at the Roadside Unit. 
In an embodiment, the generated safety response is communicated to the vehicle operator through one or more visual, audible or tactile indications. Where vehicle automation systems are available, the Vehicle Unit may additionally communicate with one or more vehicle control modules to facilitate implementation of protective measures including speed reduction, engine torque limitation, braking assistance or autonomous emergency braking according to the severity of the calculated Safety Margin. Consequently, the invention enables proactive implementation of safety measures before the vehicle enters a structurally compromised region. 
In another embodiment, the communication protocol further incorporates synchronization, integrity verification and message authentication mechanisms to improve reliability of infrastructure communication. Each transmitted communication frame may include infrastructure identification information, zone identification, timing information, checksum information, cyclic redundancy verification information, cryptographic signatures, authentication data or combinations thereof to prevent message corruption, replay attacks, spoofing and unauthorized modification of transmitted infrastructure information. The Vehicle Unit validates the received communication frame prior to executing any safety-related action, thereby ensuring that vehicle responses are generated only from authenticated infrastructure information. 
In an embodiment, the invention further supports integration with intelligent transportation infrastructure including toll collection systems, traffic management systems, fleet management systems, bridge management systems, digital infrastructure management platforms and other intelligent transportation networks. Information relating to vehicle classification, permissible loading, traffic density, infrastructure identification or operational history may be exchanged with such systems to further improve the accuracy of context-aware infrastructure evaluation while maintaining compatibility with existing transportation infrastructure. 
In another embodiment, the invention is not limited to bridges and may be deployed on highways, tunnels, flyovers, elevated corridors, railway crossings, dams, industrial structures, airport pavements, port facilities or any civil infrastructure requiring continuous structural health monitoring and real-time communication with approaching vehicles. Similarly, the optical communication subsystem may employ equivalent optical transmitters, optical receivers, modulation techniques, communication protocols or processing architectures without departing from the scope of the present invention, provided that infrastructure health information is communicated through a context-aware infrastructure-to-vehicle communication framework incorporating autonomous communication integrity monitoring and vehicle-specific safety evaluation. 
In an embodiment, the integration of continuous infrastructure monitoring, Universal Optical Broadcast communication, autonomous contamination detection, piezoelectric self-cleaning, redundant radio frequency communication, context-aware vehicle evaluation, localized edge processing and intelligent safety response generation provides an integrated infrastructure management platform capable of simultaneously improving infrastructure reliability, communication robustness, vehicular safety and long-term structural fatigue management. The coordinated interaction of these functional modules enables predictive infrastructure monitoring while providing individualized safety recommendations to approaching vehicles according to both infrastructure condition and vehicle operating characteristics, thereby overcoming the limitations associated with conventional infrastructure monitoring systems and uniform vehicle warning mechanisms.

title: WEARABLE-BASED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR PERSONALIZED ADAPTIVE YOGA TRAINING USING TRANSFER LEARNING
abstract: The present invention discloses a wearable-based artificial intelligence system (100) for personalized and adaptive yoga training. The system (100) comprises an articulated mannequin (101a–101d, 102a–102d) representing a user fitted with wearable IMU sensor modules (103, 104), a sensor hub/control unit (105a, 106a) including communication interfaces (105b, 106b) and a controller (107, 108), a real-time posture analysis display (109), a haptic feedback displays (110), and yoga mats (111a, 111b). Biomechanical and motion data captured by the wearable sensors are processed using a transfer learning-based artificial intelligence engine to generate a personalized biomechanical model through few-shot calibration. The controller (107, 108) dynamically adjusts posture evaluation thresholds, correction sensitivity, and feedback parameters based on anatomical characteristics and historical performance, while continuously refining guidance through longitudinal learning memory to deliver adaptive visual, audio, and haptic feedback for safe, accurate, and personalized yoga training across wellness, rehabilitation, and preventive healthcare applications.

[0028] The present invention relates to a wearable-based artificial intelligence (AI) system for personalized and adaptive yoga training that addresses the limitations of conventional yoga guidance platforms relying on generalized posture evaluation models and static correction mechanisms. Existing yoga training systems typically evaluate all users using the same predefined posture standards without considering individual 5 anatomical differences, flexibility levels, age, physical capability, or long-term progression. Such approaches often lead to inaccurate posture assessment, excessive corrections, reduced user engagement, and an increased risk of discomfort or injury, particularly for beginners, elderly individuals, and users undergoing rehabilitation. The present invention overcomes these limitations by introducing an intelligent, self-evolving, user-centric yoga 10 training system that continuously adapts to the unique biomechanical characteristics of each individual. By integrating wearable sensing technology, artificial intelligence, transfer learning, few-shot learning, longitudinal learning memory, adaptive feedback mechanisms, and safety-aware posture correction, the invention provides highly personalized real-time guidance that evolves with the user's physical development over time. 15
[0029] The invention comprises a comprehensive architecture including a wearable sensor assembly, a data acquisition and pre-processing module, an AI-based personalization and learning engine, a longitudinal learning memory, an adaptive feedback module, and a user interface operating through a smartphone, tablet, or cloud-connected computing device. The wearable sensor assembly is configured to be positioned on 20 strategic body locations such as the wrists, ankles, torso, waist, or combinations thereof. Each wearable module includes one or more inertial measurement units (IMUs) comprising accelerometers, gyroscopes, and optionally magnetometers for capturing detailed biomechanical and physiological information during yoga practice. These sensors continuously measure linear acceleration, angular velocity, body orientation, joint 25 movement, posture alignment, balance stability, motion smoothness, and movement dynamics. The wearable device further incorporates a microcontroller unit responsible for performing initial signal conditioning, local filtering, synchronization, and pre-processing of sensor data before transmission. A wireless communication module utilizing Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or equivalent communication protocols securely transmits the processed data to a 30 connected processing unit. The wearable device is powered by a rechargeable battery supported by power management circuitry that optimizes energy consumption to ensure prolonged operation during extended yoga sessions.
9
[0030] During operation, the wearable sensors continuously acquire real-time biomechanical data while the user performs yoga postures. The collected raw sensor signals are transmitted to the data acquisition and pre-processing module, where multiple pre-processing operations are executed. These operations include noise removal, signal normalization, timestamp synchronization, and correction of sensor drift to improve 5 measurement accuracy. Sensor fusion algorithms combine information from multiple wearable devices to reconstruct an accurate representation of the user's posture, joint positions, body orientation, and movement trajectory. This comprehensive biomechanical model provides significantly higher accuracy than conventional single-camera or single-sensor systems and maintains reliable posture estimation even under varying environmental 10 conditions, different lighting scenarios, or partial body occlusions. The processed biomechanical information is subsequently supplied to the AI software layer for posture analysis and personalized decision-making.
[0031] A significant feature of the invention is the implementation of an initial calibration phase based on few-shot learning. Unlike conventional AI systems that require 15 extensive user-specific datasets or prolonged training periods before delivering personalized guidance, the present invention achieves rapid personalization through a short calibration session requiring only a limited number of representative yoga postures. During this calibration stage, the AI system extracts individual biomechanical characteristics including joint range of motion, flexibility limits, balance stability, posture alignment 20 capability, movement smoothness, and other user-specific physiological parameters. Using few-shot learning algorithms, these limited calibration samples are sufficient to generate an individualized biomechanical baseline model that accurately represents the physical capabilities and movement characteristics of the user. Consequently, the system eliminates the need for long-term data collection or complete model retraining while enabling 25 immediate deployment of personalized yoga guidance from the very first training session.
[0032] The AI personalization engine represents the computational core of the invention and introduces a transfer learning-based personalization framework that distinguishes the present system from conventional yoga training technologies. Initially, the AI engine utilizes a pre-trained population-level yoga model developed from large and 30 diverse datasets representing users with varying physical characteristics, experience levels, and movement patterns. Rather than retraining the entire AI model for each individual, the invention selectively fine-tunes only the parameters directly associated with user-specific
10
posture evaluation, alignment thresholds, correction sensitivity, motion smoothness expectations, and flexibility constraints. This selective transfer learning approach significantly reduces computational complexity while enabling rapid adaptation to individual users. The resulting personalized biomechanical model continuously reflects the user's anatomy, flexibility, physical limitations, and skill level, thereby providing highly 5 accurate posture evaluation with substantially lower computational requirements than existing systems.
[0033] During every yoga session, the personalized AI engine continuously compares incoming biomechanical data with the individualized baseline model instead of generic posture templates. A major technical advancement introduced by the invention is 10 the implementation of adaptive error tolerance and safety-aware posture correction logic. Existing yoga guidance systems generally employ fixed posture thresholds that classify body alignment as either correct or incorrect regardless of the user's physical condition. In contrast, the present invention dynamically adjusts acceptable posture deviation margins according to multiple user-specific factors including age, physical capability, flexibility, 15 balance, rehabilitation status, experience level, and historical performance. Beginners and elderly users receive broader tolerance margins together with gentle corrective guidance that prioritizes comfort and injury prevention, whereas advanced practitioners receive narrower tolerance ranges with precision-oriented posture optimization. Furthermore, the system dynamically modifies correction sensitivity, correction frequency, and feedback 20 intensity according to posture criticality and user responsiveness. This adaptive safety mechanism prevents unnecessary overcorrection, minimizes physical strain, reduces injury risk, and creates a more supportive and natural learning environment.
[0034] Another important aspect of the invention is the incorporation of a longitudinal learning memory that enables continuous personalization throughout the user's 25 yoga journey. Unlike existing systems that evaluate each yoga session independently, the present invention persistently stores historical information associated with every training session, including posture accuracy, flexibility improvements, balance progression, recurring biomechanical errors, movement consistency, fatigue indicators, correction history, and overall performance trends. This historical database allows the AI engine to 30 evaluate current performance relative to the individual's own previous sessions rather than comparing the user against generalized population standards. As a result, the system progressively refines posture evaluation criteria, challenge levels, correction timing, and
11
personalized recommendations based on continuous learning from accumulated historical data. The longitudinal learning memory transforms the AI system into a self-evolving digital yoga coach capable of adapting naturally alongside the user's physical progress.
[0035] The invention further introduces a self-evolving AI guidance framework in which personalization parameters are automatically updated following every yoga session 5 without requiring manual intervention or complete retraining. The AI engine incrementally adjusts posture alignment thresholds, flexibility expectations, correction timing, movement smoothness criteria, balance sensitivity, and difficulty progression according to the user's observed improvements or limitations. This continuous adaptive learning mechanism ensures that guidance remains relevant throughout the user's development, allowing the 10 system to provide increasingly sophisticated recommendations as physical capability improves. Such progressive adaptation enables long-term personalization while maintaining computational efficiency and scalability for deployment across diverse user populations.
[0036] To facilitate intuitive interaction, the invention incorporates a multi-modal 15 adaptive feedback engine capable of delivering personalized real-time guidance through multiple communication channels. Based on posture evaluation results, the system generates corrective feedback using visual cues displayed on a mobile device, audio prompts communicated through speakers or headphones, and optional haptic signals transmitted through the wearable sensors. The selection of feedback modality, timing, 20 intensity, and frequency is dynamically determined according to user responsiveness, posture criticality, learning preferences, and session context. Critical posture deviations requiring immediate correction may trigger stronger or multimodal alerts, whereas minor deviations receive subtle guidance that preserves the natural flow of yoga practice. By adapting both the content and presentation of feedback, the invention improves learning 25 efficiency, user engagement, motivation, and long-term adherence to yoga training while avoiding information overload.
[0037] The invention also incorporates progression-aware challenge optimization that automatically adjusts training complexity according to user development. As the longitudinal learning memory identifies improvements in posture accuracy, flexibility, 30 stability, and movement control, the AI engine gradually introduces stricter alignment expectations, more advanced yoga postures, and higher precision feedback. Conversely, users requiring rehabilitation or possessing limited mobility continue receiving
12
conservative guidance tailored to their physical capabilities. This automated progression management enables individualized skill development without requiring instructor intervention and ensures that each user's training remains appropriately challenging while preserving safety.
[0038] The software-hardware interaction begins with wearable sensors acquiring 5 biomechanical motion data, followed by wireless transmission to the processing unit. The pre-processing module performs filtering, normalization, synchronization, and sensor fusion before forwarding the processed information to the AI personalization engine. The AI engine evaluates posture using the personalized biomechanical model generated through transfer learning and few-shot calibration while referencing historical information stored 10 within the longitudinal learning memory. Based on posture analysis, adaptive error tolerance logic determines appropriate correction strategies, and the adaptive feedback module generates personalized visual, audio, or haptic guidance. Finally, updated session data, including posture performance, flexibility changes, recurring errors, fatigue indicators, and user progress, are stored within the longitudinal learning memory to further 15 refine future personalization.
[0039] The present invention provides a comprehensive wearable-based AI system that integrates wearable sensor fusion, few-shot learning, transfer learning, adaptive safety-aware posture evaluation, longitudinal learning memory, self-evolving personalization, progression-aware challenge optimization, and multi-modal feedback within a unified 20 architecture. The invention departs significantly from conventional static yoga guidance technologies by creating a continuously learning, user-specific training platform capable of evolving with individual users over extended periods. The combination of rapid personalization, computationally efficient transfer learning, adaptive posture correction, continuous historical learning, and context-aware feedback substantially enhances posture 25 evaluation accuracy, user safety, training effectiveness, and long-term engagement. Owing to its flexible architecture and adaptive intelligence, the invention has broad applicability in personalized yoga training, rehabilitation therapy, elderly wellness, preventive healthcare, digital fitness, remote physiotherapy, and AI-assisted health monitoring, thereby representing a significant technological advancement in intelligent wearable health and 30 wellness systems. ,

title: RESOURCE-EFFICIENT EDGE COMPUTING APPARATUS FOR PEDIATRIC MULTI-SOURCE DATA ACQUISITION AND RISK STRATIFICATION
abstract: The present invention relates to a resource-efficient edge computing apparatus for pediatric multi-source data acquisition and risk stratification. The apparatus comprises a plurality of networked data-acquisition terminals configured to collect heterogeneous assessment data and an edge computing unit including an adaptive data orchestration engine, a feature processing engine, a compressed model repository, a parallel inference engine, an aggregation module, a classification module, a secure communication gateway, and a tamper-evident audit storage module. The apparatus performs resource-efficient local processing to generate a non-diagnostic risk stratification record while minimizing bandwidth utilization, processing latency, and memory consumption under constrained computing and intermittent network conditions. The architecture supports secure local data processing, privacy-preserving communication, reliable handling of partial multi-source inputs, and scalable deployment on low-cost edge hardware. The generated risk stratification output facilitates workflow prioritization for review by qualified healthcare professionals without constituting a clinical diagnosis.
specification:
The present invention relates to a resource-efficient edge computing apparatus for pediatric multi-source data acquisition and risk stratification. The disclosed apparatus is configured to acquire heterogeneous assessment data from a plurality of distributed data-acquisition terminals, perform localized edge-based processing, and generate a non-diagnostic risk stratification record for workflow prioritization. The apparatus is particularly suitable for deployment in pediatric healthcare facilities, educational institutions, community health centres, rural screening programmes, and geographically distributed environments operating under limited computational resources and intermittent network connectivity.
[0023]		The apparatus (100) comprises a plurality of networked data-acquisition terminals (110) configured to collect assessment information from multiple independent sources including children, parents, guardians, teachers, counsellors, healthcare professionals, or other authorized personnel. The networked data-acquisition terminals (110) may comprise desktop computers, laptop computers, tablet devices, smartphones, kiosks, embedded terminals, or other electronic computing devices capable of acquiring structured or semi-structured assessment information. The terminals are configured to operate in online, offline, or intermittent communication environments and may temporarily store acquired information until communication with an edge inference appliance (120) becomes available.
[0024]		The edge inference appliance (120) is deployed locally within a school, healthcare facility, community centre, or regional screening location and comprises one or more hardware processors, system memory, non-transitory storage devices, communication interfaces, and optionally hardware acceleration resources including neural processing units (NPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), tensor accelerators, field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), or equivalent processing hardware configured for resource-efficient execution of computational tasks.
[0025]		The edge inference appliance (120) first invokes an adaptive orchestration engine (122) upon receiving assessment information from the networked data-acquisition terminals (110). The adaptive orchestration engine (122) coordinates data acquisition by dynamically selecting only context-appropriate assessment subsets according to predefined configuration parameters, user category, developmental stage, operational policies, or previously acquired responses. By serving only the required assessment subset, the adaptive orchestration engine minimizes unnecessary data acquisition, reduces communication bandwidth, and improves computational efficiency, particularly under resource-constrained deployment conditions.
[0026]		The selected assessment information is subsequently supplied to a feature-engineering engine (124) configured to transform heterogeneous assessment information into standardized feature representations. The feature-engineering engine (124) normalizes inputs received from multiple languages, assessment formats, scales, and data structures to generate a fixed-length feature vector together with a corresponding missingness mask identifying unavailable, incomplete, or delayed assessment information. Consequently, the apparatus maintains reliable operation despite incomplete multi-source assessment data.
[0027]		The edge inference appliance (120) accesses a model store (126) configured to maintain one or more compressed, quantized, or resource-efficient processing models suitable for execution on low-cost edge computing hardware. In one embodiment, the model store (126) stores compressed or 8-bit quantized machine-learning models, thereby reducing storage requirements, memory utilization, and computational overhead while supporting rapid deployment and efficient model updating without hardware modification.
[0028]		The standardized feature vector generated by the feature-engineering engine (124) together with one or more processing models retrieved from the model store (126) are supplied to a parallel ensemble-inference unit (128). The parallel ensemble-inference unit (128) executes multiple inference models concurrently using available hardware acceleration resources, including NPUs or equivalent processing hardware. The ensemble may comprise gradient boosting models, bagged decision tree ensembles, multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), support vector machines (SVMs), or other computational models executed in parallel to improve processing throughput, reduce execution latency, and enhance inference robustness during large-scale pediatric screening operations.
[0029]		Outputs generated by the parallel ensemble-inference unit (128) are provided to an aggregation module (130) configured to combine multiple inference outputs into a unified assessment representation. The aggregation module (130) applies configurable weighting parameters that may be adjusted according to deployment requirements, operational policies, screening protocols, or clinician preferences without requiring modification of the underlying apparatus architecture. Such configurable weighting enables adaptation of workflow prioritization strategies while preserving architectural consistency.
[0030]		The aggregated assessment representation is subsequently supplied to a classification module (132) configured to assign one or more workflow priority categories according to configurable threshold parameters stored within the apparatus. The classification module (132) generates a non-diagnostic triage record (140) indicating workflow priority together with associated validity indicators and confidence information. The generated triage record is intended solely for workflow prioritization and explicitly requires confirmation by qualified healthcare professionals. Accordingly, the apparatus does not establish pathology, diagnose any medical or psychological condition, or replace professional clinical evaluation.
[0031]		The generated non-diagnostic triage record (140) is transmitted to a secure routing gateway (150) configured to communicate assessment outputs to one or more authorized remote systems. The secure routing gateway (150) employs authenticated communication sessions together with encryption mechanisms including AES-256 encryption, Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3), integrity verification, and secure session establishment procedures to preserve confidentiality and integrity during transmission.
[0032]		The secure routing gateway (150) communicates the generated non-diagnostic triage record to a caregiver or clinician console (170) configured to present workflow prioritization information within a case-management queue. The caregiver or clinician console (170) enables authorized clinicians, caregivers, or healthcare personnel to review assessment priorities, validate screening outcomes, and perform subsequent clinical evaluation, diagnosis, referral, counselling, or treatment planning. Final clinical decisions remain exclusively under the authority of qualified healthcare professionals.
[0033]		The classification module (132) further communicates operational information to a tamper-evident audit store (160). The tamper-evident audit store (160) maintains cryptographically verifiable, hash-chained records of acquired assessment information, software versions, processing configurations, generated outputs, communication events, and operational activities. The audit store supports traceability, reproducibility, regulatory compliance, accountability, and post-event verification while preventing unauthorized alteration of previously recorded operational data.
[0034]		The apparatus further incorporates a privacy-by-architecture module (180) integrated with the networked data-acquisition terminals (110) and the edge inference appliance (120). The privacy-by-architecture module (180) ensures that raw personal assessment information remains within the local deployment environment and is processed on-device or within the local edge infrastructure before any external communication occurs. Rather than transmitting raw assessment data, the apparatus communicates only compact feature representations, workflow-priority information, or triage results as required for downstream processing. In distributed deployments comprising multiple edge inference appliances, the privacy-by-architecture module (180) may additionally support federated operational architectures wherein model improvements are coordinated across multiple deployment sites without transferring raw personal information, thereby enhancing privacy protection while reducing communication bandwidth.
[0035]		The disclosed apparatus is specifically configured for deployment in schools, pediatric healthcare facilities, rural health centres, community screening programmes, mobile healthcare units, and geographically distributed environments where computational resources, communication bandwidth, electrical power, and internet connectivity may be limited. The integrated edge inference architecture enables reliable operation despite intermittent network availability and incomplete assessment information while maintaining low processing latency and efficient utilization of computational resources.
[0036]		The modular architecture of the apparatus further permits independent replacement, updating, expansion, or reconfiguration of assessment modules, orchestration policies, feature-engineering algorithms, processing models, communication interfaces, security mechanisms, and workflow parameters without requiring redesign of the overall apparatus architecture. Such modularity enhances long-term maintainability, scalability, interoperability, and adaptability across different pediatric screening programmes, healthcare infrastructures, demographic groups, languages, and regional deployment requirements.
[0037]		The disclosed apparatus provides several technical advantages including reduced communication bandwidth through adaptive assessment selection, resource-efficient edge inference using compressed processing models, improved computational throughput through parallel ensemble execution, reliable handling of incomplete heterogeneous assessment information, configurable workflow prioritization, secure encrypted communication, cryptographically verifiable audit capability, privacy-preserving local processing, scalability across distributed deployments, and reliable operation under intermittent network connectivity. These technical improvements collectively enable efficient, secure, and resource-optimized pediatric multi-source data acquisition and non-diagnostic risk stratification while preserving privacy, operational integrity, and deployment flexibility across diverse healthcare environments. ,

title: ADAPTIVE MULTI-SENSOR SYSTEM PREDICTING COOKING OIL HEALTH AND REMAINING LIFESPAN
abstract: The present invention relates to an Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion System for Cooking Oil Health Assessment, Remaining Useful Life Prediction, and Personalized Recommendation. The system integrates temperature, colour, viscosity, dielectric constant, and oil usage sensors with an embedded processing unit for real-time oil quality monitoring. An Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion Engine (ACMSFE) dynamically evaluates sensor reliability, assigns confidence-based weighting coefficients, and generates a unified feature representation for an Artificial Intelligence prediction engine. The system determines a Confidence-Adaptive Oil Health Score (CA-OHS), predicts Remaining Useful Life (RUL), evaluates a Prediction Confidence Index (PCI), and generates personalized recommendations for oil reuse, replenishment, blending, or replacement. An adaptive self-learning module utilizes historical operating data and prediction errors to continuously improve sensor weighting and prediction accuracy. The invention enables reliable and predictive oil management, improving food safety, reducing oil wastage, lowering operational costs, and supporting sustainable cooking practices.
specification:
The present invention has been particularly shown and described concerning certain preferred embodiments and specific features thereof. The embodiments set forth 10 herein below are to be taken as illustrative rather than limiting.
[0025] The following description outlines the preferred embodiment of one aspect of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present 15 description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting.
[0026] While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the 20 invention as defined in the claims.
[0027] In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases 25 "consisting of," "consists of, the like.
[0028] As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural unless expressly stated to designate the singular only.
[0029] The present invention relates to an Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion System for Cooking Oil Health Assessment, Remaining Useful Life 30
9
Prediction, and Personalized Recommendation. More particularly, the invention provides an intelligent real-time cooking oil monitoring and management platform configured to continuously acquire physical, chemical, thermal, and operational parameters associated with cooking oil, evaluate the reliability and confidence of individual sensor measurements, adaptively fuse heterogeneous sensor information, predict present and 5 future oil degradation using Artificial Intelligence, estimate the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the cooking oil, generate a Confidence-Adaptive Oil Health Score (CA-OHS), determine a Prediction Confidence Index (PCI), and provide personalized recommendations concerning continued use, replenishment, blending, or replacement of the cooking oil. The system is applicable to domestic kitchens, restaurants, hotels, 10 cafeterias, institutional kitchens, cloud kitchens, and food-processing environments. The overall architecture integrates sensing, embedded processing, adaptive sensor fusion, predictive analytics, historical data storage, communication, user interaction, and adaptive self-learning within a unified platform. The principal inventive contribution lies in dynamically determining the confidence and reliability of heterogeneous sensor 15 measurements before performing sensor fusion, thereby reducing the influence of unreliable measurements during subsequent prediction and decision-making.
[0030] In one embodiment, the system comprises a Cooking Oil Input Module (101), a Multi-Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (102), an Embedded Data Processing Unit (103), an Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion Engine (ACMSFE) (104), an 20 Artificial Intelligence Prediction Engine (105), a Confidence-Adaptive Oil Health Score Computation Module (106), a Remaining Useful Life Prediction Engine (107), a Prediction Confidence Index Module (108), an Intelligent Recommendation Engine (109), a User Interface Module (110), a Historical Database (111), and an Adaptive Self-Learning Module (112). The system may further comprise a communication module, power supply 25 unit, and protective enclosure. These modules cooperate sequentially such that information obtained from the cooking oil is converted into processed sensor data, confidence-weighted fused information, predictive degradation information, oil health assessment, remaining useful life estimation, prediction confidence, and context-aware recommendations.
[0031] The Cooking Oil Input Module (101) is configured to initialize an oil-30 monitoring operation by receiving contextual and operational information associated with a cooking process. The information may be entered manually through a display, touchscreen, mobile application, web interface, or other user interface, or may be automatically retrieved
10
from a previously stored cooking profile. The input parameters may include the type of cooking oil, such as sunflower oil, mustard oil, soybean oil, groundnut oil, palm oil, rice bran oil, olive oil, coconut oil, or canola oil; the category of food being fried; initial frying temperature; target frying duration; desired cooking profile; user-defined replacement criteria; kitchen identification; batch identification; operator identification; oil 5 replenishment information; and previous oil usage information. The contextual information is subsequently supplied to the prediction and sensor-fusion processes so that oil degradation is evaluated in relation to the actual operating environment rather than solely according to fixed threshold values.
[0032] The Multi-Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (102) continuously acquires real-10 time measurements associated with the physical and degradation condition of the cooking oil. In a preferred embodiment, the sensing unit comprises a temperature sensor, colour sensor, viscosity sensor, dielectric constant sensor, and an Oil Usage Monitoring Module. The temperature sensor continuously measures the temperature of the cooking oil and provides information useful for identifying overheating, thermal degradation, abnormal 15 frying behaviour, and changes in degradation rate. The colour sensor detects changes in optical characteristics of the oil associated with oxidation, polymer formation, carbon residue accumulation, food contamination, and thermal degradation. The viscosity sensor measures changes in viscosity associated with polymerization, thermal ageing, oil thickening, and deterioration severity. The dielectric constant sensor measures dielectric 20 characteristics associated with polar compounds, oxidation products, chemical degradation, Total Polar Material (TPM), and overall oil ageing. The Oil Usage Monitoring Module records frying duration, number of frying cycles, cumulative operating time, replenishment events, cooking frequency, food preparation sequence, previous replacement events, and cooking schedule. 25
[0033] In further embodiments, the Multi-Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (102) may include additional sensors such as a moisture sensor, dissolved-gas sensor, optical turbidity sensor, infrared sensor, volatile organic compound sensor, pH sensor, Total Polar Material sensor, conductivity sensor, ambient temperature sensor, humidity sensor, or equivalent sensing devices. The additional sensing elements may be selected according to the intended 30 application, required accuracy, operating environment, type of oil, or desired degradation parameters. Outputs from the respective sensors are synchronized and transmitted to the Embedded Data Processing Unit (103), thereby creating a heterogeneous set of real-time
11
and historical information representing the condition and operating context of the cooking oil.
[0034] The Embedded Data Processing Unit (103) receives the sensor measurements and performs pre-processing before the information is supplied to the adaptive fusion engine. The processing unit may comprise an ESP32, STM32, Raspberry 5 Pi, Arduino, ARM Cortex processor, FPGA, System-on-Chip, industrial embedded controller, edge Artificial Intelligence processor, or equivalent computing hardware. The processing unit performs sensor synchronization, analogue-to-digital conversion, signal conditioning, timestamp synchronization, missing-value handling, outlier detection, noise filtering, calibration, normalization, feature extraction, feature scaling, data validation, and 10 data buffering. These operations convert heterogeneous raw measurements into synchronized and normalized feature information suitable for confidence evaluation and Artificial Intelligence-based prediction. The processed information is then transmitted to the Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion Engine (104).
[0035] The Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Sensor Fusion Engine (104) 15 constitutes a principal inventive component of the system. The ACMSFE is configured to determine a confidence value for each sensing parameter before performing multi-sensor fusion. The confidence associated with an individual sensor may be dynamically determined using sensor consistency, historical prediction accuracy, measurement stability, environmental disturbances, calibration drift, sensor ageing, measurement noise, operating 20 temperature, data completeness, historical degradation behaviour, cooking conditions, oil type, and food category. Based on the calculated confidence values, the ACMSFE generates adaptive weighting coefficients for the respective sensor measurements. A highly reliable sensor is consequently permitted to contribute more strongly to the fused representation, whereas a sensor exhibiting instability, drift, noise, contamination, ageing, 25 or reduced historical accuracy is assigned a proportionally lower contribution. This dynamic mechanism reduces the influence of unreliable measurements and improves robustness under varying operating conditions.
[0036] The operation of the ACMSFE (104) proceeds sequentially by receiving synchronized sensor measurements, normalizing the sensor outputs, estimating an 30 individual confidence score for each sensor, calculating adaptive confidence weights, performing confidence-aware multi-sensor fusion, generating a unified feature vector, and forwarding the unified feature vector to the Artificial Intelligence Prediction Engine (105).
12
The confidence values are continuously updated during operation according to subsequently observed prediction performance and sensor behaviour. Thus, the system does not permanently assign a fixed importance to any particular sensor. Instead, the relative contribution of a sensing parameter can change dynamically as the operating environment, sensor condition, cooking condition, oil type, or historical prediction 5 performance changes.
[0037] The Artificial Intelligence Prediction Engine (105) receives the unified feature vector generated by the ACMSFE and performs predictive analysis of the cooking oil. The prediction engine may employ one or more machine-learning or Artificial Intelligence models including Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), 10 CatBoost, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression, Artificial Neural Networks, Deep Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, ensemble-learning models, hybrid Artificial Intelligence models, or equivalent predictive algorithms. The prediction engine analyses the confidence-weighted sensor representation together with historical degradation behaviour and contextual information to estimate the present degradation state, 15 forecast future degradation, identify abnormal deterioration behaviour, determine degradation trends, estimate Remaining Useful Life, predict remaining frying cycles and operating hours, and estimate prediction uncertainty. The prediction output is continuously updated whenever new sensor measurements become available.
[0038] The Confidence-Adaptive Oil Health Score Computation Module (106) 20 generates a quantitative representation of the overall condition of the cooking oil. The CA-OHS is calculated using normalized sensor parameters and the dynamically generated confidence weighting coefficients. In one embodiment, the resulting score may be interpreted as a numerical indication of oil condition, wherein a score of 90–100 may represent fresh oil, 70–89 may represent oil safe for continued reuse, 50-69 may represent 25 limited reuse, and a score below 50 may indicate that oil replacement is required. The classification may be modified according to the application, oil type, user-defined safety requirements, or operating conditions. Since the underlying sensor weights are dynamically adapted according to sensor reliability and operating conditions, the resulting oil health assessment is not dependent solely upon a fixed weighting arrangement. 30
[0039] The Remaining Useful Life Prediction Engine (107) determines the expected remaining operational life of the cooking oil using the degradation state and degradation trajectory predicted by the Artificial Intelligence Prediction Engine (105). The
13
RUL prediction may represent remaining safe frying cycles, remaining operating hours, expected replacement date, degradation trend, predicted end-of-life condition, and a preventive replacement schedule. The RUL is continuously recalculated as new measurements are acquired, thereby enabling the system to modify its prediction according to actual changes in oil degradation. Accordingly, instead of merely informing a user that 5 the oil has crossed a predefined limit, the system can provide an advance estimate of how much useful operational life remains before the predicted degradation reaches an unacceptable condition.
[0040] The Prediction Confidence Index Module (108) determines the reliability associated with each prediction generated by the Artificial Intelligence Prediction Engine. 10 The PCI may be determined using sensor confidence values, sensor agreement, confidence-weighted fusion results, prediction uncertainty, historical model performance, data completeness, calibration quality, measurement stability, environmental disturbances, prediction error, and operating conditions. The PCI may be represented on a percentage scale, wherein a higher percentage indicates greater confidence in the generated prediction. 15 When the PCI falls below a predefined confidence criterion, the system may request additional measurements, repeat prediction calculations, generate reliability warnings, recommend sensor calibration, reduce the influence of unreliable sensing devices, or notify the user that the prediction has reduced certainty.
