The following specification particularly describes the invention and the manner
in which it is to be performed
2
A method for controlling a material feed is disclosed. In addition, a dosing system,
which in particular comprises a material feed that can be operated using such a
method, is disclosed.
5 One of the tasks to be solved is to disclose an improved method for controlling a
material feed and to disclose an improved dosing system.
These tasks are solved, inter alia, by subject-matters comprising the features of
claims 1 and 9.
10
According to at least one embodiment of the method for controlling a material feed,
the method is configured to control or regulate a material feed for filling a first
container with a material from a second container. In the method, a rate of change
of a filling level of the first container is determined. If the rate of change is positive,
15 the material feed is reduced and if the rate of change is negative, the material feed
is increased. The rate of change is determined using a capacitive sensor.
The material feed is, for example, a chain feed. For example, a conveyor chain or
transport chain is operated with the material feed. Alternatively, the material feed
20 is a screw feed, for example. In this case, a screw conveyor is preferably operated
with the material feed.
The second container is, for example, a storage container in which the material is
stored or held. By means of a transport unit that is operated with the material feed,
25 the material can be conveyed from the second container into the first container
during intended operation.
The transport unit is, for example, a conveyor chain or a transport chain.
Alternatively, the transport unit is a screw conveyor, for example.
30
3
The first container can be a dosing container, from which the material can
preferably be emptied in a controlled and/or uniform manner. For example, the
material from the first container is applied evenly to a surface. In particular, this
means that a thickness of the material on the surface after application has a
5 homogeneous or substantially homogeneous thickness. The material is, for
example, spreading material. The surface to which the material is applied is, for
example, a road or a prepared, for example rolled, ground.
By filling the first container with the material from the second container and
10 possibly emptying the first container, the filling level of the first container changes.
In order to ensure controlled emptying of the first container, it is advantageous if
the filling level does not fall below a certain minimum.
Likewise, it is desirable if the filling level does not rise above a certain maximum
15 value in order to reduce a risk of overflowing of the first container or to prevent an
overflow. With the method described herein for controlling the material feed, it is
advantageous possible to adjust the filling of the container in such a way that the
filling level is always between the desirable minimum and maximum values.
20 If, for example, the first container is emptied faster than it is filled, the filling level
has a negative rate of change, which means that the material feed must be increased
to prevent the filling level from falling below the minimum value. If, on the other
hand, the first container is filled faster than it is emptied, the filling level has a
positive rate of change, which means that the material feed must be reduced
25 accordingly.
Using the method described herein for controlling the material feed, the filling level
of the first container can be adapted to different emptying or filling situations and
kept within the minimum and maximum limit values.
30
4
The method described herein is based inter alia on the following technical
considerations. The filling level of a container can be monitored using a capacitive
sensor. By a "capacitive sensor" is meant here and in the following a sensor with a
capacitive measuring principle. In the following, the "capacitive sensor" may also
5 be referred to simply as a "sensor". A capacitive sensor referred to below as a
"sensor" works in particular with the capacitive measuring principle and is a
capacitive sensor.
A measuring principle of the sensor is based on the fact that a capacitance of the
10 sensor changes when the filling level changes as a space of the sensor is filled with
a dielectric material, namely the material in the container. As a result of the
capacitance change of the sensor, a voltage applied to the sensor changes, which
can be detected as a measurement value or signal. Alternatively, a current strength
can also be measured at the sensor, which also changes with the capacitance of the
15 sensor. In this case, the current is the measurement value. Consequently, a
measurement value or signal value, in particular the entire signal of the sensor, is
material-dependent. This is due in particular to the different dielectric properties of
different materials. This means that for the same filling level, different materials
result in a different initial value of the capacitive sensor. Calibration of the
20 capacitive sensor is therefore necessary to determine the absolute value of the filling
level. One disadvantage of this is that the calibration must be repeated each time a
different material is filled into the container. On the other hand, such a calibration
is prone to errors. In particular, an incorrect calibration can lead to a malfunction or
even total standstill of the material feed or a machine using the first container.
25
The method described here makes use of the idea of using a gradient or rate of
change of the filling level. By determining the rate of change, the materialdependent absolute signal value of the capacitive sensor, which corresponds to the
absolute filling level, can be equalized. Material properties, in particular dielectric
30 properties of the material in the container, are therefore irrelevant.
5
Advantageously, there is no need to calibrate the capacitive sensor to the material
in the container. Only a so-called zero adjustment to ground potential is necessary.
However, this can be carried out ex works, for example, and advantageously does
not need to be repeated.
5
According to at least one embodiment or at least one of the embodiments described
above, the sensor is arranged in the first container. In particular, the sensor is
arranged in the first container in such a way that a material with which the first
container is filled or emptied passes the sensor during emptying or filling.
10
The capacitive sensor comprises, for example, an electrically conductive sensor
element and a grounded housing. The electrically conductive sensor element is, for
example, an electrically conductive rope, such as a metal rope. In this case, the
capacitive sensor is also referred to as a rope sensor. Alternatively, the electrically
15 conductive sensor element is, for example, a rod such as a metal rod or a metal
plate.
The sensor element is preferably electrically insulated from the grounded housing.
For example, the housing acts as the first electrode and the sensor element as the
20 second electrode of the capacitive sensor. Preferably, the housing of the capacitive
sensor is identical to the first container. In particular, the means that the sensor is
formed by the sensor element and the first container.
When the first container is filled, a capacitance of the capacitive sensor changes,
25 whereby a corresponding capacitor is formed by the housing or the first container
as the first electrode and the sensor element as the second electrode. If a voltage is
applied to the capacitive sensor, this change in capacitance can be detected as a
change in voltage. The voltage applied to the capacitive sensor corresponds in
particular to a signal from the capacitive sensor. A single voltage value of the
30 applied voltage corresponds to a signal value of the capacitive sensor.
6
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
embodiments described above, the rate of change is determined independently of a
material with which the first container is filled or emptied. Since in the method the
material feed is only adjusted based on the rate of change of the signal value of the
5 capacitive sensor and not based on the absolute signal values, the material feed can
be adjusted independently of the material in the first container.
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
embodiments described above, the following sub-steps are carried out to determine
10 the rate of change. In the first sub-step, a plurality of change values of the signal of
the capacitive sensor are detected over a plurality of time intervals. That is, the
change value is the change in the signal value within a certain time interval. In other
words, the change value corresponds to the average slope of the signal in a time
interval, in particular in a graphical plot of the signal versus time.
15
Preferably, a plurality of change values are detected and stored.
In a further sub-step, the rate of change is determined by calculating an average
value from the plurality of change values. For example, the stored change values
20 are arithmetically averaged. The rate of change thus corresponds to an average over
a large number of changes in individual time intervals.
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
embodiments described above, the rate of change is determined by averaging over
25 a plurality of change values. In particular, 10 or more change values are averaged
to determine the change values. For example, exactly 10 change values are averaged
to determine the rate of change.
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
30 embodiments described above, in the case of a positive rate of change, the rate of
7
change is multiplied by a first weighting factor and in the case of a negative rate of
change, the rate of change is multiplied by a second weighting factor.
Multiplication by the weighting factors preferably results in a control signal for the
5 material feed from the rate of change. Preferably, the control signal is proportional
to the rate of change. In particular, the control signal has a correspondence to the
material feed.
Preferably, the weighting factors are each selected such that a relative change in the
10 material feed is at most 10 %. Advantageously, very large changes in the material
feed can thus be reduced and the hydraulics of the overall machine can be spared.
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
embodiments described above, the first container has dosing sluices for emptying
15 the first container, wherein the material feed is stopped when the dosing sluices are
stopped. In other words, if the first container is not emptied, it is not filled any
further.
In particular, the dosing sluices are rotatable dosing sluices. This means that the
20 first container is emptied by rotating the dosing sluice. In the case of rotatable
dosing sluices, for example, the dosing sluices are rigid when they are closed.
Rotatable dosing sluices allow the first container to be emptied in a particularly
controlled manner and the material from the first container to be distributed
particularly uniformly on a surface or the like.
25
According to at least one embodiment of the method or at least one of the
embodiments described above, the method further comprises the following steps.
In a step A), a signal value of the capacitive sensor is determined. In particular, the
signal value is a raw value or a measurement value of the capacitive sensor. This
30 means that this value is preferably not calculated with a weight factor or another
factor.
8
In a step B), this signal value is compared with a minimum signal value. This
comparison ensures that the filling level within the first container has a minimum
value. This means that the minimum signal value provides a lower limit for the
5 filling level. Calibration of the capacitive sensor can advantageously be omitted, as
the minimum signal value can be selected in such a way that there is a sufficient
filling level for every conceivable relevant material if the minimum signal value is
exceeded.
10 In a further step C), the material feed is increased by 1 % in the event that the initial
signal value is less than the minimum signal value.
Steps A) to C) are in particular carried out before determining the rate of change.
15 Preferably, steps B) and C) are carried out alternately until the signal value is greater
than the minimum signal value.
Preferably, steps A) to C) are carried out before emptying of the first container takes
place. Steps A) to C) can in particular ensure that a minimum amount of the material
20 is present in the first container before the first container is emptied, so that uniform
emptying of the container is possible. Subsequent control during emptying of the
first container is achieved in particular by considering the rate of change as
described here.
25 A dosing system for a material is further disclosed. In particular, the dosing system
comprises a control unit which is configured to carry out a method described herein.
That is, all features disclosed for the method are also disclosed for the dosing system
and vice versa.
30 According to at least one embodiment, the dosing system comprises a first container
with a capacitive sensor and dosing sluices for emptying the first container. The
9
dosing system further comprises a second container. In particular, this is a storage
container for the material. The dosing system further comprises a transport unit for
filling the first container with material from the second container. In particular, the
transport unit is configured to be operated with a predeterminable material feed.
5 Furthermore, the dosing system comprises a control unit which is configured to
carry out a method described herein and to predetermine the material feed.
The dosing system can be used to feed the material from the second container into
the first container and empty it from the first container in a controlled manner via
10 dosing sluices.
The dosing system can, for example, be integrated into a construction vehicle or the
like for spreading material. For example, the material is then spreading material,
which is spread via the first container and the dosing sluices. For example, the
15 spreading material is to be distributed evenly over a surface, such as a road or the
like. It is particularly advantageous if the spreading material is distributed evenly.
For this purpose, the first container is preferably filled to a certain filling level. The
method described herein can be used to ensure that the filling level always remains
within a desired range.
20
For example, the first container serves as an intermediate container between the
storage container and the dosing sluices and is configured to distribute the material,
for example the spreading material, evenly to the dosing sluices.
25 Further advantages and advantageous embodiments and further developments of
the method and the dosing system are shown in the following in connection with
the exemplary embodiments shown in the schematic drawings. Identical, similar
and identically acting elements are provided with the same reference signs in the
figures. The figures and the proportions of the elements shown in the figures are
30 not to be regarded as being to scale. Rather, individual elements may be shown
exaggeratedly large for better visualization and/or improved comprehensibility.
10
THE FIGURES SHOW
Figure 1 a schematic perspective view of a dosing system described herein
5 according to an exemplary embodiment;
Figure 2 a diagram of a time course of a signal value of a sensor described
herein;
10 Figure 3 a schematic block diagram of a method described herein according
to an exemplary embodiment;
Figure 4 a schematic illustration of a sensor as it can be used in a method
described herein.
15
The dosing system 1 of figure 1 comprises a first container 2 and a second container
3. The first container 2 can be filled with material 20 from the second container 3
via a transport chain 6, which can be operated with a material feed 100.
20 The second container 3 is, in particular, a storage container for the material 20. The
material 20 is, for example, a spreading material that can be applied to a surface in
a controlled and preferably uniform manner using the dosing system 1.
The first container 2 has rotatable dosing sluices 5. The first container 2 can be
25 emptied through the rotatable dosing sluices 5.
The first container 2 further comprises a capacitive sensor 10. The sensor 10
comprises an electrically conductive sensor element 12, such as a metal cable. The
sensor 10 is, for example, a rope sensor. The sensor element 12 is preferably
30 electrically insulated from the first container 2. The first container 2 is a housing 11
for the sensor 10.
11
The sensor 10 is a capacitive sensor. In operation as intended, a voltage is applied
to the sensor 10, wherein the housing 11 is grounded and the sensor element 12 is
brought to a specific electrical potential. The housing 11 forms a first electrode of
5 the capacitive sensor 10 and the sensor element 12 forms a second electrode.
If a filling level changes in a space between the housing 11 and the sensor element
12, i.e. between the first and second electrodes of the sensor 10, the capacitance of
the sensor 10 and the voltage applied to the sensor 10 changes. A filling level of the
10 first container 2 can thus be determined on the basis of the measured voltage at the
sensor 10. However, a signal value 15, which corresponds to the measured voltage,
of the sensor 10 is material-dependent, as different materials influence the change
in the capacitance of the sensor 10 differently due to their different dielectric
constants. Therefore, calibration of the sensor 10 is necessary in order to obtain an
15 absolute value for the filling level.
The method described here makes use of the idea of not considering the absolute
signal values 15 of the sensor 10, but of determining a rate of change 4 from a
change in the voltage of the sensor 10 or the signal of the sensor 10 in order to
20 control the material feed 100. This makes it possible, for example, to control the
filling or emptying of the container 2 so that the container 2 does not overflow or is
completely emptied. It is therefore possible to keep the filling level of the container
2 within predeterminable limits using the sensor 10 described here.
25 Figure 2 shows a diagram illustrating the progression of a signal value 15 over time.
The signal value 15 is plotted against time 51. In the exemplary embodiment of the
method shown in Figure 2, a plurality of change values 10n are recorded. The
change values 10n are recorded in time intervals 11n. In other words, in the method
described here, a change in the signal value 15 over time in a specific time interval
30 11n is recorded and stored as a change value 10n. Figure 2 illustrates the detection
of a change value 10n in a time interval 11n.
12
In the method described here, a rate of change 4 of the filling level of the first
container 2 is determined from these change values 10n. For this purpose, the
change values 10n are averaged, for example.
5
In the method according to the exemplary embodiment of Figure 3, a first signal
value 15 is determined in a first method step 201. In method step 201, the signal
value 15 is compared with a minimum signal value 19. The signal value 15
corresponds to a filling level of the first container.
10
If the signal value 15 is smaller than the minimum signal value 19, the material feed
100 is increased in method step 210 in order to increase the signal value 15. For
example, in method step 210, the material feed 100 is increased relatively by 1%
every 100 ms. The signal value 15 is continuously determined and compared with
15 the minimum signal value 19.
If the signal value 15 is greater than the minimum signal value 19, it is determined
in a method step 202 whether the dosing sluices 5 are open or closed. If the dosing
sluices are rotatable dosing sluices, it is determined in step 202 whether the dosing
20 sluices are rigid or rotating.
If the dosing sluices are closed or rigid, the material feed 100 is stopped in step 211.
The reason for this is that if the dosing sluices are closed or rigid, the first container
is not emptied any further and further filling of the first container 2 with material
25 20 from the second container 3 carries the risk of the first container 2 overflowing.
If the dosing sluices 5 are open or rotating, a rate of change 4 is determined in
method step 203 and it is determined whether a new rate of change 4 is available.
If no new rate of change 4 is available, i.e. if the rate of change 4 has not changed
30 compared to a previous run of the method, for example, then no change takes place
(method step 212).

title: METHODS FOR PREPARING FLUORINE-CONTAINING PROPYLENE AND INTERMEDIATE THEREOF
abstract: Disclosed in the present invention are methods for preparing fluorine-containing propylene and a fluorochloropropane intermediate thereof. The method for preparing the fluorochloropropane intermediate comprises: subjecting dichloromethane, difluoromethane, and a fluorine-containing olefin of general formula CF2=CR1R2 to a liquid-phase addition reaction under the action of an addition catalyst to prepare fluorochloropropane of general formula of CF3CR1R2CH2Cl, wherein the content of the fluorine-containing olefin in a reaction system is monitored during the reaction process, and the content of the fluorine-containing olefin thereof is controlled to be less than or equal to 5%; and the addition catalyst is a mixed catalyst formed from a metal fluoride, a metal chloride, and a metal oxide, and the metal is selected from metal elements in group IIIA, IVB, or VA. The obtained fluorochloropropane intermediate is subjected to a hydrogen chloride removal reaction under the action of activated carbon or a metal alkali solution to obtain fluorine-containing propylene. The method of the present invention has the advantages of a simple process flow, mild reaction conditions, easy product separation, good product purity, a remarkably improved service life of the addition catalyst, etc.
specification:
The present invention relates to preparation of fluorochloropropane and a fluorinecontaining propylene, in particular, to a method for preparing a fluorine-containing propylene,
which includes preparing a fluorochloropropane intermediate having a general formula of
5 CF3CR1R2CH2Cl from a fluorine-containing olefin having a general formula of CF2=CR1R2,
dichloromethane, difluoromethane under the action of a metal LEWIS acid, and subjecting the
fluorochloropropane intermediate to a dehydrochlorination reaction to obtain the fluorinecontaining propylene.
BACKGROUND
10 [0002] 3,3,3-Trifluoropropene, 2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropene, 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene,
and 1-chloro-2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene are four common kinds of fluorine-containing propylene.
In particular, 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene, owing to its superior environmental performance and
refrigeration performance similar to that of 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (R134a), has gradually
replaced R134a as a mainstream refrigerant in the air conditioning field of new energy vehicles.
15 Preparation of fluorine-containing propylene is usually achieved by dehydrochlorination reaction
of fluorochloropropane; therefore, how to obtain fluorochloropropane is key to the preparation of
fluorine-containing propylene.
[0003] 1-Chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane (HCFC-253fb), 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1-trifluoropropane
(HCFC-243db), 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane (HCFC-244eb), and 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1,2-
20 tetrafluoropropane (HCFC-234ba) are important fluorine-containing fine chemicals. They can be
used to prepare novel refrigerants such as HCFO-1224yd and HFO-1234yf by dehalogenation
reactions, and thus have great application potential.
[0004] Currently, there are relatively few studies on the synthesis of 1-chloro-3,3,3-
trifluoropropane, 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane, and 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1,2-
25 tetrafluoropropane compounds.
[0005] (I) Research on synthesis of 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane
[0006] US Patent US2644845A discloses a method for obtaining 1-chloro-3,3,3-
trifluoropropane by photo-chlorination using 1,1,1-trifluoropropane and chlorine as raw materials.
3
The method has a simple process, but the product yield is low. Under irradiation with a 200 W
incandescent lamp and a reaction temperature of 110 degrees centigrade, the yield of 1-chloro3,3,3-trifluoropropane is only 56%.
[0007] China patent CN1488614A discloses a two-step method for synthesizing 1-chloro5 3,3,3-trifluoropropane, including: 1) preparing an intermediate 1,3,3,3-tetrachloropropane from
carbon tetrachloride and ethylene under the action of an initiator such as ferric chloride or
phosphate esters; and 2) subjecting the 1,3,3,3-tetrachloropropane to a liquid-phase fluorination
reaction with anhydrous hydrogen fluoride under the action of a catalyst such as tin tetrachloride
or titanium tetrachloride to produce 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane. This process route has low
10 requirements for reaction equipment, low energy consumption, and easy separation and
purification of the product. However, it suffers from low raw material utilization. Under optimal
conditions, the conversion rate of carbon tetrachloride is 75%, and the product yield in the
fluorination step is only 65%.
[0008] China patent CN107162871A discloses a two-step method for preparing 1-chloro15 3,3,3-trifluoropropane, using activated carbon as a catalyst and trifluoromethane as a starting
material. A catalytic chlorination reaction is carried out in a fixed-bed reactor to obtain the
intermediate trifluorochloromethane, which is then subjected to a telomerization reaction with
ethylene under the action of an iron-molybdenum catalyst to generate 1-chloro-3,3,3-
trifluoropropane. The yield of this process can reach 86%, but the intermediate product requires
20 purification steps such as alkali washing, drying, and extraction, making the post-treatment
complex. In addition, the reaction temperature is high, with the gas-phase chlorination temperature
exceeding 300 degrees centigrade.
[0009] (II) Research on synthesis of 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1-trifluoropropane
[0010] China patent CN101168494A discloses a method for synthesizing 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1-
25 trifluoropropane by liquid-phase fluorination using 1,1,1,2,3-pentachloropropane as a raw material
under the action of catalysts such as chromium fluoride, magnesium fluoride, and titanium fluoride.
The process route is simple and the raw materials are readily available, but the product yield is
low. After reacting at a temperature in a range of 90 degrees centigrade to 130 degrees centigrade
4
for 4 hours to 10 hours, the product yield is only about 85%.
[0011] China patent CN10197936A discloses a method for synthesizing 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1-
trifluoropropane in a tubular reactor or a tank reactor using 1,1,1-trifluoropropene and chlorine as
raw materials under irradiation with an ultraviolet lamp. This method achieves a raw material
5 conversion rate of 95% and a selectivity exceeding 90%, but it has high equipment requirements
and poses significant hazards to human health.
[0012] (III) Research on synthesis of 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane
[0013] Patent WO2019003896A discloses a method for preparing 2-chloro-1,1,1,2-
tetrafluoropropane and/or 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane by liquid-phase photocatalytic
10 chlorination using 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane as a raw material. The process is simple, but the main
product is 2-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane, with selectivity for 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-
tetrafluoropropane below 20%. Moreover, there are many by-products with similar boiling points,
making separation and purification difficult.
[0014] Patent CN115023490A discloses a method for preparing 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-
15 tetrafluoropropane, in which 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene is hydrogenated under the action of a
palladium-on-carbon catalyst to obtain 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane, and then the 1,1,1,2-
tetrafluoropropane reacts with chlorine to obtain a mixture of HCFC-244bb, HCFC-244eb, and
HCFC-234ea. The mixture is then purified by distillation to obtain 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-
tetrafluoropropane. However, patent CN115023490A does not disclose the reaction conditions or
20 the reaction effect.
[0015] (IV) Research on synthesis of 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane
[0016] Patents CN103524293A, CN105753638A, CN105777484A, etc., disclose methods for
synthesizing 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane by two-step fluorination (gas-phase and
liquid-phase) using a compound having a general formula of CF3-xClxCH2-yClyCH3-zClz as a starting
25 material under the action of a fluorination catalyst. Under optimal conditions, the raw material
conversion rate reaches 93.7% and the selectivity reaches 83.5%. However, this method requires
relatively high reaction temperatures: the gas-phase fluorination temperature is in a range of 200
degrees centigrade to 350 degrees centigrade, and the liquid-phase fluorination temperature is in a

range of 110 degrees centigrade to 150 degrees centigrade. Moreover, the reaction process requires
a combination of gas-phase fluorination and liquid-phase fluorination, making the process difficult.
Additionally, the patent does not disclose the service life of the catalyst.
[0017] In summary, in the related art, the synthesis of fluorochloropropane is either obtained
5 by chlorination or fluorination with low product yield; or obtained by two-step reactions, but the
technical route is relatively complex, the target product yield is not high, the reaction conditions
are harsh, and problems such as high difficulty in product separation and purification exist.
SUMMARY
[0018] In order to solve the technical problems above, the present invention provides a method
10 for preparing a fluorochloropropane intermediate by an addition reaction. The method has simple
process and mild reaction conditions. The product is easy to separate and has good purity.
Moreover, a service life of the catalyst is significantly improved.
[0019] The object of the present invention can be achieved by following technical solutions.
[0020] A method for preparing fluorochloropropane by an addition reaction is disclosed in the
15 present invention. The method includes following steps: subjecting dichloromethane,
difluoromethane, and a fluorine-containing olefin of Formula I to a liquid-phase addition reaction
under the action of an addition catalyst, so as to prepare fluorochloropropane of Formula II, and a
reaction equation is as follows:

10 thereof.
[0023] In some embodiments, the metal element of the metal fluoride, the metal element of

[0024] In some embodiments, the fluorine element, the chloride element and the oxide element
in the addition catalyst sources from the corresponding metal fluoride, metal chloride and metal
15 oxide. By adjusting a content of the metal fluoride, a content of the metal chloride and a content

[0025] In order to improve reaction effect, in the addition catalyst, a molar content of fluorine
element is in a range of 40% to 70% of a total anion molar content, a molar content of chlorine
20 element is in a range of 20% to 50% of the total anion molar content, and a molar content of oxygen

molar content of chlorine element is in a range of 30% to 40% of the total anion molar content,
and the molar content of oxygen element is in a range of 10% to 20% of the total anion molar
25 content.
[0026] In the present invention, the addition catalyst can efficiently dissociate the raw
materials difluoromethane and dichloromethane to generate active ions such as F⁻, CH₂F⁺, Cl⁻, and
CH₂Cl⁺. The addition reaction between the halogenated hydrocarbon and the halogenated olefin is
7
electrophilic addition reaction. According to Markovnikov’s rule and the electronegativity of
charged groups, F⁻ and CH₂Cl⁺ can undergo a directed addition reaction with the fluorinecontaining olefin compound to obtain the addition product CF3CR1R2CH2Cl with high selectivity.
[0027] The fluorine-containing olefin of the present invention is selected from the group
5 consisting of vinylidene fluoride (CF₂=CH₂F), chlorodifluoroethylene (CF₂=CHCl),
trifluoroethylene (CF₂=CHF), chlorotrifluoroethylene (CF₂=CFCl), and any combination thereof,
and the corresponding fluorochloropropane are 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane (CF₃CH₂CH₂Cl),
2,3-dichloro-1,1,1-trifluoropropane (CF₃CHClCH₂Cl), 3-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane
(CF₃CHFCH₂Cl), and 2,3-dichloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoropropane (CF₃CFClCH₂Cl), respectively.
10 [0028] In the method for preparing fluorochloropropane of the present invention, a molar ratio
of raw materials, a molar ratio of raw materials to the addition catalyst, the reaction temperature,
the reaction duration, the feeding method, etc., all affect the reaction results, and in particular, have
a significant impact on the service time of the catalyst and the selectivity of the target product.
[0029] A molar ratio of the dichloromethane to the fluorine-containing olefin is in a range of
15 0.5 : 1 to 2 : 1. In some embodiments, the molar ratio of the dichloromethane to the fluorinecontaining olefin is in a range of 0.5 : 1 to 1 : 1. In some embodiments, the molar ratio of the
dichloromethane to the fluorine-containing olefin is in a range of 0.6 : 1 to 0.7 : 1.
[0030] Furthermore, a weight ratio of the dichloromethane to the addition catalyst is greater
than or equal to 2. When the weight ratio of the dichloromethane to the addition catalyst is less
20 than 2, liquid holdup in a reaction kettle is insufficient, and the reaction system cannot be
effectively stirred, resulting in a decrease in product yield. In some embodiments, a weight ratio
of the dichloromethane to the addition catalyst is in a range of 2 to 10. In some embodiments, the
weight ratio of the dichloromethane to the addition catalyst is in a range of 4 to 6.
[0031] It was concluded from the research of the present invention that during the process for
25 preparing fluorochloropropane by the addition reaction, the raw material fluorine-containing olefin
tends to be adsorbed onto active sites of the catalyst and polymerize, thereby preventing contact
between the reactants and the active sites, causing reduced catalyst activity or even catalyst
deactivation. Thus, in the present invention, a content of the fluorine-containing olefin in a reaction
8
system is monitored during a reaction process, and the content of the fluorine-containing olefin is
controlled to be equal to or less than 5%. In some embodiments, the content of the fluorinecontaining olefin is controlled to be equal to or less than 3%. In some embodiments, the content
of the fluorine-containing olefin is controlled to be equal to or less than 1%. When the content of
5 the fluorine-containing olefin is greater than 5%, the active sites of the catalyst will be occupied
by the fluorine-containing olefin polymers, gradually resulting in catalyst deactivation.
[0032] In order to maximize the inhibition of polymerization of the fluorine-containing olefin
on active sites during the reaction and further improve the service life of the catalyst, the fluorinecontaining olefin of the present invention is continuously fed under pressure via a metering pump,
10 wherein the continuous feeding rate is mainly determined by a consumption rate of the fluorinecontaining olefin in the reaction system. In order to prevent the fluorine-containing olefin from
accumulating in the reaction system, a feeding rate of the fluorine-containing olefin is in a range
of 20 g/h to 120 g/h; and in some embodiments, the feeding rate of the fluorine-containing olefin
is in a range of 60 g/h to 80 g/h. When the content of the fluorine-containing olefin is monitored
15 to be greater than 5%, the feeding rate of the fluorine-containing olefin is reduced. In actual
operation, when the content of the fluorine-containing olefin is close to 5% or up to 5%, the feeding
rate of the fluorine-containing olefin is moderately reduced.
[0033] Furthermore, in order to avoid catalyst deactivation caused by polymerization of the
fluorine-containing olefin at the active sites of the catalyst, the fluorine-containing olefin should
20 react completely as much as possible. In the addition reaction, a total amount of the fluorinecontaining olefin satisfies a following relationship:

[0034] The content of fluorine-containing olefin in the reaction system is mainly monitored
5 by subjecting a material consumption in the reaction system to chromatographic analysis.
[0035] In the method for preparing the fluorochloropropane of the present invention, after the

[0036] Optionally, the addition catalyst and the dichloromethane are mixed together to obtain
a uniform mixture and continuously added into the reactor; and the difluoromethane and the
15 fluorine-containing olefin are mixed together and continuously added into the reactor or
continuously added into the reactor, respectively.
[0037] In the method for preparing the fluorochloropropane of the present invention, any of
the feeding methods described above can be applied, as long as the fluorine-containing olefin is
continuously added into the reaction system. In some embodiments, the addition catalyst is
20 prefilled in the reactor, then the dichloromethane and the difluoromethane can be added, and the

[0038] In the method for preparing the fluorochloropropane of the present invention, a
temperature of the addition reaction is in a range of -20 degrees centigrade to 100 degrees
centigrade, and a duration of the addition reaction is in a range of 4 hours to 20 hours. In some
25 embodiments, the temperature of the addition reaction is in a range of 0 degrees centigrade to 80

In some embodiments, the temperature of the addition reaction is in a range of 30 degrees

hours to 12 hours.
[0039] The pressure invention, it is not necessary to control a reaction pressure, as long as the
reactor is ensured to be sealed. The reaction pressure is determined by a saturated vapor pressure
of the difluoromethane in the reactor, and is generally around 2 MPa. During the reaction, the
5 reaction pressure gradually reduces while the difluoromethane consumes.
[0040] Since the saturated vapor pressure of the difluoromethane and saturated vapor pressure
of the fluorine-containing olefin are much greater than that of the dichloromethane, the

10 addition reaction of the present invention is a solvent-free reaction, and it is not necessary to add
other solvents into the reaction system during the reaction process. Thus, separation process of the
products can be reduced.
[0041] The addition product obtained after the reaction is subjected to filtration and the

15 fluorochloropropane, a difference between a boiling point of a target product CF3CR1R2CH2Cl and
a by-product CF2ClCR1R2CH2Cl is in a range of 15 degrees centigrade and 30 degrees centigrade.
Thus, a fluorochloropropane intermediate having a purity greater than or equal to 99% can be
obtained by distillation or rectification.

step (1), preparing a fluorochloropropane intermediate by any of the methods described above;

embodiments, step (2) is a liquid-phase dehalogenation reaction.
[0045] In some embodiments, the gas-phase dehalogenation reaction is performed under the
action of activated carbon, a temperature of the dehydrochlorination reaction is in a range of 200
degrees centigrade to 500 degrees centigrade. In some embodiments, the temperature of the
5 dehydrochlorination reaction is in a range of 300 degrees centigrade to 350 degrees centigrade. In
some embodiments, an activated carbon catalyst is selected from the group consisting of nut shell
activated carbon, coal-based activated carbon, wood-based activated carbon, and any combination
thereof. In some embodiments, the activated carbon catalyst is the nut shell activated carbon.
[0046] In some embodiments, the liquid-phase dehalogenation reaction is performed under the
10 action of the metal alkali solution. In some embodiments, the liquid-phase dehalogenation reaction
is performed under the action of the metal alkali solution and a quaternary ammonium salt. A molar
ratio of the fluorochloropropane intermediate to a metal alkali is in a range of 1 : 0.1 to 1: 5. In
some embodiments, the molar ratio of the fluorochloropropane intermediate to a metal alkali is in
a range of 1 : 1 to 1: 2. A temperature of the dehydrochlorination reaction is in a range of 10 degrees
15 centigrade to 100 degrees centigrade. In some embodiments, the temperature of the
dehydrochlorination reaction is in a range of 30 degrees centigrade to 60 degrees centigrade. The
metal alkali solution is selected from the group consisting of a sodium hydroxide solution, a
potassium hydroxide solution, a sodium carbonate solution, a potassium carbonate solution, a
sodium bicarbonate solution, a potassium bicarbonate solution, and any combination thereof, and
20 a mass concentration of the metal alkali solution is in a range of 5 wt% to 60 wt%. In some
embodiments, the metal alkali solution is selected from a sodium hydroxide solution or a
potassium hydroxide solution. In some embodiments, the metal alkali solution is a potassium
hydroxide solution. In some embodiments, the mass concentration of the metal alkali solution is
in a range of 10 wt% to 40 wt%. The quaternary ammonium salt is selected from the group
25 consisting of tetrabutylammonium bromide, tetramethylammonium hydroxide,
tetramethylammonium chloride, and any combination thereof. In some embodiments, the
quaternary ammonium salt is tetramethylammonium hydroxide.
[0047] In some embodiments, the method for preparing the fluorine-containing propylene
12
includes following steps.
[0048] Steps of liquid-phase addition reaction: 1) subjecting dichloromethane,
difluoromethane and fluorine-containing olefin to a liquid-phase addition reaction under the action
of an addition catalyst, wherein the fluorine-containing olefin is selected from the group consisting
5 of vinylidene fluoride, chlorodifluoroethylene, trifluoroethylene, chlorotrifluoroethylene, and any
combination thereof; and 2) after the addition reaction, collecting unreacted gas-phase material,
and subjecting a reaction liquid in the reaction kettle to solid-liquid separation, wherein a solid
part obtained after the solid-liquid separation is the addition catalyst, and a liquid part obtained
after the solid-liquid separation is subjected to rectification to obtain the fluorochloropropane
10 intermediate; and the unreacted gas-phase material and the addition catalyst can be reused.
[0049] Steps of gas-phase/liquid-phase dehydrochlorination reaction: 3) filling an activated
carbon catalyst in a second reactor, optionally, adding a metal alkali solution in the second reactor,
optionally, adding a mixture of a metal alkali solution and a quaternary ammonium salt in the
second reactor; 4) setting a corresponding reaction temperature, adding the fluorochloropropane
15 intermediate into the second reactor and subjecting the fluorochloropropane intermediate to a gasphase/liquid-phase dehydrochlorination reaction; and 5) subjecting a reactant to alkali washing
process and neutralizing, subjecting the resultant to rectification to obtain a fluorine-containing
propylene product.
[0050] Compared with the prior art, the present invention has the following beneficial effects.
20 [0051] 1. The present invention requires only one-step addition reaction to prepare
fluorochloropropane, with a simple technological process, mild reaction conditions, and high
product yield.
[0052] 2. The present invention, by monitoring the content of the fluorine-containing olefin in
the reaction system and adjusting the feeding rate accordingly, the polymerization of the fluorine25 containing olefin on active sites is inhibited, and the service life of the catalyst is significantly
prolonged.
[0053] 3. The three-component liquid-phase addition process of the present invention has
simple post-treatment operations, easy product separation, and high product purity, making it
13
highly suitable for industrial application.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0054] The present invention will be further illustrated in conjunction with the specific
embodiments below, but the present invention is not limited to these particular embodiments.
5 Those skilled in the art should recognize that the present invention encompasses all alternative,
modified, and equivalent forms within the scope of the claims.
[0055] In a first aspect, the present invention provides embodiments for preparing a
fluorochloropropane intermediate and comparative embodiments for preparing a
fluorochloropropane intermediate.
10 [0056] Embodiment 1
[0057] The present embodiment provided a method for preparing a 1-chloro-3,3,3-
trifluoropropane, which included following steps.
[0058] 20.2 g (0.24 mol) of anhydrous aluminum trifluoride, 18.7 g (0.14 mol) of anhydrous
aluminum trichloride and 6.1 g (0.06 mol) of aluminum oxide were weighed and added into a
15 reaction kettle. The reaction kettle was sealed and subjected to vacuum treatment. Then, 225 g of
dichloromethane was added into the reaction kettle via a sampling device, and the reaction kettle
was placed in a cooling circulation bath controlled by a cooling circulation pump at -30 degrees
centigrade and reacted for 30 min. The reaction kettle was taken out of the cooling circulation
pump, and 125 g of difluoromethane was continuously added into the reaction kettle. The
20 vinylidene fluoride was added in the reaction kettle at a flow rate of 60 g/h under pressure via a
metering pump, and a duration of the feeding process was 5 hours. After the feeding process, the
raw materials reacted under conditions of a stirring rate of 300 rpm at 30 degrees centigrade for 5
hours.
[0059] During the reaction, variation of reaction pressure in the reaction kettle and variation
25 of the temperature in the reaction kettle were recorded, and a content of the vinylidene fluoride in
the reaction kettle was monitored at the same time. Specifically, sample was collected every 30
minutes, and the sample was tested by gas-phase chromatographic analysis. The results showed
that in the whole process, the content of the vinylidene fluoride in the reaction system was smaller
14
than or equal to 2.8%. After the reaction completed and the temperature in the reaction kettle
lowered to room temperature, a gas-phase valve was opened to collect gas-phase materials (i.e.,
unreacted difluoromethane and a small amount of addition product). A liquid-phase material in the
reaction kettle was filtered, and a solid part was the addition catalyst. A filter liquor was subjected
5 to rectification to obtain a target product 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane, and the purity of the
target product 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane was 99.7%.
[0060] The liquid-phase material and the gas-phase material obtained in the addition reaction
were subjected to chromatographic analysis. It was calculated that a conversion rate of the
vinylidene fluoride was 96.2%, a selectivity of 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane was 85.6%, and a
10 selectivity of a by-product 1,3-dichloro-1,1-difluoropropane was 13.7%. A small amount of other
by-products was produced, and the by-product was identified by GC-MS analysis and as an isomer
of 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane.

[0062] The present embodiment was substantially the same as embodiment 1, except the
15 following steps. Firstly, the feeding rate of the vinylidene fluoride was improved to 100 g/h, and

[0063] Variation of the content of vinylidene fluoride in the reaction kettle was monitored,

kettle gradually reduced to 0.8%.
[0064] The liquid-phase material and the gas-phase material obtained in the addition reaction
25 were subjected to chromatographic analysis. It was calculated that a conversion rate of the

by-products was produced, and the by-product was identified by GC-MS analysis and as an isomer
15
of 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane. The product 1-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropane obtained after
rectification had a purity of 99.6%.
[0065] Embodiment 3
[0066] The present embodiment was substantially the same as embodiment 1, except the
5 following steps. Firstly, the feeding rate of the vinylidene fluoride was improved to 90 g/h, and the
duration of the feeding process of the vinylidene fluoride was 2 hours. Then, the feeding rate of
vinylidene fluoride was lowered to 40 g/h, and the duration of feeding process of difluoromethane
was 3 hours. After the feeding processes, the reaction under conditions of stirring lasted for 5 hours.
[0067] Variation of the content of vinylidene fluoride in the reaction kettle was monitored,
10 and the content of vinylidene fluoride increased as the reaction progressed. After reacted for 2
hours, the content of vinylidene fluoride in the reaction system reached 4.8%. Then, the feeding
rate of vinylidene fluorine was reduced to 40 g/h, and the content of vinylidene fluorine in the

[0068] The liquid-phase material and the gas-phase material obtained in the addition reaction
15 were subjected to chromatographic analysis. It was calculated that a conversion rate of the

20 rectification had a purity of 99.7%.

title: PROCESSES FOR PRODUCING OPTICAL EFFECTS LAYERS
abstract: The invention relates to the field of the protection of security documents such as for example banknotes and identity documents against counterfeit and illegal reproduction In particular, the present invention provides processes for producing optical effect layers (OELs) comprising at least a first motif and a second motif, each of said motifs independently comprising platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles oriented according to a specific magnetic pattern, wherein said first motif and second motif have different magnetic orientation patterns and are at least partially adjacent and in proper register.
specification:
The present invention relates to the field of processes for producing optical effect layers (OELs)
5 comprising magnetically oriented platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles. In
particular, the present invention provides processes for magnetically orienting platelet-shaped magnetic
or magnetizable pigment particles in more than one coating layers so as to produce OELs and the use
of said OELs as anti-counterfeit means on security documents or security articles as well as decorative
purposes.
10 BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002] It is known in the art to use inks, compositions, coatings or layers containing oriented magnetic
or magnetizable pigment particles, particularly also optically variable magnetic or magnetizable pigment
particles, for the production of security elements, e.g. in the field of security documents. Coatings or
layers comprising oriented magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles are disclosed for example in US
15 2,570,856; US 3,676,273; US 3,791,864; US 5,630,877; and US 5,364,689. Coatings or layers
comprising oriented magnetic color-shifting pigment particles, resulting in particularly appealing optical
effects, useful for the protection of security documents, have been disclosed in WO 2002/090002 A2
and WO 2005/002866 A1.
[003] Security features, e.g. for security documents, can generally be classified into “covert” security
20 features on the one hand, and “overt” security features on the other hand. The protection provided by
covert security features relies on the principle that such features are difficult to detect, typically requiring
specialized equipment and knowledge for detection, whereas “overt” security features rely on the
concept of being easily detectable with the unaided human senses, e.g. such features may be visible
and/or detectable via the tactile sense while still being difficult to produce and/or to copy. However, the
25 effectiveness of overt security features depends to a great extent on their easy recognition as a security
feature.
[004] Magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in printing inks or coatings allow for the production
of magnetically induced images, designs and/or patterns (also referred in the art as “Optical Effect
Layers (OELs”) through the application of a correspondingly structured magnetic field, inducing a local
30 orientation of the magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in the not yet hardened (i.e. wet) coating,
followed by the hardening of the coating. The result is a fixed and stable magnetically induced image,
design or pattern. Materials and technologies for the orientation of magnetic or magnetizable pigment
particles in coating compositions are known. The magnetically induced images in question can only be
produced by having access to both, the magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles or the
35 corresponding ink, and the particular technology employed to print said ink and to orient said pigment
in the printed ink.
[005] With the aim of optimizing and increasing the counterfeiting resistance of security documents,
in particular banknotes, striking and sophisticated magnetically induced images and optical effects
layers (OELs) have been developed. Said OELs are obtained by using specific magnetic assemblies
40 and advantageously exhibit a dynamic appearance upon tilting. Examples of such dynamic OELs
3
include reflection zone bars moving as the OEL is tilted, loop-shaped bodies moving as the OEL is tilted,
loop-shaped bodies having a varying shape as the OEL is tilted, bright areas and dark areas moving as
the OEL is tilted. WO 2012/104098 A1 discloses OELs comprising more than one magnetically induced
images, each image having a different magnetic orientation pattern. WO 2012/104098 A1 discloses an
5 OEL comprising two areas, each one exhibiting a reflection zone bar moving as the OEL is tilted, one
of said bar moving away the observer upon tilting of the OEL and the other said bar moving towards the
observer upon tilting of the OEL.
[006] Processes for producing OELs comprising at least two areas made of a single cured layer,
comprises i) applying on the substrate a UV curable ink comprising magnetic or magnetizable particles so
10 as to form a coating layer; ii) exposing the coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating
device, thereby orienting the pigment particles, iii) curing one or more first areas of the coating layer to a
second state so as to fix the magnetic or magnetizable particles in their adopted positions and orientations,
said curing being performed by selectively irradiating the coating layer with a radiation source; iv) exposing
the coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating device thereby re-orienting the
15 magnetic or magnetizable particles which are comprised in the coating layer still being in a wet, liquid state
and not yet-cured due to the selective curing of step iii) and v) curing the coating layer so as to fix the
magnetic or magnetizable particles in their new adopted positions and orientations.
[007] It is known in the art of curing a coating or ink composition for producing OELs with the help of
a UV radiation source, that the characteristics and the construction of the UV irradiation source and the
20 precise exposure conditions of the coating or ink composition to the UV radiation source are crucial for
obtaining a high-resolution image and a fast curing of the composition. However, known methods for
selective curing suffer from several drawbacks.
[008] A method includes the use of fixed photomasks including one or more voids corresponding to a
pattern to be formed as a part of an image on the coating layer being carried by the fixed substrate is
25 disclosed. However, the disclosed method may result in the potential creation of shadow effects on the
coating layer due to the constraints that a) the photomask may not touch the not yet cured ink layer, but
must be disposed at a certain distance from it, and that b) the UV-source is necessarily an extended
light source. All of these resulting in low-resolution images and require operation at low printing speeds
due to the need for keeping in a fixed constellation the substrate, the photomask, and the UV-source
30 during the exposure time. Alternatively, a fixed photomask may be used with a coating layer being carried
by a moving substrate. Said method may also result in the production of shadow effects on the coating
layer and/or image blurring due to a substrate movement at industrial speeds during exposition to
irradiation, without any possibility to implement a variable image information during printing. Alternatively,
a moving photomask may be used with a moving substrate. However, said method may also result in the
35 production of shadow effects on the coating layer resulting in a low-resolution imaging and would be
highly complex to implement.
[009] Another method uses laser beams. However, said method is known to require highly special
equipments and high costs.
[010] Another method uses LED Light Emitting Diode (LED) arrays. However, this method may suffer
40 from unnecessary losses of light density resulting in longer curing times and degrading the printing
4
performance.
[011] A need remains for improved and controlled processes for producing eye-catching optical effect
layers (OELs) for security printers at industrial speed, wherein said so-produced OELs are easily
authenticated by the man in the street while said processes are highly difficult to be implemented on a
5 mass-scale production by counterfeiters and the illicit market.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[012] Accordingly, it is an object of the present invention to overcome the deficiencies of the prior art
as discussed above. This is achieved by the provision of a process for producing an optical effect layer
10 (OEL) on a substrate (x10), said optical effect layer (OEL) comprising a first motif comprising plateletshaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles oriented according to a first magnetic pattern and
a second motif comprising the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles oriented
according to a second magnetic pattern, the first magnetic pattern being different from the second
magnetic pattern, said process comprising:
15 a first set of steps consisting of
a’) applying onto the substrate (x10) a first radiation curable coating composition, preferably a first UVVis-curable curable coating composition, exhibiting a color and comprising the platelet-shaped magnetic
or magnetizable pigment particles so as to form a first coating layer (x20’) on said substrate (x10), said
coating composition being in a first state;
20 b’) exposing the radiation curable coating composition of step a’) to a first magnetic field of a magnetic
assembly (x30’) so as to magnetically orient at least a part of the platelet-shaped magnetic or
magnetizable pigment particles;
c’) at least partially curing the radiation curable coating composition of step b’) to a second state so as
to fix the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in their adopted positions and
25 orientations and so as to produce the first motif; and
a second set of steps consisting of
a’’) applying in register a second radiation curable coating composition, preferably UV-Vis-curable
curable coating composition, having a same color as the first radiation curable coating composition of
step a’) so as to form a second coating layer (x20’’) on said substrate (x10), said coating composition
30 being in a first state, and at least a part of the second coating layer (x20’’) is adjacent to at least a part
of the first coating layer (x20’);
b’’) exposing the radiation curable coating composition of step a’’) to a second magnetic field of a
magnetic assembly (x30’’) so as to magnetically orient at least a part of the platelet-shaped magnetic or
magnetizable pigment particles; and
35 c’’) at least partially curing the radiation curable coating composition of step b’’) to a second state so as
to fix the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in their adopted positions and
orientations and so as to produce the second motif, said second motif being in proper register with the
first motif.
[013] Also described herein are processes for producing OELs comprising the first motif comprising
40 the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles oriented according to the first magnetic
5
pattern described herein, the second motif comprising the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable
pigment particles oriented according to the second magnetic pattern described herein, and a third motif
comprising the platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles oriented according to a third
magnetic pattern, wherein the first, second and third magnetic patterns are different from each other,
5 wherein at least a part of the third motif is adjacent to at least a part of the first motif and/or at least a
part of the second motif (i.e. the third motif is at least partially adjacent to and in proper register with the
first motif and/or at least partially adjacent to and in proper register with the second motif), and wherein
the process comprises the first set of steps a’), b’) and c’) described herein, the second set of steps a’’),
b’’) and c’’) described herein and a third set of steps a’’’), b’’’) and c’’’), said third step a’’’) being carried
10 out subsequently to and continuously with step c’’).
[014] Also described herein are processes wherein the second radiation curable coating composition
is applied in register on the same side of the substrate (x10) carrying the first coating layer (x20’) and
processes wherein the second radiation curable coating composition is applied in register on the
opposite side of the substrate (x10) carrying the first coating layer (x20’).
15 [015] Also described herein are optical effect layers (OELs) produced by the process described herein
and security documents as well as decorative elements and objects comprising one or more optical
OELs described herein.
[016] Also described herein are methods of manufacturing a security document or a decorative
element or object, comprising a) providing a security document or a decorative element or object, and
20 b) providing an optical effect layer obtained by the process described herein, so that it is comprised by
the security document or decorative element or object.
[017] The present invention provides processes advantageously allowing the manufacture of eyecatching optical effect layers (OELs) which are easily authenticated by the man in the street. In
particular, the OELs produced by the process described herein comprises the first and second motifs
25 described herein having the same color thus allowing an easy authentication due to the continuity of
said color while combining a high level of counterfeit resistance due to the sophisticated adjacent in
register motifs of different magnetic orientation patterns. Thanks to the controlled process described
herein and the so-obtained optical effect layers (OELs), authentication of said overt security features
allows an observer to easily discriminate against imitations (visually similar result obtained with a
30 different process) as well as against poor reproduction (obtained with the same process but less well
controlled).

title: PROCESSES FOR PRODUCING OPTICAL EFFECTS LAYERS
abstract: The invention relates to the field of the protection of security documents such as for example banknotes and identity documents against counterfeit and illegal reproduction. In particular, the present invention provides processes for producing optical effect layers (OELs) comprising at least a first motif and a second motif being at least partially adjacent to each other, each of said motifs independently comprising magnetically oriented platelet-shaped magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles.
specification:
The present invention relates to the field of processes for producing optical effect layers (OELs)

particular, the present invention provides processes for magnetically orienting platelet-shaped magnetic
or magnetizable pigment particles in more than one coating layers so as to produce OELs and the use

10 BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002] It is known in the art to use inks, compositions, coatings or layers containing oriented magnetic
or magnetizable pigment particles, particularly also optically variable magnetic or magnetizable pigment
particles, for the production of security elements, e.g. in the field of security documents. Coatings or
layers comprising oriented magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles are disclosed for example in US
15 2,570,856; US 3,676,273; US 3,791,864; US 5,630,877; and US 5,364,689. Coatings or layers
comprising oriented magnetic color-shifting pigment particles, resulting in particularly appealing optical
effects, useful for the protection of security documents, have been disclosed in WO 2002/090002 A2
and WO 2005/002866 A1.
[003] Security features, e.g. for security documents, can generally be classified into “covert” security
20 features on the one hand, and “overt” security features on the other hand. The protection provided by
covert security features relies on the principle that such features are difficult to detect, typically requiring
specialized equipment and knowledge for detection, whereas “overt” security features rely on the
concept of being easily detectable with the unaided human senses, e.g. such features may be visible
and/or detectable via the tactile sense while still being difficult to produce and/or to copy. However, the
25 effectiveness of overt security features depends to a great extent on their easy recognition as a security
feature.
[004] Magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in printing inks or coatings allow for the production
of magnetically induced images, designs and/or patterns (also referred in the art as “Optical Effect
Layers (OELs”) through the application of a correspondingly structured magnetic field, inducing a local
30 orientation of the magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles in the not yet hardened (i.e. wet) coating,
followed by the hardening of the coating. The result is a fixed and stable magnetically induced image,
design or pattern. Materials and technologies for the orientation of magnetic or magnetizable pigment
particles in coating compositions are known. The magnetically induced images in question can only be
produced by having access to both, the magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles or the
35 corresponding ink, and the particular technology employed to print said ink and to orient said pigment
in the printed ink.
[005] With the aim of optimizing and increasing the counterfeiting resistance of security documents,
in particular banknotes, striking and sophisticated magnetically induced images and optical effects
layers (OELs) have been developed. Said OELs are obtained by using specific magnetic assemblies
40 and advantageously exhibit a dynamic appearance upon tilting. Examples of such dynamic OELs
3
include reflection zone bars moving as the OEL is tilted, loop-shaped bodies moving as the OEL is tilted,
loop-shaped bodies having a varying shape as the OEL is tilted, bright areas and dark areas moving as
the OEL is tilted. WO 2012/104098 A1 discloses OELs comprising more than one magnetically induced
images. WO 2012/104098 A1 discloses an OEL comprising two areas, each one exhibiting a reflection
5 zone bar moving as the OEL is tilted, one of said bar moving away the observer upon tilting of the OEL
and the other said bar moving towards the observer upon tilting of the OEL.
[006] Processes for producing OELs comprising at least two areas made of a single cured layer,
comprises i) applying on the substrate a UV curable ink comprising magnetic or magnetizable particles so
as to form a coating layer; ii) exposing the coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating
10 device, thereby orienting the pigment particles, iii) curing one or more first areas of the coating layer to a
second state so as to fix the magnetic or magnetizable particles in their adopted positions and orientations,
said curing being performed by selectively irradiating the coating layer with a radiation source; iv) exposing
the coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating device thereby re-orienting the
magnetic or magnetizable particles which are comprised in the coating layer still being in a wet, liquid state
15 and not yet-cured due to the selective curing of step iii) and v) curing the coating layer so as to fix the
magnetic or magnetizable particles in their new adopted positions and orientations.
[007] It is known in the art of curing a coating or ink composition for producing OELs with the help of
a UV radiation source, that the characteristics and the construction of the UV irradiation source and the
precise exposure conditions of the coating or ink composition to the UV radiation source are crucial for
20 obtaining a high-resolution image and a fast curing of the composition. However, known methods for
selective curing suffer from several drawbacks.
[008] A method includes the use of fixed photomasks including one or more voids corresponding to a
pattern to be formed as a part of an image on the coating layer being carried by the fixed substrate is
disclosed. However, the disclosed method may result in the potential creation of shadow effects on the
25 coating layer due to the constraints that a) the photomask may not touch the not yet cured ink layer, but
must be disposed at a certain distance from it, and that b) the UV-source is necessarily an extended
light source. All of these resulting in low-resolution images and require operation at low printing speeds
due to the need for keeping in a fixed constellation the substrate, the photomask, and the UV-source
during the exposure time. Alternatively, a fixed photomask may be used with a coating layer being carried
30 by a moving substrate. Said method may also result in the production of shadow effects on the coating
layer and/or image blurring due to a substrate movement at industrial speeds during exposition to
irradiation, without any possibility to implement a variable image information during printing. Alternatively,
a moving photomask may be used with a moving substrate. However, said method may also result in the
production of shadow effects on the coating layer resulting in a low-resolution imaging and would be
35 highly complex to implement.
[009] Another method uses laser beams. However, said method is known to require highly special
equipments and high costs.
[010] Another method uses LED Light Emitting Diode (LED) arrays. However, this method may suffer
from unnecessary losses of light density resulting in longer curing times and degrading the printing
40 performance.
4
[011] Processes for producing OELs comprising at least two areas made of two different inks involve
several passes on a printing press such as disclosed in EP 2 433 798 B1. Said processes comprise i)
applying on a substrate a first UV curable ink comprising magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles so
as to form a first coating layer; ii) exposing the first coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field5 generating device, thereby orienting the pigment particles, iii) curing the first coating layer to a second
state so as to fix the pigment particles in their adopted positions and orientations, iv) removing the substrate
carrying the first coating from the printing press and re-introducing in said press so as to v) apply a second
UV curable ink comprising magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles so as to form a second coating
layer; vi) exposing the second coating layer to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating device,
10 thereby orienting the pigment particles, and vii) curing the second coating layer to a second state so as to
fix the pigment particles in their adopted positions and orientations. Due to the requirement of several
passes in the printing press, said processes require a tedious and time-consuming alignment of the
substrate prior to the second application step. Since said alignment is highly difficult to control and achieve,
a significant amount of optical effect layers suffering from a poor and unacceptable register are obtained
15 thus leading to a high amount of wasted substrates and inks.
[012] Alternatively, OELs comprising at least two areas made of two different inks may be produced
with processes comprising i) applying on a substrate a first UV curable ink comprising magnetic or
magnetizable pigment particles so as to form a first coating layer; ii) applying on the substrate a second
UV curable ink comprising magnetic or magnetizable pigment particles so as to form a second coating
20 layer, iii) exposing the coating layers to the magnetic field of a magnetic-field-generating device, thereby
orienting the pigment particles, iv) curing the first and second coating layers to a second state so as to fix
the pigment particles in their adopted positions and orientations. However, said method is extremely
complex to be implemented since it implies printing the two inks in a liquid state and requires the printing
of the second ink while the first ink is still liquid without disturbing it thus allowing only the preparation of
25 spaced apart coating layers.
[013] A need remains for improved and controlled processes for producing eye-catching optical effect
layers (OELs) for security printers at industrial speed, wherein said so-produced OELs are easily
authenticated by the man in the street while said processes are highly difficult to be implemented on a
mass-scale production by counterfeiters and the illicit market.

20 step b’) and a second magnetic assembly (x30’’) is used during step b’’), wherein said assemblies are
