title: VEHICLE MOUNTED SMART SYSTEM FOR SOURCE-LEVEL SEGREGATION OF MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE
abstract: The present invention discloses a vehicle-mounted smart system (100) and method for source-level segregation of municipal solid waste. The system comprises a waste input hopper (101) equipped with a QR code scanner (102) for source authentication of incoming waste, a weighing platform (103) for automatic weight measurement, and a primary storage chamber (104). A mechanical squeezer (105) separates the waste into solid waste, which is collected in a solid storage tank (106), and leachate, which is collected in a leachate tank (107). A sensor unit (108) monitors pH, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), and temperature of the leachate. An IoT transmission module (109) and a GPS and capacity monitoring module (110) enable real-time data transmission and vehicle tracking to a central server communication module (111). The central server processes the data to predict biogas yield from leachate, forecast waste generation patterns, and improve fermentation efficiency. The invention enables efficient on-site segregation, real-time monitoring, and data-driven waste management.
specification:
VEHICLE MOUNTED SMART SYSTEM FOR SOURCE-LEVEL SEGREGATION OF MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[001]	The present invention relates to the field of waste management, renewable energy generation, and environmental engineering. More particularly, the invention relates to a vehicle mounted smart system integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) for segregation of municipal solid waste into solid waste and leachate extraction which can be further converted into valuable products such as biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilizers.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002]	Municipal solid waste (MSW) management is a major challenge for urban local bodies. Improper segregation leads to inefficient processing, environmental pollution, and loss of recoverable resources. Leachate generated from mixed waste contains both organic and inorganic components and is often treated as waste rather than a resource.
[003]	Rapid urbanization, population growth, and changing consumption patterns have led to a massive increase in municipal solid waste generation in India. As per available data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), India generates approximately 160,000 tonnes per day (TPD) of MSW, with projections indicating a rise to over 165 million tonnes annually by 2030. Of the collected waste, a significant portion—often exceeding 50%—undergoes limited or no scientific treatment, while substantial amounts are disposed of in unscientific landfills or remain unaccounted for. Over 90% of MSW in urban areas is traditionally disposed of in open dumps or landfills, leading to severe environmental degradation, including soil and groundwater contamination, greenhouse gas emissions (particularly methane), and public health hazards.
[004]	Effective segregation at source or processing stage remains a critical challenge. Mixed waste complicates downstream processing, reduces the efficiency of recycling, composting, or energy recovery, and increases operational costs for municipalities. Leachate, the liquid percolating through waste in landfills or during processing, poses additional risks as a major source of pollution if not properly managed. Traditional waste management systems in India largely rely on manual sorting, which is labor-intensive, inconsistent, error-prone, and inefficient at scale. Conventional treatment methods, such as basic landfilling or rudimentary composting, fail to maximize resource recovery and often result in low yields of biogas or poor-quality by-products.
[005]	While some advancements exist in bio methanation, waste-to-energy plants, and basic segregation technologies, these systems frequently suffer from limitations such as lack of real-time monitoring, poor adaptability to heterogeneous waste composition, high dependency on manual intervention, suboptimal leachate handling, and inadequate integration of data-driven decision-making. IoT and AI/ML have shown promise in smart waste applications globally (e.g., for bin monitoring, route optimization, and automated sorting), but integrated solutions tailored for Indian Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) characteristics—combining intelligent segregation, leachate extraction, and valorization into biogas, bio-CNG, and fertilizers—remain limited or fragmented.
[006]	Existing bio methanation systems primarily focus on solid organic waste and do not utilize leachate efficiently. Additionally, there is a lack of real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent logistics management in current waste collection systems. Therefore, there is a need for an integrated system that ensures source-level segregation, efficient leachate utilization, real-time monitoring, and optimized waste collection and processing.

[007]	The present invention aims to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks of the prior art by providing a comprehensive, intelligent, and scalable solution for Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) management.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[008]	 The present invention discloses a vehicle mounted smart, integrated system for source-level segregation of municipal solid waste, real-time extraction of leachate from collected solid waste, IoT-based monitoring of waste collection, vehicle capacity, and logistics - AI/ML-based prediction of biogas generation and waste patterns and ultimately, bio methanation of leachate for production of biogas and upgraded fuels. 
[009]	 In one aspect of the present invention, a vehicle mounted smart integrating system comprises of waste input hopper, QR Code Scanner Unit, weighing unit, primary storage chamber, mechanical squeezer, leachate tank, sensor unit, Iot transmission module, GPS and leachate capacity monitoring module and central server communication module.

[0010]	In another aspect of the present invention, the vehicle mounted smart system ensures source-level authentication, precise quantification, efficient separation of solid waste and leachate, and real-time IoT-based monitoring of leachate extraction. It significantly improves the quality of collected waste streams for downstream valorization into biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilizers while supporting circular economy

[0011]	In yet another aspect of the present invention, the vehicle mounted smart system provides a scalable, intelligent, and environmentally sustainable solution for modern municipal solid waste management.

title: Computerized Yarn Cross-Sectional Geometry Analyzer with AI and Environmental Simulation
abstract:
Computerized Yarn Cross-Sectional Geometry Analyzer with AI and Environmental Simulation
This invention describes an automated apparatus for yarn cross-sectional geometry analysis employing step-rotational imaging, computerized three-dimensional reconstruction, and artificial intelligence–based classification. A yarn specimen is rotated in calibrated angular increments, with high-resolution images captured and processed to generate a digital twin of its cross-sectional structure. The reconstructed model is analyzed by trained algorithms to classify geometries—circular, elliptical, collapsed, or irregular—and to correlate anomalies with predictive mechanical behaviors including tensile strength, elasticity, and wear resistance. The apparatus optionally incorporates an environmental simulation chamber capable of varying humidity, temperature, salinity, and pressure, thereby enabling evaluation of yarn deformation under operational and extreme conditions such as aerospace or marine environments. An inline monitoring configuration allows real-time assessment during spinning and weaving processes, issuing alerts upon deviation from control parameters. The invention thus provides an objective, reproducible, and predictive framework for textile quality assurance, performance validation, and certification.
specification:
FIELD OF INVENTION

[0001] This invention relates to the field of textile engineering more particularly, to automated systems and methods for the computerized analysis of yarn cross-sectional geometry. The invention is directed to an apparatus that employs step-rotational imaging in conjunction with high-resolution photo-microscopy, computational three-dimensional reconstruction, and artificial intelligence–based classification to evaluate yarn structural characteristics with accuracy and reproducibility. The apparatus is further configured to simulate operational stress conditions, including variations in humidity, temperature, salinity, and atmospheric pressure, thereby enabling performance analysis under real-world and extreme environments. Additionally, the invention encompasses an inline monitoring configuration for integration with spinning and weaving equipment, providing continuous quality assessment during textile production. By combining imaging precision, intelligent analysis, environmental adaptability, and real-time monitoring, the invention advances textile characterization and predictive performance evaluation across industrial, defense, aerospace, and academic applications.

PRIOR ART AND PROBLEM TO BE SOLVED


[0002]  Yarn geometry—defined by parameters like cross-sectional shape, fiber packing, twist, and density—is a foundational determinant of textile performance characteristics such as tensile strength, dye uptake, abrasion resistance, and elasticity. Accurate assessment of this geometry is essential for engineering materials with precision functionalities, such as flame resistance in firefighter uniforms, aerodynamic drag reduction in sportswear, or tensile stability in aerospace fabrics. Conventionally, yarn cross-sectional analysis is carried out using destructive sampling methods. A short length of yarn is embedded in resin, sliced using a microtome, and observed under a microscope. This manual method is time-consuming, prone to human error, and lacks reproducibility. More critically, it provides only a static, 2D snapshot of a geometry that is intrinsically dynamic. Yarns, especially those composed of synthetic filaments or designed for composite integration, undergo continuous deformation due to mechanical tension, environmental changes (like humidity and temperature), and even orientation with respect to gravity. This dynamism becomes critical
 
in high-performance applications—e.g., in aerospace environments where yarns are exposed to fluctuating temperatures and near-zero gravity, or in impact-protective garments where material integrity depends on rapid, transient structural responses. Static imaging, therefore, is insufficient and potentially misleading.

[0003]  The textile industry faces significant limitations in accurately characterizing yarn geometry, particularly when precision and reproducibility are critical. Current methods for assessing yarn cross-sections rely heavily on manual processes that introduce a high degree of variability and are prone to operator error. These conventional approaches, such as slicing and microscopy, are inherently destructive—rendering the yarn sample unusable for further evaluation or practical use. Additionally, these methods only offer a static, two-dimensional view of a highly dynamic and three-dimensional structure. Yarn behavior is far from fixed; it deforms under mechanical tension, environmental stress, and gravitational influence. This is particularly problematic in applications involving synthetic or composite yarns, where even slight deviations in cross-sectional geometry can drastically alter material performance. Despite the increasing complexity and specialization of yarns in modern textiles, no reliable method exists for analyzing their structure in real-time or under actual working conditions. This lack of in-situ and inline measurement capabilities severely hampers innovation, quality control, and material optimization.

[0004] Several technologies have been developed in an attempt to overcome the limitations of traditional yarn geometry analysis. One such approach involves the use of high-resolution optical microscopy combined with automated image processing algorithms. While this method aims to reduce human error, it still requires the destructive slicing of yarn samples and cannot accommodate dynamic, real-use deformations. Advanced imaging modalities like X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) have been explored for non-destructive 3D reconstruction of yarn cross-sections. Although they offer detailed insights, these techniques are costly, slow, and unsuitable for industrial-scale or real-time implementation. Laser scanning and profilometry techniques, including confocal laser scanning microscopy, provide surface mapping capabilities that can infer cross-sectional shape, but they also depend on stabilizing and mounting the yarn, which negates the ability to capture behavior under operational stress. Recently, machine learning models have been applied to infer geometry from visual data, offering some promise for non-invasive analysis. However, these models require extensive training on labeled datasets and tend to falter when applied to novel, non-standard yarn types or when the yarn undergoes mechanical deformation.
 
None of these technologies offer a holistic, automated solution capable of simulating real-world conditions or providing continuous analysis during yarn production.

[0005]  To resolve the above mentioned problem here the invention overcomes these limitations by introducing an automated system that captures rotational microscopic images of yarn samples at 100 discrete angles. These images are computationally reconstructed into a 3D model, enabling precise measurement of cross-sectional attributes. The system integrates artificial intelligence to classify yarn shapes and predict how deviations affect end-use behavior. Deployed either as a laboratory instrument or inline quality-control module, the system ensures continuous, objective, and reproducible yarn analysis. It provides industries with predictive insights into yarn behavior under operational conditions and establishes a digital database of yarn profiles, supporting traceability, quality benchmarking, and certification.

THE OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION:


[0006]  It has already been proposed that despite the various technologies developed to address yarn geometry analysis, significant problems persist. Existing solutions do not support real-time or inline implementation, meaning that manufacturers and engineers cannot monitor yarn behavior as it is produced or used. High-end techniques like micro-CT, while non-destructive, are impractical for routine deployment due to their cost, complexity, and slow throughput. Even advanced optical and laser scanning systems are fundamentally limited by their requirement for sample stabilization, thereby excluding dynamic, in-situ measurements. Efforts involving machine learning are heavily reliant on pre-existing datasets and struggle to generalize across diverse yarn types and environmental conditions. Crucially, no existing technology offers analytical correlation between observed geometry and the resulting physical properties of the yarn, such as strength, flexibility, or thermal resistance. As a result, there is a disconnect between geometric analysis and practical performance assessment. Moreover, none of the current methods can replicate or observe yarn behavior under variable mechanical loading, temperature fluctuation, or gravitational orientation—conditions that are central to the real-world use of technical and high-performance textiles. This technological shortfall leaves the field unable to fully characterize or optimize yarn-based materials for modern, demanding applications.
 
[0007]  The principal objective of the invention is to provide a comprehensive and integrated system capable of performing precise, reproducible, and automated analysis of yarn cross-sectional geometry. The invention is directed toward enabling step-wise rotational imaging of yarn specimens, wherein high-resolution images are captured at calibrated angular increments and subsequently processed through a computerized three-dimensional reconstruction engine. The reconstructed models are subjected to advanced artificial intelligence algorithms that classify yarn cross-sectional geometries into defined categories, including circular, oval, collapsed, and irregular forms. Further, the invention is configured to simulate environmental stressors within a controlled micro-chamber, including but not limited to variations in humidity, salt exposure, temperature fluctuations, and reduced pressure conditions, thereby permitting the analysis of yarn behavior under operational environments. The system is further adapted for inline integration with spinning and weaving equipment such that real-time monitoring of yarn geometry may be achieved without interruption of the production process.

[0008] Another objective of the invention is to provide a non-destructive and operator-independent methodology for yarn cross-sectional evaluation, thereby eliminating the inconsistencies and subjectivities associated with manual or conventional optical inspection techniques. This objective ensures that the assessment of textile quality, strength, and mechanical predictability is not dependent on human interpretation but is instead governed by quantifiable, algorithmic analysis.

[0009]  The further objective of the invention is to establish a permanent and traceable digital twin of each analyzed yarn specimen, wherein the three-dimensional cross-sectional data may be stored, retrieved, and compared across multiple production batches or industrial sites. This facilitates robust quality assurance, regulatory compliance, and cross-factory consistency verification, thereby strengthening standardization in the textile industry.

[0010] The further objective of the invention is to enhance predictive modeling of yarn performance by correlating anomalies detected in cross-sectional geometry with known mechanical properties and failure modes. This predictive capacity extends the utility of the system beyond mere structural analysis, enabling proactive interventions in textile design, production control, and material certification.

[0011] The further objective of the invention is to provide modular adaptability, wherein the apparatus may function as a standalone laboratory instrument for research and certification
 
purposes, or alternatively, as an inline monitoring module configured for continuous industrial operation. This adaptability ensures that the system may be deployed across diverse operational settings, including academic research laboratories, industrial production floors, and specialized fields such as aerospace and defense textile evaluation.

[0012]  The further objective of the invention is to the mechanization of yarn imaging, but to the establishment of a fully integrated framework combining automated step-rotational capture, AI-based digital reconstruction, environmental condition simulation, and inline real-time monitoring, thereby advancing the field of textile metrology from static, manual observation toward a dynamic, intelligent, and legally certifiable standard of analysis.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION


[0013] From the perspective of high-performance and technical applications, yarn deformation under stress is not merely a theoretical concern but a practical and safety-critical issue. In contexts such as aerospace textiles, parachute systems, and impact-resistant garments, even minor fluctuations in geometry can compromise functionality. Yet, conventional analysis methods remain blind to these dynamic transformations. In the manufacturing sector, the demand for real-time monitoring of yarn properties is rapidly growing, especially as yarns become increasingly complex with embedded electronics, conductive fibers, or smart functionalities. Although inline testing systems exist for parameters like yarn tension and twist, there is a conspicuous absence of tools capable of capturing geometric characteristics continuously during production. This gap leads to inconsistent quality and wasted material. From a materials science standpoint, accurate geometric data is vital for simulation and modeling tasks, especially when designing composite yarns or advanced woven structures. Without real-time geometry inputs, digital twins and finite element models remain speculative and often inaccurate. Lastly, sustainability considerations add further pressure to replace destructive and resource-intensive testing methods. The waste generated by embedding resins, discarded samples, and manual inspection is incompatible with the textile industry’s growing push toward eco-friendly practices and lifecycle accountability.

[0014]  So here in this invention a precision instrument for automated yarn cross-sectional geometry evaluation, designed to advance textile testing from manual inspection toward intelligent, digital analysis. At its core, the system rotates yarn specimens in calibrated micro-steps, capturing 100 photo-microscopic images per revolution. These are processed by advanced reconstruction software to generate a digital twin of the yarn’s structure.
 
[0015]  The analytical suite measures dimensional attributes such as diameter variation, roundness, and cross-sectional irregularity, while neural-network-based AI models classify geometrical profiles into standardized categories. Beyond classification, correlations are drawn between observed shapes and performance indicators like tensile failure, elasticity loss, or dye irregularities.

[0016]  For high-demand sectors such as aerospace and defense, the system offers an optional micro-environmental chamber that replicates stressors—humidity, salt spray, extreme temperatures, and microgravity conditions. This enables predictive modeling of yarn deformation under actual usage conditions.

[0017]  The invention further includes an inline configuration, where it can be mounted onto spinning or weaving machinery. In this mode, yarn geometry is assessed continuously without halting production, with real-time alerts issued upon detection of non-compliant profiles.

[0018] Thus, the disclosed apparatus establishes an intelligent framework for yarn quality assurance, merging structural analysis, AI-driven predictions, and environmental adaptability into a scalable, industrially relevant solution.

[0024]  The present invention is a specialized system designed to overcome the deficiencies inherent in conventional methods of yarn evaluation. The primary purpose of the invention is to provide a non-destructive, objective, and reproducible means of analyzing yarn cross-sectional geometry, thereby enhancing textile quality assurance, predictive performance evaluation, and regulatory compliance across industrial and research domains.
[0025] The invention is utilized to assess yarn structure under both standard and stress-induced conditions. Its application extends beyond simple dimensional measurement to the generation of digital twins that accurately represent yarn cross-sections in three-dimensional space. By employing an automated rotational imaging methodology coupled with advanced
 
reconstruction software, the invention produces highly precise digital profiles of yarn specimens. These digital models are then subjected to artificial intelligence classification techniques that identify, with a high degree of accuracy, whether a yarn exhibits circular, elliptical, collapsed, or irregular structural characteristics. The invention thereby provides insight not merely into geometry but also into the mechanical implications of such geometry, offering predictive correlations with strength, elasticity, dye uptake, and other performance parameters.
[0026]  A defining feature of the invention lies in its capacity to simulate environmental stressors that replicate operational or extreme conditions. The system is configured to expose yarn specimens to controlled variations of humidity, temperature, salinity, and pressure, thereby enabling the study of structural deformations that arise under real-world conditions, including those encountered in aerospace, defense, and marine textile applications. This capability ensures that yarns may be certified and validated for performance prior to deployment in mission-critical or high-stress environments.
[0027] Equally significant is the adaptability of the invention for deployment within continuous production settings. The system is designed to operate either as a standalone laboratory-grade instrument for academic, industrial, or certification purposes, or alternatively, as an inline monitoring module seamlessly integrated with spinning or weaving operations. In the inline configuration, the invention performs real-time evaluation of yarn cross-sections without interruption of production, issuing immediate alerts when deviations from control parameters are detected. This continuous oversight introduces a preventive layer of quality control, reducing waste, enhancing efficiency, and ensuring consistency in large-scale manufacturing.
[0028]  The invention further distinguishes itself by creating a permanent and traceable digital archive of yarn analyses. Each yarn sample examined through the system is converted into a digital twin that may be stored, retrieved, and compared across production batches or geographical manufacturing sites. Such traceability strengthens quality management frameworks, supports international certification standards, and establishes an auditable record for compliance in regulated industries.
[0029]  In its totality, the invention is not limited to a singular operational function but constitutes an integrated framework for intelligent textile metrology. It combines automated imaging, intelligent reconstruction, environmental simulation, and continuous monitoring into a unified methodology that advances the science of yarn evaluation. By transforming traditional manual observation into a legally certifiable digital standard, the invention provides an indispensable tool for industries where precision, reliability, and predictive validation of yarn performance are paramount.
 
[0030] Here the apparatus presents as a compact, bench-grade scientific instrument with a rectilinear silhouette softened by radiused edges and continuous fillets, yielding a deliberate impression of precision and stability. The primary enclosure is formed of a rigid metallic shell exhibiting a satin or bead-blasted finish with low-gloss reflectivity to suppress glare under laboratory luminaires. The visible surfaces are uninterrupted by exposed fasteners, employing concealed seam treatments that read as crisp shadow lines at panel interfaces. The colorway is neutral and professional—typically a graphite or natural anodized tone—contrasted by a lighter fascia that frames the user-interaction zone and visually centers the working aperture.
[0031]  The front elevation is organized around a clear viewing portal proportioned to the internal working volume, allowing the user to observe the specimen region without visual distortion. The portal is flush-bonded into the façade to present a planar surface that is easy to sanitize and resistant to scratching, with its perimeter captured by a micro-bezel that sits proud by a minimal, uniform offset. Surrounding the portal, the fascia transitions into a shallow chamfer that guides the eye toward the interactive interface and establishes an intuitive visual hierarchy between observation and control.
[0032]  To the right or left of the viewing portal, depending on handedness configuration, resides an integrated touch interface with a tempered cover lens and anti-smudge oleophobic coating. The display appears optically laminated to the cover lens to eliminate parallax and to deliver high legibility of numeric readouts and status banners. Beneath the active area, a narrow light guide forms a continuous status indicator bar that conveys machine state through steady or pulsed illumination patterns. The surface of the interface zone is monolithic, with all haptics implemented under-glass, such that cleaning may be performed in a single, uninterrupted wipe path.
[0033]  The upper plane of the apparatus resolves into a gently crowned top cover designed to shed incidental liquids away from the viewing portal and interface. Discrete ventilation louvers are recessed into shadowed regions and are visually masked by perforation arrays aligned to the enclosure’s datum lines. Branding and compliance markings are applied as low-contrast transfers on the non-interactive faces, maintaining a subdued, technical aesthetic while ensuring legibility for regulatory inspection. Corners terminate in consistent radii that match the front-face fillets, creating a coherent industrial design language when viewed from oblique angles.
[0034] The side profiles are intentionally quiet, featuring continuous panels that taper imperceptibly toward the rear to slim the visual mass of the instrument on a bench. Flush-mounted carry grips are sculpted into the sidewalls; when not in use, they read as subtle negative-relief features, preserving the instrument’s planar geometry. Along the lower
 
beltline, a shadow gap visually lifts the enclosure above the supporting surface and conceals a compliant mounting system that dampens environmental vibrations, yet the gap remains uniform to maintain the design’s measured precision.
[0035]  The rear panel is service-oriented and visually disciplined. Connective interfaces are arrayed along a single horizontal datum and recessed within a cable-management trough that routes conductors to either lateral edge, thereby preventing visible cable drape across the user’s working zone. Each receptacle is iconographically labeled with laser-etched legends. A safety interlock indicator and tamper-evident seal region are co-located in the upper right quadrant, framed by a thin emboss that differentiates regulatory elements from user I/O without visual clutter. A removable dust cover may be provided for unused ports, colored to harmonize with the enclosure rather than introduce visual noise.
[0036]  The base of the apparatus is articulated to communicate permanence and alignment. Four low-profile feet are nested behind a continuous skirting line so that, in normal viewing, the apparatus appears to float just above the bench. Where mobility is required in larger formats, concealed micro-casters retract within the base profile to avoid disrupting the instrument’s stance. The underside includes a recessed label well that preserves the continuity of the exterior planes, ensuring that inventory or asset tags do not protrude or collect soil during cleaning cycles.
[0037] When furnished with the environmental simulation capability, the external expression remains unified and restrained. The working aperture elongates subtly in the vertical axis, and the enclosure extends rearward in a controlled increment that reads as an integrated volume rather than an add-on. Exterior seams around the extended volume are gasketed and visually compressed, communicating containment and reinforcing the perception of environmental integrity.
[0038] In an inline production configuration, the apparatus adopts a modular envelope with orthogonal faces designed to key against standard machine-frame members. The front face substitutes the bench-top viewing portal with a longitudinal inspection slit shielded by a transparent, shatter-resistant curtain that remains optically clear. Status annunciators are promoted to larger, tri-segment light columns positioned at the upper corners to ensure visibility across the manufacturing aisle, while the touch interface pivots on a low-profile arm so the operator can swivel the display into the safe envelope of adjacent equipment. The exterior maintains the same restrained finishes and radii, preserving visual continuity across laboratory and factory deployments.
 
[0039] Throughout all embodiments, the tactile experience is deliberately minimized to planar touches, smooth radii, and cool metallic temperatures consistent with precision instrumentation. Tolerances at panel breaks are uniform to the eye and fingertip, communicating accuracy before operation commences. Every exterior interaction—viewing, touching, cleaning, and observing status—is forecast by the enclosure’s visual grammar: the portal invites inspection, the interface presents control, the light bar and columns broadcast state, and the quiet profiles recede, ensuring that the user’s attention is captured only where action is intended.
[0040]  Collectively, the external appearance operates as a declaration of function and compliance. The apparatus reads as sealed, sanitary, and methodical, signaling that imaging accuracy, environmental stewardship, and operational continuity are not merely internal capabilities but are embodied in the visible architecture. The result, when encountered by a user in a laboratory or an industrial aisle, is an instrument that presents immediate comprehensibility of purpose, disciplined restraint in form, and a level of finish commensurate with certification-grade textile metrology.
[0041]  The apparatus is constituted of a series of interdependent modules, each of which performs a distinct yet complementary function that, when integrated, forms a seamless analytical framework. At the foundation lies the yarn holding and rotational drive assembly, which serves as the specimen interface. This unit secures the yarn sample under calibrated tension to ensure positional stability and then advances it in micro-stepped increments dictated by a programmable motor system. The precision of this module is critical, for every rotational advance defines the angular fidelity of the imaging process. Its integration with the imaging assembly is orchestrated through a synchronized control system that ensures that each incremental rotation is immediately followed by an imaging sequence, thereby eliminating positional lag and guaranteeing angular continuity across the dataset.
[0042]  The imaging subsystem comprises a high-resolution photo-microscope assembly, equipped with calibrated optics and a digital sensor of sufficient pixel density to capture the minute variations in yarn cross-sectional geometry. The lighting arrangement is harmonized with the optics to eliminate shadow artifacts and maintain consistent illumination across all angular positions. This subsystem communicates directly with the rotational unit such that every micro-step triggers a precisely timed capture, preventing motion blur and ensuring dimensional accuracy. The images generated here are not static representations but constitute raw data inputs for the reconstruction engine, meaning that the imaging assembly is inherently dependent upon and synchronized with both the mechanical precision of the rotation system and the computational demands of the software layer.
 
[0043] The computational engine forms the analytical core of the invention. It receives the sequential image dataset, aligns them within a common coordinate framework, and reconstructs a digital twin of the yarn cross-section using volumetric rendering techniques. This three-dimensional model allows for calculation of geometric parameters such as roundness, eccentricity, and sectional asymmetry. Within the same environment, an artificial intelligence module—trained on extensive datasets of yarn structures and corresponding mechanical behaviors—classifies the reconstructed geometry into predetermined categories such as circular, elliptical, collapsed, or irregular. The intelligence layer does not operate in isolation; it references historical datasets and performance metrics, thereby enabling predictive modeling of mechanical outcomes such as tensile failure, elasticity degradation, or dye penetration anomalies. Thus, the computational subsystem integrates inputs from the imaging assembly, cross-validates them with algorithmic learning, and outputs actionable classifications and predictions.
[0044] To extend analysis beyond static laboratory conditions, the apparatus incorporates an optional environmental simulation chamber. This module encloses the yarn specimen and exposes it to controlled variations of humidity, temperature, salinity, and atmospheric pressure. The chamber interfaces seamlessly with the rotational and imaging assemblies, such that the environmental variables can be altered dynamically while the step-rotational imaging continues uninterrupted. The significance of this integration is that the three-dimensional reconstruction and AI classification can be performed not only under ambient conditions but also under simulated operational stresses. For example, deformation detected under high humidity or reduced pressure is directly recorded and correlated to predictive failure models, thereby enabling condition-specific certification of yarn performance.
[0045] The inline monitoring module represents an industrial extension of the invention. Configured for integration with spinning or weaving lines, this module adapts the rotational and imaging principles into a compact, pass-through design. Here, the yarn is monitored continuously as it progresses along the production path, with optical sensors and dynamic rotation mechanisms adapted to accommodate motion. The inline module remains tethered to the computational engine, allowing for real-time reconstruction and AI analysis. Alerts are issued instantly when the geometry deviates from predetermined control parameters, ensuring immediate corrective action. The integration of this module with the broader system allows the same dataset architecture to be employed, meaning that laboratory evaluations, environmental simulations, and production-line monitoring are all harmonized within a single analytical framework.
 
[0046]  Each component of the apparatus, while individually functional, derives its full utility only through integration with the others. The rotational unit ensures angular accuracy, which directly affects imaging fidelity. The imaging assembly provides raw data, which in turn dictates the resolution and accuracy of the computational reconstruction. The computational engine transforms this raw data into classified, predictive outputs, which gain added dimensionality when coupled with the environmental chamber. Finally, the inline module extends the system into industrial operation, ensuring that the analytical rigor of laboratory-grade testing is preserved under real-time manufacturing conditions. The collective interplay of these modules produces a system that transcends the limitations of traditional inspection, advancing yarn analysis into a domain characterized by automation, intelligence, and environmental adaptability.
[0047] The working of the “Automated Apparatus for Yarn Cross-Sectional Geometry Analysis Using Step-Rotational Imaging, AI-Based 3D Reconstruction, Environmental Simulation, and Inline Monitoring” is structured as a coordinated sequence of mechanical, optical, and computational operations, each stage being interdependent and collectively producing a comprehensive analytical outcome. The process commences with the secure placement of a yarn specimen within the holding and rotational mechanism, where the yarn is maintained under calibrated conditions of alignment and tension to ensure dimensional stability during testing. Upon initiation of the programmed sequence, the rotational system advances the specimen in predetermined angular increments, each advancement being of 3.6 degrees, thereby completing a full 360-degree revolution across one hundred discrete steps. The controlled stepping action ensures that each angular position of the yarn cross-section is uniquely represented without overlap or omission, thereby guaranteeing the completeness of the dataset.
[0048] At each rotational increment, the imaging assembly is triggered in exact temporal synchronization, capturing a high-resolution microscopic image of the yarn’s cross-section. The illumination and focus parameters remain constant across all captures to eliminate variability arising from external conditions. The resultant collection of images forms a sequential dataset that represents the specimen’s geometry across the entire angular spectrum. These images are transmitted in real time to the computational engine, where advanced software routines perform alignment, normalization, and volumetric integration to generate a three-dimensional digital twin of the yarn cross-section.
[0049]  Once the reconstruction is complete, the artificial intelligence engine is engaged. Utilizing neural network models trained on extensive datasets of yarn morphologies and associated performance metrics, the system classifies the reconstructed geometry into standardized categories including circular, elliptical, collapsed, and irregular. Beyond classification, the
 
artificial intelligence module executes predictive correlations, mapping the detected geometrical features against established mechanical behaviors such as tensile performance, elasticity, dye absorption, and resistance to wear. This predictive function transforms the apparatus from a diagnostic tool into a prognostic instrument, capable of forecasting material behavior under future operational loads.
[0050] When operated in conjunction with the environmental simulation chamber, the working sequence acquires an additional dimension. The chamber subjects the specimen to controlled environmental variations in humidity, temperature, salinity, and atmospheric pressure, each condition being independently adjustable and precisely monitored. The rotational and imaging processes continue without interruption during these variations, thereby enabling dynamic analysis of the yarn cross-section under simulated stress conditions. The reconstructed digital models thus reveal not only the geometry of the yarn in static laboratory environments but also its deformation pathways under operational or extreme conditions, such as those encountered in aerospace, defense, or marine applications.
[0051]  In the inline monitoring configuration, the working principle is adapted for integration with spinning or weaving machinery. Here, yarns in continuous motion are subjected to rotational imaging through a pass-through optical window, with real-time captures being fed directly into the reconstruction and classification engine. The working cycle is uninterrupted, enabling instantaneous detection of deviations from established control parameters. Whenever anomalies are detected, the system issues real-time alerts to operators or automated control systems, permitting corrective interventions without halting production. This working mode ensures continuous assurance of quality during industrial-scale manufacturing.
[0052] In its entirety, the working of the invention embodies a closed-loop system of precision capture, computational reconstruction, intelligent classification, environmental simulation, and real-time monitoring. Each stage supports and enhances the subsequent stage, with the collective sequence yielding an outcome that is not merely descriptive but predictive, not merely observational but certifiable. The apparatus therefore advances the working methodology of textile metrology from fragmented manual inspection toward a unified, intelligent, and reproducible process that meets the legal, industrial, and scientific requirements of contemporary yarn evaluation.

[0053]  Case Study: In a representative case study, a manufacturer of aerospace-grade textiles is preparing a specialized yarn intended for deployment in high-altitude parachute canopies. Conventional quality inspection methods, relying on static microscopic imaging, indicate that the yarn appears structurally sound under ambient laboratory conditions, with no visible
 
irregularities. On this basis, the batch would ordinarily be cleared for weaving into critical load-bearing fabric. When subjected to analysis using the Automated Apparatus for Yarn Cross-Sectional Geometry Analysis Using Step-Rotational Imaging, AI-Based 3D Reconstruction, Environmental Simulation, and Inline Monitoring, a markedly different result emerges. The yarn is first imaged through the step-rotational sequence, producing a complete three-dimensional reconstruction of its cross-sectional profile. Under normal laboratory conditions, the reconstructed geometry is classified as near-circular with minor eccentricity, falling within acceptable tolerances. However, when the same yarn is placed within the environmental simulation chamber and exposed to reduced atmospheric pressure in conjunction with elevated humidity—conditions that closely approximate those encountered during high-altitude deployment—the apparatus records a progressive collapse of the cross-section along one axis. The artificial intelligence engine correlates this structural deformation with historical performance datasets, concluding that such collapse under combined low-pressure and moisture conditions is predictive of a substantial reduction in tensile strength at critical moments of canopy inflation. The system issues a classification alert indicating that the yarn batch poses a heightened risk of catastrophic failure in its intended aerospace application. As a result, the batch is immediately disqualified from production use, thereby preventing its incorporation into parachute assemblies where material failure could lead to loss of life and mission assets. This case study illustrates the unique operational value of the invention. Whereas conventional inspection methods would have permitted a defective yarn batch to proceed undetected, the disclosed apparatus identifies latent structural vulnerabilities under simulated real-world conditions, delivers predictive performance warnings through its AI-driven analytics, and provides a legally certifiable record of failure analysis. The working of the system thereby ensures that textile products intended for defense and aerospace applications are not merely inspected but are comprehensively validated against the precise environmental stresses they will encounter in service.

Here in this study I have fabricated a testing instrument as shown in figure 12 for yarn crosssection measurement and developed a novel method for calculating the correct yarn crosssectional area of the yarn.

title: AI-INTEGRATED POSITIVE DRIVE MECHANISM FOR CONSISTENT ROVING DELIVERY IN RING FRAMES
abstract:
AI-Integrated Positive Drive Mechanism for Consistent Roving Delivery in Ring Frames
This invention describes an AI-Integrated Positive Drive Mechanism for ring frame creel systems, configured as a retrofittable unit to replace conventional negative drive arrangements. The mechanism employs a variable-speed motor to actively rotate roving bobbins, thereby maintaining consistent delivery tension independent of bobbin diameter or density variations. Real-time torque and diameter sensing assemblies provide continuous feedback, while an artificial intelligence–based predictive engine anticipates tension fluctuations and preemptively adjusts motor parameters. A multi-bobbin synchronization controller ensures uniform rotational behavior across the creel, preventing drafting irregularities and twist imbalance. An eco-mode operational logic optimizes power consumption by reducing motor load under low-torque conditions, thereby achieving significant energy efficiency. Universally adaptable to legacy and modern ring frames, and operable with natural, synthetic, and recycled fibers, the invention enhances yarn quality, reduces defects, and improves sustainability, establishing a transformative advancement in spinning technology.
specification:
This invention relates to the field of textile engineering, more particularly a mechanisms employed in ring frame creel systems for controlling the delivery of roving to the drafting zone. Specifically, the invention concerns an AI-Integrated Positive Drive Mechanism with Real-Time Torque-Diameter Sensing, Multi-Bobbin Synchronization (Future Scope), and Eco-Mode Functionality, configured as a retrofittable solution for both legacy and modern ring frame installations. The invention addresses the limitations inherent in conventional negative drive systems, wherein bobbin rotation is induced passively and results in unstable yarn delivery tension. By integrating active motorized control, predictive artificial intelligence algorithms, real-time sensing assemblies, and energy optimization logic, the invention ensures uniform roving delivery, improved drafting stability, and superior yarn quality. The field of invention therefore encompasses advanced spinning control systems, with particular applicability to textile mills engaged in the production of natural, synthetic, and recycled fiber-based yarns.

PRIOR ART AND PROBLEM TO BE SOLVED


[0002] Ring frame spinning machines are critical to modern yarn production, where precise tension and uniform feed are essential to maintaining yarn quality, strength, and consistency. At the heart of this process is the roving creel—the delivery system that supplies pre-drafted roving to the ring spinning zone. The performance of this subsystem significantly influences the quality of the spun yarn. Traditional ring frame machines use a negative drive mechanism in which the roving bobbin is rotated passively, relying solely on the pulling force exerted by the drafting rollers. This inherently unstable mechanism leads to fluctuating roving tension. As the bobbin unwinds and its diameter decreases, the torque needed to
 
rotate the bobbin changes, further destabilizing the tension delivered to the drafting system.
[0003]  The consequences are well-documented: inconsistent yarn thickness, frequent yarn breakage (end breaks), reduced productivity, poor-quality packages, and ultimately increased wastage and rework. The situation becomes more complex when synthetic or recycled fibers such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—derived from discarded plastic bottles—are involved. These materials often present inconsistent feed densities and varying mechanical properties, which exacerbate the issue by causing non-uniform unwinding resistance. Compounding the problem, textile mills located in geographies with fluctuating climate conditions encounter additional tension instabilities. Humidity and temperature variations affect fiber friction, elasticity, and cohesion, further compromising the roving tension delivered by conventional systems.
[0004] Despite advancements in spinning machine control systems, the roving creel remains largely unevolved—still dependent on static, mechanical designs without integrated sensing, control logic, or adaptive torque systems. Over the years, various technologies and methods have been proposed to address the challenges associated with tension instability in ring frame spinning machines. Traditional approaches often relied on mechanical braking systems affixed to the bobbin support arms, where adjustable friction pads or spring-based resistors were used to impose drag on the unwinding bobbin. While this introduced a rudimentary form of tension control, it lacked responsiveness to dynamic changes in bobbin diameter, fiber type, or spinning speed. Moreover, mechanical brakes are prone to wear, environmental degradation, and often require frequent manual adjustment, which makes them unreliable in long-term high-volume operations.
[0005]  Subsequent innovations introduced tension sensors placed between the roving creel and the drafting system, intended to detect and regulate tension by feeding real-time data into control units. However, these systems are inherently reactive. They can only respond after a change in tension has occurred, rather than preventing the fluctuation in the first place. These systems are also unable to influence the root cause—the bobbin’s rotational behavior—which continues to operate under a passive, torque-dependent mechanism. Thus, while tension sensors
 
provide some degree of mitigation, they fall short of offering a comprehensive solution.
[0006] In more advanced setups, servo-driven bobbin systems have been implemented, allowing for active control of bobbin rotation based on load conditions. These servo motors can apply or reduce torque to stabilize tension. Though promising, such systems come with significant trade-offs. They are often prohibitively expensive, especially for retrofitting existing machinery, and introduce considerable complexity to system integration. Additionally, these systems generally lack intelligent, data-driven control logic capable of learning and adapting over time. Without predictive models or contextual awareness of material properties or ambient conditions, their operation remains largely mechanical.
[0007] Efforts have also been made to improve roving uniformity by altering upstream material preparation processes. This includes modifying sliver compaction techniques or optimizing bobbin winding density. While these process-level improvements can reduce some downstream variability, they do not address changes that occur during the actual spinning process. As a result, the underlying limitation of the passive drive mechanism remains, and the solutions do not offer in-situ control or real-time compensation during yarn production.

[0008] To resolve the above-mentioned problem a positive drive system for ring frame creels, intended to replace conventional passive mechanisms. In traditional systems, bobbin rotation relies solely on the drafting zone’s pull, resulting in variable tension and poor yarn consistency. The proposed system eliminates these shortcomings by actively driving the bobbin with a variable-speed motor that responds to real-time data from torque and diameter sensors. Unlike negative drive setups, this mechanism ensures stable yarn delivery tension, significantly reducing end-breaks and improving drafting stability. It incorporates an AI-based predictive control engine that learns from continuous operation data, enabling pre-emptive corrections to tension fluctuations. In future a multi-bobbin synchronization module ensures uniform behavior across multiple spindles, while the eco-mode feature optimizes energy usage. The invention is universally retrofittable, compact, and designed for seamless integration into legacy ring frames. Its adaptability to a wide range of fibers—including natural, synthetic, and recycled yarns—positions it as a
 
vital solution for mills seeking both sustainability and high precision. The mechanism enhances yarn quality, reduces waste, and enables consistent performance even in climate-variant or recycled-fiber-based operations.

THE OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION:

[0009]  Existing solutions fail primarily because they do not directly address the need for intelligent, real-time control at the point of roving delivery. Mechanical systems, whether they use brakes or resistors, operate on fixed settings that are incapable of adapting to dynamic conditions. They degrade over time, require frequent maintenance, and introduce additional variability rather than mitigating it. Feedback-based tension control systems, while offering some level of monitoring, are reactive and not inherently preventive. Their inability to adjust bobbin torque directly makes them ineffective in addressing core issues of passive drive systems.

[0010] It has already been proposed that servo-based active drive systems, while technically advanced, are constrained by their cost, integration complexity, and lack of embedded intelligence. Without machine learning or contextual awareness, they cannot predict when tension inconsistencies are likely to arise based on patterns in material feed, bobbin fill levels, or environmental shifts. Additionally, these solutions are often developed as standalone subsystems rather than integrated elements of a holistic spinning strategy, which limits their scalability and adaptability across different machine platforms or material types. Ultimately, the current landscape of solutions treats symptoms rather than causes. No existing system offers a truly adaptive, predictive, and integrated solution capable of stabilizing roving tension in the face of modern spinning challenges—whether those stem from high-speed demands, recycled input variability, or changing environmental conditions.

[0011]  The principal objective of the invention is to provide an AI-Integrated Positive Drive Mechanism with Real-Time Torque-Diameter Sensing, Multi-Bobbin Synchronization, and Eco-Mode Functionality, specifically configured for retrofitting into ring frame creel systems. The mechanism is designed to actively
 
control bobbin rotation through a variable-speed drive unit, thereby maintaining uniform roving delivery tension across diverse fiber types, including natural, synthetic, and recycled fibers. It integrates advanced sensor assemblies for monitoring torque and bobbin diameter, employs artificial intelligence for predictive tension regulation, ensures synchronized multi-bobbin operation for drafting uniformity, and incorporates an energy-saving eco-mode to optimize operational efficiency while preserving yarn quality and machine reliability. The invention thereby addresses the deficiencies of conventional negative-drive creels and establishes a universal, sustainable, and technologically advanced solution for contemporary spinning mills.
[0012]  Another objective of the invention is to provide a Positive Drive Mechanism that eliminates dependency on passive yarn pull and instead utilizes an electronically regulated motor drive to actively rotate the bobbin, ensuring stable and continuous roving delivery tension irrespective of bobbin diameter reduction or density inconsistency.
[0013] The further objective of the invention is to provide a Real-Time Torque and Diameter Sensing Assembly comprising precision torque sensors and non-contact optical diameter detectors, configured to generate continuous feedback signals indicative of bobbin load variations and unwinding geometry, thereby enabling closed-loop tension regulation.
[0014] The further objective of the invention is to provide an AI-Predictive Tension Control System trained on extensive operational datasets, wherein machine learning algorithms analyze sensor-derived data to forecast potential tension instabilities and pre-adjust motor parameters, thereby preventing yarn defects, end-breaks, and drafting irregularities.
[0015] The further objective of the invention is to provide a Multi-Bobbin Synchronization Module configured to maintain rotational uniformity across multiple bobbins within the creel, such that synchronization deviation remains within a defined tolerance, ensuring consistent drafting stability and twist uniformity across parallel yarn lines.
[0016] The further objective of the invention is to provide an Eco-Mode Functionality wherein the system dynamically reduces energy consumption by modulating
 
motor load under low-torque conditions, thereby achieving energy savings with improving the yarn quality or machine performance.
[0017] The further objective of the invention is to provide a Retrofit-Compatible Mounting System designed as a modular and compact unit, permitting direct installation on legacy and modern ring frame creels without substantial modification of existing machine infrastructure, thereby reducing adoption barriers and enhancing industrial applicability.
[0018] The further objective of the invention is to provide a Universal Fiber Compatibility Mechanism enabling the system to operate effectively with natural, synthetic, and recycled fibers—including PET-derived yarns—by dynamically compensating for material-specific density variations and environmental influences such as humidity and temperature.
[0019]  The further objective of the invention is to provide a Diagnostic and Connectivity Interface incorporating wireless communication capability, allowing remote monitoring, firmware updates, and predictive maintenance, thereby ensuring continuous operational reliability and reducing downtime in textile production environments.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION


[0020] Road In modern high-speed spinning environments, where machines operate at elevated production rates, the stability of roving delivery becomes increasingly critical. The passive creel systems, with their reliance on the drafting system to pull and rotate the bobbin, cannot accommodate the rapid torque changes required during fast acceleration and deceleration cycles. Any slight lag in bobbin response or variability in friction results in sudden tension spikes or dips, which propagate directly into yarn faults or machine stoppages. The inability of the creel to regulate tension actively becomes a fundamental bottleneck in achieving high-speed, high-consistency yarn production.

[0021] As the industry shifts toward sustainable yarns made from recycled or synthetic inputs, new challenges arise that further strain conventional systems. Recycled materials, especially those derived from PET bottles or mixed waste streams,
 
exhibit unpredictable mechanical properties. These inconsistencies manifest in the roving’s behavior during unwinding—some sections are denser or more compacted than others due to upstream sliver variability. A passive creel mechanism lacks the intelligence and control flexibility to detect or respond to these changes, leading to highly inconsistent tension profiles, particularly over the course of an entire bobbin’s depletion.

[0022] Compounding these material-related challenges are the effects of fluctuating environmental conditions in textile mills, particularly those located in tropical or seasonally volatile climates. Changes in humidity and temperature significantly affect fiber friction, cohesion, and elasticity. For instance, natural fibers absorb moisture, becoming more pliable or sticky, while synthetic fibers may stiffen or behave erratically. Conventional creel systems, devoid of any sensing or compensating mechanism, continue to deliver roving under a one-size-fits-all mechanical model, regardless of how dramatically the physical behavior of the fiber has shifted due to ambient changes.

[0023] So here in this invention a novel positive drive system for ring frame creels, engineered to deliver uniform roving tension and superior yarn quality. Unlike conventional negative drive mechanisms that rely on passive bobbin rotation, this system employs an active motorized drive, thereby eliminating fluctuations caused by decreasing bobbin diameters or uneven packing densities. At its core, the system integrates variable-speed brushless motors with real-time torque and diameter sensing. The feedback loop is reinforced by an AI-powered predictive model, which anticipates instability in yarn delivery and automatically corrects drive parameters before defects occur. This ensures that roving delivery remains constant, minimizing end-breaks and improving drafting precision.
[0024] As a future scope the system further includes centralized multi-bobbin synchronization for balanced yarn production and an energy-saving eco-mode that reduces power consumption when torque demand is low. Its retrofit-friendly modular design allows for quick installation on both legacy and modern ring frames without requiring structural modification. With special applicability in recycled PET yarn production, where bobbin packing irregularities often impair tension stability, the invention provides
 
critical improvements in efficiency and sustainability. Its robust adaptability to varying fibers, combined with predictive intelligence and energy-conscious design, makes it a significant technological advancement for modern spinning mills.
