[0030]  The present invention is an AI-Integrated Positive Drive Mechanism with Real-Time Torque-Diameter Sensing, Multi-Bobbin Synchronization, and Eco-Mode for Retrofit Ring Frame Creel Systems, devised to overcome the long-standing deficiencies of conventional negative drive arrangements. The purpose of the invention is to ensure consistent and uniform delivery tension during the unwinding of roving, thereby enhancing drafting stability and improving the quality of spun yarn. By replacing the reliance on passive pull-based systems, the invention introduces a proactive and intelligent method of drive regulation, which significantly reduces the incidence of yarn defects, end-breaks, and production inefficiencies.
[0031] The invention is intended for use in textile spinning operations where high precision and reliability of yarn delivery are paramount. It is particularly suited to environments where roving bobbins exhibit irregular packing densities, such as in mills producing recycled or technical fibers, and in regions where climatic
 
fluctuations affect fiber behavior. Through its advanced control methodology, the invention ensures that roving delivery remains stable under diverse operating conditions, thereby maintaining product quality and reducing wastage. Its retrofit design allows for seamless integration into both modern and legacy ring frame creel systems, enabling textile mills to adopt the technology without extensive modifications to existing infrastructure.
[0032] A distinctive feature of the invention lies in its ability to deliver continuous adaptive control over roving tension by integrating real-time feedback with predictive intelligence. The mechanism anticipates fluctuations that would otherwise compromise yarn stability and intervenes proactively to maintain uniform delivery. This predictive functionality establishes a substantial improvement over conventional systems, which merely respond to inconsistencies after they occur.
[0033] Another important feature of the invention is its capability to maintain synchronized operation across multiple bobbins within the creel. This ensures that all yarn lines exhibit balanced tension and drafting stability, which is particularly critical in high-speed production environments where minor deviations can compound into significant quality defects. The synchronization function provides a harmonized output across the creel, thereby achieving a higher level of consistency in yarn production.

[0034] In an additional aspect, the present invention provides an improvement in yarn quality by substantially eliminating undesirable creel draft occurring at the ring frame creel. The invention further ensures maintenance of the predetermined draft setting throughout the spinning process, thereby enabling the production of yarn with the intended count (linear density) and enhanced uniformity. Consequently, the invention contributes to improved yarn quality, consistency, and process reliability.

[0035]  Collectively, these features render the invention a transformative solution in the field of spinning technology. Its integration of intelligent control, synchronization, energy optimization, and retrofit adaptability provides textile mills with a tool that simultaneously enhances productivity, reduces operational costs, and improves yarn quality, establishing a new benchmark in the evolution of ring frame creel systems.
 
[0036] Here the external appearance of the invention has been deliberately conceived to embody compactness, durability, and unobtrusiveness, while at the same time projecting an impression of advanced technological refinement. To the user, the mechanism presents itself as a self-contained modular unit, seamlessly mountable upon the existing framework of a ring frame creel without disrupting the conventional layout of the machine. Its overall geometry is streamlined and proportioned so as to blend with the existing creel infrastructure, avoiding unnecessary protrusions or structural complexities that could interfere with normal operator access.
[0037]  The housing is designed as a protective enclosure, fabricated from industrial-grade materials such as anodized aluminum or equivalent metal alloys, imparting both mechanical robustness and resistance to environmental conditions prevalent in textile mills. The surfaces are smooth, with edges softened to prevent operator injury, and finished in corrosion-resistant coatings that project a professional, machine-integrated aesthetic. The visual profile is minimalistic yet modern, signaling to the operator that the unit is not an external accessory but an integral part of the ring frame system itself.
[0038] From the perspective of the user, the invention is visually characterized by its compact frontal panel, which discreetly integrates status indicators and, where applicable, an interface surface for operational monitoring. The indicator arrangement communicates operational states through a combination of light signals or displays that are easily perceptible in a mill environment without distracting from the operator’s tasks. The design avoids clutter or excessive control elements, preserving the principle that the unit operates autonomously with minimal manual intervention, while still offering visible reassurance of its functioning.
[0039] The external body is proportioned so as to sit flush with the bobbin holding assembly, extending outward only to the degree necessary to accommodate its internal functional assemblies. This creates a symmetrical and balanced visual alignment with the bobbin, ensuring that the operator perceives it as part of the standard creel configuration rather than as a separate device. The compactness of the unit, coupled with its symmetrical alignment, facilitates ergonomic handling and ease of cleaning, which are critical considerations in the textile environment.
 
[0040]  The apparatus also incorporates a series of sealed joints and enclosures designed to protect internal mechanisms from lint, dust, and humidity, while at the same time presenting a unified and uninterrupted exterior surface. This sealing contributes not only to durability but also to a visually clean and unbroken exterior, which enhances the perception of reliability and sophistication. The user, upon inspection, perceives a system that is not only technologically advanced but also deliberately engineered for seamless integration into the practical realities of mill operation.
[0041]  Overall, the invention externally communicates a sense of precision, modernity, and refinement. Its compact housing, smooth contours, discreet interface features, and integration into the visual language of existing creel systems create an impression of a purpose-built, intelligent enhancement rather than an intrusive aftermarket attachment. For the user, the external look of the invention embodies both the technical promise of improved roving control and the visual assurance of industrial reliability, thereby reinforcing its suitability for continuous, high-quality textile production.
[0042] The invention comprises a carefully orchestrated assembly of integrated components, each designed to perform a distinct function yet engineered to operate in synergy, thereby ensuring that the system fulfills its intended objective of maintaining stable and predictive roving delivery tension. At the heart of the mechanism lies the positive drive motor unit, which serves as the active element responsible for imparting controlled rotational force to the roving bobbin. Unlike conventional passive arrangements, this motor does not merely respond to the drafting pull but instead dictates the bobbin’s motion in accordance with feedback signals, making it the central actuator within the architecture of the invention. Its responsiveness and variable-speed functionality establish the foundation upon which other components operate.
[0043]  To enable such controlled actuation, the invention incorporates a real-time sensing assembly consisting of precision torque detectors and non-contact optical diameter sensors. These sensing modules continuously monitor the condition of the bobbin, registering both the resistive torque generated by varying packing densities and the progressive reduction in bobbin diameter during unwinding. This continuous stream of data is not an isolated output but is directly communicated to the control
 
system, where it is processed in real time. In functional integration, the sensors act as the perceptual organs of the mechanism, providing the motor with the contextual intelligence necessary to perform its active regulation. Without this constant feedback, the motor would revert to a simple driver, but with the sensors, it becomes a finely tuned actuator capable of ensuring precise tension stability.
[0044]  The intelligence governing this interplay is furnished by the artificial intelligence–based predictive control engine, which resides within the embedded computational unit of the mechanism. This engine is not limited to reacting to instantaneous data; rather, it interprets historical and real-time sensor inputs to anticipate fluctuations before they materialize into destabilizing tension events. The AI engine generates preemptive commands that modulate motor parameters, effectively adjusting rotational speed and torque output in advance of anticipated irregularities. In this manner, the control engine acts as the cognitive core of the invention, elevating the system from reactive compensation to predictive stabilization. Its integration with the motor and sensor assemblies is seamless, with all three elements functioning in a closed-loop framework that delivers both accuracy and foresight in yarn delivery.
[0045] As a future objective of this invention for creels handling multiple bobbins simultaneously, the invention employs a synchronization controller that ensures harmonious rotation across all drive units. This controller serves as the coordinating mechanism, receiving inputs from each motor-sensor pair and issuing collective adjustments to prevent deviations among the bobbins. The synchronization ensures that all yarn lines progress at uniform tension and speed, thereby preventing drafting irregularities and twist imbalances that could otherwise arise from even minor inconsistencies. The controller thus transforms multiple independent drive units into a unified system, reinforcing drafting stability at a collective level. Its integration with the AI engine is critical, as predictive corrections made at the individual bobbin level are coordinated to align with the broader operational rhythm of the creel.
[0046]  In parallel from further improvement it can be possible by this invention that integrates an eco-mode logic system that supervises power consumption during operation. This subsystem is designed to analyze torque demand relative to bobbin diameter and unwinding resistance. When conditions permit—such as during early stages of unwinding where torque requirements are minimal—the eco-mode logic reduces motor power draw, achieving measurable
 
energy savings without impairing yarn stability. The eco-mode does not operate in isolation; it is deeply interlinked with the sensor assembly and AI engine, drawing upon torque feedback and predictive load analysis to determine the precise moments when energy reduction is permissible. In effect, it constitutes a sustainability layer seamlessly interwoven into the control structure of the invention.
[0047] The integration of all these components is realized through a central embedded control unit, which serves as the nexus for data exchange, decision-making, and command issuance. The sensors feed continuous data streams to the unit, the AI engine interprets and predicts based on those streams, the motor receives actuation commands for immediate execution, the synchronization module aligns the outputs across multiple bobbins, and the eco-mode logic intervenes to optimize energy usage. Each component therefore performs a specialized task, yet none functions independently; instead, they interact in a constant cycle of sensing, prediction, actuation, and coordination. This interdependence ensures that the invention operates as a holistic system rather than as a mere aggregation of parts.
[0048]  In practical use, this integration enables the invention to adapt dynamically to real-world variances in bobbin density, environmental conditions, and fiber characteristics. The motor provides the physical force, the sensors supply contextual awareness, the AI engine delivers predictive intelligence, the synchronization module ensures collective harmony, and the eco-mode contributes energy efficiency. Together, these components collectively transform the conventional creel into an intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable system, thereby fulfilling the invention’s purpose of elevating yarn quality, improving operational reliability, and reducing energy consumption in textile spinning mills.
[0049]  The working of the invention commences when the roving bobbin is mounted within the creel and the system is activated. Unlike conventional negative drive mechanisms, where the bobbin rotation is induced solely by the drafting pull, the present system initiates active motorized rotation of the bobbin under the command of a variable-speed drive. From the outset, the rotation is not arbitrary but governed by continuous streams of data communicated by torque and diameter sensing modules. These sensing elements provide real-time information relating to the resistive load exerted by the bobbin’s internal packing density and the progressive
 
reduction of its diameter during unwinding. This information is transmitted directly to the embedded control unit, which serves as the operational nexus of the system.
[0050]  Within this control unit resides the artificial intelligence–based predictive engine, which processes sensor inputs in real time and compares them against learned datasets. The engine does not merely respond to instantaneous fluctuations; it anticipates the onset of instability by identifying patterns that precede irregular tension conditions. Upon such prediction, the engine issues corrective instructions to the drive motor, adjusting its rotational speed and torque output prior to the occurrence of a destabilizing event. In this manner, the system maintains stable roving delivery tension continuously, avoiding yarn imperfections and preventing end-breaks that would otherwise arise under conventional passive systems.
[0051]  Simultaneously, the synchronization module functions to harmonize the operation of multiple bobbin drives across the creel. Each motorized bobbin is independently controlled yet collectively aligned, ensuring that all roving ends are delivered at uniform rates and tensions. This uniformity is critical in preventing drafting irregularities and twist imbalances, particularly in high-speed spinning operations where even slight deviations can escalate into significant defects. The synchronization module integrates directly with the predictive control engine, thereby ensuring that corrections issued at the level of an individual bobbin do not disrupt the collective harmony of the creel.
[0052]  As the system progresses through different stages of bobbin unwinding, the eco-mode functionality continuously monitors torque requirements relative to bobbin size and operational load. When conditions permit, such as during early unwinding stages where torque demand is minimal, the system reduces power draw without compromising tension stability. This energy optimization occurs seamlessly, with the eco-mode logic drawing upon predictive analysis and sensor data to determine safe intervals for energy reduction. Consequently, the system achieves measurable energy efficiency while preserving operational reliability, aligning with modern sustainability imperatives in textile production.
[0053]  The overall working of the invention is thus characterized by a closed-loop cycle of sensing, prediction, actuation, synchronization, and optimization. The sensors perceive the operational state of the bobbin, the predictive engine interprets and
 
forecasts potential instabilities, the motor executes corrective commands, the synchronization module ensures uniformity across all bobbins, and the eco-mode minimizes energy expenditure wherever feasible. Each element functions not in isolation but in constant interaction, ensuring that the entire mechanism operates as a cohesive and intelligent unit.
[0054] In practical operation within a spinning mill, this integrated working results in uninterrupted roving delivery, enhanced drafting stability, reduced defect rates, and lower energy consumption. By maintaining uniform yarn quality under varying conditions of bobbin density, environmental fluctuation, and fiber type, the invention fulfills its purpose of establishing a superior and sustainable advancement over traditional negative drive creel systems.
[0055] Case Study: In a representative case of industrial application, the invention was deployed in a spinning mill engaged in the production of yarn derived from recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles. Such mills are known to encounter irregularities in roving bobbins, particularly owing to non-uniform packing densities that arise from fluctuations in the extrusion and sliver preparation processes. During operation under conventional negative drive systems, these irregularities manifest as torque spikes when the yarn is drawn from denser segments of the bobbin, leading to erratic tension levels, increased incidences of drafting faults, and frequent yarn breakages. Upon integration of the present invention, the roving bobbins were actively driven by variable-speed motors under the governance of the control system. As the bobbin with irregular density was unwound, the torque sensor assembly immediately detected a rise in resistive load, registering this anomaly in real time. The corresponding data was relayed to the embedded control unit, wherein the artificial intelligence–based predictive engine identified the potential for tension destabilization and issued pre-emptive corrective instructions. The drive motor, acting on these instructions, compensated by altering its rotational speed and torque output, thereby neutralizing the disruptive effect of the density variation before it could propagate to the drafting zone. Simultaneously, the synchronization controller ensured that the corrective adjustment applied to the affected bobbin did not create a misalignment with the other bobbins operating in parallel. Uniformity of rotation was maintained across the creel, preserving consistent drafting stability and twist distribution throughout
 
the yarn lines. The eco-mode logic, operating concurrently, optimized energy consumption by scaling down power delivery in segments of operation where torque demand remained low, thereby conserving energy without impairing yarn quality. As a result of this coordinated functioning, the recycled PET yarn was delivered with uniform tension, free from the breaks and irregularities typically associated with density fluctuations in the bobbin. Production continuity was maintained, defect rates were significantly reduced, and energy expenditure was optimized. The case study thus demonstrates the invention’s capacity to transform a problematic operational condition into a stable and efficient process, underscoring its industrial applicability and superiority over conventional systems.
[0056]  This work shows a comparative study of properties of 30s Ne yarns produced from the roving of twist multiplier i.e. 0.96, 1.04 and 1.16 produced from the 100% cotton fibres. In this study a new attempt has been made by feeding the roving bobbins with and without (by negative and positive feeding) stretch at ring frame creel. The positive roving feeding avoids the undue stretch at ring frame creel even for the low twist roving bobbins. High twist roving leads to the chances of undrafted material delivery on the ring frame as well as it reduces the speed frame delivery. But the more twist roving helps in enhancing the yarn strength by fibre straightening as well as the number of end brakes were less at the speed frame. The manufactured yarn samples were tested for properties like, tensile strength, Elongation, CSP, Friction, Uster and yarn imperfection.



[0057]   Material and Methodology:
Sample Preparation: 100% cotton fibers were processed in blow room and then processed through card and two passage of draw frame. The finisher draw frame sliver was then processed to get roving with 0.65 ktex linear density with 1.0 twist multiplier. After that the roving bobbins were first conditioned at standard atmospheric condition and then taken for the processing in ring fame machine with delivery hank of 32 Ne having 3.4 TM. On ring frame first the material has been processed with normal manor and ring yarn is manufactured then with the use of same roving bobbins the roving has been fed by rotating the roving bobbins positively and roving has been fed without the stretch and another yarn sample was
 
produced. Then both the yarn samples were tested for the important yarn quality parameters.
Sample Testing:
The Uster tester 3 was used to measure the evenness of yarn and the yarn imperfections. The yarn samples were tested on tenso-lab tester for single end strength. With the use of lea strength tester yarn lea strength has been tested.

[0059] Above tables 1-2 and figure 1 shows that the yarn manufactured with positive feeding of roving has 5.29% less unevenness than the yarn manufactured with regular feed roving this may be because of chances of untwisting of roving before feeding in the ring frame break draft zone. When the yarn samples were tested for yarn CV 10mt it is found that the positive roving feed yarn has 20.06% less CV 10mt than the regular roving feed yarn this is attributed due to the fact that in case of regular negatively roving feed during unwinding of roving bobbin while pulling the roving from stationary bobbin there is stretch and this stretch is more for full bobbin and less for smaller bobbin which results in to increase in the CV 10mt.

[0064]  As the imperfections of stretch-ail yarn were 24% less, the application of this yarn in the fabric reduces some of the fabric faults which are sourced due to the yarn imperfections and it also helps in good quality dyeing effects in the fabric.

title: PLASTIC-BASED BRICK MANUFACTURING DEVICE
abstract: A plastic-based brick manufacturing device, comprising a housing 101, an input means to provide input command regarding initiation, an electronic nozzle 104 to dispense a predetermined quantity of the stored materials into a mixing container 106, a robotic gripper 107 to securely grasp plastic waste pieces from a box 108 for subsequent grinding and mixing with the other materials to form a brick-forming mixture, a motorized grinding unit 109 to grind, mix, and homogenize the received materials by means of rotating blades to produce a uniform slurry suitable for brick moulding, an articulated bar 112 to selectively extend the pins to imprint predetermined identification patterns, letters, or symbols on a top surface of the slurry contained within each of the molds 111, an articulated pole 115 having a pressing plate 116 to uniformly level and compact the mixture prior to setting, a Peltier module 117 for controlled setting and stabilization of the brick mixture.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a plastic-based brick manufacturing device developed for producing plastic-based bricks by processing plastic waste with construction materials to form durable bricks suitable for construction and building purposes.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	 Plastic waste management and sustainable construction practices have become important concerns in recent years. Conventional brick manufacturing approaches rely heavily on natural resources such as clay and soil, which leads to depletion of fertile land and environmental imbalance. At the same time, plastic waste continues to accumulate, creating pollution and disposal challenges. Existing brick-making processes are largely manual, requiring significant labor and time, and result in inconsistent quality due to variations in mixing and curing. The absence of automation in material handling, grinding, and molding makes production less efficient and difficult to scale. These limitations highlight the need for improved approaches that combines waste utilization with efficient brick production.

[0003]	In traditional methods, brick manufacturing involves manual collection of raw materials such as clay, cement, and water, followed by mixing and molding into desired shapes. The process requires workers to physically grind and homogenize materials, which labor-intensive and prone to inconsistency. Drying and curing are usually performed under uncontrolled conditions, leading to variations in strength and durability. Identification or marking of bricks is also done manually, adding further effort and reducing uniformity. Removing bricks from molds is difficult, requiring force that risks damaging the product. Additionally, conventional methods do not integrate monitoring or feedback systems, leaving users unaware of production efficiency or quality control. These drawbacks make traditional brick-making processes less sustainable, less efficient, and unable to address modern challenges of waste management and resource conservation.

[0004]	US9919452B2 discloses a brick includes a thermoplastic material, such as high density polyethylene (HDPE), and a cement-containing material. The brick may be made by mixing thermoplastic material and dry, uncured cement-containing material. This mixture is placed in a mold. The mold is heated while the mixture is compressed to melt or soften the thermoplastic material and to bind the particulate material in the mold into the shape of a brick. After the hardened brick is removed from the mold, the surface of the brick may be sprayed with water to cure cement-containing material on the surface of the brick.

[0005]	CN101104297A discloses a method of using waste rubber plastic materials to produce bricks for production and construction. The method includes the following procedures: 1, material preparation: firstly clean the waste plastic and rubble products and crash into particles; crash the smelting slag and slag cement into ore particles with particle size on standby; purchase organ-tin heat stabilizer and auxiliary heat stabilizer on standby; 2, proportion: take the rubber plastic particles and ore particles with the mass proportion of rubber particles 20-40 percent and ore particles 60-80 percent, then add organo-tin heat stabilizer and auxiliary heat stabilizer with 5-25percent of mass of the rubber plastic materials; mix all the materials and stir the material evenly; 3, molding: put the mixture into the mould and heat up, then use the hydraulic pressure machine to forge and press the mixture into adobes or directly into bricks; 4, cutting: use the cutter to cut the made-up adobes into bricks. The method of producing construction bricks by using the waste rubber, plastics and industrial waste residue, not only turn the harmful into the beneficial, reduce the pollution, protect the environment, but also save the land resources and provide the society with the construction materials to achieve circular utilization of resources.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices for producing plastic-based bricks rely on heating and compression of mixed materials or manual preparation of waste plastics and additives. These approaches require complex processing steps, high energy consumption, and careful handling of stabilizers. Users face challenges with inconsistent brick quality, limited scalability, and difficulty in achieving uniform curing, which reduces efficiency and reliability in large-scale applications.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that ensures efficient utilization of waste materials, reduces energy consumption, maintains consistent quality, simplifies production steps, and provides scalable, reliable output suitable for sustainable construction applications across diverse environments.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of producing plastic-based bricks in an automated manner with minimal manual intervention.

[0009]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of enabling controlled preparation of a uniform brick-forming mixture and its dispensing for consistent brick formation.

[0010]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of ensuring uniform shaping, compaction, and stabilization of bricks to obtain consistent brick quality.

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of facilitating user operation and monitoring of the brick manufacturing process in a simple and efficient manner.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	The present invention relates to a plastic-based brick manufacturing device developed for forming bricks using plastic waste combined with construction materials to produce solid and usable bricks for building and construction purposes.

[0014]	According to an aspect of the present invention, a plastic-based brick manufacturing device comprising of a housing arranged to enclose the operational components, an input means operatively linked with a microcontroller configured to enable a user to provide input commands for initiation and control of automated brick production, an electronic nozzle connected to each section of a multi-sectioned chamber storing red soil cement and water arranged within the housing configured to dispense predetermined quantities of materials into a mixing container, a robotic gripper installed within the housing configured to securely grasp plastic waste pieces from a box and place them into the container for subsequent grinding and mixing, a motorized grinding unit integrated within the container configured to grind mix and homogenize the received materials by means of rotating blades to produce a uniform slurry suitable for brick moulding, an electronic spout connected to the container configured to dispense slurry over a plurality of molds arranged with a circular rotatable ring in a sequential manner, an articulated bar arranged within the housing having a plate at the end integrated with a plurality of pneumatic pins configured to selectively extend the pins to imprint identification patterns letters or symbols on the slurry surface within each mold.

[0015]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the device disclosed further includes an articulated pole having a pressing plate at the end configured to apply controlled downward pressure over the slurry to uniformly level and compact the mixture prior to setting, a Peltier module integrated with each mold configured to regulate temperature for controlled setting and stabilization of the brick mixture, a vibrating unit integrated with each mold configured to generate controlled vibrations for loosening a formed brick from the mold, and simultaneously an articulated arm installed within the housing configured to securely grasp the formed brick from the mold and place it within a user accessible tray in a sequential manner, wherein the workflow begins with user input to initiate operations followed by material dispensing plastic waste handling grinding slurry preparation mold filling imprinting pressing temperature regulation vibration assisted release and final placement of the formed brick in the tray.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.
