[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a plastic-based brick manufacturing device.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of, the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to a plastic-based brick manufacturing device developed for manufacturing bricks by utilizing plastic waste in combination with construction materials to obtain solid bricks suitable for use in construction activities.

[0022]	Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a plastic-based brick manufacturing device is illustrated, comprising of a housing 101, a plurality of suction cups 102 arranged underneath the housing 101, a microphone 103 installed with the housing 101, an electronic nozzle 104 connected to each section of a multi-sectioned chamber 105 arranged within the housing 101, a mixing container 106 arranged within the housing 101, a robotic gripper 107 installed within the housing 101, a box 108 arranged within the housing 101, a motorized grinding unit 109 integrate within the container 106, an electronic spout 110 connected to the container 106, a plurality of molds 111 arranged with a circular rotatable ring, arranged within the housing 101, an articulated bar 112 arranged within the housing 101, having a plate 113 at the end integrated with plurality of pneumatic pins 114, an articulated pole 115 having a pressing plate 116 at the end, a Peltier module 117 integrated with each of the mold, a speaker 118 arranged with the housing 101, an articulated arm 119 installed within the housing 101, a user-accessible tray 120 arranged within the housing 101

[0023]	The device disclosed herein comprises of a housing 101 is provided as a structural enclosure configured to support and protect internal components while maintaining stable positioning during operation. A plurality of suction cups 102 is arranged underneath the housing 101 and operatively coupled thereto, wherein the suction cups 102 are adapted to establish temporary vacuum engagement with an underlying surface. The suction cups 102 cooperate to generate sufficient holding force to securely adhere the housing 101 to the surface, thereby preventing unintended displacement during operation. 

[0024]	The housing 101 functions as a stationary support structure during operation. Upon placement over a target surface, the housing 101 maintains a fixed orientation while accommodating internal components and connection interfaces. Once the suction cups 102 positioned beneath the housing 101 are activated and secure adhesion is achieved, the housing 101 remains immobilized relative to the surface. This structural stability ensures that all mounted components operate within predetermined positional parameters while minimizing displacement, vibration, or misalignment during functional activities performed by the associated device.

[0025]	The plurality of suction cups 102 operates by establishing vacuum-based adhesion between the underside of the housing 101 and the supporting surface. Upon contact with the surface, air present within the suction cup cavities is evacuated through a vacuum operation, causing the flexible rims of the cups to seal tightly against the surface. The pressure differential created between the internal cavity and the external atmosphere generates a holding force that anchors the housing 101 securely in position. The multiple suction cups 102 distribute the adhesion force evenly, thereby enhancing stability and preventing shifting or detachment during operation of the device.

[0026]	An input means is operatively connected with a microcontroller and configured to enable a user to initiate and regulate an automated plastic-based brick production operation through user-generated commands. The input means facilitates transmission of control signals to the microcontroller for activating, pausing, or modifying operational parameters of the device. The input means includes at least one of a microphone 103 configured to capture voice-based instructions or a display unit configured to receive manual inputs. Upon receiving the command, the microcontroller interprets the input signal and executes corresponding control instructions to manage sequential functions of the automated brick manufacturing process.

[0027]	The input means operates by receiving a command generated by a user and converting the received command into an electrical signal that is transmitted to the microcontroller. Upon receipt, the microcontroller processes the signal according to pre-programmed instructions and initiates the corresponding operational sequence of the automated brick production device. The input means enables initiation, pausing, and modification of operational cycles through successive commands. During operation, the microcontroller continuously monitors incoming signals from the input means and accordingly regulates actuation of device components to maintain synchronized execution of the brick manufacturing process.

[0028]	The microphone 103 operates by detecting voice commands generated by the user and converting acoustic sound waves into corresponding electrical signals through a transducer. The generated signals are transmitted to the microcontroller, where a voice recognition module interprets the signal patterns and identifies predefined command instructions. Upon recognition, the microcontroller triggers the designated operational sequence associated with the command. The microphone 103 continuously remains in a receptive state during device operation to capture additional voice instructions. Subsequent commands are similarly converted and transmitted, enabling real-time control of the automated brick production operation.

[0029]	The display unit operates by presenting an interactive interface through which a user provides operational commands to the device. The user selects or enters commands using touch-based or button-based inputs displayed on the interface. Upon selection, the display unit generates a corresponding electrical signal that is transmitted to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received signal and executes the designated operational function within the automated brick production device. The display unit further updates visual indicators reflecting operational status, device responses, or command confirmation, thereby enabling continuous monitoring and control of the brick production process.

[0030]	An electronic nozzle 104 is operatively connected to each section of a multi- sectioned chamber 105 configured to separately store red soil, cement, and water within a housing 101. The electronic nozzle 104 is adapted to dispense a predetermined quantity of the stored materials into a mixing container 106 arranged within the housing 101 in response to control signals generated by the microcontroller. The electronic nozzle 104 operates in response to control signals generated by the microcontroller to regulate the discharge of materials from the associated chamber section. 

[0031]	Upon receiving an activation signal, an internal valve opens to allow a controlled flow of red soil, cement, or water through the nozzle 104 outlet toward the mixing container 106. Flow duration and opening intervals are electronically regulated to ensure dispensing of a predetermined quantity. During operation, the nozzle 104 maintains a directed and consistent discharge stream. Upon completion of the dispensing cycle, the microcontroller commands closure of the valve, thereby stopping material flow. The multi- sectioned chamber 105 functions by maintaining red soil, cement, and water within separate internal compartments arranged inside the housing 101. 

[0032]	During operation, each section selectively releases its stored material toward the corresponding electronic nozzle 104 upon receiving a dispensing command from the microcontroller. Internal pathways guide the materials toward the outlet region without intermixing between compartments. The materials remain contained until the associated nozzle 104 valve is actuated. Sequential or simultaneous dispensing may occur depending on programmed instructions. The chamber thereby enables controlled storage and regulated supply of each material to the mixing container 106 during the automated brick-forming process.

[0033]	A weight sensor is integrated with the mixing container 106 and is configured to continuously detect the quantity of materials received therein. The weight sensor further transmits corresponding signals to the microcontroller, wherein the microcontroller is programmed to initiate a mixing operation upon determination that the detected material weight has reached a predetermined threshold. The weight sensor operates by continuously measuring the load exerted by materials accumulated within the mixing container 106. 

[0034]	As red soil, cement, and water are dispensed into the container 106, the sensor detects incremental weight changes and converts the measured load into electrical signals. These signals are transmitted in real time to the microcontroller for monitoring and comparison with a predefined weight threshold. The sensing process continues throughout the dispensing stage to ensure accurate measurement. Upon detection that the measured weight has reached the predetermined value, the sensor signal triggers the microcontroller to initiate the subsequent mixing operation.

[0035]	A robotic gripper 107 is installed within the housing 101 and is operatively configured to selectively grasp plastic waste pieces stored in a box 108 arranged within the housing 101. The robotic gripper 107 comprises gripping members adapted to engage and hold the plastic waste pieces in a controlled manner during transfer. Upon receiving an operational command from the microcontroller, the robotic gripper 107 retrieves the plastic waste pieces from the box 108 and subsequently deposits the retrieved pieces into a container positioned within the housing 101. The container is configured to receive the plastic waste pieces for subsequent grinding and mixing with other materials, thereby forming a brick-forming mixture suitable for further processing.

[0036]	The robotic gripper 107 operates through coordinated actuation of gripping members controlled by the microcontroller. Upon receiving a command signal, the gripper 107 moves toward the box 108 containing plastic waste pieces and positions the gripping members around a selected piece. The gripping members close to secure the waste piece and maintain stable retention during transfer. The gripper 107 then moves along a predefined path toward the container positioned within the housing 101. Upon reaching the designated location, the gripping members open to release the plastic waste piece into the container. The gripper 107 subsequently returns to the pickup position to repeat the operation.

[0037]	The box 108 functions as a storage unit configured to contain a plurality of plastic waste pieces within the housing 101. The box 108 maintains the waste pieces in a confined and accessible arrangement to enable reliable pickup by the robotic gripper 107. During operation, the robotic gripper 107 approaches the box 108 and accesses the waste pieces positioned within the interior of the box 108. The box 108 remains stationary while the gripper 107 selectively retrieves individual waste pieces from the stored collection. By maintaining the waste pieces in a defined holding area, the box 108 ensures continuous availability of material for transfer into the container for further grinding and mixing processes.

[0038]	A motorized grinding unit 109 is integrated within the container and configured to receive and process materials introduced therein. The motorized grinding unit 109 includes rotating blades operatively connected to a motor to facilitate grinding, mixing, and homogenization of the received materials to form a uniform slurry suitable for brick moulding. A torque sensor is operatively integrated with the motorized grinding unit 109 to monitor resistance encountered by the rotating blades during operation. The torque sensor continuously transmits resistance-related signals to the microcontroller, which dynamically regulates the rotational speed of the grinding unit 109 to maintain consistent mixing conditions and ensure formation of a homogeneous slurry with controlled viscosity and uniform material distribution.

[0039]	The motorized grinding unit 109 operates upon receiving an activation signal from the microcontroller, causing an electric motor to rotate the grinding blades positioned within the container. As the blades rotate, they mechanically break down incoming material particles and simultaneously circulate the contents to achieve uniform blending. The rotational motion creates continuous agitation, allowing solid components and liquids to combine into a consistent slurry. During operation, the unit maintains controlled rotational movement while the microcontroller adjusts the speed based on operational feedback. The grinding action continues until the materials reach a predetermined uniformity suitable for subsequent brick moulding processes.

[0040]	The torque sensor operates by continuously detecting the resistance encountered by the rotating blades during grinding activity. As the motor drives the blades through the material mixture, variations in material density or particle size produce corresponding changes in mechanical load. The torque sensor measures these load variations and converts them into electrical signals representing the torque applied to the motor shaft. These signals are transmitted to the microcontroller in real time. Based on the detected torque values, the microcontroller automatically adjusts the motor rotational speed to compensate for resistance changes, thereby maintaining stable grinding conditions and consistent slurry formation.

[0041]	An electronic spout 110 is operatively connected to a container storing slurry and is configured to dispense the slurry over a plurality of molds 111 arranged along a circular rotatable ring positioned within a housing 101. The spout 110 is electronically controlled to enable regulated and directed discharge of the slurry into individual molds 111 in a sequential manner as the rotatable ring positions each mold beneath the spout 110. A flow sensor is integrated with the spout 110 to continuously monitor the rate of slurry discharge and generate corresponding feedback signals. The feedback signals are transmitted to the microcontroller, which dynamically regulates the dispensing process to ensure uniform filling of each mold.

[0042]	The electronic spout 110 operates through signals received from the microcontroller to initiate and control slurry discharge from the container. Upon receiving a command, an electronically actuated valve within the spout 110 opens to allow slurry flow toward a mold positioned beneath the outlet. As the circular rotatable ring sequentially aligns molds 111 under the spout 110, the microcontroller regulates opening duration to control the dispensed quantity. The spout 110 maintains directed flow to minimize spillage and ensure accurate filling. Once the predetermined volume is delivered, the valve closes automatically, stopping discharge before the next mold advances into the dispensing position.

[0043]	The flow sensor operates by detecting the movement of slurry passing through the spout 110 and converting the detected flow characteristics into electrical signals. During dispensing, the sensor continuously measures the flow rate and transmits real-time data to the microcontroller. The microcontroller compares the received signals with predefined dispensing parameters to determine whether the discharge rate falls within an acceptable range. If deviation occurs, corrective control signals are generated to adjust the valve operation of the spout 110. This feedback loop continues throughout dispensing, thereby maintaining consistent slurry delivery into each mold positioned beneath the spout 110.

[0044]	An articulated bar 112 is arranged within the housing 101 and is operatively connected to a plate disposed at a terminal end thereof, wherein the plate supports a plurality of pneumatic pins 114 configured for selective actuation. The articulated bar 112 facilitates controlled positioning of the plate relative to a plurality of molds 111 containing slurry material. Upon actuation, the pneumatic pins 114 extend downward from the plate to contact the top surface of the slurry and thereby imprint predetermined identification patterns, letters, or symbols. The arrangement ensures accurate marking of the slurry prior to curing while maintaining uniform depth, controlled pressure application, and repeatable positioning across successive molds 111 during the production process.

[0045]	The articulated bar 112 operates through controlled mechanical movement provided by a drive connected to the microcontroller. Upon receiving an operational command, the bar pivots and translates within the housing 101 to move the plate toward a target mold containing slurry. Jointed segments of the articulated bar 112 enable angular adjustment and vertical positioning to ensure that the plate aligns precisely above the mold surface. Sensors provide positional feedback to maintain accuracy during movement. Once alignment is achieved, the bar stabilizes in position to permit actuation of the pneumatic pins 114.

[0046]	The plate functions as a support member that carries and maintains spatial arrangement of the plurality of pneumatic pins 114 during the imprinting operation. During operation, the plate is guided by the articulated bar 112 to a predetermined position above the slurry-filled mold. The plate remains stabilized in a horizontal orientation to ensure uniform contact between the pneumatic pins 114 and the slurry surface. Structural rigidity of the plate maintains consistent spacing and alignment of the pins. After positioning, the plate holds the pneumatic pins 114 in proper orientation while pneumatic actuation extends the pins to create the intended imprint patterns.

[0047]	The plurality of pneumatic pins 114 operates through pneumatic actuation supplied by a pressurized air unit connected to individual or grouped pin operations. Upon receiving an activation signal, compressed air drives the pins downward from the plate toward the slurry surface within the mold. Each pin extends to a controlled depth, thereby imprinting portions of predetermined identification patterns, letters, or symbols on the slurry surface. The pins maintain contact for a defined interval to ensure clear marking. Subsequently, release of pneumatic pressure causes the pins to retract back into the plate, completing the marking cycle before movement to the next mold.

[0048]	An articulated pole 115 is operatively coupled with a pressing plate 116 positioned at a terminal end thereof, wherein the pressing plate 116 is configured to apply controlled downward pressure over slurry contained within each mold. The articulated configuration enables adjustable angular and vertical displacement to ensure uniform engagement across the slurry surface. Upon actuation, the pressing plate 116 contacts the slurry and distributes compressive force evenly to level the mixture and eliminate surface irregularities. Such controlled compaction facilitates uniform density and surface finish within the mold cavity prior to the slurry setting stage, thereby ensuring consistent formation, structural stability, and dimensional uniformity of the molded product.

[0049]	The articulated pole 115 operates through controlled pivoting and vertical displacement governed by a mechanical or motor-driven actuator. Upon receiving an operational command, the pole moves downward toward the mold region while maintaining alignment through jointed articulation. The articulation permits angular adjustment to ensure proper positioning of the pressing plate 116 over the slurry surface. The pole stabilizes at a predetermined height and maintains consistent force transmission through the pressing plate 116, allowing the compaction process to occur effectively before the pole retracts to its initial position.

[0050]	The pressing plate 116 functions by directly engaging the slurry surface contained within the mold upon downward movement of the articulated pole 115. As the plate contacts the slurry, controlled pressure is distributed across the surface area to compress and level the mixture. The rigid structure of the plate ensures even force transmission, thereby eliminating uneven slurry distribution and surface irregularities. During operation, the applied pressure is maintained for a predetermined duration to achieve proper compaction. After completion of the leveling process, the plate disengages from the slurry as the articulated pole 115 retracts upward, allowing the compacted mixture to proceed toward the setting stage.

[0051]	A Peltier module 117 is integrated with each mold and is operatively configured to regulate temperature within the molds 111 during formation of the brick mixture. The Peltier module 117 functions as a thermoelectric device capable of selectively generating heating or cooling effects in response to an electrical input. When positioned in thermal communication with the mold surface, the module facilitates controlled thermal regulation to maintain a predetermined temperature range suitable for curing and stabilization of the brick mixture. Such regulated temperature control ensures uniform setting, reduces irregular solidification, and enhances structural integrity of the formed bricks during the molding and stabilization process.

[0052]	The Peltier module 117 operates by receiving an electrical current that induces thermoelectric heat transfer across two dissimilar semiconductor junctions. Upon activation, one side of the module absorbs heat while the opposite side dissipates heat, thereby creating a controlled temperature gradient. The module is positioned in thermal contact with the mold surface so that heat absorption or release directly influences the mold temperature. The microcontroller regulates the supplied current based on sensed temperature conditions, thereby maintaining the required thermal environment within the mold and ensuring stable setting of the brick mixture during formation.

[0053]	A vibrating unit is operatively integrated with each mold to generate controlled vibrational motion configured to facilitate loosening and separation of a formed brick from an internal mold surface after completion of the molding process. The vibrating unit is arranged to reduce adhesion between the formed brick and the mold, thereby enabling smooth removal without structural damage. Concurrently, an articulated arm 119 installed within the housing 101 is configured to move toward the mold, securely grasp the loosened brick, and transfer the brick from the mold location. The articulated arm 119 subsequently places the brick within a user-accessible tray 120 arranged inside the housing 101, wherein the bricks are deposited in a sequential and orderly manner for convenient retrieval by a user.

[0054]	The vibrating unit operates by generating periodic mechanical oscillations transmitted to the mold structure after completion of brick formation. Upon receiving an activation signal from the microcontroller, a vibration actuator produces controlled amplitude and frequency vibrations directed toward the mold walls. The induced vibrations reduce frictional adhesion between the molded brick and the mold surface, thereby enabling gradual detachment of the brick. The vibration continues for a predetermined duration until sensors detect sufficient loosening of the brick. Thereafter, the vibrating unit ceases operation to stabilize the mold, enabling subsequent engagement of the articulated arm 119 for brick removal.

[0055]	The articulated arm 119 operates through coordinated rotational and translational movements controlled by a drive operation within the housing 101. Upon receiving a signal indicating mold vibration completion, the arm 119 moves toward the mold cavity while maintaining a predetermined orientation. A gripping operation at the terminal end engages the loosened brick and applies controlled holding force to secure the brick. The arm 119 subsequently retracts from the mold and follows a guided path toward the tray 120 location. During movement, position sensors regulate alignment and speed. The arm 119 ultimately positions the brick above the tray 120 and releases the brick to complete the transfer sequence.

[0056]	The user-accessible tray 120 operates as a receiving platform configured to collect formed bricks delivered by the articulated arm 119. The tray 120 remains positioned within the housing 101 at a predetermined receiving location aligned with the arm 119 movement path. Upon arrival of the articulated arm 119, the tray 120 receives the released brick and supports the brick in a stable orientation. The tray 120 accommodates sequential placement of multiple bricks without disturbing previously deposited bricks. Structural guides within the tray 120 maintain orderly arrangement and prevent displacement. The tray 120 remains accessible to the user through an opening of the housing 101, enabling convenient manual retrieval of accumulated bricks.

[0057]	A speaker 118 is operatively arranged with the housing 101 and electrically coupled with the microcontroller to provide an audible notification to a user upon completion of a predefined operational cycle. The speaker 118 is configured to receive signal instructions from the microcontroller and convert the received electrical signal into a corresponding audible output. The audible notification serves to inform the user regarding completion of the operation, thereby facilitating timely user awareness and device monitoring. The speaker 118 is positioned within or adjacent to the housing 101 to ensure clear sound transmission while maintaining integration with the structural configuration of the device.

[0058]	Upon completion of the operational cycle, the microcontroller generates an electrical signal corresponding to a predefined notification command. The signal is transmitted through an electrical interface to the speaker 118. A diaphragm within the speaker 118 responds to the electrical signal by producing controlled vibrations, thereby generating an audible sound output. The generated sound propagates outwardly from the housing 101 to alert the user regarding completion of the operation. The notification may be produced as a tone, beep, or preconfigured audio signal.

[0059]	A communication module is operatively integrated within the microcontroller to facilitate wireless data exchange between the device and a computing unit inbuilt with a user interface associated with the device. The communication module enables bidirectional transmission of operational data, control commands, and status information, thereby supporting remote access and monitoring of device functions. The module may include a Wi-Fi module configured to communicate through a wireless local network or a GSM module configured to transmit data through a cellular network. Such configuration ensures reliable connectivity between the microcontroller and the computing unit, enabling real-time supervision, device diagnostics, and user-controlled operation of the device.

[0060]	The communication module operates by receiving digital signals from the microcontroller representing operational parameters, status information, or control commands. Upon activation, the module converts the signals into wireless data packets and transmits them through a selected communication medium. When configured as a Wi-Fi module, the data packets are transmitted through a wireless local network to the computing unit. When configured as a GSM module, the data is transmitted through a cellular communication network. Incoming instructions from the computing unit are received by the module, decoded, and forwarded to the microcontroller for execution of corresponding device operations.

[0061]	The computing unit operates by receiving transmitted operational data from the communication module and processing the received information through embedded software routines. The processed data is displayed through the user interface to enable a user to observe device status, operational parameters, and alerts in real time. User-generated commands entered through the interface are converted into control instructions by the computing unit and transmitted back through the communication module to the microcontroller. The microcontroller interprets the received instructions and adjusts device operations accordingly, thereby enabling remote monitoring, parameter modification, and controlled execution of device functions.

[0062]	The present invention works in the following manner, wherein the device comprises the housing 101 forms a structural enclosure accommodating the functional components of the device, while the plurality of suction cups 102 arranged underneath the housing 101 securely adheres the housing 101 over the surface to maintain operational stability during brick production. The input means operatively linked with the microcontroller enables the user to provide command for initiation and control of the automated plastic-based brick production operation through the microphone 103 or the display unit, whereupon the microcontroller receives and processes the user command to activate subsequent operations. Upon initiation, the electronic nozzle 104 connected to each section of the multi- sectioned chamber 105 storing the red soil, the cement, and the water dispenses the predetermined quantity of the stored materials into the mixing container 106 arranged within the housing 101. The weight sensor integrated with the mixing container 106 detects the quantity of materials received within the container and transmits signal to the microcontroller when the predetermined material weight is reached, thereby initiating the next operational stage. The robotic gripper 107 installed within the housing 101 securely grasps the plastic waste pieces from the box 108 arranged within the housing 101 and places the plastic waste pieces within the container for grinding and mixing. The motorized grinding unit 109 integrated within the container rotates the blades to grind, mix, and homogenize the received materials into the uniform slurry suitable for brick moulding, while the torque sensor detects resistance encountered by the grinding blades and transmits feedback to the microcontroller to dynamically regulate rotational speed of the grinding unit 109 for maintaining mixture consistency. 

[0063]	Subsequently, the electronic spout 110 connected to the container dispenses the slurry over the plurality of molds 111 arranged with the circular rotatable ring in the sequential manner, while the flow sensor monitors the rate of slurry discharge and enables the microcontroller to regulate the dispensing quantity within each mold. The articulated bar 112 having the plate integrated with the plurality of pneumatic pins 114 selectively extends the pins to imprint predetermined identification patterns on the slurry surface, following which the articulated pole 115 having the pressing plate 116 applies controlled downward pressure over the slurry to uniformly level and compact the mixture. The Peltier module 117 integrated with each mold regulates temperature for controlled setting of the mixture, and the vibrating unit generates vibration to loosen the formed brick from the mold, where after the articulated arm 119 grasps the formed brick and places the formed brick within the user-accessible tray 120 in the sequential manner. The speaker 118 arranged with the housing 101 provides notification regarding completion of the operation, and the communication module integrated within the microcontroller establishes wireless communication with the computing unit having the user interface to enable remote monitoring and operational control of the device.

[0064]	The present invention has industrial applicability in construction material manufacturing industries engaged in brick production and waste management. The invention enables utilization of plastic waste along with construction materials to produce bricks suitable for building activities. The device implemented in small-scale brick manufacturing units, recycling facilities, construction material production plants, and waste processing industries. The device assists industries in converting plastic waste into usable construction products while maintaining uniform brick formation and quality. Further, the invention supports sustainable manufacturing practices by promoting reuse of plastic waste and reducing environmental pollution, thereby making it suitable for large-scale industrial deployment in brick production and recycling sectors.

[0065]	Although the field of the invention has been described herein with limited reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense. Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.  ,

title: WEATHER RESPONSIVE CLOTHES DRYING DEVICE
abstract: A weather responsive clothes drying device comprising a frame 101 to support hanging clothes, a canopy deployment assembly to automatically deploy a protective canopy above the hanging clothes, a lateral shield assembly to deploy one or more protective panels 106 around the hanging clothes, a rotating base assembly to rotate the hangers 102 relative to a ground surface, a weather sensing module 112 to detect environmental parameters including rain, humidity, wind speed, temperature and ambient light, a stabilization unit to anchor the frame 101 on a ground surface during high wind condition, a ventilation module to circulate air across the drying stand during high wind conditions, a control unit to process environmental data to deploy the canopy, activate the lateral shields, rotate the drying frame 101 toward available sunlight, stabilize the stand during high wind conditions, and activate the ventilation module for enhanced drying of the clothes.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001]	The present invention relates to a weather responsive clothes drying device that is capable of automatically adapting to changing environmental conditions for cloths by sensing climatic parameters and autonomously adjusting itself operational functions to protect clothes and enhance drying efficiency, thereby providing improved reliability, convenience, and optimized utilization of natural drying conditions.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
	
[0002]	In recent years, outdoor drying stands have gained popularity as an eco-friendly alternative to electric dryers. However, exposure to unpredictable weather often results in inconvenience and damage to clothes. Rainfall, high humidity, strong winds, and fluctuating sunlight intensity directly affect the drying process, leading to longer drying times and potential deterioration of fabric quality. Conventional drying stands generally lack protective features, leaving clothes vulnerable to sudden showers or dust carried by wind. Moreover, limited adaptability to environmental changes reduces efficiency, especially in regions with variable climates. As households increasingly seek sustainable solutions, there is a growing demand for drying equipment that adapts to environmental conditions while ensuring fabric protection and faster drying performance.

[0003]	Traditionally, drying stands have been designed with simple frames and hangers, offering only basic support for clothes. Protective covers, when available, are often manually operated and fail to respond to sudden weather changes. Lateral shielding is rarely incorporated, leaving clothes exposed to wind-driven dust and rain. Rotating frames for better sunlight exposure are uncommon, and stabilization features against strong winds are generally absent. Ventilation for enhanced drying under humid conditions is also overlooked, resulting in prolonged drying cycles. The absence of integrated sensing and responsive features has limited the effectiveness of conventional designs, creating a need for advanced drying equipment that adapts to diverse environmental parameters while maintaining convenience and reliability for users.

[0004]	CN201842984U discloses about an automatic controlled clothes aired, which comprises a plurality of drying rods, and a controller is provided at one end of the left drying rod, and is characterized in that: the drying rods are connected to each other through foldable shrinkable connecting pipes, and the controller It is connected with one end of the drying rod on the left side by a wire rope. After the controller of the utility model detects abrupt weather signals such as wind and rain, it controls its internal motor module to pull the steel wire rope, so that the connecting pipe is folded and shrunk, preventing the clothes from being blown off by the wind or getting wet by the rain. Easy to use.

[0005]	US20100162588A1  discloses about a device for drying clothes includes a tunnel portion, a funnel portion provided at least at one end of the tunnel portion, and a hanging assembly  for clothes provided within the tunnel portion.
	
[0006]	Conventionally, many devices have relied on basic structures with limited adaptability to changing weather. Designs often emphasize simplicity and affordability, yet they fail to address challenges posed by rain, wind, and fluctuating humidity. As a result, clothes remain exposed to environmental factors, leading to longer drying times and potential fabric damage.

[0007]	In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that requires to be capable of protecting clothes from sudden weather changes, enhancing drying efficiency under varying conditions, maintaining stability during adverse environments, and ensuring reliable performance while supporting sustainable household practices.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION
[0008]	An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of automatically responding to changing weather conditions to protect clothes and improve drying efficiency during outdoor drying operations.

[0009]	Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of adjusting operations as per current environmental conditions such as rain, sunlight, wind, and humidity to maintain effective and reliable drying performance.

[0010]	 Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing an automated clothes drying arrangement that reduces manual effort by continuously monitoring surrounding environmental conditions and responding appropriately to ensure proper drying of clothes

[0011]	Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a drying device that improves reliability and safety of outdoor clothes drying while maintaining consistent drying performance under varying and unpredictable weather conditions.
    	
[0012]	 The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]	 The present invention relates to a weather responsive clothes drying device that is capable of automatically responding to changing environmental conditions by sensing weather variations and adjusting drying operations accordingly to protect clothes, improve drying efficiency, reduce manual effort, and ensure reliable and safe outdoor drying performance.
[0014]	According to an aspect of the present invention, a frame configured with multiple hangers adapted to support hanging clothes is provided, a canopy deployment assembly mounted on an upper portion of the frame is adapted to automatically deploy a protective canopy above the hanging clothes, the canopy deployment assembly includes multiple extendable links configured to extend and retract a foldable canopy structure above the drying frame, the canopy comprises a zig-zag articulated frame configured to form a V-shaped protective roof for directing rainwater away from the hanging clothes, a lateral shield assembly arranged along lateral sides of the frame is adapted to deploy one or more protective panels around the hanging clothes, the lateral shield assembly includes transparent sliding panels mounted on a rack-and-pinion arrangement configured to deploy along lateral portions of the frame, a rotating base assembly supporting the frame is adapted to rotate the hangers relative to a ground surface, the rotating base assembly includes a motor-driven turntable configured to orient the drying frame toward a direction of highest ambient light intensity detected by the weather sensing module.

[0015]	According to another aspect of the present invention, the device further comprises of a weather sensing module integrated in the frame adapted to detect environmental parameters including rain humidity wind speed temperature and ambient light, the weather sensing module includes a rain sensor a humidity sensor a wind speed sensor an ambient light sensor and a temperature sensor configured to continuously monitor environmental conditions, a stabilization unit arranged with the base is adapted to anchor the frame on a ground surface during high wind conditions, the stabilization unit includes one or more deployable stabilizer pins and friction pads configured to increase ground grip of the drying stand during high wind conditions, a ventilation module integrated with the frame is configured to circulate air across the drying stand during high wind conditions, the ventilation module includes multiple airflow fans integrated within hangers to circulate air across the hanging clothes during high humidity conditions, a control unit operatively linked with the canopy deployment assembly the lateral shield assembly, the rotating base assembly, the stabilization unit, the ventilation module and the weather sensing module is configured to process environmental data to autonomously deploy the canopy activate the lateral shields rotate the drying frame toward available sunlight stabilize the stand during high wind conditions and activate the ventilation module for enhanced drying of the clothes, the control unit is configured to activate the ventilation module when ambient humidity exceeds a predefined threshold to accelerate drying of the clothes, the control unit is linked with a wireless communication module configured to transmit environmental data operational status and alerts to a computing unit for remote monitoring.

[0016]	 While the invention has been described and shown with particular reference to the preferred embodiment, it will be apparent that variations might be possible that would fall within the scope of the present invention.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS 

[0017]	 These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become better understood with regard to the following description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings where:
Figure 1 illustrates an isometric view of a weather responsive clothes drying device.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 

[0018]	 The following description includes the preferred best mode of one embodiment of the present invention. It will be clear from this description of the invention that the invention is not limited to these illustrated embodiments but that the invention also includes a variety of modifications and embodiments thereto. Therefore, the present description should be seen as illustrative and not limiting. While the invention is susceptible to various modifications and alternative constructions, it should be understood, that there is no intention to limit the invention to the specific form disclosed, but, on the contrary, the invention is to cover all modifications, alternative constructions, and equivalents falling within the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the claims.

[0019]	 In any embodiment described herein, the open-ended terms "comprising," "comprises,” and the like (which are synonymous with "including," "having” and "characterized by") may be replaced by the respective partially closed phrases "consisting essentially of," consists essentially of," and the like or the respective closed phrases "consisting of," "consists of, the like.

[0020]	 As used herein, the singular forms “a,” “an,” and “the” designate both the singular and the plural, unless expressly stated to designate the singular only. 	

[0021]	The present invention relates to a weather responsive clothes drying device that is capable of adapting to current environmental conditions by sensing weather parameters and dynamically providing protection, directional exposure, and assisted airflow, thereby improving drying efficiency, protecting garments from sudden weather changes, and enabling autonomous outdoor drying.

[0022]	 Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a weather responsive clothes drying device is illustrated, comprising a frame 101 configured with multiple hangers 102, a canopy deployment assembly mounted on an upper portion of the frame 101, the canopy deployment assembly includes multiple extendable links 103, a foldable canopy structure 104, a zig-zag articulated frame 105, a lateral shield assembly arranged along lateral sides of the frame 101, the lateral shield assembly includes transparent sliding panels 106 mounted on a rack-and-pinion arrangement 107, a rotating base assembly supporting the frame 101, the rotating base assembly includes a motor-driven turntable 108, a stabilization unit arranged with the base, the stabilization unit includes one or more deployable stabilizer pins 109 and friction pads 110, a ventilation module integrated with the frame 101, the ventilation module includes multiple airflow fans 111 integrated within hangers 102, a weather sensing module 112 integrated in the frame 101.

[0023]	 The device disclosed herein includes a frame 101 is developed to be positioned on a surface and constructed from durable, and configured with multiple hangers 102 adapted to support clothes in a suspended position. The frame 101 is equipped with a push button for activating and deactivating the device.

[0024]	 The push button is accessed by the user for activating the device. When the user presses the push button, the electrical circuit is completed, which in response turns the device on. The push button is integrated with an actuator and a spring, which are automatically activated when pressed. The actuator and spring work together to move the internal contact, completing the circuit and allowing electrical current to flow, thereby activating the device.

[0025]	 When the push button is pressed, the button sends a signal (usually a change in voltage or current) to an inbuilt control unit associated with the device to either power up or shut down the device. The control unit is pre-fed to detect this signal and respond accordingly. The control unit used herein is pre-fed using artificial intelligence and machine learning protocols to coordinate the working of the device.

[0026]	 A weather sensing module 112 is integrated within the frame 101 and is configured to detect environmental parameters, including rain, humidity, wind speed, temperature, and ambient light. The module comprises a rain sensor, humidity sensor, wind speed sensor, ambient light sensor, and temperature sensor, each designed to continuously monitor respective environmental conditions to provide real-time data for autonomous operation of the drying device.

[0027]	The rain sensor detects the presence of precipitation on the drying stand. The rain sensor comprises a conductive or capacitive surface exposed to the environment. When raindrops contact the sensing surface, they change the electrical conductivity or capacitance, generating a signal. This signal is transmitted to the control unit, which interprets the control unit to deploy the canopy and lateral shields. The rain sensor is connected with signal conditioning circuitry to filter noise and prevent false triggers. The rain sensor rapid response ensures timely protection of clothes, and the module is weather-resistant to maintain long-term functionality in outdoor conditions.

[0028]	The humidity sensor measures the relative humidity of the surrounding air. The humidity sensor consists of a capacitive or resistive sensing element that changes its electrical properties based on moisture content. The sensor continuously transmits real-time data to the control unit, which uses this information to activate the ventilation module, adjusting the airflow to accelerate drying. Some sensors also include temperature compensation circuitry to maintain accuracy under varying environmental conditions. The humidity sensor is housed within a protective casing that allows exposure to ambient air while shielding the humidity sensor from dust, water, and debris, ensuring reliable long-term operation.

[0029]	The wind speed sensor, or anemometer, detects the velocity of airflow around the drying stand. The wind speed sensor uses rotating cups, propellers, or ultrasonic transducers to measure wind speed. The sensor converts mechanical rotation or ultrasonic time-of-flight changes into electrical signals proportional to wind velocity. Data from the sensor is transmitted to the control unit, which accordingly adjusts the ventilation for optimal airflow. The sensor is designed to withstand outdoor exposure and provides continuous monitoring, enabling the control unit to respond promptly to gusts or changes in wind direction for safety and efficiency.

[0030]	The ambient light sensor measures the intensity of sunlight or ambient illumination. The ambient light sensor consists of a photodiode or phototransistor that converts light intensity into an electrical signal. The control unit receives real-time data from the sensor to rotate the drying frame 101 toward the direction of highest light intensity. This maximizes solar exposure and accelerates drying. The ambient light sensor includes filters or lenses to ensure accurate readings under direct sunlight or cloudy conditions. Housed in a weather-resistant casing, the sensor maintains long-term functionality while providing precise measurements to optimize autonomous orientation and energy-efficient drying.

[0031]	The temperature sensor measures ambient air temperature surrounding the drying stand. Common types include thermistors, RTDs, or semiconductor-based sensors that produce an electrical output corresponding to temperature changes. The control unit uses this data in combination with humidity and wind readings to adjust fan speed, canopy deployment, and overall drying strategy. Protective housings allow the sensor to function accurately outdoors while preventing damage from rain, dust, or sunlight. Continuous temperature monitoring ensures optimal drying conditions, prevents overheating of clothes in direct sunlight, and provides data for remote monitoring or alerts via a wireless communication module.

[0032]	A rotating base assembly is supporting the frame 101 and is configured to rotate the hangers 102 relative to the ground surface. The assembly comprises a motor-driven turntable 108 designed to orient the drying frame 101 toward the direction of maximum ambient light intensity, as detected by the weather sensing module 112, to optimize sunlight exposure for efficient drying of the clothes.

[0033]	 The rotating base assembly forms the foundation of the drying frame 101, providing rotational movement to orient the hangers 102 relative to the ground surface. The rotating base assembly comprises a sturdy, low-friction turntable 108 platform mounted on the lower portion of the frame 101, designed to support the weight of the frame 101 and hanging clothes while allowing smooth rotation. Bearings and a support ring ensure stability and minimize mechanical wear. The assembly is integrated with the control unit, which receives input from the weather sensing module 112. Based on sunlight intensity, the control unit signals the assembly to adjust the frame 101 orientation, optimizing sunlight exposure for efficient drying.

[0034]	 The motor-driven turntable 108 within the rotating base assembly converts electrical energy into controlled rotational motion. A DC or stepper motor is connected to a gear that drives the turntable platform. When the control unit detects the direction of maximum ambient light, the control unit actuates the motor to rotate the turntable 108, aligning the frame 101 accordingly. Sensors, such as rotary encoders, provide position feedback to ensure precise orientation. The control unit stop the turntable 108 automatically when the desired direction is reached and continuously adjust for changing sunlight conditions, allowing the clothes to receive consistent solar exposure throughout the drying process.

[0035]	A canopy deployment assembly positioned at the upper portion of the frame 101, configured to automatically extend a protective canopy over the hanging clothes. The canopy deployment assembly includes multiple extendable links 103 configured to extend and retract a foldable canopy structure 104 above the drying frame 101. The extension and retraction of the multiple extendable links 103 is controlled by the control unit through a pneumatic unit associated with the canopy deployment assembly. The pneumatic unit includes an air compressor, air cylinders, air valves, and pistons, which work in coordination to facilitate the smooth extension and retraction of the foldable canopy structure 104. In operation, the control unit actuates the air valves to allow the passage of compressed air from the air compressor into the air cylinders. 

[0036]	The compressed air generates pressure against the pistons, causing them to move and push the connected extendable links 103, thereby extending the canopy. To retract the canopy, the control unit closes the valves, releasing the compressed air and allowing the pistons to return to their original position, which draws the extendable links 103 and the canopy back into a folded state. Thus, the control unit precisely regulates the extension and retraction of the extendable links 103 to ensure the canopy deploys and retracts smoothly in response to environmental conditions.

[0037]	 The canopy comprises a zig-zag articulated frame 105 arranged to form a V-shaped protective roof, configured to channel rainwater away from the hanging clothes. The canopy’s zig-zag articulated frame 105 consists of interconnected hinge-linked segments arranged in a repeating zig-zag pattern. Each hinge allows pivoting, enabling the frame 105 to expand into a V-shaped roof that channels rainwater away from hanging clothes. Deployment and retraction are controlled pneumatically: pistons in air cylinders, actuated by the control unit, push the links 103 to unfold the canopy and retract the canopy by releasing air. Bearings at the joints reduce friction, ensuring smooth motion. This arrangement allows the canopy to respond automatically to environmental conditions, providing reliable protection while maintaining compact storage when not in use.

[0038]	A lateral shield assembly is arranged along the sides of the frame 101 and is configured to deploy one or more protective panels 106 around the hanging clothes. The assembly comprises transparent sliding panels 106 mounted on a rack-and- pinion arrangement 107, enabling controlled horizontal movement along the lateral portions of the frame 101 to shield the clothes from wind, rain, or dust.

[0039]	 The transparent sliding panels 106 serve as protective barriers along the lateral sides of the frame 101, shielding the hanging clothes from wind, rain, and dust. Each panel 106 is made of durable, lightweight, weather-resistant material, allowing visibility while providing protection. The panels 106 are mounted on the rack-and- pinion arrangement 107 that ensure smooth linear movement along the sides of the frame 101. The edges of the panels 106 are reinforced to prevent deformation, and the guides minimize friction and wear. The control unit ensure accurate deployment and retraction in response to environmental conditions

[0040]	The rack-and- pinion arrangement 107 converts rotary motion into linear motion to deploy and retract the sliding panels 106. A motor-driven pinion engages with a toothed rack attached to each panel 106. When the control unit activates the motor, the pinion rotates, causing the rack and therefore the panel 106 to slide along its track. Reversing the motor rotation retracts the panel 106. This mechanical arrangement allows precise, synchronized movement of multiple panels 106 simultaneously, ensuring complete coverage when deployed. The rack-and- pinion arrangement 107 is powered by the control unit, which coordinates panel movement based on inputs from the weather sensing module 112 to protect clothes automatically during rain or high winds.

[0041]	 A stabilization unit arranged with the base and is configured to anchor the drying frame 101 to the ground surface upon detection of high wind conditions. The unit comprises one or more deployable stabilizer pins 109 and friction pads 110, which enhance the ground grip of the stand, preventing tipping or displacement and ensuring stability of the frame 101 under strong wind or adverse environmental conditions.

[0042]	 The deployable stabilizer pins 109 are mechanical components designed to anchor the drying frame 101 securely to the ground during high wind conditions. Each pin 109 is retractable and housed within the lower section of the frame 101 when not in use. Upon receiving a signal from the control unit, triggered by wind speed data from the weather sensing module 112, the pins 109 are extended downward into the ground, providing additional support. Actuated either pneumatically, electrically, or via a mechanical screw drive, the pins 109 penetrate soil or other surfaces to prevent lateral movement or tipping, thereby maintaining the stability of the drying stand.

[0043]	The friction pads 110 are integrated with the base of the frame 101 to enhance grip on the ground surface. Typically made of high-friction, wear-resistant material, the pads 110 increase surface contact and reduce slippage under windy or uneven conditions. The pads 110 work in conjunction with the deployable pins 109: while the pins 109 provide deep anchoring, the pads 110 stabilize the frame 101 laterally. When the control unit detects high wind or instability, the control unit slightly adjust the pressure of the pads 110 via spring-loaded or adjustable arrangement. This ensures the frame 101 remains firmly positioned while distributing weight evenly across the ground for enhanced stability and safety.

[0044]	A ventilation module is integrated with the frame 101 and is configured to circulate air across the drying stand, enhancing drying efficiency under high humidity conditions. The module comprises multiple airflow fans 111 mounted within the hangers 102, which direct a continuous flow of air over the hanging clothes to accelerate moisture evaporation and maintain optimal drying performance.
 
[0045]	 The multiple airflow fans 111 are designed to circulate air efficiently across the hanging clothes, accelerating drying during high humidity conditions. Each fan consists of a brushless DC motor coupled with a rotor and fan blades, which generate a controlled airflow when electrically energized. The fans 111 are mounted within or adjacent to the hangers 102 to direct air over the surfaces of the clothes. The control unit monitors ambient humidity via the weather sensing module 112 and actuates the fans 111 when humidity exceeds a predefined threshold. Speed controllers modulate the rotational speed of each fan to optimize airflow, minimize energy consumption, and ensure uniform drying across the entire drying stand.

[0046]	 The control unit is linked with the wireless communication module, which is configured to transmit environmental data, operational status, and alerts to a computing unit for remote monitoring. The communication module establishes a wireless connection between the control unit and the computing unit, which includes, but is not limited to, a smartphone, tablet, or laptop. The module incorporates a user interface that allows the user to provide input commands, configure operational parameters, and receive notifications regarding the status of the drying device.

[0047]	The communication module includes, but is not limited to, a Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, or GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module. Preferably, a Wi-Fi module is employed, which serves as a hardware component enabling the control unit to connect wirelessly with the computing unit. The Wi-Fi module operates by transmitting and receiving data over radio waves according to IEEE 802.11 standards, which define protocols for wireless local area networking (WLAN). Once a connection is established, the module allows the control unit to send and receive data packets, enabling remote monitoring, control, and real-time feedback regarding environmental conditions and the operational status of the drying device.

[0048]	Lastly, a battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device to supply power to electrically powered components which are employed herein. The battery is comprised of a pair of electrode named as a cathode and an anode. The battery uses a chemical reaction of oxidation/reduction to do work on charge and produce a voltage between their anode and cathode and thus produces electrical energy that is used to do work in the device.

[0049]	The present invention works best in the following manner, where the frame 101 configured with multiple hangers 102 supports hanging clothes while integrating the operational components required for automated drying. The weather sensing module 112 integrated within the frame 101 continuously monitors environmental parameters including rain, humidity, wind speed, temperature, and ambient light through rain sensor, humidity sensor, wind speed sensor, ambient light sensor, and temperature sensor. Environmental data collected by the sensors is transmitted to the control unit, which processes the data and coordinates operation of canopy deployment assembly, lateral shield assembly, rotating base assembly, stabilization unit, ventilation module, and wireless communication module. 

[0050]	In continuation, upon detection of rainfall, the control unit actuates canopy deployment assembly including extendable links 103 and zig-zag articulated frame 105 to extend foldable canopy forming V-shaped protective roof that directs rainwater away from hanging clothes, while lateral shield assembly deploys transparent sliding panels 106 through rack-and- pinion arrangement 107 to protect clothes from wind-driven rain and dust. Simultaneously, rotating base assembly including motor-driven turntable 108 rotates drying frame 101 toward direction of highest ambient light intensity detected by ambient light sensor to maximize solar exposure. During high wind conditions, stabilization unit deploys stabilizer pins 109 and friction pads 110 to anchor frame 101 firmly to ground surface. When humidity exceeds predefined threshold, ventilation module including multiple airflow fans 111 integrated within hangers 102 circulates air across hanging clothes to accelerate evaporation of moisture. Wireless communication module transmits environmental data, operational status, and alerts to computing unit for remote monitoring and user interaction, thereby ensuring efficient, autonomous, and weather-responsive drying operation.

Various modifications of the disclosed embodiments, as well as alternate embodiments of the invention, will become apparent to persons skilled in the art upon reference to the description of the invention.
