title: A Dough Processing Device for Mixing, Dividing, and Dough-Ball Forming and Method of Operation
abstract: The present disclosure proposes a dough processing device (100) for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. The dough processing device (100) employs a common planetary gear-based drive configured to produce opposite-direction rotation of a selectively mounted processing head and a corresponding mixing bowl (148) and circular shaping head (152), thereby enabling counter-rotational dough processing. The dough processing device (100) comprises a driving unit (120), a gear assembly (124) having a sun gear (128), planet gears (130), and an outer ring gear (138), and a spindle shaft (142) selectively receiving a circular mixing head (144) carrying pivot-mounted mixing levers (146) or a circular shaping head (152) carrying radially arranged cutters (158). Opposite-direction rotation of the circular mixing head (144) and the mixing bowl (148) kneads dough, while opposite-direction rotation of the circular shaping head (152) and the circular tray (150) divides a dough mass and forms dough balls.
specification:
DESCRIPTION:
Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of food-processing appliances and mechanical dough-processing systems, and in specific, relates to a dough processing device for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. The dough processing device employs a common planetary gear-based drive configured to produce opposite-direction rotation of a selectively mounted processing head and a corresponding mixing bowl or circular tray, thereby enabling counter-rotational dough processing.
Background of the invention:
[0002] In general, dough preparation involves multiple stages, such as mixing ingredients, kneading the resulting dough mass, dividing the dough into smaller portions, and rounding the divided portions into dough balls. In household settings, these stages are commonly performed using separate implements, including mixing bowls, hand-operated scrapers, cutters, dividers, and shaping tools. Mixing and kneading frequently require repeated manual effort, while division and rounding are performed individually. The use of separate tools increases handling time, occupies additional workspace, and requires repeated transfer of the dough between different processing surfaces.
[0003] Known household dough mixers generally employ a rotating agitator operating within a stationary bowl or a rotating bowl interacting with a substantially stationary mixing element. Certain mixers use multiple rotating hooks or planetary motion to improve kneading. For example, US20240423217A1 discloses a double-hook dough kneading structure in which two hooks are driven through planetary gears engaging an internally toothed ring. However, the double-hook dough kneading structure is principally directed to dough kneading and does not integrate dough dividing and rounding. Further, the double-hook dough kneading structure does not disclose coordinated opposite-direction rotation between a processing head and a dough receptacle for performing multiple dough-processing stages.
[0004] Conventionally developed combined dough mixing, cutting, and ball-forming tool reduced dependence on separate appliances but retained certain functional limitations. The mixing operation employed a motor-driven rotating element while the mixing bowl remained stationary, thereby providing limited relative movement between the dough and mixing element and potentially causing uneven kneading and increased processing time. Dough cutting and ball formation were performed sequentially, with individual portions being processed one after another. Further, the formed dough balls could contact and adhere to one another, requiring additional manual separation and reducing the convenience and efficiency of the overall processing operation.
[0005] In prior art, CN217164109U discloses a food-processing mixer having a rotating kettle driven through a worm-and-worm-wheel transmission and stirring paddles undergoing vertical reciprocating movement. The combined kettle rotation and paddle movement improve mixing of raw materials. Nevertheless, the disclosed machine is directed primarily to general material mixing and does not perform dough dividing or dough-ball rounding. The machine also employs separate drive arrangements for kettle rotation and paddle reciprocation, thereby increasing structural complexity. However, the food-processing mixer does not provide a compact, common processing platform for completing successive dough preparation stages.
[0006] In another prior art, CN210445478U discloses an intelligent dough dividing and rounding machine having an extrusion device, pressing device, cutter device, rounding device, conveying device, control device, and display device. The dough is conveyed through a series of independently operating sections for extrusion, portioning, cutting, transport, and rounding. Although the machine combines several processing functions, the use of multiple dedicated modules, conveying positions, and coordinated actuators results in a comparatively large and complex system. Such an arrangement requires increased installation space, maintenance, manufacturing cost, and operational control, thereby limiting suitability for ordinary household kitchens.
[0007] Therefore, there is a need for a dough processing device for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. The dough processing device employs a common planetary gear-based drive configured to produce opposite-direction rotation of a selectively mounted processing head and a corresponding mixing bowl or circular tray, thereby enabling counter-rotational dough processing. There is also a need for a dough processing device that performs mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming through a common household-scale processing platform, thereby reducing dependence on separate appliances, repeated transfer of dough, and successive manual operations. There is also a need for a dough processing device that increases relative movement between a dough-contacting processing member and a dough receptacle during mixing. Furthermore, there is also a need for a dough processing device that divides a dough mass into multiple portions and forms the divided portions into dough balls with reduced sequential handling.
Objectives of the invention:
[0008] The primary objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. The dough processing device employs a common planetary gear-based drive configured to produce opposite-direction rotation of a selectively mounted processing head and a corresponding mixing bowl or circular tray, thereby enabling counter-rotational dough processing.
[0009] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that integrates mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming within a common household-scale structure, thereby reducing separate appliances, dough transfers, manual handling, and processing time.
[0010] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that uses a planetary gear-based drive to rotate a processing head and a corresponding bowl or tray simultaneously in opposite directions from a single driving unit input.
[0011] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that incorporates a dual-threaded spindle selectively receiving a mixing head and a shaping head, thereby enabling tool-free conversion between mixing and dough-ball-forming modes.
[0012] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that includes mixing levers configured to repeatedly lift, fold, stretch, and press dough from changing contact directions for improved and uniform kneading.
[0013] Another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that includes a circular shaping head having radially arranged cutters for dividing a dough mass into multiple portions and forming the separated portions into dough balls.
[0014] Yet another objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that includes height-adjustment levers, guiding grooves, groove pads, pins, clamp slots, and clamp pads for positioning the processing assembly and securing the bowl or tray.
[0015] Further objective of the present invention is to provide a dough processing device that includes removable processing components and non-stick dough-contacting surfaces for reducing dough adhesion, facilitating dough-ball release, simplifying cleaning, and improving household operating convenience.
Summary of the invention:
[0016] The present disclosure proposes a dough processing device for mixing, dividing, and dough-ball forming and method of operation. The following presents a simplified summary in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects of the claimed subject matter. This summary is not an extensive overview. It is not intended to identify key/critical elements or to delineate the scope of the claimed subject matter. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.
[0017] In order to overcome the above deficiencies of the prior art, the present disclosure is to solve the technical problem to provide a dough processing device for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. The dough processing device employs a common planetary gear-based drive configured to produce opposite-direction rotation of a selectively mounted processing head and a corresponding mixing bowl or circular tray, thereby enabling counter-rotational dough processing.
[0018] According to one aspect, the invention provides a dough processing device. In one embodiment herein, the dough processing device comprises a base plate, a vertical support stand, a top circular plate, a housing, a driving unit, a gear assembly, a spindle shaft, and a pair of side handles. In one embodiment herein, the base plate is configured to removably support a selected one of a mixing bowl and a circular tray thereon. The vertical support stand is mounted on the base plate and includes a bottom end fixed to the base plate and a top end supporting the top circular plate, thereby maintaining structural rigidity and alignment during operation.
[0019] In one embodiment herein, the top circular plate defines an inner hollow portion and supports the housing mounted thereon. The housing encloses the driving unit configured to provide rotational drive for the dough processing device. In one embodiment herein, the gear assembly is disposed within the inner hollow portion of the top circular plate. The gear assembly comprises a sun gear coupled to a drive shaft of the driving unit, a plurality of planet gears circumferentially arranged around and meshing with the sun gear, a carrier support plate fixed relative to the top circular plate and rotatably supporting the plurality of planet gears through respective gear carriers, and an outer ring gear concentrically surrounding and internally meshing with the plurality of planet gears.
[0020] In one embodiment herein, the drive shaft extends downwardly from the gear assembly and is coupled to the sun gear. The drive shaft comprises external threads formed at a lower portion thereof. The spindle shaft comprises internal threads at an upper portion thereof threadedly engaged with the external threads of the drive shaft and further comprises external lower threads configured to releasably receive interchangeable processing heads. The spindle shaft selectively receives the circular mixing head carrying the plurality of mixing levers or the circular shaping head carrying the plurality of radially arranged cutters, thereby permitting selective operation of the dough processing device in a mixing configuration and a dividing and dough-ball-forming configuration through the common drive mechanism.
[0021] In one embodiment herein, activation of the driving unit supplies rotational input to the sun gear. The sun gear, the drive shaft, and the spindle shaft define a first rotational transmission pathway configured to rotate the selected one of the circular mixing head and the circular shaping head in a first rotational direction. The plurality of planet gears, the outer ring gear, the pair of flat bars, the pair of side handles, the height-adjustment levers, the clamp slots, and the clamp pads define a second rotational transmission pathway configured to rotate the corresponding selected one of the mixing bowl and the circular tray in a second rotational direction opposite to the first rotational direction. The carrier support plate remains fixed relative to the top circular plate such that rotation of the plurality of planet gears drives the outer ring gear in the second rotational direction.
[0022] In the mixing configuration, the circular mixing head is mounted to the spindle shaft and the mixing bowl is coupled to the outer ring gear through the receptacle-coupling arrangement. The first rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular mixing head in the first rotational direction while the second rotational transmission pathway rotates the mixing bowl in the second rotational direction. The resulting opposite-direction rotation causes the plurality of mixing levers to repeatedly contact, lift, fold, stretch, and press dough contained in the mixing bowl from changing angular directions.
[0023] In the dividing and dough-ball-forming configuration, the circular shaping head is mounted to the spindle shaft and the circular tray is coupled to the outer ring gear through the receptacle-coupling arrangement. Downward movement of the circular shaping head causes the plurality of radially arranged cutters to divide the dough mass contained in the circular tray into a plurality of dough portions. Thereafter, the first rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular shaping head in the first rotational direction while the second rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular tray in the second rotational direction, thereby subjecting the plurality of dough portions to rolling and compressive movement for formation of a plurality of dough balls.
[0024] In one embodiment herein, the base plate comprises a center protrusion, and each of the mixing bowl and the circular tray comprises a corresponding slot removably positionable over the center protrusion. The engagement between the center protrusion and the slot concentrically aligns the selected one of the mixing bowl and the circular tray with the spindle shaft and the selected processing head, thereby improving operational stability during mixing and shaping operations.
[0025] In one embodiment herein, the internal threads of the spindle shaft threadedly engage the external threads of the drive shaft, and the external lower threads of the spindle shaft selectively engage corresponding internal threads of the circular mixing head or a hollow shaft of the circular shaping head. The threaded engagement permits rapid removal and interchange of the circular mixing head and the circular shaping head while maintaining secure mechanical coupling during operation.
[0026] In one embodiment herein, each of the plurality of mixing levers is connected to the circular mixing head through a respective pivot connection that permits limited angular movement of the corresponding mixing lever during contact with the dough. The pivotable arrangement enables the mixing levers to adapt to variations in dough consistency while reducing excessive resistance during kneading.
[0027] In one embodiment herein, the circular shaping head comprises the hollow shaft having internal threads engaged with the external threads of the spindle shaft. The plurality of radially arranged cutters extends from an underside of the circular shaping head, and a plurality of gripping members is positioned adjacent to the hollow shaft. The gripping members are configured to receive downward pressure applied by a user to facilitate penetration of the plurality of radially arranged cutters into the dough mass for dividing the dough into individual portions.
[0028] In one embodiment herein, each side handle comprises a guiding groove extending longitudinally along the side handle and a pin slot. A corresponding height-adjustment lever comprises groove pads positioned in engagement with the guiding groove and a pin received within the pin slot, thereby guiding longitudinal movement of the height-adjustment lever relative to the corresponding side handle. The height-adjustment lever further comprises a clamp slot formed at a lower region thereof. The clamp slot is releasably engageable with a corresponding clamp pad provided on the selected one of the mixing bowl and the circular tray. Engagement of the clamp slot with the corresponding clamp pad retains the selected receptacle in an aligned operating position and couples the selected receptacle to the side handle for transmission of rotational movement from the outer ring gear.
[0029] In one embodiment herein, the plurality of planet gears is circumferentially spaced around the sun gear. The carrier support plate is fixed within the inner hollow portion of the top circular plate and comprises a centrally disposed circular pad connected to the housing to provide structural support to the driving unit while maintaining accurate positioning of the gear assembly during operation.
[0030] In one embodiment herein, dough-contacting surfaces of at least one of the plurality of mixing levers, the circular tray, the circular shaping head, and the plurality of radially arranged cutters comprise a non-stick coating configured to reduce adherence of dough thereto. In one exemplary embodiment, the non-stick coating comprises polytetrafluoroethylene. The non-stick coating reduces accumulation of dough on the dough-contacting surfaces, facilitates release of the dough portions, and simplifies cleaning after completion of a dough-processing operation.
[0031] In one embodiment herein, the dough processing device further comprises a controller electrically connected to the driving unit and a plurality of control buttons electrically connected to the controller. The plurality of control buttons is configured to selectively energize the driving unit, stop the driving unit, and select one of a plurality of predetermined rotational speeds. In another embodiment herein, the controller is configured to regulate operation of the driving unit according to user-selected operating modes, thereby enabling controlled mixing and dough-ball-forming operations.
[0032] According to another aspect, the invention provides a method for operating the dough processing device. At one step, the user mounts the mixing bowl on the base plate and engages the clamp pad of the mixing bowl with the clamp slot of the height-adjustment lever connected through the side handle and the flat bar to the outer ring gear. At another step, the circular mixing head with the plurality of mixing levers connects to the spindle shaft of the driving unit. At another step, the controller activates the driving unit to rotate the sun gear in the first rotational direction, thereby rotating the drive shaft, the spindle shaft, and the circular mixing head in the first rotational direction.
[0033] At another step, the sun gear, through the plurality of planet gears, transmits the rotation to the outer ring gear, thereby rotating the mixing bowl, the flat bar, the side handle, and the height-adjustment lever in a second rotational direction opposite to the first rotational direction. At another step, the mixing bowl contained dough with the plurality of mixing levers during the counter-rotational relative motion between the circular mixing head and the mixing bowl to repeatedly lift, fold, stretch, and press the dough mass. At another step, the controller deactivates the driving unit upon completion of mixing, and removes the circular mixing head and the mixing bowl from the dough processing device.
[0034] At another step, the user mounts the circular tray containing the mixed dough on the base plate and connects the circular shaping head carrying the plurality of radially arranged cutters to the spindle shaft. At another step, the user engages the clamp pad of the circular tray with the clamp slot of the height-adjustment lever, and applies downward pressure to the circular shaping head to cause the plurality of radially arranged cutters to divide the mixed dough into plurality of dough portions. Further, at another step, the controller activates the driving unit to rotate the circular shaping head in the first rotational direction and the circular tray through the outer ring gear in the second rotational direction opposite to the first rotational direction, thereby subjecting the plurality of dough portions to rotational compression and rolling movement between the circular shaping head and the circular tray to form the plurality of dough balls.
[0035] Further, objects and advantages of the present invention will be apparent from a study of the following portion of the specification, the claims, and the attached drawings.
Detailed description of drawings:
[0036] The accompanying drawings, which are incorporated in and constitute a part of the specification, illustrate an embodiment of the invention, and, together with the description, explain the principles of the invention.
[0037] FIGs. 1A-1B illustrate isometric views of a dough processing device with a mixing bowl and a circular shaping head, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0038] FIGs. 2A-2B illustrate cross-sectional views of the dough processing device, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0039] FIG. 3 illustrates a front perspective view of the dough processing device in a mixing configuration, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0040] FIGs. 4A-4B illustrate perspective views of the dough processing device that is adapted in the mixing configuration, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0041] FIG. 5 illustrates a perspective view of the circular shaping head positioned above the circular tray containing the dough mass, the circular shaping head is configured to divide the dough mass into plurality of dough portions, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0042] FIG. 6A illustrates a perspective view of the circular shaping head positioned below the spindle for threaded engagement of the hollow shaft with the spindle, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0043] FIG. 6B illustrates a perspective view of the circular shaping head connected to the spindle and the height-adjustment levers moved downwardly relative to side handles for positioning the circular shaping head and securing the circular tray, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0044] FIG. 6C illustrates a perspective view of the sun gear and the drive shaft rotating the circular shaping head in a first direction, while the planet gears and the outer ring gear rotate the circular tray in an opposite direction, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
[0045] FIGs. 7A-7B illustrate a flowchart of a method for operating the dough processing device, in accordance to an exemplary embodiment of the invention.
Detailed invention disclosure:
[0046] Various embodiments of the present invention will be described in reference to the accompanying drawings. Wherever possible, same or similar reference numerals are used in the drawings and the description to refer to the same or like parts or steps.
[0047] The present disclosure has been made with a view towards solving the problem with the prior art described above, and it is an object of the present invention to provide a dough processing device 100 for mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming. [0091] Rotation of the sun gear 128 in the anticlockwise direction causes the planet gears 130 to rotate about their respective axes in a clockwise direction. The planet gears 130 mesh with the internally toothed outer ring gear 138, thereby driving the outer ring gear 138 in the clockwise rotational direction shown in FIG. 4B. The outer ring gear 138 is mechanically connected through the flat bars 160 to the opposed side handles 162. The side handles 162 are coupled through the height-adjustment levers 164, clamp slots 176, and clamp pads 178 to the mixing bowl 148. The clockwise rotational movement of the outer ring gear 138 is thereby transmitted through the receptacle-coupling arrangement to the mixing bowl 148.
[0092] Simultaneously, the sun gear 128 transmits anticlockwise rotational movement through the drive shaft 140 and spindle shaft 142 to the circular mixing head 144. The circular mixing head 144 and the mixing levers 146 therefore rotate anticlockwise while the mixing bowl 148 rotates clockwise. In one dimensional embodiment, the sun gear 128 comprises a diameter of approximately 36 mm, each of the three planet gears 130 comprise a diameter of approximately 27 mm, and the outer ring gear 138 has an inner diameter of approximately 90 mm. The carrier support plate 134 may have a diameter of approximately 140 mm, the drive shaft 140 may have a length of approximately 180 mm, and the spindle shaft 142 may have a length of approximately 120 mm.
[0093] In the preferred mixing operation, dough ingredients are introduced into the mixing bowl 148, and the circular mixing head 144 is positioned such that the plurality of pivot-mounted mixing levers 146 extends into the mixing bowl 148. The mixing operation is initiated at the medium-speed setting to combine the dough ingredients. The high-speed setting is subsequently selected to continue lifting, folding, stretching, and pressing dough 10 through opposite-direction rotation of the circular mixing head 144 and the mixing bowl 148. The mixing bowl 148 is driven through the outer ring gear 138, the pair of flat bars 160, the pair of side handles 162, the height-adjustment levers 164, the clamp slots 176, and the clamp pads 178. Simultaneously, the circular mixing head 144 is driven through the sun gear 128, the drive shaft 140, and the spindle shaft 142. The resulting opposite-direction rotation changes the angular position of dough 10 relative to the plurality of pivot-mounted mixing levers 146 during successive contact actions.
[0094] As the mixing levers 146 pass through the dough 10, the mixing levers 146 repeatedly contact, lift, stretch, fold, and press the dough 10. The limited angular movement permitted by the pivot connections allows the mixing levers 146 to deflect in response to changing contact with the dough 10. The opposite rotation of the mixing bowl 148 changes the angular position of the dough 10 relative to the mixing levers 146 during successive contacts. The mixing levers 146 consequently approach and engage the dough 10 from changing angular directions rather than repeatedly contacting the dough 10 along a single fixed direction. For comparative rotational analysis, the relative rotational-speed measure between two oppositely rotating members may be represented by the sum of their rotational speeds. Where the circular mixing head 144 rotates at 150 RPM in the anticlockwise direction and the mixing bowl 148 rotates at 60 RPM in the clockwise direction, the combined relative rotational-speed measure is represented as 210 RPM-equivalent.
[0095] By comparison, the circular mixing head 144 rotating at 150 RPM relative to a stationary bowl provides a relative rotational-speed measure of 150 RPM. The ratio of 210 to 150 corresponds to an analytical increase of approximately 40 percent in the relative rotational-speed measure at the dough-processing interface. The foregoing comparison represents a rotational-speed relationship and should not be interpreted as a direct calculation of linear velocity or shear force without additionally accounting for the applicable radial position and dough-contact conditions. The repeated contact between the mixing levers 146 and the dough 10 increases the number of lifting, folding, stretching, and pressing actions occurring during a mixing interval. The counter-rotation of the mixing bowl 148 changes the relative orientation of the dough 10 during successive contacts, thereby providing multi-directional dough-working action. The repeated folding and pressing action with aeration of the dough 10 associates the changing directions of contact with more uniform dough-working action. These effects depend on the dough composition, quantity, operating speed, lever geometry, and duration of operation.
[0096] In one analytical comparison, a conventional mixing operation requiring ten minutes at a head speed of 150 RPM is compared with the counter-rotational arrangement having the circular mixing head 144 at a speed of 150 RPM and the mixing bowl 148 at a speed of 60 RPM in the opposite direction. Applying the disclosed rotational-speed ratio provides a predicted mixing duration of approximately 7.14 min and a predicted analytical reduction of approximately 28.6 percent. The stated reduction of approximately 15 percent to 25 percent attributed to multi-directional shear, and the resulting combined predicted reduction of approximately 40 percent to 55 percent, are predictive values and should be identified as analytical estimates unless supported by corresponding experimental test results.
[0097] In comparative laboratory-scale prototype testing disclosed for the dough processing device 100, a dough load corresponding to approximately 1.0 kg of wheat-flour dough was processed with the sun gear 128 and circular mixing head 144 operating at approximately 150 RPM. With the mixing bowl 148 rotating in the opposite rotational direction, a substantially uniform dough consistency was obtained in approximately 6 minutes to approximately 7 minutes, compared with approximately 10 minutes to approximately 12 minutes for the disclosed comparative single-direction configuration operating at approximately the same processing-head speed. 
[0098] In the disclosed comparative testing, energy consumption for the counter-rotational mixing configuration ranged from approximately 0.015 kWh to approximately 0.025 kWh per batch, while energy consumption for the comparative single-direction configuration ranged from approximately 0.025 kWh to approximately 0.040 kWh per batch. The counter-rotational configuration further produced a visually and texturally uniform dough and changing dough-contact directions through cooperation between the oppositely rotating mixing bowl 148 and the plurality of pivot-mounted mixing levers 146. The comparative values represent the disclosed prototype operating conditions and vary according to dough composition, dough quantity, processing speed, processing duration, and geometry of the dough-contacting components.

[00107] The user operates the control button 116 provided on the housing 112 to switch on the driving unit 120. Additionally, the driving unit 120 supplies rotational input to the sun gear 128. The sun gear 128 rotates the drive shaft 140, the spindle shaft 142, and the circular shaping head 152 in the anticlockwise direction. [00108] According to another exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 6C illustrates operation of the dough processing device 100 in the dividing and dough-ball-forming configuration. Before powered rounding, downward pressure applied by the user through the plurality of gripping members 156 moves the circular shaping head 152 toward the dough mass 12 distributed across the circular tray 150. The plurality of radially arranged cutters 158, extending downwardly from the underside of the circular shaping head 152, penetrates the dough mass 12 and simultaneously forms a plurality of separated dough portions. Upon activation of the driving unit 120, the sun gear 128, the drive shaft 140, and the spindle shaft 142 rotate the circular shaping head 152 in a first rotational direction, while the plurality of planet gears 130 drives the outer ring gear 138 to rotate the circular tray 150, through the pair of flat bars 160, the pair of side handles 162, the height-adjustment levers 164, the clamp slots 176, and the clamp pads 178, in a second rotational direction opposite to the first rotational direction.
[00109] Continued opposite-direction rotation of the circular shaping head 152 and the circular tray 150 subjects the plurality of separated dough portions to rotational compression and rolling movement between the circular shaping head 152 and the circular tray 150. The counter-rotational movement acts on the plurality of dough portions during the same operating cycle, thereby forming the plurality of dough portions into dough balls simultaneously rather than sequentially. The radial distribution of the plurality of radially arranged cutters 158, together with the continued counter-rotational movement, maintains physical separation between adjacent dough portions during the rounding operation and reduces merging or contact between the dough portions. The substantially flat-bottom configuration of the circular tray 150 provides a supporting surface beneath the plurality of dough portions during the rolling and compressive movement. Dough-contacting surfaces of the circular shaping head 152, the plurality of radially arranged cutters 158, and the circular tray 150 comprise the disclosed non-stick coating, thereby reducing adherence of dough to the dough-contacting surfaces and facilitating release of the formed dough balls following completion of the operation.
[00110] The circular tray 150 has a flat-bottom configuration that provides a stable and level supporting surface for distributing pressure across the dough portions during simultaneous dough-ball formation. Dough-contacting surfaces of the plurality of pivot-mounted mixing levers 146, the circular tray 150, the circular shaping head 152, and the plurality of radially arranged cutters 158 have a non-stick coating comprising polytetrafluoroethylene. The non-stick coating reduces adhesion and accumulation of dough on the coated surfaces and facilitates release of the processed dough.
[00111] After the plurality of dough portions attains a selected rounded configuration, the user operates one of the plurality of control buttons 116 to stop the driving unit 120. After the rotating components stop, the clamp pads 178 of the circular tray 150 are disengaged from the clamp slots 176, and the circular tray 150 is removed from the base plate 102 for collection of the dough balls. The controlled counter-rotational movement during shaping prevents the dough balls from adhering to one another and permits collection of the dough balls without additional manual separation. Following completion of the dough-mixing and dough-rounding operations, the mixing bowl 148, the circular tray 150, the mixing levers 146, and the circular shaping head 152 may be cleaned with reduced effort due to the non-stick dough-contacting surfaces.
[00112] In comparative laboratory-scale dough-ball-forming testing disclosed for the dough processing device 100, the circular shaping head 152 and the circular tray 150 were configured for simultaneous formation of approximately 46 to approximately 48 dough portions during a batch. In the disclosed example, approximately eight dough balls were formed in approximately 1 minute to approximately 2 minutes using the simultaneous counter-rotational arrangement, compared with approximately 6 minutes to approximately 8 minutes for the disclosed sequential configuration. The formed dough balls exhibited a disclosed weight variation ranging from approximately ±5 percent to approximately ±8 percent, compared with approximately ±15 percent to approximately ±20 percent for the disclosed manual comparison.
[00113] The dough processing device 100 integrates mixing, kneading, dividing, and dough-ball forming through functionally interdependent components rather than through separate independently operating appliances. The driving unit 120 and the gear assembly 124 jointly generate a first rotational output through the sun gear 128, the drive shaft 140, and the spindle shaft 142, and a second oppositely directed rotational output through the plurality of planet gears 130, the outer ring gear 138, the flat bars 160, the side handles 162, the height-adjustment levers 164, the clamp slots 176, and the clamp pads 178.
[00114] During the mixing operation, the first rotational output drives the circular mixing head 144, while the second rotational output drives the mixing bowl 148. During the dividing and dough-ball-forming operation, the first rotational output drives the circular shaping head 152, while the second rotational output drives the circular tray 150. The circular mixing head 144 and the mixing bowl 148 thereby cooperate to produce multi-directional dough-working movement, while the circular shaping head 152 and the circular tray 150 cooperate to divide and round the plurality of dough portions through a continuous counter-rotational operation. The two operating modes accordingly use the common transmission pathway and the interchangeable spindle connection rather than separate independent drive mechanisms.
[00115] The components of the dough processing device 100 operate through mechanically interdependent transmission pathways rather than as independently functioning dough-processing components. Rotational input generated by the driving unit 120 is simultaneously utilized by the first rotational transmission pathway through the sun gear 128, the drive shaft 140, and the spindle shaft 142, and by the second rotational transmission pathway through the plurality of planet gears 130, the outer ring gear 138, the pair of flat bars 160, the pair of side handles 162, the height-adjustment levers 164, the clamp slots 176, and the clamp pads 178. In the mixing configuration, the first rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular mixing head 144 relative to the mixing bowl 148, while the second rotational transmission pathway simultaneously rotates the mixing bowl 148 in the opposite rotational direction. The resulting counter-rotational relationship changes the angular position of dough 10 relative to the plurality of pivot-mounted mixing levers 146 during successive contacts, thereby producing repeated lifting, folding, stretching, and pressing actions from changing angular directions.
[00116] In the dividing and dough-ball-forming configuration, the same first rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular shaping head 152, while the same second rotational transmission pathway rotates the circular tray 150 in the opposite rotational direction. The plurality of radially arranged cutters 158 initially divides the dough mass 12 into a plurality of separated dough portions, after which the opposite-direction rotation subjects the separated dough portions to rolling and compressive movement between the circular shaping head 152 and the circular tray 150 for simultaneous dough-ball formation. Accordingly, the mixing configuration and the dividing and dough-ball-forming configuration utilize the same driving unit 120 and gear assembly 124, with interchangeable processing heads coupled through the spindle shaft 142, to produce respective cooperative dough-processing actions.

title: Temperature Dependent Biochemical Mechanism Governing Cellular Growth and Embryonic Development in Animal and Plant System
abstract:
ABSTRACT
The current invention pertains to a system and method for temperature-controlled biological regulation, aimed at managing cellular growth and embryonic development in both plant and animal systems. This invention establishes a comprehensive technical framework where thermal conditions are precisely controlled to influence temperature-sensitive biochemical processes. These processes include enzymatic activity, intracellular signaling, gene expression, protein synthesis, cellular metabolism, ATP production, and responses to oxidative stress. The synchronized biochemical activities foster cell proliferation, differentiation, morphogenesis, organogenesis, and embryonic development while ensuring cellular homeostasis is maintained. The system described includes a temperature regulation module, a biological specimen, a biochemical regulation module, and a developmental response module, all designed to enhance growth and developmental results under specific thermal conditions. This invention is relevant to areas such as controlled-environment agriculture, plant tissue culture, greenhouse cultivation, embryo incubation, livestock breeding, aquaculture, regenerative medicine, biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, and biomedical laboratories. By combining temperature regulation with biochemical monitoring and developmental control, the invention offers improved biological reproducibility, increased developmental efficiency, optimized metabolic performance, and extensive industrial applicability. Implementation of the invention can be achieved through the use of incubators, environmental chambers, bioreactors, tissue culture systems, embryo culture systems, and automated temperature-control platforms.

title: Self-Adjusting Student Chair with Integrated Height and Weight Detection System
abstract: The present invention discloses an automatically adjustable ergonomic chair system designed for use in educational environments. The system comprises a piezoelectric pressure sensor array embedded within the seat surface, an infrared height sensor, an ultrasonic lumbar sensor, a 32-bit ARM microcontroller, and motorized pneumatic actuators. Upon a student occupying the seat, the pressure sensors confirm occupancy, while the infrared and ultrasonic sensors measure the student's seated height and lumbar distance respectively. The microcontroller processes the acquired data using a pre-programmed ergonomic algorithm and automatically adjusts the seat height within a range of 280mm to 520mm and the backrest angle between 90° and 115° to achieve an optimal ergonomic seating position tailored to the individual student's body dimensions. The entire adjustment cycle is completed within 3–5 seconds without any manual intervention. The system incorporates obstruction detection, load limiting, manual override, and a status indicator LED for safe classroom operation. An optional RFID-based student profile memory enables instant recall of previously stored adjustment settings. The invention addresses the widespread problem of standardized classroom furniture failing to accommodate the varied body sizes of growing students, thereby promoting correct posture, reducing musculoskeletal strain, and improving student comfort and concentration during academic activities.
specification:
1. Occupant Detection
A 5×5 piezoelectric pressure sensor array embedded beneath the seat cushion detects when a student sits. A 1.5-second confirmation delay prevents false triggering from books or bags placed on the seat.
2. Body Measurement
An infrared sensor mounted on the seat frame measures the student's seated torso height. A secondary ultrasonic sensor on the backrest measures lumbar distance. Combined pressure data estimates the student's weight category — light, medium, or heavy.
3. Processing and Control
A 32-bit ARM microcontroller receives all sensor data, filters noise, and calculates the optimal seat height and backrest angle using a pre-programmed ergonomic algorithm. Adjustment commands are sent as PWM signals to the motor drivers.
4. Mechanical Adjustment
A pneumatic actuator with lead screw adjusts seat height between 280mm and 520mm at 15mm/second. A worm gear motor adjusts the backrest between 90° and 115°. Both mechanisms complete adjustment within 3–5 seconds of seating. ,

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning And Temporal Deep Learning Framework For Short-Term Energy Demand Forecasting
abstract: The present invention provides a hybrid forecasting framework for short-term prediction of electrical energy demand that combines classical machine learning with temporal deep learning to address the shortcomings of relying solely on one type of model. The framework consists of a data acquisition and preprocessing module for generating engineered tabular features (lagged demand, rolling statistics, cyclical time encodings, calendar and weather variables) and normalized sequential load data from historical demand data. Tabular features are passed into a machine learning prediction branch, which consists of an ensemble of gradient-boosted decision trees that produces a first demand prediction as well as a feature importance profile. At the same time, a temporal deep learning prediction branch, which uses a recurrent neural network or temporal convolutional network, is used to process the sequential load data, and a second prediction of the load demand is obtained, which can better reflect the short-term and long-term load demand. The adaptive fusion module uses weights that are calculated dynamically from the respective rolling forecasting error of each branch to provide a combination of both forecasts, thus giving more weight to the better-performing branch. All modules are retrained periodically with more recent data to remain flexible with changing consumption patterns. The invention is applicable for deployment in a utility, microgrid and/or energy management and provides improved accuracy, anomaly robustness and interpretability.
specification:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The invention is related to the field of electrical power systems and computational intelligence and, more particularly, a hybrid forecasting model for accurate, short-term forecasting of electrical energy demand for efficient operation of the electrical power grid, load dispatch and planning of the energy resources, which combines classical machine learning regressors with temporal deep learning architectures.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Electricity can't be economically stored on a large scale, so electrical power utilities and electrical grid operators have to continuously balance electricity generation with electricity consumption. In fact, short term energy demand forecasting, as a process having a few minutes up to a few days ahead, plays a key role in unit commitment, economic dispatch, demand response scheduling and integration of variable renewable energy (VRE) like solar and wind. Energy demand is a highly non-linear and non-stationary time series, which is affected by a variety of factors, such as day of the week, time of day, season, weather and calendar effects such as holidays, and slowly evolving consumption behaviour.
Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models and simple regression methods are able to reasonably describe the linear trends and seasonality, but are not very suitable for the complex non-linear interactions between the weather and the demand. Short and long range temporal dependencies are not naturally addressed by purely machine learning based approaches, like gradient boosted trees or support vector regression, which model non-linear feature interactions. Purely deep learning systems like standalone recurrent or temporal convolutional networks do well at modeling sequential patterns but are relatively data-hungry and are slower to learn, and can be less successful on abrupt regime changes or when the exogenous tabular features in the data, e.g., weather forecast or calendar flags, carry more weight. It is therefore necessary to develop a forecasting system that can benefit from the complementary strengths of both feature and sequence models through a single coordinated architecture, while at the same time not exceeding the compute limits of deployment for grid operators of different sizes and enabling the solution to be accurate in short-term forecasting.
OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION
●	To build a hybrid forecasting model which integrates classical machine learning regressors with temporal deep learning models for short-term electrical energy demand forecasting.
●	To identify the influence of exogenous factors (including weather variables and calendar effects) on the load data in a non-linear way, while at the same time being able to recognize the sequential temporal dependencies in load data.
●	To offer an adaptive combination mechanism which would give the machine learning and temporal deep learning outputs a fixed static mix, instead of based on their actual forecasting performance.
●	To minimize forecast error and enhance robustness to sudden demand shock, holidays and weather anomaly compared with single model forecasting. 
●	To provide a fast and scalable forecasting tool that could be deployed by energy management systems, microgrid operators and utilities of different sizes, and be retrainable.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides a hybrid forecasting system for forecasting short-term electrical energy demands, which includes a feature engineering and preprocessing module, a machine learning prediction branch, a temporal deep learning prediction branch, and an adaptive fusion module for generating an overall, calibrated energy demand forecast from the two branches. The key novelty of the invention lies in the coordinated, dual-branch architecture in which a gradient-boosting or ensemble tree based machine learning model processes engineered tabular features, such as time-of-day, day-of-week, calendar flags and weather variables, while a temporal deep learning model, such as a long short-term memory (LSTM), gated recurrent unit (GRU) or temporal convolutional network, processes the raw and normalized historical load sequence to capture short and long range temporal dependencies, and the outputs of both branches are combined by a learned, performance-adaptive fusion module rather than by a fixed or manually tuned weighting scheme.
Historical load data is preprocessed in the feature engineering and preprocessing module, by cleaning the data, resampling to a common time interval, introducing lag features, rolling statistical aggregates over time, encoding the time of day and day of week as cycles and (where available) weather forecast features like temperature, humidity and cloud cover. The processed data is then separated into a tabular feature representation for the machine learning branch and a normalized sliding-window sequence representation for the temporal deep learning branch, with each branch working on a common underlying dataset but in the representation that is most beneficial for modelling strengths. 
The machine learning branch generates a point forecast for the target horizon along with an associated feature-importance profile using a gradient-boosted decision tree ensemble or similar model being trained on the tabular features engineered with the load sequence data, while the temporal deep learning branch generates an independent point forecast with its associated feature-importance profile based on a recurrent or convolutional sequence model trained on the load sequence data of the load over a sliding window, which captures the autocorrelation and trend continuation effects not explicitly encoded as tabular features.
The adaptive fusion module takes the individual forecasts from the machine learning branch and the temporal deep learning branch, as well as a rolling window of the forecasting error of each branch, and calculates a fusion forecast based on a learned weighting function (such as the light-weight meta-regressor or inverse-error weighting scheme), which is updated when new actual demand values are received. This enables the framework to have a stronger preference towards the branch which is predicting better the most – in this case, the machine learning branch during calendar anomalies like public holidays, and the temporal deep learning branch during periods of trend-continuing, smooth demand. 
Accordingly, it is an object of the invention to provide a technically integrated forecasting solution that is composed of a set of feature-driven energy demand forecasting models as well as a set of sequence-driven energy demand forecasting models, which models are run in parallel and fused adaptively to provide short-term energy demand forecasts, more accurate and more robust across different demand regimes than either set of models alone, which short-term energy demand forecasts can be periodically retrained and deployed to existing grid management and energy management systems.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
1. Data Acquisition and Preprocessing Module
Historical electrical demand data is gathered from smart meters, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems or a utility billing database and exogenous data (weather observations or predictions, calendar data, etc.) is gathered. The module cleans the data by filling in missing values and outliers, re-samples it to a regular time interval, generates engineered features such as lagged values of the demand, rolling mean and standard deviation statistics, cyclical sine-cosine features for the hour-of-day and day-of-week, and binary features for weekends and holidays.
2. Machine Learning Prediction Branch
The target forecast horizon is modeled using a gradient-boosted decision tree ensemble (or other machine learning regressor) over the engineered tabular feature set. In addition to its ability to model non-linear interactions between exogenous variables, such as the interaction between a hot afternoon and a weekday, and the resulting demand response, this branch also provides a feature importance ranking which can be shown to grid operators for explanation.
3. Temporal Deep Learning Prediction Branch
A recurrent neural network (RNN) like a long short term memory (LSTM) network or a gated recurrent unit (GRU) network, or a temporal convolutional network is trained with normalized window of historical demand values to predict the same demand value for the target forecast horizon. This branch models sequential dependencies, trend continuation and periodicity in the raw load time series that manifest as no discrete tabular feature and is trained separately from but on the same underlying data as the machine learning branch.
4. Adaptive Fusion Module
The point forecasts generated by the machine learning branch and the temporal deep learning branch are provided alongside a rolling record of the forecasting error of each branch over the previous forecasts generated by that branch, to a fusion module that learns a weighted average of the outputs of the two branches and weights the outputs of the two branches adaptively based on recent forecasting error. The fusion weights are dynamically updated as new actual demand readings come in, so the module automatically adjusts its focus to the branch that has been more accurate for the past observation window, instead of a fixed blending ratio.
5. Forecast Output and Grid Integration Interface
The short-term demand forecast, along with per-branch forecasts and a confidence indicator based on recent fusion error, is made available via an application programming interface or dashboard to be consumed by downstream systems like unit commitment tools, demand response platforms, energy management systems or microgrid controllers, which can then use it directly in generation scheduling and load balancing decisions.
6. Periodic Retraining and Model Adaptation Module
The machine learning branch, the temporal deep learning branch and the fusion module are retrained or fine-tuned periodically using the most recent historical data, enabling the framework to evolve to new consumption trends or seasonal shifts in consumption and creation of new consumers (large or distributed) or new production (DGs) without having to rebuild the entire framework from scratch.
ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
•	Enhanced the short term forecast accuracy by the synergy of feature-driven machine learning model and temporal deep learning model. 
•	Adaptive, error-based fusion of branch forecasts which automatically re-weight the better performing model, not based on a fixed blend ratio scheme. 
•	Improved resistance to calendar-driven anomalies, weather-driven demand spikes, and sudden change of the regime relative to single-model forecasting approaches. 
•	The feature-importance output of the machine learning branch combined with the pattern-capturing ability of the temporal deep learning branch helps interpretability. 
•	The architecture is retrainable and scalable for deployment by both microgrid operators and energy management systems of different sizes and by utilities.

title: Intelligent Predictive Modulation and Coding Selection System with Adaptive Reliability Margin for Dynamic Wireless Channels
abstract: The intelligent wireless communication system should provide increased reliability, efficiency and adaptability of data transmission in dynamic and unpredictable environments. The system is based on predictive modelling which uses historical and current signal measurements to predict future channel conditions. It can dynamically optimize important transmission parameters like power, margin, modulations, channel coding rates and more in advance in response to variations in the signal quality. The adaptive behavior enables to keep the system connected in rapidly changing interference, mobility and fading environments.This system features a learning mechanism that continuously optimizes performance by learning from past transmissions, besides prediction and adaptation. Successful and failed packet delivery is studied to improve decision making policies, so that the system can maximize its throughput while keeping packet error rates and packet re-transmissions as low as possible. Machine learning methods are used to detect patterns of channel behavior and user needs, enabling more efficient use of resources throughout the network.Combining these elements creates a self-optimizing communication system ready to function in various wireless environments, such as mobile networks, Internet of Things (IoT) deployments and next-generation wireless infrastructures (5G, 6G). The system optimizes reliability and spectral efficiency, minimizes latency, and boosts quality of service.In the end, this intelligent wireless solution is a step from being fixed and static to truly adaptive communication, truly adaptive wireless, that's going to be constantly learning and predicting, improving performance. It offers the basis for future wireless networks which need to operate in increasingly challenged and congested spectral environments, with high data rates and high reliability demands, under conditions of massive connectivity.
specification:
4.	DESCRIPTION

Background of the Invention: 

        Radio signals are subject to constant and sometimes random variations in wireless communication systems as a consequence of environmental and physical factors such as fading, interference, multipath propagation, user mobility, and changes in transmission distance. The resulting channel variation results in channel conditions that change with time, which can affect the quality of the link, and negatively affect data integrity, throughput and network efficiency. Aiming towards solving those challenges, modern communication systems use adaptive transmission schemes that adapt the signal parameters according to the observed channel behavior.
      Many current implementations use modulation schemes and forward error correction coding rates based on estimated channel quality indicators. They are usually based on measurement values like received signal strength or signal to noise ratio, and assigned to transmission configuration by predefined thresholds or rule based decision tables. Although these techniques can be effective in relatively stable channel conditions, their performance suffers in highly dynamic channels (fast channel variations or inaccurate channel estimates). In such cases, the mismatches between estimated and actual channel states can cause suboptimal parameter selections, which can cause a higher packet loss and retransmission rate.
         Machine learning techniques have recently been suggested to enhance adaption by learning adaptation rules over channel observations and best transmission parameters through a learning algorithm. Many of the currently available solutions are based on either prediction of the state of the channel or explicit selection of the transmission parameters but cannot adequately capture the complex phenomenon that is difficult to model analytically. They rarely take into account feedback from real transmission results (e.g., error rates, delivery success, etc.) when adjusting transmission process. As a result, there may be some error between the prediction of the system and the actual result, which may result in a limited optimization capability.
         Therefore, there is a need for an enhanced adaptive communication mechanism that incorporates the channel estimation and performance feedback. Such a mechanism should continuously adapt transmissions decisions based on the correlation between channel state prediction and communication results. The system can provide real-time feedback for the adaptation loop to increase robustness, minimize transmission errors, and maximize efficiency in wireless environments with fast varying characteristics. This helps to better match network decisions to the true performance of the channels over time in dynamic conditions.




Present technologies that exist in the field of invention:
        The current wireless communication technologies mainly employ Adaptive Modulation and Coding (AMC) to adapt the transmission parameters based on the current channel conditions. The quality of a channel is typically expressed with a measurement like Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Channel Quality Indicator (CQI), Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), Bit Error Rate (BER), or Packet Error Rate (PER). A modulation and coding combination (MCC) is determined by the estimated channel quality.
        Typical modulation schemes used with conventional AMC technologies include BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM and 256-QAM, and various error-correction coding rates. Higher order modulation and higher coding rates are usually used under good channel conditions to achieve a higher data throughput and lower-order modulation and stronger coding are used under poor channel conditions to achieve more reliable transmission.
        Additionally, channel prediction, channel adaptation, Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request (HARQ), and feedback-based transmission control are used in modern wireless systems. All these technologies rely on the feedback received by the receiver to adjust the following transmission parameters and to minimize communication errors. Channel estimation, channel prediction, modulation classification and adaptive modulation coding selection are also some of the areas that have been explored using machine-learning and artificial-intelligence techniques.
       Many current technologies, however, still use fixed thresholds, pre-programmed adaptation rules or decisions mainly based on the current channel measurements. Machine-learning approaches could benefit parameter selection, but often do not yield a continuously self-adjusting reliability margin given the difference between the predicted channel behavior and the actual transmission performance.
      It is an object of the present invention to overcome these disadvantages by providing a channel prediction, adaptive reliability-margin generation, joint modulation and coding selection, and closed-loop transmission-performance feedback. This offers a way of continually updating adaptation decisions based on model predictions of channel behavior and actual transmission outcomes.

Limitations that exist in the field of invention
        Even with the adaptive transmission control in a hypothetical wireless communication setup, there are some constraints that affect and impact the overall efficiency and reliability of the setup. Preset decision boundaries are frequently used to determine which transmission configurations are used, and these may not be optimal if the environment changes significantly. Adaptation is usually only done when the present or recently perceived channel information is different from that expected, so a sudden drop in channel quality can cause temporary degradation of performance before adaptation occurs. When the future action of the channel is predicted, there are often errors between the expected and the actual transmission and these are not fully incorporated into further decisions. Another potential drawback of the mechanism is that the selected transmission modes are not necessarily optimised for the respective operating situation and may not necessarily be the most efficient in some of them. Also, the process of selecting the transmission parameters is done sometimes independently of each other and not as a combined evaluation of their influence on reliability, data rate and energy consumption. This can result in conservative configurations that reduce the throughput that can be achieved when potentially higher throughput is possible. Additionally, although feedback from the receiver is used, it is mostly for adjusting the receiver, and is not used for learning the relationship between the predicted conditions, the selected configurations and the received communication results, so that the system can be optimized for a longer time.

Explanation of the Invention to overcome the limitations in the existing technologies
          The present invention relates to an intelligent adaptive modulation and coding for reliable and efficient wireless communication in dynamically changing channel environment. The invention overcomes the above drawbacks of the conventional systems by providing a closed loop decision mechanism, which takes into account both predicted channel behavior and actual channel transmission performance.
         Channel-quality parameters like SNR, RSSI, BER, PER, channel variation characteristics etc are monitored continuously. Rather than using only the channel information it receives at any given instant, a prediction unit computes the temporal behavior of the channel information that it collects and predicts what the channel condition is going to be in the future. This allows the system to detect the channel degradation or improvement in advance without having a large impact on data transmission.
         Based on the predicted channel condition and a predefined reliability requirement, a reliability-margin controller determines an adaptive reliability margin. The proposed margin may be raised or lowered depending on the expected channel performance and the desired communication reliability, as opposed to fixed safety margins. This way, there will be no need to have the system excessively conservative in transmitting and the chances of transmission errors will be reduced.
         The system then tests combinations of modulation and coding schemes and rates to determine whether a suitable combination of modulation and coding exists.The system then simultaneously tests combinations of modulation coding schemes and rates to see if a suitable combination of modulation and coding exists. They may take into account the reliability of the transmission, the rate of data transfer they can attain, and how much energy the transmission uses. If it is believed that the channel is likely to fail, it can proactively switch to a stronger configuration. For better forecasted channel, a higher throughput configuration may be chosen.

        The system is then transmitted and the actual communication performance is measured. The actual transmission error is compared with predicted performance and the difference is fed into the controller for reliability-margin. The controller adjusts the reliability margin based on this feedback, so as to make future transmission decisions. Therefore, the system learns from the actual communication results continually, rather than depending on fixed thresholds for adaptation repeatedly.
      The invention, therefore, provides a self-learning adaptive mechanism that combines channel monitoring, channel prediction, reliability-margin adjustment, joint modulation and coding selection and transmission-performance feedback. This simultaneous operation enhances reliability in fast varying channel conditions and minimizes unnecessary re-transmission as well as the unwarranted decrease in data rate. The proposed system can be applied to different wireless communication systems such as mobile communication systems, wireless sensor network, internet of things system and other variable wireless links.

Detailed Explanation of the Invention along with working examples

Step 1: Wireless Data Input and Transmission 
         Wireless Data Input and Transmission Module receives raw data from user applications or from sensor sources and prepares this data for wireless transmission. It does initial formatting, packetizing, and buffering to guarantee smooth data flow. The module also integrates with higher application layers and lower physical layer elements, ensuring smooth data transfers. The following are some of the features that it can contain: simple error checking, a ability to add date and time stamps, and the capability to prioritize data streams according to system needs. After processing, the data is passed to the modulation and coding block to be processed. The module provides a way of ensuring input data is synchronized with system timing constraints and transmission schedules. It also controls temporary storage to cope with burst traffic and loss of data. Overall, this module serves as a gateway point within the wireless communication system, it ensures that the incoming information has been appropriately formatted for efficient and reliable transmission through the wireless channel. Latency and reliability optimisation has been achieved with minimal latency and high reliability.
         This module is used to generate or receive the data to be sent wirelessly. The input can be sensor data, text, audio, video, control data or even general digital packets. The module prepares the input data into transmission frames and provides the data to the adaptive transmission controller. It is possible to also feed the module's application level requirements, for example minimum reliability, required data rate or energy constraints.




Step 2: Channel Monitoring and Measurement 
         This module is continually monitoring and measuring the wireless channel and getting real-time data of the channel's quality and variability. It measures the signal to noise ratio (SNR), received signal strength indicator (RSSI), bit error rate (BER), packet error rate (PER), fading depth, Doppler shift, and overall channel stability. Such measurements are conducted on a regular basis and/or dynamically based on transmission activity to keep the channel awareness up to date. The module also monitors short- and long-term fluctuations of the channel, which helps to make accurate analysis. Data collected is pre-processed, filtered and normalized to eliminate noise and inconsistencies and sent to the channel prediction and analysis modules. This will provide reliable and accurate channel information to the following decision-making processes for adaptive modulation and coding selection.

Step 3: Channel Prediction and Trend Analysis 
         This module is used for analyzing channel measurements to forecast channel response to past conditions and to forecast future channel response. Uses statistical methods or machine learning models to detect patterns, like stability, improvement, or degradation trends of channels. Based on this analysis, it estimates the expected channel condition for the next transmission interval. The prediction output enables the system to adapt its transmission plans in anticipation of the impending new channel. This is a predictive function that decreases an unexpected breakdown in the transmission and enhances communication reliability. The system can also choose modulation and coding schemes in advance, in consideration of the channel variations. This is a crucial module in the application of intelligence and prediction rather than just a response to events in a wireless communication setting.

Step 4: Self-Learning Reliability Margin Module
         The objective of this module is to calculate and maintain a channel-adaptive reliability margin, depending on the channel conditions and the desired quality of service. It is not a fixed-margin system, but a dynamic one, which changes the level of protection depending on the actual and forecasted behavior of the channel. It compares between the predicted performance and the measured performance of the system after each transmission like BER, PER, and packet success rate. Expected vs. observed results are used as learning feedback to improve the calculation of margins in the future. As time goes on, the module will get better and better in establishing optimal safety margins, which combine reliability and spectral efficiency. This adaptive learning process allows the system to not be over-protective (wasting bandwidth) or under-protective (resulting in errors) and keeps the wireless communication efficient and reliable under different channel conditions.



Step 5: Adaptive Modulation Selection 
          This module adaptively chooses the most suitable modulation scheme according to the channel quality and the adaptive reliability margin. It compares various modulation schemes like BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM and 256QAM, which have different levels of robustness and data rates. The module will choose lower order modulation schemes in poor channel conditions to achieve better reliability and lower error rates. It automatically adapts to higher order modulation schemes in good channel conditions to achieve high throughput and spectral efficiency. The selection process is coordinated to the coding module, so that the overall transmission stability is ensured. This module makes sure the system responds to channel changes dynamically and provides a balance between how reliable the communication is, and how efficient the data is sent.

Step 6: Adaptive Coding Selection 
          This module selects the appropriate code rate for the error correcting code to be used depending on the channel type, modulation type and the desired reliability. Adaptively codes the signal strength according to the actual communication environment. For lower channel conditions the module switches to high-quality error correcting codes at lower code rates to make them more resistant to noise and interference. It selects higher code rates where it is supported in the channel to maximize data throughput and to minimize redundancy overhead in the channel, as long as this is a stable or high quality channel. This module will be used in close cooperation with the module for selection of modulation to assure a balanced and efficient transmission configuration. This module adapts coding strategies continuously, ensuring reliable communication and optimizing the channel efficiency, depending upon the varying wireless channel conditions.

Step 7: Wireless Transmission and Feedback Evaluation 
        This module is to apply the modulation/coding scheme chosen to the prepared data and to modulate/code the data and send it through the wireless channel. The signal is demodulated and demodulated at the receiver side to recover the original data. Once it has been transmitted, the system checks performance by measuring the bit error rate (BER), the packet error rate (PER), throughput, packet success rate, etc. The performance results are then provided to the modules of learning and adaptation for further analysis. This loop allows the system to assess what it is doing against the expected performance. The module continually assesses the transmission quality, which allows the system to make informed decisions about future communications and optimise its communication reliability and efficiency in a dynamic wireless environment.



Step 8: Intelligent Decision and Continuous Adaptation
         This module acts as a central control unit for the system which is able to combine data from all other modules and make real-time transmission decisions. It takes in measurements from various channels, forecasts the environment, includes adaptive reliability margins, and gets feedback from past transmissions. From this overall information, it infers the best modulation and coding scheme used during the current transmission cycle. The module makes decisions continuously, based on the evolving channel conditions to adapt in proactively rather than reactively. This coordinates the whole closed-loop process, allowing for a seamless interaction between monitoring processes, prediction processes, learning processes, and transmission processes. By continually adapting and refining decisions, this module allows the system to maintain high reliability, increased spectral efficiency and strong performance in dynamically changing wireless communication environments.

Working Example:
          The data is transmitted wirelessly through Rayleigh fading channel with additive noise. A Channel Monitoring Module records the important link quality parameters like SNR, Packet Error Rate and Channel Stability. A Channel Prediction Module takes into account the history of channel statistics and predicts channel changes in the future over the next interval of transmission. Using this prediction and quality-of-service requirements, a Reliability Margin Module can adaptively adjust the reliability margin to ensure reliable communication.
         A Modulation and Coding Selection Module dynamically selects an appropriate transmission scheme, such as choosing between higher order modulation with higher coding rates, and lower order modulation with more powerful error-correcting coding, based on the anticipated channel quality. The selected configuration is used for data transmission.
         A Performance Evaluation Module at the receiver end performs this function and computes the parameters of the received signal, including Bit Error Rate (BER), Packet Error Rate (PER) and Throuput. If there are differences between the expected and actual results of the system, a Feedback and Learning Module will adjust system parameters, such as the reliability margin for future transmissions. The system adjusts its reliability margin and changes the modulation and coding scheme according to the changes of the channel condition. The transmission strategy is therefore continuously adjusted in accordance with the channel predictions and actual channel behaviour to ensure a balance between reliability and spectral efficiency.
