1.	An adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) method in a wireless communication system, which method comprises:
Estimating future channel state by measuring the channel in the temporal dimension; deriving a predicted transmission performance from the estimated future channel state; computing a reliability margin, dynamically, from the predicted transmission performance; determining a modulation and coding scheme (MCS) for the transmission of data based on the reliability margin; and transmitting the data using the determined modulation and coding scheme.
2.	The method of claim 1 further comprising:
Calculating an actual transmission performance after data transmission; calculating a prediction error between the predicted transmission performance and the actual transmission performance; and updating the reliability margin based on the calculated prediction error.
3.	The method of claim 2, wherein updating the reliability margin comprises increasing the reliability margin when the actual transmission performance is lower than the predicted transmission performance, and decreasing the reliability margin when the actual transmission performance exceeds the predicted transmission performance.
4.	The method of claim 1, wherein the reliability margin is dynamically adjusted at each transmission interval or in real-time, as a closed-loop function of a series of prediction errors, such that the reliability margin approaches a value that minimizes the probability of transmission failure while maintaining throughput efficiency.
5.	An adaptive link adaptation system for wireless communications, comprising: 
A channel prediction module, which is set to predict future channel conditions; and A performance estimation module with a configuration to calculate estimated transmission performance;
 A reliability margin learning module that updates a reliability margin based on the difference between the predicted and actual transmission performance; and 
A modulation and coding selection module for selecting an MCS with the updated reliability margin, and
 In which the system has a feedback mechanism to continually adjust the reliability margin to minimize the error in the prediction over time.

title: A NOVEL RAPID AND COST EFFECTIVE METHOD FOR EXTRACTION OF DEOXYRIBONUCLEIC ACID (DNA) USING FUNCTIONALIZED MAGNETIC NANOPARTICLES
abstract:
The present invention discloses a novel rapid and cost-effective method for extraction of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) using functionalized magnetic nanoparticles. The invention belongs to the fields of biotechnology, nanotechnology, and molecular diagnostics, and provides an efficient technique for isolating high-quality DNA from various biological samples. The proposed method utilizes surface-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles designed to selectively bind DNA molecules through electrostatic and affinity-based interactions.
Initially, biological samples such as blood, saliva, plant tissues, microbial cultures, or other biological materials are treated with lysis buffers to release intracellular DNA. Functionalized magnetic nanoparticles are then introduced into the sample mixture to facilitate selective DNA adsorption onto the nanoparticle surface. Following DNA binding, an external magnetic field is applied to rapidly separate DNA-bound nanoparticles from contaminants and unwanted cellular debris. Washing steps are performed to remove residual impurities, and purified DNA is subsequently eluted using an appropriate buffer solution.
The proposed method eliminates multiple centrifugation steps involved in conventional extraction procedures, thereby reducing processing time, reagent consumption, and operational complexity. The invention offers advantages including improved DNA purity, higher extraction efficiency, reduced sample loss, and cost-effective operation. Furthermore, the method can be adapted for automation and large-scale applications. The purified DNA obtained through this process is suitable for downstream applications such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR), sequencing, forensic analysis, disease diagnostics, pathogen detection, and biotechnology research. Therefore, the invention provides a simple, scalable, and economically feasible alternative for rapid DNA extraction.

The present invention relates to the fields of biotechnology, nanobiotechnology and molecular diagnostics. More particularly, the invention relates to a novel rapid and cost-effective method for extraction of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) using functionalized magnetic nanoparticles. The invention provides an efficient, simple and scalable approach for isolating DNA from biological samples  through magnetic separation techniques. The method significantly reduces processing time, lowers reagent consumption, minimizes laboratory complexity and improves extraction efficiency compared to conventional DNA isolation methods. The Invention is particularly useful in biomedical research, molecular biology laboratories, clinical diagnostics, forensic investigations, environmental monitoring, agricultural biotechnology and point-of-care testing applications. The proposed technology utilizes magnetic nanoparticle-based extraction systems capable of producing purified DNA with high yield and quality suitable for downstream applications.

     Detailed Description of the Invention
D DNA extraction is a critical process in molecular biology and diagnostics because DNA serves as the fundamental genetic material of living organisms. Extraction and purification of DNA are necessary for various applications including polymerase chain reaction (PCR), sequencing, pathogen detection, forensic identification, genetic studies, and disease diagnosis.
Conventional DNA extraction methods involve multiple centrifugation steps, expensive chemicals, silica-column purification systems, and lengthy procedures. Such approaches often require sophisticated laboratory equipment and skilled personnel. In addition, repeated washing and centrifugation can increase sample loss and processing time.
To overcome these limitations, the present invention introduces functionalized magnetic nanoparticles for rapid DNA extraction. Magnetic nanoparticles possess unique characteristics including high surface area, strong magnetic response, biocompatibility, and ease of separation. These properties make them suitable for nucleic acid isolation.
       In one embodiment, magnetic nanoparticles are synthesized using iron oxide materials due to their strong magnetic behaviour and stability. The nanoparticles are coated with suitable functional groups such as amino groups, silica layers, carboxyl groups, or other biocompatible surface modifiers. Functionalization enhances selective interaction between DNA molecules and nanoparticle surfaces     .
T    The prepared nanoparticles possess increased affinity toward nucleic acids while maintaining stability under biological conditions. Surface functionalization improves adsorption efficiency and prevents particle aggregation.

title: CONTROLLED-RELEASE PH SENSING ASSEMBLY FOR SUSTAINABLE HYGIENE SYSTEMS
abstract: The present invention relates to a biodegradable absorbent hygiene product comprising a controlled chemical sensing system for early detection of abnormal pH variations in body fluids. Traditional hygiene products like sanitary napkins, diapers, and period underwear are not health-monitoring capable, primarily focusing on absorption and disposal. In addition, the synthetic materials of these products are also a huge source of pollution in the environment. The present invention relates to a biodegradable absorbent core made from natural compostable fibers and an integrated pH-responsive sensing module comprising a natural anthocyanin-based indicator. The sensing material is incorporated into a biodegradable alginate–chitosan encapsulation matrix to enhance storage stability and prevent premature activation. The invention provides a moisture-responsive protective barrier for controlled activation after sufficient fluid exposure, thus reducing false triggering and increasing detection accuracy. The proposed system generates distinguishable visual patterns corresponding to different abnormal pH levels, which can be interpreted more easily by the user, unlike conventional indicator strips. An important aspect of the present invention is that it is modular and adaptable for use in a variety of absorbent hygiene products such as sanitary napkins, diapers, reusable period panties, and medical absorbent pads. The invention provides a green and health-conscious hygiene solution by integrating biodegradability, controlled chemical sensing, and multi-product adaptability into a single integrity

The pH indicator is wrapped in a biodegradable protective layer that ensures its protection during storage. The activation occurs only when there is sufficient liquid absorbed.

COMPLETE SPECIFICATION
1. FIELD OF THE INVENTION
This invention pertains to biodegradable hygiene products. It more precisely pertains to a controlled-release pH detection system that is integrated into various hygiene products, such as sanitary pads, diapers, and reusable menstrual panties for detecting unusual pH levels in body fluids.
2. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Hygiene products such as sanitary napkins, diapers, and period underwear are commonly employed for fluid absorption today. These items are usually composed of plastic materials, which are environmentally unfriendly and contribute to pollution.
Moreover, conventional hygiene products do not have a way of identifying any health conditions. Abnormal pH in body fluids may indicate an infection or some other health concerns, but these products will not reveal this information.
Therefore, there is a need for the development of an environmentally friendly hygiene product that would also be able to detect unusual pH levels in the body.

title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR PREVENTING PREDETERMINED ADVERSE EVENT IN INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) NETWORK
abstract: The present disclosure discloses a system (100) and a method (200) for preventing predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (IoT) network. The system (100) includes input acquisition unit (102) to acquire data associated with environmental parameters of IoT network. A processor (104) coupled to an input acquisition unit (102) includes memory (106) storing instructions that cause processor (104) to receive acquired data as present-time environmental data. The processor (104) encodes present-time environmental data through a temporal signal encoder (108) into quantum-state representations corresponding to a future time interval. A chronon field modulator (110) generates temporally displaced signal link enabling reception of future-state information through a retrocausal signal transmission path (112). The future-state information is validated and integrated with present-time environmental data through temporal-spatial integrator (114) to generate risk-mapped environmental representations. A pre-emptive control unit (116) controls operational parameters of IoT network prior to occurrence of predetermined adverse event.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD 
[0001]	The present disclosure relates to the field of Internet of Things (IoT) networks and event prevention systems. More particularly, the present disclosure provides a system for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (hereinafter “IoT”) network using temporal data processing and predictive control mechanisms, and a method thereof.

BACKGROUND
[0002]	Internet of Things (IoT) networks have become integral to modern infrastructure by enabling interconnected sensing, communication, and actuation across a wide range of environments. Such networks are commonly deployed in industrial automation, smart grids, intelligent transportation systems, environmental monitoring, healthcare infrastructure, and large-scale building management systems. IoT networks typically rely on distributed sensor nodes to capture environmental parameters, networked processors to analyse the captured data, and control units to regulate system behaviour based on observed conditions.
[0003]	Conventional IoT monitoring and control systems primarily operate on present-time or historical data. Data collected from sensors is processed to detect anomalies, threshold violations, or trends, following which corrective actions are initiated. While such approaches provide reactive or near-real-time responses, they remain limited by latency in data acquisition, processing delays, and the inability to anticipate adverse events before their manifestation. As IoT networks grow in scale and complexity, such limitations increase the risk of cascading failures, safety hazards, service interruptions, and economic loss.
[0004]	Various predictive and forecasting techniques have been introduced to improve proactive decision-making in IoT environments. These techniques commonly employ statistical models, machine learning algorithms, or rule-based inference systems to estimate future system states based on historical patterns. However, such approaches are typically constrained by model uncertainty, incomplete data, and sensitivity to rapidly changing environmental conditions. Moreover, prediction accuracy often degrades in highly dynamic or non-linear systems where environmental parameters interact across spatial and temporal dimensions.
[0005]	Patent document, “US 20,050,159,894 A1” titled “Space weather prediction system and method” discloses a system and method of forecasting space weather (at Earth or another location) based on identifying complex patterns in solar, interplanetary, or geophysical data. These data may include current or historical measurements and/or modeled data (predicted or simulated). Data patterns (both non-event and event-related) are identified (even when another event is occurring). Such patterns may vary with recent/cyclic variations in solar (e.g. solar max/min), interplanetary, or geophysical activity. Embodiments are built around: (1) templates, (2) expert systems, (3) neural networks, (4) hybrid systems comprising combinations of (1), (2) and/or (3), and multimodal intelligent systems. Forecasts are customized and/or updated as new data arise and as systems are dynamically modified (e.g. via feedback between system parts). Numerical or other indices are generated representing: forecasts, associated confidence levels, etc. The invention predicts events/non-events and/or other values or parameters associated with space weather (e.g. Dst, event onset time, duration, etc.)
[0006]	Hence, in view of the aforementioned challenges and shortcomings in prior art, there is a dire need in the art to provide a system for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (hereinafter “IoT”) network using temporal data processing and predictive control mechanisms, and a method thereof.

OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0007]	It is an object of the present disclosure is to provide a system for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (IoT) network and a method thereof.
[0008]	It is another object of the present disclosure is to provide a system and a method that enables acquisition and processing of environmental data in a manner that supports anticipation of future network conditions.
[0009]	Yet another object of the present disclosure is to provide a system and a method that facilitate correlation between present-time environmental data and future-state information for improved risk assessment.

SUMMARY
[0010]	Aspects of the present disclosure relate to the field of Internet of Things (IoT) networks and event prevention systems. More particularly, the present disclosure provides a system for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (hereinafter “IoT”) network using temporal data processing and predictive control mechanisms, and a method thereof.
[0011]	In an aspect, the present disclosure, the system includes an input acquisition unit and a processor coupled with a memory. The memory stores instructions executable by the processor to receive environmental data from the Internet of Things network as present-time environmental data. The processor encodes the present-time environmental data into temporally ordered data representations corresponding to a future time interval. The processor further generates a temporally displaced signal link to enable reception of future-state information associated with the environmental parameters. The received future-state information is validated by correlation with the present-time environmental data.
[0012]	In an aspect, the validated future-state information may be integrated with present-time environmental data to generate risk-mapped environmental representations. The system may further control one or more operational parameters of the Internet of Things network based on the risk-mapped environmental representations before the occurrence of the predetermined adverse event.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0019]	The present disclosure relates to the field of Internet of Things (IoT) networks and event prevention systems. More particularly, the present disclosure provides a system for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (hereinafter “IoT”) network using temporal data processing and predictive control mechanisms, and a method thereof.
[0020]	Hereinafter, exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to the accompanying drawings FIGs. 1-6.
[0021]	FIG. 1 illustrates an exemplary representation of a block diagram of a system (100) for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (IoT) network, in accordance with an exemplary embodiment of the present disclosure.
[0022]	In an embodiment of the present disclosure, the system (100) operates within an Internet of Things (IoT) network to prevent a predetermined adverse event by processing environmental data across temporal and spatial dimensions. The system (100) can include an input acquisition unit (102) arranged to acquire data associated with one or more environmental parameters of the IoT network. The environmental parameters include measurable physical, electromagnetic, structural, or operational conditions such as temperature, pressure, vibration, radiation intensity, electrical load, fluid flow, positional deviation, or communication latency. The input acquisition unit (102) receives the environmental data from distributed sensing nodes deployed across the IoT network using wired interfaces, wireless communication protocols, or sensor buses. In an embodiment, the input acquisition unit (102) aggregates the environmental data as synchronized data streams indexed to a current processing instant.
[0023]	In an embodiment, the system (100) further includes a processor (104) operatively coupled to the input acquisition unit (102). The processor (104) includes a memory (106) storing a set of instructions executable by the processor (104). Upon execution of the instructions, the processor (104) receives the acquired data from the input acquisition unit (102) as present-time environmental data. The present-time environmental data represents a real-time snapshot of the environmental parameters corresponding to the IoT network at a given processing instant. In an embodiment, the present-time environmental data is normalized, timestamped, and aligned across multiple sensor sources prior to further processing.
[0024]	In such embodiment, the processor (104) encodes the present-time environmental data through a temporal signal encoder (108). The temporal signal encoder (108) transforms the present-time environmental data into quantum-state representations carrying temporal ordering information corresponding to a future time interval. The quantum-state representations refer to mathematically constructed state vectors, probability amplitudes, or high-dimensional encoded data structures that preserve temporal correlation patterns across successive observation windows. In an embodiment, the temporal signal encoder (108) applies techniques including quantum-inspired encoding, tensor-based temporal embedding, Hilbert space mapping, or probabilistic state superposition modelling to represent future evolution tendencies of the environmental parameters. In an alternative embodiment, the temporal signal encoder (108) applies recurrent neural temporal embeddings, spectral decomposition, or phase-space reconstruction to generate the quantum-state representations without requiring physical quantum hardware.
[0025]	In such embodiment, the processor (104) applies the quantum-state representations to a chronon field modulator (110). The chronon field modulator (110) performs temporal transformation operations on the quantum-state representations to generate a temporally displaced signal link between the quantum-state representations and present-time signal states. The temporally displaced signal link represents a computational association channel that aligns projected future-state representations with present-time signal states through time-index manipulation, predictive inference, and temporal offset mapping. In an embodiment, the chronon field modulator (110) applies time-warping functions, state transition modelling, causal graph inversion, or forward–backward temporal indexing to establish the temporally displaced signal link. In another embodiment, the chronon field modulator (110) operates using predictive state machines, Kalman filtering with future-state extrapolation, or Markov decision modeling indexed to future time intervals.
[0026]	In such embodiment, the processor (104) receives future-state information associated with the environmental parameters through a retrocausal signal transmission path (112) enabled by the temporally displaced signal link. The retrocausal signal transmission path (112) refers to a logical data path by which future-state information derived from temporal projection, predictive modelling, or reverse-time indexing is delivered for present-time evaluation. The future-state information includes predicted parameter values, anticipated threshold violations, or projected anomaly indicators corresponding to the defined future time interval. In an embodiment, the retrocausal signal transmission path (112) uses buffer-based future indexing, reverse temporal queues, or prediction-to-present mapping tables. In an alternative embodiment, the retrocausal signal transmission path (112) is implemented using machine learning prediction outputs tagged with future timestamps and injected into present-time processing pipelines.
[0027]	In an embodiment, the processor (104) validates the received future-state information by correlating the future-state information with the acquired present-time environmental data. The validation operation verifies temporal consistency, signal coherence, and plausibility between predicted future-state information and current environmental conditions. In an embodiment, the validation operation includes statistical correlation, confidence threshold verification, anomaly cross-checking, or deviation scoring between predicted values and present-time trends. In another embodiment, the validation operation includes rule-based consistency checks, temporal coherence scoring, or predictive confidence weighting to suppress invalid or contradictory future-state information.
[0028]	Further, the processor (104) integrates the validated future-state information with the present-time environmental data through a temporal-spatial integrator (114). The temporal-spatial integrator (114) aligns data across time and space dimensions of the IoT network to generate risk-mapped environmental representations. The temporal-spatial integrator (114) associates validated future-state information with specific spatial locations, network nodes, infrastructure zones, or operational domains of the IoT network. In an embodiment, the temporal-spatial integrator (114) constructs multi-layer risk maps, spatio-temporal matrices, or network topology overlays identifying zones of elevated risk within the future time interval. In an alternative embodiment, the temporal-spatial integrator (114) generates graph-based risk propagation models, heat maps, or node-level risk scores linked to predicted adverse conditions.
[0029]	In such embodiment, the processor (104) controls one or more operational parameters of the IoT network through a pre-emptive control unit (116) based on the risk-mapped environmental representations prior to the occurrence of the predetermined adverse event. The pre-emptive control unit (116) converts the risk-mapped environmental representations into control instructions affecting actuators, network controllers, or system management modules within the IoT network. In an embodiment, the pre-emptive control unit (116) adjusts power levels, routing paths, cooling mechanisms, access permissions, structural load distributions, or communication scheduling parameters. In another embodiment, the pre-emptive control unit (116) initiates isolation of affected nodes, modifies operational thresholds, or triggers automated mitigation protocols to prevent the occurrence of the predetermined adverse event.
[0030]	In a real-world implementation, the system (100) operates within industrial automation networks, smart infrastructure deployments, autonomous facilities, energy grids, or safety-critical monitoring environments. The described processing architecture enables temporal anticipation and pre-emptive intervention using realizable computational techniques without requiring physical manipulation of time or violation of causality.
[0031]	In an embodiment, the system (100) can include a control panel (118) connected to the processor (104) to allow access to a user using one or more means. The control panel (118) enables interaction with the system (100) for monitoring, configuration, and supervisory control. The one or more means include physical input interfaces, graphical user interfaces, voice-based interfaces, gesture-based interfaces, or remote access terminals. In an example implementation, the control panel (118) presents visual representations of risk-mapped environmental representations and permits manual override or prioritization of control actions executed by the pre-emptive control unit (116).
[0032]	In an embodiment, the processor (104) stores the received future-state information within a reverse-temporal buffer (120) operating as a temporal cache. The reverse-temporal buffer (120) maintains future-state information indexed to corresponding present-time environmental data to enable synchronized temporal analysis. The reverse-temporal buffer (120) can be implemented using high-speed memory structures, quantum-inspired memory architectures, or predictive data caches that preserve temporal ordering. In an alternative embodiment, the reverse-temporal buffer (120) selectively retains future-state information based on validation confidence or risk relevance.
[0033]	In an embodiment, the present-time signal states include sensor-derived physical signal states, electrical and electromagnetic signal states, network and communication signal states, actuator and control feedback states, system operational status states, spatial and positional signal states, or any combination thereof. Sensor-derived physical signal states include temperature, pressure, vibration, or radiation measurements. Electrical and electromagnetic signal states include voltage levels, current flow, signal interference, or field intensity. Network and communication signal states include latency, packet loss, bandwidth utilization, or node availability. Actuator and control feedback states include actuation response status and control loop feedback. System operational status states include fault indicators, load conditions, or performance metrics. Spatial and positional signal states include location coordinates, orientation data, or structural displacement values.
[0034]	In an embodiment, the risk-mapped environmental representations include spatial risk zone representations, temporal risk horizon representations, parameter-specific risk distributions, node-level or component-level risk maps, multi-parameter composite risk representations, priority-ranked risk representations, threshold-exceedance risk representations, or any combination thereof. Spatial risk zone representations identify geographic or structural regions associated with elevated predicted risk. Temporal risk horizon representations indicate time windows within which adverse events are projected. Parameter-specific risk distributions represent risk contribution associated with individual environmental parameters. Node-level or component-level risk maps associate predicted risk with specific IoT nodes or infrastructure components. Multi-parameter composite risk representations aggregate risk across multiple environmental parameters. Priority-ranked risk representations order risks based on severity or urgency. Threshold-exceedance risk representations identify parameters projected to exceed predefined operational limits.
[0035]	In an embodiment, the temporal-spatial integrator (114) receives scanning data from a quantum LiDAR array to generate three-dimensional environmental risk maps. The quantum LiDAR array emits and detects quantum-enhanced optical signals to acquire spatial depth, structural geometry, and environmental reflectivity data. The temporal-spatial integrator (114) aligns the scanning data with validated future-state information and present-time environmental data to construct three-dimensional representations identifying projected risk zones within physical space. In an alternative embodiment, the scanning data is obtained from non-quantum LiDAR systems, radar-based scanners, or imaging sensor arrays.
[0036]	In an embodiment, the system (100) can include a temporal log database (122) to record present-time operational data and corresponding future-state predictions for correlation analysis. The temporal log database (122) stores time-stamped records enabling comparison between predicted future conditions and observed outcomes. The temporal log database (122) supports offline analysis, system calibration, and performance evaluation. In an alternative embodiment, the temporal log database (122) implements encrypted storage or distributed ledger-based logging for data integrity.
[0037]	In an embodiment, the system (100) can include an energy harvesting unit (124) to supply operating power to at least the reverse-temporal buffer (120) and the chronon field modulator (110). The energy harvesting unit (124) extracts energy from ambient sources, including electromagnetic radiation, thermal gradients, vibrational energy, or electrical field fluctuations. The harvested energy maintains the operation of temporally sensitive components during power interruptions or remote deployment. In an alternative embodiment, the energy harvesting unit (124) operates in combination with auxiliary power storage elements.
[0038]	In an embodiment, the input acquisition unit (102) can include a plurality of quantum chronodynamic sensors (102-1) to detect variations in temperature, pressure, electromagnetic radiation, structural stress, or any combination thereof. The quantum chronodynamic sensors (102-1) employ quantum-enhanced sensitivity techniques to detect minute environmental changes correlated with the temporal evolution of system conditions. In an alternative embodiment, the quantum chronodynamic sensors (102-1) operate alongside classical sensors to enhance detection accuracy and temporal resolution.
[0039]	FIG. 2 illustrates an exemplary representation of a step-by-step illustration of a method (200) for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (IoT) network, in accordance with an exemplary embodiment of the present disclosure.
[0040]	At block 202, the method (200) for preventing a predetermined adverse event in an Internet of Things (IoT) network can include an acquiring step (202). During the acquiring step (202), the input acquisition unit (102) acquires data associated with one or more environmental parameters of the IoT network. [0041]	At block 204, the method (200) can further include a receiving step (204). During the receiving step (204), the processor (104) receives the acquired data from the input acquisition unit (102) as present-time environmental data. The processor (104) is connected to the input acquisition unit (102) and includes a memory (106) storing a set of instructions for execution. title: Adaptive Fan Speed Control Using Human Presence and Body Heat Sensing
abstract:
ABSTRACT
Adaptive Fan Speed Control Using Human Presence and Body Heat Sensing
The present invention relates to an adaptive fan speed control system (100) and method for automatically regulating an AC ceiling fan (108) according to human presence and occupant-related thermal conditions. The system comprises a PIR human presence sensor (101), a non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102), an ambient temperature sensor (103), and a microcontroller (104) having a thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) and a speed mapping module (104c). The microcontroller (104) combines occupancy information, occupant count and body heat measurements to determine a thermal parameter and generates a corresponding fan-speed command. An isolation/driver circuit (105) and TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106) regulate the fan speed. A control and timing module (104d) provides hysteresis to prevent rapid switching, while a user display (107) provides operating information. The system enables multi-level, occupancy-responsive and body-heat-responsive fan control while reducing unnecessary operation in vacant spaces.

specification:
Adaptive Fan Speed Control Using Human Presence and Body Heat Sensing
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates generally to smart home automation, embedded control systems, energy-efficient thermal comfort systems, and intelligent electrical appliance control. More particularly, the invention relates to a sensor-fusion-based fan control system and corresponding method that detects human presence using a Passive Infrared (PIR) sensor, determines human body heat using a non-contact infrared thermometric sensor, and adaptively regulates the operating speed of an AC ceiling fan according to occupancy and detected thermal load. The invention is particularly applicable to residential buildings, offices, classrooms, hospitals, hotels, commercial premises, and other indoor spaces requiring energy-efficient and responsive thermal comfort management.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Conventional ceiling fans generally operate according to manually selected speed levels or through relatively simple temperature-based control arrangements. In a conventional arrangement, a user manually selects a fan speed irrespective of whether a person is actually present within the room. Consequently, the fan may continue operating even after occupants leave the room, resulting in unnecessary electrical energy consumption. Temperature-controlled systems can reduce this problem to some extent; however, ambient temperature alone does not accurately represent the instantaneous thermal load produced by occupants. Human beings continuously release heat, and the amount of heat released can vary according to the number of occupants, physical activity, metabolic condition, clothing, and other environmental factors.
Occupancy-based HVAC control systems have attempted to address the problem by detecting whether a room is occupied and controlling heating, ventilation, or air-conditioning equipment accordingly. For example, US9671134B2, “Occupancy-based HVAC control system,” associated with Ecobee Technologies, provides occupancy-responsive HVAC control. However, the cited system does not provide the particular combination of real-time human presence detection with non-contact body heat measurement for determining an occupant-related thermal load and proportionally controlling the speed of an individual ceiling fan. The disclosure in the present invention identifies this distinction as a technical gap in existing occupancy-responsive systems.
PIR-based fan controllers provide another approach in which movement or presence of a person is detected and the fan is switched ON or OFF. However, a binary occupancy decision does not provide sufficient information for selecting an appropriate fan speed. A single occupant sitting quietly and several occupants performing physical activity may produce substantially different thermal comfort requirements, although a conventional PIR controller may treat both situations substantially alike. Similarly, a temperature sensor positioned in the room measures ambient conditions rather than the thermal radiation specifically associated with occupants.
The disclosed invention addresses these limitations through dual-sensor fusion, in which a PIR or equivalent infrared presence sensor determines occupancy information while a non-contact infrared thermometric sensor, such as an MLX90614, detects body-surface thermal radiation. A microcontroller processes these inputs to determine an adaptive fan-speed command. The disclosed implementation further considers the number of occupants and the difference between detected body heat and ambient temperature, thereby enabling fan-speed modulation based on a more representative thermal condition rather than relying solely upon room temperature.
Accordingly, there exists a need for a low-cost, retrofit-compatible fan control system capable of detecting occupancy, estimating occupant-related thermal load, and automatically adjusting fan speed while reducing unnecessary operation in vacant spaces.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides an adaptive fan speed control system and method configured to intelligently regulate the speed of an AC ceiling fan based on human presence, occupancy information, and detected human body heat. The invention provides a technical arrangement in which a human-presence sensing subsystem and a non-contact thermal sensing subsystem operate together rather than independently. The resulting sensor information is processed by a microcontroller to generate a fan-speed control signal that adapts to the detected thermal condition of the occupied space. The core architecture and operating principle disclosed in the source invention are based on combining PIR occupancy detection with infrared body-heat sensing and using a weighted speed-mapping algorithm for fan control.
In one embodiment, the system comprises a PIR sensor (101) for detecting human presence and estimating occupancy, a non-contact infrared temperature sensor (102) for detecting thermal radiation associated with one or more occupants, an optional ambient-temperature sensor (103), a microcontroller (104), a fan-speed control circuit (105), an AC ceiling fan (106), and a user-information display (107). The microcontroller may comprise an ESP32 or Arduino-based controller. The fan-speed control circuit may include a BT136 TRIAC and MOC3021 optocoupler arrangement configured to regulate the AC fan motor. A display, such as a 16×2 I²C LCD, may indicate occupancy status, detected temperature information, and the selected fan-speed level. The system may be powered by a 5 V DC supply and configured as a retrofit controller without requiring modification of the fan motor itself.
During operation, the PIR sensor continuously monitors a defined sensing region and provides an occupancy signal. When no person is detected for a predetermined period, the controller commands the fan to an OFF state. Upon detecting an occupant, the infrared thermometric sensor acquires body-surface temperature measurements. In an embodiment, multiple measurements are collected and processed as a rolling average to reduce instantaneous measurement variation. Where an ambient-temperature sensor is provided, the controller calculates a temperature difference between the detected body temperature and ambient temperature. The controller then combines the occupancy information, occupant count, and thermal difference to determine a suitable fan-speed level. The disclosed embodiment provides five operating states, namely OFF, low, medium, medium-high, and high, with the corresponding control signal supplied to the TRIAC-based speed-regulation circuit.
A further inventive enhancement proposed for incorporation into the system is a thermal-load persistence and confidence index. Instead of responding solely to a single instantaneous body-temperature measurement, the controller may determine whether the detected thermal signature persists over a predefined number of sampling intervals and whether the thermal signature spatially corresponds with the detected occupancy region. The controller can assign a confidence value to the detected thermal load and use the confidence value together with occupancy count and temperature difference for selecting the fan-speed command. This feature can reduce erroneous speed increases caused by transient heat sources, reflections, or short-duration sensor fluctuations while maintaining rapid response to genuine occupant thermal loads. Such a persistence-based fusion layer may therefore provide a more stable and reliable relationship between sensed human activity and fan-speed modulation.
The controller may further incorporate hysteresis or a delayed occupancy-release condition to prevent frequent ON/OFF switching when an occupant temporarily moves outside the sensing field. The complete control cycle can thereby provide responsive thermal comfort while reducing unnecessary energy consumption. The disclosed experimental prototype reported occupancy detection accuracy of approximately 97.3%, a measured body-heat detection range of 31.2–35.8°C, five confirmed fan-speed levels, an average response time of approximately 2.8 seconds, and an observed energy reduction of approximately 41.6% compared with always-on fan operation under the reported test conditions.
Accordingly, the invention provides a practical combination of occupancy awareness, body-heat-responsive control, multi-occupant scaling, thermal-load persistence, hysteresis-based stability, and retrofit AC-fan speed regulation, thereby providing an energy-efficient and responsive fan-control architecture suitable for residential and commercial environments.
In one aspect, the invention provides an adaptive fan speed control system (100) comprising a human presence sensing unit (101), a body heat sensing unit (102), an optional ambient temperature sensing unit (103), a processing and control unit (104), a thermal-load and occupancy fusion module (105), a speed-mapping module (106), an AC fan speed regulation unit (107), an AC ceiling fan (108), and an output/display unit (109).
The human presence sensing unit (101) comprises a PIR sensor configured to detect infrared radiation variations corresponding to human movement or presence within a predetermined sensing region. The unit may further provide occupancy information or an estimated number of occupants. The body heat sensing unit (102) comprises a non-contact infrared thermometric sensor, such as an MLX90614, configured to acquire thermal radiation from an occupant without physical contact.
The optional ambient temperature sensing unit (103) may comprise a DHT22 or equivalent temperature sensor configured to provide an ambient-temperature reference. The processing and control unit (104), preferably an ESP32 or Arduino microcontroller, receives the sensing signals and executes a programmed control algorithm. The thermal-load and occupancy fusion module (105) combines occupancy information, occupant count, detected body temperature, and, where available, ambient temperature to calculate a thermal-load parameter.
The speed-mapping module (106) determines a fan-speed command from the thermal-load parameter and occupancy information. In an embodiment, the thermal difference ΔT is obtained from the difference between averaged body temperature and ambient temperature, and the fan-speed level is selected according to predefined thresholds. The occupancy count may further cause an upward adjustment in the selected speed level where multiple occupants are detected.
The AC fan speed regulation unit (107) comprises a TRIAC-based switching arrangement, such as a BT136 TRIAC driven through a MOC3021 optocoupler, for regulating the electrical power supplied to the AC ceiling fan (108). The output/display unit (109) may provide occupancy status, temperature readings, and selected fan-speed information.
The system further comprises a thermal-load persistence and confidence module (110) configured to evaluate successive thermal measurements over multiple sampling intervals and determine whether a detected thermal signature is sufficiently persistent and correlated with the detected occupancy condition before allowing a significant speed increase. This feature can prevent transient thermal measurements from unnecessarily increasing fan speed.
In another aspect, the invention provides a method for adaptive fan-speed control comprising initializing the microcontroller and sensing units; continuously detecting human presence using the PIR sensor; determining whether the monitored region is occupied; acquiring non-contact body-temperature measurements when occupancy is detected; processing multiple temperature samples to determine an averaged thermal value; optionally acquiring ambient temperature; calculating a thermal difference between body temperature and ambient temperature; determining occupant count; generating a thermal-load persistence or confidence value from successive measurements; fusing the occupancy count, thermal difference and confidence value; mapping the resulting fused parameter to a predetermined fan-speed level; generating a corresponding control signal through the microcontroller; operating the TRIAC-based speed controller to regulate the AC ceiling fan; and maintaining the selected speed subject to hysteresis and subsequent sensor measurements.
When the system determines that the room is vacant for longer than a predetermined delay period, the controller generates an OFF command. When an occupant is detected, the controller progressively selects a suitable fan speed according to the sensed thermal load. The method thereby provides real-time, occupancy-aware and body-heat-responsive fan control while avoiding unnecessary operation in unoccupied conditions.
The method may further comprise continuously recalculating the thermal-load persistence and confidence index so that transient readings are rejected or assigned lower influence, whereas a persistent thermal signature associated with detected human presence is assigned higher influence. This permits stable control without requiring the user to manually select the fan speed and enables the controller to respond differently to varying occupant numbers and thermal conditions.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWING
FIG. 1 illustrates a schematic block diagram of an adaptive fan speed control system (100) configured for detecting human presence, sensing occupant body heat, determining an occupant-related thermal condition, and automatically regulating the operating speed of an AC ceiling fan. The system (100) comprises a PIR human presence sensor (101), a non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102), an ambient temperature sensor (103), a microcontroller (104) having a sensor interface module (104a), a thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b), a speed mapping module (104c), and a control and timing module (104d), an isolation/driver circuit (105), a TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106), a user display (107), an AC supply and ceiling fan arrangement (108), and a power supply unit (111).
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to an adaptive fan speed control system (100) and a corresponding method for automatically controlling the operating speed of an AC ceiling fan according to human presence, occupancy information and thermal radiation associated with one or more occupants. The invention is particularly intended for indoor environments such as residential rooms, offices, classrooms, laboratories, hospitals, hotels, commercial premises and other enclosed spaces in which ceiling fans are used for providing thermal comfort. The system (100) is configured as an embedded electronic control arrangement capable of being installed as a retrofit controller with an existing AC ceiling fan, thereby avoiding the need for substantial modification of the fan motor. The principal technical concept is the coordinated use of human-presence sensing and non-contact body-heat sensing so that fan operation is not determined merely by a manually selected speed or by ambient room temperature. The invention disclosure identifies the dual-sensor fusion of PIR presence information and infrared body-heat information as the principal inventive architecture.
As illustrated in FIG. 1, the adaptive fan speed control system (100) comprises a plurality of sensing units positioned to monitor an indoor environment, a processing and control unit, an electrical fan-speed regulating unit and a user-output unit. A first sensing input is provided by a PIR human presence sensor (101). The PIR human presence sensor (101) is configured to detect infrared radiation changes associated with a human occupant entering, leaving or moving within a predetermined sensing region. The sensor (101) may be positioned on or near the ceiling fan, on a wall, or at another suitable location from which the intended room area can be monitored. In one implementation, the sensor (101) provides an occupancy indication and may additionally provide information usable by the controller for estimating the number of occupants. The source disclosure specifies a typical sensing range of approximately 5–8 metres for the PIR arrangement.
A second sensing input is provided by a non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102). The sensor (102) may comprise an MLX90614 or another suitable infrared thermometric device capable of detecting thermal radiation from an object without physical contact. When a human occupant is detected by the PIR human presence sensor (101), the body heat sensor (102) acquires thermal radiation corresponding to the occupant's exposed or detectable body surface. The body heat sensor (102) therefore provides a thermal parameter associated more directly with the occupant than a conventional ambient temperature sensor. In the disclosed implementation, the infrared sensor is capable of measuring a body-surface temperature in a range generally associated with human skin under normal conditions. The source invention specifies acquisition of the body temperature at approximately 0.5-second intervals and processing of multiple samples to obtain a rolling average, thereby reducing the effect of instantaneous measurement fluctuations.
The system (100) may further comprise an ambient temperature sensor (103), such as a DHT22 or an equivalent temperature sensing device. The ambient temperature sensor (103) provides a reference temperature corresponding to the surrounding room environment. The use of the ambient temperature sensor (103) is advantageous because the controller can distinguish between the absolute detected body temperature and the thermal difference between the occupant and the surrounding environment. In an embodiment, the controller obtains an averaged body temperature and determines a temperature difference ΔT between the averaged body temperature and the ambient temperature. This thermal difference is subsequently used as one of the parameters for determining the required fan speed. The source disclosure also indicates that the body-heat-based control can operate independently of room temperature, with the ambient temperature sensor serving as an optional reference input.
The outputs of the PIR human presence sensor (101), the non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102), and, where provided, the ambient temperature sensor (103) are supplied to the microcontroller (104). The microcontroller (104) may comprise an ESP32, Arduino UNO or another programmable embedded controller having suitable digital and analogue interfaces, processing capability, memory and output-control capability. The microcontroller (104) functions as the central processing unit of the system (100) and executes the control algorithm for converting the sensor inputs into an electrical command for controlling the fan. The source disclosure specifically identifies an ESP32 or Arduino microcontroller for sensor fusion and PWM generation.
Within the microcontroller (104), a sensor interface module (104a) receives and conditions the signals generated by the sensors (101), (102) and (103). The sensor interface module (104a) may perform signal acquisition, sampling, basic filtering, conversion and communication with the respective sensors. The sensor interface module (104a) enables the microcontroller (104) to periodically acquire the occupancy condition from the PIR human presence sensor (101), body-temperature information from the infrared body heat sensor (102), and ambient temperature information from the ambient temperature sensor (103), where the latter is implemented.
A thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) receives the acquired sensor information and combines the occupancy-related and thermal information. In particular, the module (104b) determines whether the monitored region is occupied and uses the detected occupant count, body heat measurement and thermal difference to derive an occupant-related thermal condition. The sensor-fusion approach is important because the PIR human presence sensor (101) by itself primarily provides presence or motion information, while the infrared body heat sensor (102) provides thermal information. Combining the two allows the controller to distinguish a vacant condition from an occupied condition and further differentiate between different occupant thermal conditions. The source invention expressly identifies the combination of PIR presence detection and non-contact IR body heat sensing as the basis for adaptive fan control.
The thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) may process a plurality of body-temperature samples rather than relying on a single instantaneous reading. In the disclosed embodiment, a five-sample rolling average is calculated to obtain a representative body-temperature parameter. The controller may further determine the number of occupants based on the occupancy information obtained from the PIR human presence sensor (101). Consequently, a room containing several occupants can be treated differently from a room containing only one occupant. The source disclosure provides an arrangement in which the presence of multiple occupants can shift the selected fan-speed level upward by one level, thereby introducing multi-occupant scaling into the control process.
The speed mapping module (104c) receives the processed thermal and occupancy parameters from the thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) and converts them into a corresponding fan-speed command. In one embodiment, the controller determines the difference ΔT between the averaged body temperature and the ambient temperature and maps the resulting value to a plurality of predefined fan-speed levels. The disclosed mapping provides a low-speed condition for a relatively small thermal difference and progressively higher speed levels as the thermal difference increases. Five operational states may therefore be provided, namely OFF, low, medium, medium-high and high. The speed mapping module (104c) may further modify the selected level according to the number of detected occupants. Accordingly, the fan speed is not determined solely from the room temperature but from a combination of occupancy and occupant-related thermal information.
The microcontroller (104) further comprises a control and timing module (104d). The control and timing module (104d) regulates the temporal behaviour of the system and provides hysteresis or delay control to prevent unwanted rapid switching. In particular, when an occupant momentarily moves outside the detection region of the PIR human presence sensor (101), the fan is not immediately switched OFF. Instead, a predetermined delay period can be applied before a vacant condition is confirmed. The disclosed implementation provides a 30-second hysteresis timer for preventing rapid cycling when an occupant temporarily leaves the sensor field. The principal sensor-control loop may be executed approximately every two seconds.
The control output from the microcontroller (104) is supplied to the isolation/driver circuit (105). The isolation/driver circuit (105) may comprise an optocoupler, such as a MOC3021, configured to electrically isolate the low-voltage control electronics from the AC switching circuitry. The isolation arrangement improves electrical separation between the microcontroller-side circuitry and the AC fan-control circuitry while enabling the microcontroller (104) to control the subsequent TRIAC-based speed regulation stage. The source disclosure identifies a BT136 TRIAC together with a MOC3021 optocoupler as the principal AC fan speed regulation components.
The output of the isolation/driver circuit (105) is supplied to the TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106). The TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106) may comprise a BT136 TRIAC or an equivalent AC power semiconductor configured to regulate power supplied to the fan motor. The microcontroller (104) can generate an appropriate control signal, such as a PWM-derived or phase-control command, which is transferred through the isolation/driver circuit (105) to the TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106). The TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106) thereby controls the effective electrical power delivered to the AC ceiling fan within the permitted operating range, resulting in different fan-speed levels. The disclosed arrangement therefore allows the intelligent electronic controller to operate with a conventional AC ceiling fan rather than requiring a specially manufactured fan motor.
The TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106) is electrically associated with the AC supply and ceiling fan arrangement (108). The arrangement (108) represents the AC electrical supply and the ceiling fan being controlled. The AC ceiling fan receives the controlled electrical supply and rotates at the speed selected by the microcontroller (104). The system (100) can consequently be installed between the existing electrical supply and an existing AC ceiling fan, subject to appropriate electrical isolation, protection and installation practices. The retrofit configuration is one of the practical aspects identified in the source invention, which specifies compatibility with standard ceiling fans without modification to the fan motor.
The system (100) further comprises a user display (107), which may be implemented as a 16×2 I²C LCD or another suitable visual indicator. The display (107) receives status information from the microcontroller (104) and can indicate whether the room is occupied or vacant, the currently selected fan-speed level, and sensor-related information. Such an output allows an operator to observe the control state without interfering with the automatic operation of the fan. The source disclosure specifically provides for an LCD or LED indication of the current speed mode and identifies a 16×2 I²C LCD as one suitable hardware component.
The electrical and electronic components of the system (100) may be supplied by the power supply unit (111). The power supply unit (111) may comprise a 5 V, 2 A DC adapter or another suitably rated isolated low-voltage power supply. The power supply unit (111) provides operating power to the microcontroller (104), the sensing units (101), (102), (103), the display (107), and associated low-voltage electronic components. Suitable resistors, capacitors, PCB conductors and protective components may be incorporated in the controller circuitry, including components associated with signal conditioning and the TRIAC switching stage.
In operation, the system (100) is first initialized by the microcontroller (104), during which the sensing units are allowed to stabilize. The PIR human presence sensor (101) then continuously monitors the room. When no human presence is detected for a predetermined period, the thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) identifies a vacant condition and the control and timing module (104d) confirms the condition after the applicable hysteresis period. The speed mapping module (104c) then generates an OFF command, which is passed through the isolation/driver circuit (105) to the TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106), causing the AC ceiling fan in arrangement (108) to stop. Thus, the fan does not continue operating unnecessarily in an unoccupied room. The source disclosure identifies automatic switching OFF in the absence of human presence as an energy-saving function.
When a person enters the room, the PIR human presence sensor (101) detects the person and supplies an occupancy signal to the microcontroller (104). The body heat sensor (102) then acquires non-contact thermal measurements associated with the occupant. The sensor interface module (104a) receives the measurements, while the thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) processes the measurements to obtain a representative body-temperature value and occupancy condition. Where the ambient temperature sensor (103) is installed, the controller also obtains the ambient temperature and calculates the corresponding thermal difference. The speed mapping module (104c) uses these values to determine the required fan-speed level. The resulting control command is transferred through the isolation/driver circuit (105) and TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106) to the AC ceiling fan (108). The user display (107) simultaneously indicates the operating state.
For example, consider a real-life application in a 12 × 12 ft laboratory room containing a 48-inch ceiling fan, corresponding to the experimental arrangement disclosed by the inventors. The sensors (101), (102) and (103) may be positioned at or near ceiling level, with the PIR human presence sensor (101) monitoring the room and the infrared body heat sensor (102) directed toward the occupant region. When the laboratory is empty, the PIR sensor (101) detects no occupant and, after the predetermined delay, the controller commands the fan to the OFF state. When one researcher enters and remains seated at a workstation, the PIR sensor (101) detects occupancy and the infrared sensor (102) detects the associated body heat. The controller (104) processes the thermal measurements and selects a corresponding low or medium fan speed depending upon the determined thermal difference.
If additional researchers enter the laboratory, the occupancy information changes and the thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) accounts for the increased occupancy condition. The speed mapping module (104c) can consequently increase the fan-speed level to provide greater air movement. If the occupants subsequently perform physical activity, the detected body heat condition can increase, resulting in a further speed adjustment. Conversely, when the occupants leave the room, the PIR sensor (101) eventually confirms vacancy and the control and timing module (104d) prevents premature switching during a momentary sensing interruption before the fan is ultimately switched OFF.
The experimental information provided in the invention disclosure indicates that the prototype was tested under conditions involving zero, one, two and three occupants under both static and active conditions. The disclosed prototype achieved approximately 97.3% occupancy detection accuracy, measured body-temperature values of approximately 31.2–35.8°C with reported measurement error of about ±0.4°C, five confirmed fan-speed levels corresponding to measured RPM values of approximately 0, 320, 540, 760, 980 and 1150 RPM, and an average response time of approximately 2.8 seconds. The disclosed test further reported approximately 41.6% energy reduction over a 30-minute period compared with always-on fan operation under the stated test conditions.
Thus, the adaptive fan speed control system (100) provides a hardware-integrated arrangement in which human presence, occupant thermal radiation, optional ambient temperature, occupancy scaling, temporal hysteresis and AC fan-speed regulation are combined within a single embedded control architecture. The technical interaction among the PIR human presence sensor (101), non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102), ambient temperature sensor (103), microcontroller (104), isolation/driver circuit (105), TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106), user display (107), AC ceiling fan arrangement (108) and power supply unit (111) enables the fan to respond dynamically to actual occupancy and occupant-related thermal conditions. The invention thereby provides an energy-efficient retrofit solution capable of reducing unnecessary fan operation while maintaining adaptive thermal comfort in occupied indoor environments.
ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
1.	Adaptive energy-efficient operation: The invention automatically switches the AC ceiling fan (108) OFF when no human presence is detected and dynamically regulates the fan speed according to detected occupant thermal load, thereby reducing unnecessary electrical energy consumption.
2.	Dual-sensor thermal comfort control: By combining the PIR human presence sensor (101) with the non-contact infrared body heat sensor (102), the invention provides a more representative control parameter than conventional temperature-only or PIR-only fan controllers. The system can respond to actual occupant-related thermal conditions rather than merely ambient room temperature.
3.	Multi-occupant adaptive control: The thermal load and occupancy fusion module (104b) and speed mapping module (104c) enable the fan speed to be adjusted according to both detected body heat and the number of occupants, thereby providing differentiated thermal comfort for changing occupancy conditions.
4.	Retrofit compatibility and stable operation: The TRIAC-based speed control circuit (106), together with the isolation/driver circuit (105), enables the system to control a conventional AC ceiling fan (108) without requiring modification of the fan motor. The control and timing module (104d) further provides hysteresis/delay operation to prevent undesirable rapid ON/OFF switching.
