title: HOME ASSISTANCE SYSTEM FOR HEARING AND SPEECH IMPAIRED USERS AND METHOD THEREOF
abstract: A home assistance system (100) for hearing and speech impaired users includes a wearable device (102) to generate haptic alerts, and user-actuatable inputs; an image acquisition unit (110) positioned a door near an entrance of a building to capture images of visitors standing at door; a face recognition unit (112) to generate facial embeddings from captured images and compare generated facial embeddings with pre-stored identity of facial embeddings to classify visitors as recognized or unrecognized; a sensor (114) positioned on building to detect ambient environmental conditions exceeding a threshold; and a processor (116) transmits visitor classification information from face recognition unit (112) to wearable device (102) to display a visual notification and generates a haptic alert pattern in response to visitor classification information or environmental conditions exceeding threshold. The processor (116) causes the visitor-facing display to display a predefined message to a visitor upon actuation of the user-actuatable input.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD
[0001]	The present disclosure generally relates to a field of home automation systems. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to a home assistance system and a method for providing environmental awareness and visitor communication assistance to hearing impaired and speech impaired users.

BACKGROUND
[0002]	Hearing impaired and speech impaired individuals face significant challenges in perceiving visitors, hazardous household events, and emergency situations within a residential environment. Conventional audio-based doorbells, alarms, and communication methods are ineffective for such users, while speech impairment further limits communication with visitors at the entrance.
[0003]	Existing smart home systems, video doorbells, wearable notification devices, and assistive technologies provide limited functionality, such as motion detection, mobile notifications, flashing indicators, or vibration alerts. However, such systems generally operate as independent devices and do not provide an integrated solution combining visitor recognition, environmental hazard monitoring, wearable notifications, and silent visitor communication.
[0004]	Conventional wearable devices typically generate identical vibration alerts for different events, making it difficult for users to distinguish between routine notifications and emergency situations. Further, known systems generally lack contextual event prioritization, adaptive haptic feedback, and coordinated processing of multiple environmental sensors, resulting in false alarms, delayed responses, and reduced operational reliability.
[0005]	Existing solutions also rely heavily on smartphones, fixed displays, or cloud connectivity, which may become unavailable during network failures. Moreover, known systems do not provide secure biometric processing, fail-safe local operation, or personalized notification mechanisms based on user interaction.
[0006]	Although prior-art references disclose individual features such as gas leakage detection, facial recognition, wearable vibration alerts, or environmental monitoring, none discloses an integrated accessibility-oriented system capable of combining visitor recognition, contextual event prioritization, multi-sensor hazard detection, adaptive haptic notifications, silent bidirectional communication, and resilient edge-cloud processing for hearing impaired and speech impaired users.
[0007]	Therefore, there exists a need for an integrated assistive system capable of providing identity-based visitor notifications, environmental hazard alerts, distinguishable haptic feedback, silent communication with visitors, and uninterrupted operation while ensuring secure handling of biometric information.

OBJECTIVES OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0008]	A general objective of the present disclosure is to develop a wearable smart-home assistance system and method for deaf and speech-impaired users. 
[0009]	An objective of the present disclosure is to notify users of known and unknown visitors through haptic vibration and visual alerts. 
[0010]	Another objective of the present disclosure is to enable silent communication with visitors using predefined text messages displayed at the door. 
[0011]	Another objective of the present disclosure is to detect abnormal sounds or safety-related events in the home and provide timely alerts.
[0012]	Yet another objective of the present disclosure is to integrate face recognition, wearable notifications, and environmental monitoring into a single system. 

SUMMARY
[0013]	Present disclosure generally relates to home automation systems. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to an improved home assistance system and a method for providing environmental awareness and visitor communication assistance to hearing impaired and speech impaired users.
[0014]	According to an aspect, the proposed home assistance system for hearing and speech impaired users includes a wearable device that includes a microcontroller, a display, a vibration motor to generate haptic alerts, and at least one user-actuatable input. The system includes an image acquisition unit positioned a door near an entrance of a building to capture images of visitors standing at the door, facing the image acquisition unit. The system includes a face recognition unit to generate facial embeddings from the captured images of the visitor and compare the generated facial embeddings with pre-stored identity of facial embeddings to classify visitors as recognized or unrecognized.
[0015]	The system includes a sensor unit positioned on the building to detect ambient environmental conditions exceeding a threshold. The system includes a processor in communication with the wearable device, the image acquisition unit, the face recognition unit, the sensor unit. The processor transmits visitor classification information from the face recognition unit to the wearable device to display a visual notification, and generates a haptic alert pattern via the vibration motor in response to the visitor classification information or the environmental conditions exceeding the threshold. The processor upon actuation of the user-actuatable input, causes the visitor-facing display to display a predefined message to a visitor.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS
[0016]	FIGs. 1A and 1B illustrates an exemplary block diagram showing the proposed home assistance system for providing environmental awareness and visitor communication assistance to hearing impaired and speech impaired users, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure.
[0017]	FIG. 2 illustrates an exemplary flow diagram showing a method for providing environmental awareness and visitor communication assistance to hearing impaired and speech impaired users, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION 
[0018]	According to an aspect, the disclosure generally relates to home automation systems. The system for hearing and speech impaired users includes a wearable device to generate haptic alerts, and user-actuatable inputs; an image acquisition unit positioned a door near an entrance of a building to capture images of visitors standing at door; a face recognition unit to generate facial embeddings from captured images and compare generated facial embeddings with pre-stored identity of facial embeddings to classify visitors as recognized or unrecognized; a sensor unit positioned on building to detect ambient environmental conditions exceeding a threshold; and a processor transmits visitor classification information from face recognition unit to wearable device to display a visual notification and generates a haptic alert pattern in response to visitor classification information or environmental conditions exceeding threshold. The processor causes the visitor-facing display to display a predefined message to a visitor upon actuation of the user-actuatable input.
[0019]	Referring to FIG. 1A, the proposed home assistance system (hereinafter referred to as "system 100") for hearing and speech impaired users is described in detail. The system (100) includes a wearable device (102), at least one image acquisition unit (110), a face recognition unit (112), at least one sensor (114), a processor (116), and a visitor-facing display (118). The processor (116) is disposed within the wearable device (102) and remains in communication with the image acquisition unit (110), the face recognition unit (112), the sensor (114), and the visitor-facing display (118), such that the entire orchestration logic of the system (100) is hosted on-body and remains available to the user irrespective of the location of the user within a building.
[0020]	In an embodiment, the wearable device (102) includes a microcontroller (104), a display (106), a vibration motor (108) generates haptic alerts, at least one user-actuatable input (120), a memory (122), a communication interface (124), and a power supply (126). The wearable device (102) is worn on the body of the user and delivers visual and tactile notifications without dependence upon auditory perception or upon speech-based interaction. The microcontroller (104) receives structured event messages over the communication interface (124), parses the received event messages, formats corresponding text for the display (106), and drives the vibration motor (108) in accordance with an alert pattern associated with the event category.
[0021]	In an embodiment, the display (106) is an organic light emitting diode (OLED) display module mounted on a face of the wearable device (102) and renders event identity, visitor identity, environmental warnings, emergency indicators, and contextual communication prompts. The display (106) further renders a persistence duration and a display prominence determined by the processor (116) in accordance with the priority class assigned to the detected event.
[0022]	In an embodiment, the vibration motor (108) generates the haptic alerts, wherein the haptic alerts include a pattern pertaining to event-specific vibration signatures. The event-specific vibration signatures include configurable combinations of pulse sequences, oscillation intervals, vibration amplitudes, temporal modulation patterns, and repetition structures, wherein each event-specific vibration signature corresponds to a semantically identifiable event category. By way of illustration, an emergency environmental hazard such as a gas leakage or an abnormal appliance behaviour triggers a continuous high-intensity oscillatory vibration sequence combined with a persistent warning displayed on the display (106); detection of an unrecognized visitor during night-time conditions triggers an escalating intermittent vibration sequence together with a high-priority visual alert; and detection of a recognized family member or an authorized caregiver triggers a low-intensity short-duration tactile signature optimized for reduced cognitive burden and improved user comfort. The user thereby distinguishes among multiple environmental situations without requiring visual interaction with the display (106). In alternative embodiments, the vibration motor (108) is implemented as a linear resonant actuator, an eccentric rotating mass motor, an electro-tactile stimulator, or a multi-point distributed vibration array.
[0023]	In an embodiment, the at least one user-actuatable input (120) includes one or more push-buttons, capacitive touch elements, or gesture-sensing elements provided on the wearable device (102). Actuation of the user-actuatable input (120) allows the user to acknowledge a received alert or to select and transmit a predefined message to the visitor-facing display (118).
[0024]	In an embodiment, the image acquisition unit (110) is positioned at at least one door near an entrance of the building and captures one or more images of visitors standing at the at least one door and facing the at least one image acquisition unit (110). Image capture is initiated continuously, at a timed interval, or upon a motion trigger generated by a motion detection element associated with the at least one door. In alternative embodiments, the image acquisition unit (110) includes a dedicated internet-protocol camera, an embedded edge camera device, or multiple synchronized cameras positioned at different viewing angles to improve visitor recognition reliability under varying illumination conditions and occlusion scenarios. The image acquisition unit (110) further includes at least one of a thermal imaging camera, an infrared sensing module, and a depth-sensing camera to improve visitor detection accuracy during night-time operation or low-visibility conditions.
[0025]	In an embodiment, the face recognition unit (112) generates facial embeddings from the captured images of the visitor and compares the generated facial embeddings with pre-stored identity facial embeddings retained in an identity database (128) so as to classify visitors as recognized or unrecognized. The face recognition unit (112) includes an InsightFace unit (112A) that applies a facial embedding model to the captured images so as to produce a multi-dimensional embedding vector. In one implementation, the InsightFace unit (112A) applies an InsightFace model executed by an application programming interface backend, and the identity database (128) is implemented as a Supabase database storing the embedding vectors together with a name and an identifier of each enrolled person. 
[0026]	The generated facial embeddings are compared with the stored embeddings using cosine similarity, such that a match is returned when the similarity exceeds a threshold and an indicator corresponding to an unrecognized visitor is returned when no stored embedding satisfies the threshold. In alternative embodiments, the comparison employs Euclidean distance evaluation or adaptive confidence scoring, and the facial embedding model is replaced or complemented by a cloud-hosted recognition service so as to enable multi-camera deployment, multi-home management, and centralized administration. A recognition confidence value associated with each comparison is dynamically adjusted in accordance with environmental illumination quality, image stability, face orientation, temporal consistency, and historical recognition reliability.
[0027]	In an embodiment, the face recognition unit (112) further classifies the visitor into contextual categories including an authorized visitor, a caregiver, a family member, an unknown individual, a suspicious person, an emergency responder, and delivery personnel, and associates a contextual priority value with the classification in accordance with environmental conditions, behavioural history, temporal context, and security risk evaluation parameters.
[0028]	In an embodiment, the at least one sensor (114) is positioned on the building at a safety-critical location and detects ambient environmental conditions exceeding a threshold. The at least one sensor (114) includes an acoustic sensor positioned near a gas cylinder area, a baby bed, a washing machine, or a front gate, and detects a sound level exceeding a calibrated threshold indicative of a leakage warning, an abnormal knock, an appliance alarm, or a comparable incident. 
[0029]	The at least one sensor (114) additionally includes at least one of a gas concentration detector, a smoke sensor, a flame detector, a thermal sensor, a temperature sensor, a motion sensor, a proximity sensor, a vibration anomaly detector, a pressure sensor, an air-quality sensor, a water-leakage sensor, a fall-detection module, a door-state sensor, and an appliance-monitoring module. Distinct sensor units (114) placed at different locations are assigned different alert priorities, whereby an acoustic event near the gas cylinder area is escalated ahead of an acoustic event near the washing machine.
[0030]	In an embodiment, the visitor-facing display (118) is a liquid crystal display module mounted near the at least one door and presents a predefined message to the visitor upon actuation of the user-actuatable input (120). The predefined message includes messages such as "I am busy, please wait" and "Please leave the parcel at the door". The set of predefined messages is expanded or personalized through a mobile application or a web application operated by the user or by a caregiver.
[0031]	In an embodiment, the communication interface (124) establishes data channels among the wearable device (102), the image acquisition unit (110), the face recognition unit (112), the sensor (114), and the visitor-facing display (118). The data channels are established by way of serial communication, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, ZigBee, LoRaWAN, MQTT, near-field communication, or a hybrid combination of the foregoing, selected in accordance with the size of the building and the number of users supported.
[0032]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) is in communication with the wearable device (102), the image acquisition unit (110), the face recognition unit (112), and the sensor (114). The processor (116) transmits visitor classification information from the face recognition unit (112) to the wearable device (102) so as to display a visual notification on the display (106), and generates a haptic alert pattern by way of the vibration motor (108) in response to the visitor classification information or in response to the environmental conditions exceeding the threshold. The processor (116) upon actuation of the user-actuatable input (120), causes the visitor-facing display (118) to display a predefined message to a visitor.
[0033]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes a secure accessibility communication unit (116A) encrypts facial embeddings, visitor identification data, sensor transmissions, and wearable communication channels using secure cryptographic mechanisms, wherein the secure accessibility communication unit (116A) supports tokenized biometric representation, localized identity abstraction, and secure edge-device authentication so as to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive accessibility-related information associated with the user.
[0034]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes a multi-sensor event fusion unit (116B) aggregates and correlates data received from the at least one sensor (114) and to execute correlation logic so as to determine whether multiple environmental indicators collectively satisfy predefined or adaptive event confidence conditions prior to generating notifications. The multi-sensor event fusion unit (116B) performs signal filtering, signal normalization, temporal synchronization, anomaly analysis, and weighted confidence estimation upon the acquired data streams. By way of illustration, a simultaneous detection of an elevated gas concentration, an acoustic leakage signature, and a thermal anomaly collectively satisfies an emergency hazard confidence condition, whereas an isolated acoustic transient failing to correlate with any further indicator is suppressed as a non-critical noise event, whereby false-positive notifications are substantially reduced.
[0035]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes a contextual event processing unit (116C) continuously analyses environmental, visitor-related, and user-interaction data streams, wherein the contextual event processing unit (116C) performs dynamic event classification based on severity, urgency, event source, temporal context, sensor confidence level, and behavioural interaction history, and categorizes detected events into priority classes including emergency events, security alerts, environmental hazards, communication requests, informational notifications, and low-priority routine activities. Based upon the assigned priority class, the contextual event processing unit (116C) modifies notification delivery behaviour including vibration intensity, pulse duration, alert repetition frequency, formatting of the display (106), visual persistence duration, and escalation logic. The contextual event processing unit (116C) further suppresses repetitive low-priority notifications so as to minimize alert fatigue and selectively prioritizes emergency alerts over routine environmental events.
[0036]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes an edge-cloud processing unit (116D) supports both local inference processing and cloud-assisted recognition workflows. The processor (116) stores compressed facial embeddings, emergency recognition rules, and predefined event-processing logic within local memory resources of the memory (122). The processor (116) performs local visitor recognition, hazard analysis, and emergency alert generation during internet interruption, cloud service failure, or communication instability.
[0037]	The edge-cloud processing unit (116D) autonomously transitions the system (100) between a cloud-assisted operational mode and a local fail-safe operational mode in accordance with internet connectivity status, network latency, and communication reliability, wherein the transition occurs without manual intervention by the user, whereby accessibility functionality remains uninterrupted during network outages.
[0038]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes a behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E) monitors historical user interactions including response latency, acknowledgement frequency, ignored alerts, frequently selected visitor responses, and event-specific behavioural patterns, wherein the behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E) modifies alert persistence, notification priority, haptic encoding intensity, and escalation timing based upon continuously accumulated interaction data. By way of illustration, alerts historically ignored by the user gradually receive reduced notification persistence, whereas critical alerts associated with a rapid user response receive higher prioritization and faster escalation routing. 
[0039]	The behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E) employs machine-learning algorithms to analyse user response history, environmental patterns, time-based interaction behaviour, visitor frequency, and emergency response characteristics so as to improve contextual event classification, tactile communication distinguishability, and visitor-recognition reliability.
[0040]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes an emergency escalation management unit (116F) to autonomously initiate caregiver notification, emergency communication transmission, remote alert forwarding, or secondary alarm activation when critical environmental events remain unacknowledged for a predefined threshold duration. The emergency escalation management unit (116F) continuously evaluates whether an acknowledgement has been received by way of the user-actuatable input (120) within the predefined threshold duration and, upon failure of acknowledgement, initiates secondary safety workflows including caregiver notification transmission, centralized monitoring activation, external alarm generation, emergency-message forwarding, and emergency-service communication.
[0041]	In an embodiment, the processor (116) includes a low-power management unit to optimize battery utilization of the power supply (126) through intelligent sensor polling, event-triggered activation, contextual processing scheduling, low-power wireless communication management, and dynamic notification-persistence optimization.
[0042]	In an embodiment, the system (100) supports a multi-user residential deployment where the wearable devices (102) associated with individual identity profiles and individual accessibility preferences simultaneously receive personalized tactile notifications generated by the processor (116).
[0043]	In an embodiment, the wearable device (102) is implemented in the form of a smartwatch, a smart wristband, a ring device, a pendant, a belt-mounted module, a smart footwear insert, or a garment-integrated wearable interface, selected in accordance with user comfort requirements, accessibility preferences, and operational deployment conditions.
[0044]	In an embodiment, the predefined messages presented on the visitor-facing display (118) support multilingual text generation, artificial-intelligence-assisted contextual response recommendation, symbol-based communication interfaces, sign-language avatar rendering, and remote caregiver-assisted communication workflows, wherein a recommended response is selected in accordance with the visitor classification, temporal conditions, delivery-event detection, and security-related event classification.
[0045]	In an embodiment, the system (100) is deployed in elderly-care facilities, hospitals, rehabilitation centres, industrial safety environments, educational institutions, hostels, assisted-living infrastructures, public accessibility systems, and emergency response facilities, and integrates with internet-of-things automation platforms, intelligent lighting systems, mobile accessibility applications, emergency communication servers, cloud-based monitoring dashboards, and caregiver supervision networks.
Working of the System
[0046]	Referring to FIG. 1B, the operation of the system (100) is described. In a registration phase, an image of an authorized person such as a family member or a caregiver is captured by way of the image acquisition unit (110) and transmitted to an enrolment endpoint of the face recognition unit (112). The InsightFace unit (112A) generates an embedding vector from the captured image, and the generated embedding vector is stored within the identity database (128) together with a name and an identifier of the authorized person. A plurality of authorized persons is enrolled in the same manner. The secure accessibility communication unit (116A) encrypts the stored embedding vectors prior to storage.
[0047]	In an operational phase, the image acquisition unit (110) monitors the door area and captures a facial image of a visitor upon a motion trigger or upon expiry of a timed interval. The captured facial image is transmitted to a verification endpoint of the face recognition unit (112), whereupon the InsightFace unit (112A) generates an embedding vector from the captured facial image and compares the generated embedding vector against the stored embedding vectors within the identity database (128) using cosine similarity. Where a similarity value exceeding the threshold is obtained, the name of the closest matching enrolled person is returned; otherwise, an indicator corresponding to an unrecognized visitor is returned.
[0048]	The returned result is forwarded to the microcontroller (104) of the wearable device (102) by way of the communication interface (124) as a structured message. The microcontroller (104) parses the structured message and renders a corresponding text upon the display (106), such as "[Name] is at the main door" for a recognized visitor and "Unrecognized person is at the main door" for an unrecognized visitor, and concurrently drives the vibration motor (108) in accordance with the event-specific vibration signature associated with the corresponding event category, whereby the user is alerted even when the user is not observing the display (106).
[0049]	Upon actuation of the user-actuatable input (120), the microcontroller (104) transmits a command to the visitor-facing display (118), whereupon a selected predefined message such as "I am working, please wait" or "Please leave the package at the door" is presented near the at least one door for the visitor to read, whereby silent and rapid communication with the visitor is achieved without speech and without any requirement for the visitor to understand sign language.
[0050]	In parallel, the at least one sensor (114) monitors an analog or digital value corresponding to the ambient environmental condition at the safety-critical location. Where the monitored value exceeds the calibrated threshold, the multi-sensor event fusion unit (116B) correlates the monitored value with further sensor outputs so as to confirm satisfaction of the event confidence condition, the contextual event processing unit (116C) assigns a priority class to the confirmed event, and a safety alert such as "Alert: Loud sound near gas cylinder" is rendered upon the display (106) together with a distinct vibration pattern differentiating the safety alert from a visitor alert.
[0051]	Where the confirmed event belongs to an emergency priority class and no acknowledgement is received by way of the user-actuatable input (120) within the predefined threshold duration, the emergency escalation management unit (116F) initiates the secondary safety workflow. Where connectivity to the cloud-assisted recognition workflow is interrupted at any stage, the edge-cloud processing unit (116D) transitions the system (100) into the local fail-safe operational mode using the compressed facial embeddings and cached event rules stored within the memory (122), whereby visitor recognition, hazard detection, and notification delivery continue without interruption. Throughout operation, the behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E) records acknowledgement latency, interaction frequency, dismissed alerts, and frequently selected communication responses, and modifies subsequent alert intensity, repetition timing, escalation thresholds, and tactile persistence accordingly.
Working Example:
[0052]	By way of a non-limiting working example, the system (100) is installed in a two-bedroom residence occupied by a hearing and speech impaired user. The wearable device (102) is embodied as a wristband carrying a microcontroller (104), a 0.96-inch OLED display (106), a coin-type vibration motor (108), two push-buttons forming the user-actuatable input (120), and a rechargeable power supply (126). The image acquisition unit (110) is mounted above the main door, the visitor-facing display (118) is a 16×2 liquid crystal display mounted beside the main door at eye level, and a first sensor (114) embodied as an acoustic sensor is mounted approximately half a metre from a liquefied petroleum gas cylinder within the kitchen, while a second sensor (114) is mounted adjacent to a washing machine.
[0053]	During enrolment, images of four family members and one domestic caregiver are captured and the corresponding embedding vectors are stored within the identity database (128).
[0054]	In a first scenario, the caregiver arrives at the main door. The image acquisition unit (110) captures a facial image, the InsightFace unit (112A) generates an embedding vector, and a cosine similarity of 0.71 against the stored embedding vector of the caregiver, exceeding a threshold of 0.55, returns the name of the caregiver. The display (106) renders "Priya is at the main door" and the vibration motor (108) executes a low-intensity signature of two short pulses of 200 milliseconds separated by an interval of 300 milliseconds. The user actuates the first push-button, whereupon the visitor-facing display (118) presents "I am busy, please wait", and the caregiver waits at the door.
[0055]	In a second scenario, an unenrolled delivery agent arrives at 21:40 hours. No stored embedding vector satisfies the threshold, and the contextual event processing unit (116C), taking into account the night-time temporal context and the unrecognized classification, assigns a security-alert priority class. The display (106) renders "Unrecognized person is at the main door" and the vibration motor (108) executes an escalating intermittent signature of five pulses of increasing amplitude. The user actuates the second push-button, whereupon the visitor-facing display (118) presents "Please leave the parcel at the door".
[0056]	In a third scenario, a regulator of the gas cylinder develops a leak, producing a sustained hiss. The acoustic sensor (114) within the kitchen registers a level exceeding the calibrated threshold for longer than three seconds, and the multi-sensor event fusion unit (116B) correlates the acoustic reading with a rising reading from a co-located gas concentration detector, thereby satisfying the emergency hazard confidence condition. The contextual event processing unit (116C) assigns an emergency priority class, the display (106) renders "Alert: Loud sound near gas cylinder" with persistent visual formatting, and the vibration motor (108) executes a continuous high-intensity oscillatory sequence. The user, being asleep, fails to acknowledge the alert within a predefined threshold duration of sixty seconds, whereupon the emergency escalation management unit (116F) transmits a notification to a registered caregiver mobile number and activates an external alarm within the residence.
[0057]	In a fourth scenario, the residential internet connection fails while a family member approaches the main door. The edge-cloud processing unit (116D) detects the loss of connectivity and transitions the system (100) into the local fail-safe operational mode, whereupon the compressed embedding vectors stored within the memory (122) are used to identify the family member locally, and the display (106) renders "Arun is at the main door" without any interruption perceptible to the user.
[0058]	Over a period of four weeks of operation, the behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E) records that alerts arising from the washing machine sensor (114) are dismissed by the user on twenty-three of twenty-five occasions, and accordingly reduces the notification persistence and vibration intensity associated with the corresponding event category, while retaining unaltered the persistence and intensity associated with the gas cylinder event category.
[0059]	Referring to FIG. 2, the proposed method (hereinafter referred to as "method 200") for providing environmental awareness and visitor communication assistance to a hearing or speech impaired user in a residential environment is described in detail. The method (200) is executed by the system (100) described hereinabove, wherein the processor (116) disposed within the wearable device (102) orchestrates each of the steps of the method (200), whereby the environmental awareness and communication functions remain available to the user irrespective of the location of the user within the residential environment.
[0060]	Prior to execution of the method (200), an enrolment operation is performed, wherein an image of each authorized person including a family member and a caregiver is captured by way of the image acquisition unit (110), a corresponding embedding vector is generated by the InsightFace unit (112A), and the generated embedding vector is stored within the identity database (128) together with a name and an identifier of the authorized person, the stored embedding vector being encrypted by the secure accessibility communication unit (116A).
[0061]	The method (200) includes a step (202) of capturing a facial image of a visitor by an image acquisition unit (110) positioned at at least one door near an entrance of the residential environment. The facial image is captured continuously, upon expiry of a timed interval, or upon a motion trigger generated at the at least one door, and the captured facial image is supplemented, in low-visibility or night-time conditions, by image data acquired from a thermal imaging camera, an infrared sensing module, or a depth-sensing camera associated with the image acquisition unit (110).
[0062]	The method (200) includes another step (204) of generating a facial embedding from the captured facial image by a face recognition unit (112). The face recognition unit (112) applies a facial embedding model by way of the InsightFace unit (112A) so as to produce a multi-dimensional embedding vector representative of the visitor, wherein the facial embedding is generated either by way of local edge-based inference or by way of a cloud-assisted recognition workflow selected in accordance with a prevailing connectivity status.
[0063]	The method (200) includes a step (206) of comparing the generated facial embedding with stored identity embeddings retained within the identity database (128) using a similarity metric. The similarity metric includes cosine similarity, Euclidean distance evaluation, or an adaptive confidence score, and a recognition confidence value associated with the comparison is dynamically adjusted in accordance with environmental illumination quality, image stability, face orientation, temporal consistency, and historical recognition reliability.
[0064]	The method (200) includes another step (208) of classifying the visitor as recognized or unrecognized based on whether the similarity metric exceeds a threshold. Where the similarity metric exceeds the threshold, a name of the closest matching enrolled person is returned; and where no stored identity embedding satisfies the threshold, an indicator corresponding to an unrecognized visitor is returned. The step (208) further includes assigning the visitor to a contextual category including an authorized visitor, a caregiver, a family member, an unknown individual, a suspicious person, an emergency responder, or delivery personnel, and associating a contextual priority value with the contextual category in accordance with temporal context, behavioural history, and security risk evaluation parameters.
[0065]	The method (200) includes a step (210) of transmitting visitor classification information to a wearable device (102) worn by the user. The visitor classification information is transmitted as a structured message by way of the communication interface (124) over a data channel established by serial communication, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, ZigBee, LoRaWAN, MQTT, or near-field communication, and the structured message is encrypted by the secure accessibility communication unit (116A) prior to transmission.
[0066]	The method (200) includes another step (212) of presenting, on a display (106) of the wearable device (102), a visual notification indicating the visitor classification. The microcontroller (104) parses the received structured message and renders a corresponding text upon the display (106), such as "[Name] is at the main door" for a recognized visitor and "Unrecognized person is at the main door" for an unrecognized visitor, wherein a visual persistence duration and a display prominence of the visual notification are determined in accordance with a priority class assigned to the corresponding event.
[0067]	The method (200) includes a step (214) of generating, by a vibration motor (108) of the wearable device (102), a haptic alert pattern corresponding to the visitor classification. The haptic alert pattern includes an event-specific vibration signature formed of a configurable combination of pulse sequences, oscillation intervals, vibration amplitudes, temporal modulation patterns, and repetition structures, wherein each event-specific vibration signature corresponds to a semantically identifiable event category. Accordingly, a recognized family member or authorized caregiver triggers a low-intensity short-duration signature, whereas an unrecognized visitor detected during night-time conditions triggers an escalating intermittent signature, whereby the user distinguishes the nature of the event without observing the display (106).
[0068]	The method (200) includes another step (216) of monitoring, by at least one sensor (114) positioned near a safety-critical location of the residential environment, an environmental condition. The safety-critical location includes a gas cylinder area, a baby bed, a washing machine, or a front gate, and the monitored environmental condition includes an acoustic level, a gas concentration, a smoke density, a thermal reading, a motion event, a vibration anomaly, an air-quality reading, a water-leakage indication, or a door-state indication. The monitoring includes acquiring an analog or digital sensor value and subjecting the acquired sensor value to noise filtering, signal normalization, temporal synchronization, and sensor-confidence estimation.
[0069]	The method (200) includes a step (218) of transmitting an environmental alert to the wearable device (102) and generating a distinct haptic alert pattern upon detecting the environmental condition exceeding a threshold. Prior to transmission of the environmental alert, the acquired sensor value is correlated with sensor values received from further sensor units (114) by way of the multi-sensor event fusion unit (116B) so as to determine whether multiple environmental indicators collectively satisfy a predefined or adaptive event confidence condition, whereby a false-positive notification arising from an isolated acoustic transient is suppressed. Upon satisfaction of the event confidence condition, the contextual event processing unit (116C) assigns a priority class to the detected event, a corresponding warning text such as "Alert: Loud sound near gas cylinder" is rendered upon the display (106), and the vibration motor (108) executes a vibration signature distinct from the vibration signature associated with a visitor event.
[0070]	The method (200) includes a further step (220) of causing, upon receiving a user input by way of the user-actuatable input (120) of the wearable device (102), a visitor-facing display (118) positioned at the entrance to present a predefined message to the visitor. The predefined message includes a message such as "I am busy, please wait", "I am working, please wait", or "Please leave the parcel at the door", whereby the user communicates silently and rapidly with the visitor without recourse to speech and without any requirement for the visitor to understand sign language. The predefined message is selected from a message set that is expandable or personalizable by way of a mobile application or a web application, and the predefined message is optionally rendered in a selected language, as a symbol-based representation, or as a contextual response recommended in accordance with the contextual category assigned to the visitor at the step (208).
[0071]	The method (200) includes a further step (222) of transitioning, upon detection of an internet interruption, a cloud service failure, or a communication instability, into a local fail-safe operational mode by way of the edge-cloud processing unit (116D), wherein compressed facial embeddings, emergency recognition rules, and predefined event-processing logic stored within the memory (122) are used so as to perform local visitor recognition, hazard analysis, and emergency alert generation, and wherein the transitioning occurs autonomously without manual intervention by the user.
[0072]	The method (200) includes a further step (224) of monitoring historical user interactions including response latency, acknowledgement frequency, ignored alerts, frequently selected visitor responses, and event-specific behavioural patterns by way of the behavioural learning and accessibility optimization unit (116E), and modifying, based upon continuously accumulated interaction data, an alert persistence, a notification priority, a haptic encoding intensity, and an escalation timing applied at subsequent executions of the steps (212), (214), and (218).
[0073]	The method (200) includes a further step (226) of determining whether an acknowledgement of an environmental alert belonging to an emergency priority class has been received by way of the user-actuatable input (120) within a predefined threshold duration, and, upon failure of acknowledgement, autonomously initiating by way of the emergency escalation management unit (116F) a secondary safety workflow including caregiver notification transmission, emergency communication transmission, remote alert forwarding, centralized monitoring activation, or secondary alarm activation.
[0074]	In a further embodiment, the method (200) is executed concurrently in respect of a plurality of wearable devices (102) associated with individual identity profiles and individual accessibility preferences, whereby a plurality of hearing or speech impaired users occupying the residential environment simultaneously receives personalized visual and tactile notifications.
[0075]	While considerable emphasis has been placed herein on the preferred embodiments, it will be appreciated that many embodiments can be made and that many changes can be made in the preferred embodiments without departing from the principles of the disclosure. These and other changes in the preferred embodiments of the disclosure will be apparent to those skilled in the art from the disclosure herein, whereby it is to be distinctly understood that the foregoing descriptive matter to be implemented merely as illustrative of the disclosure and not as limitation.

ADVANTAGES OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE
[0076]	The present disclosure provides a home assistance system that enables wearable visual and haptic notifications for recognized and unrecognized visitors and environmental events, thereby enabling a hearing or speech impaired user to receive timely event notifications without relying on auditory perception.
[0077]	The present disclosure enables silent communication with visitors through a visitor-facing display that presents predefined messages upon actuation of a user-actuatable input on the wearable device, thereby facilitating communication without speech.
[0078]	The present disclosure enables detection of environmental conditions exceeding a threshold and generation of corresponding haptic alerts through the wearable device, thereby providing environmental awareness to the user.

title: System and Method for Misalignment-Aware Wireless EV Charging Analysis
abstract:
ABSTRACT
System and Method for Misalignment-Aware Wireless EV Charging Analysis
The present invention relates to a misalignment-aware wireless electric vehicle charging system and method for improving inductive power transfer efficiency under lateral displacement conditions. The system comprises an alternating current power source (10), a high-frequency inverter (20), a Double-D transmitter coil assembly (30), a Double-D receiver coil assembly (40), a rectifier and power conditioning unit (50), a battery charging controller (60), ferrite backing structures (70), a misalignment detection module (80), a magnetic flux analysis module (90), a finite element magnetic modelling module (100), an electromagnetic validation module (110), a data processing module (120), and an intelligent predictive compensation controller (130). The invention determines magnetic flux asymmetry by analysing magnetic flux density along multiple magnetic paths under aligned and laterally displaced conditions, validates electromagnetic characteristics through hybrid modelling, processes magnetic field information, and dynamically adjusts charging parameters to maintain efficient magnetic coupling. The invention provides improved charging efficiency, reduced magnetic leakage, enhanced operational reliability, and intelligent wireless charging suitable for electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
Figure-1
specification:
System and Method for Misalignment-Aware Wireless EV Charging Analysis

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates generally to wireless power transfer (WPT) systems for electric vehicles and, more particularly, to a system and method for analyzing, detecting, and compensating for lateral misalignment between transmitter and receiver Double-D coils through magnetic flux asymmetry evaluation. The invention further relates to electromagnetic simulation, wireless charging infrastructure, magnetic field analysis, and intelligent charging systems for enhancing power transfer efficiency and charging reliability under practical vehicle parking conditions.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Wireless power transfer technology has emerged as an attractive alternative to conventional plug-in charging systems for electric vehicles because it enables convenient, contactless, and automated charging. Inductive wireless charging systems generally comprise a primary transmitting coil embedded in the ground and a secondary receiving coil installed underneath the vehicle. During charging, alternating current supplied to the transmitting coil generates a magnetic field that induces electrical energy in the receiving coil through magnetic coupling. Despite significant technological advancements, the efficiency of such systems is highly dependent upon the geometric alignment between the transmitter and receiver coils.
In practical parking environments, perfect alignment is rarely achieved because of driver positioning errors, varying vehicle dimensions, environmental disturbances, and uneven parking surfaces. Even relatively small lateral displacement between the transmitting and receiving coils can significantly reduce mutual inductance, weaken magnetic coupling, increase leakage magnetic flux, reduce charging efficiency, generate localized heating, and adversely affect electromagnetic compatibility. Consequently, reliable wireless charging under real-world misalignment conditions remains one of the major engineering challenges in electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
Among the available coil geometries, Double-D (DD) coils have demonstrated superior magnetic coupling characteristics compared to circular coils. However, existing charging systems primarily focus on optimizing coil geometry or resonance compensation while providing only limited understanding of magnetic flux redistribution caused by lateral misalignment. Most conventional approaches evaluate overall efficiency degradation without analyzing magnetic flux asymmetry along multiple magnetic paths. Furthermore, existing evaluation techniques generally rely upon expensive electromagnetic simulation platforms without incorporating computationally efficient preliminary analysis methods capable of reducing design cost and development time.
A representative prior art reference is Budhia et al., "Wireless Power Transfer for EV Charging" (2013), which discusses wireless power transfer architectures for electric vehicles and coil design considerations. However, the disclosed system mainly addresses general wireless charging principles and provides limited investigation into magnetic flux asymmetry occurring during receiver misalignment. It neither performs path-wise magnetic flux evaluation nor proposes a hybrid validation methodology for accurately characterizing asymmetric magnetic behavior.
Additional literature, including the Double-D coil structure proposed by Covic and Boys (2015), studies on misalignment analysis by Zhang et al. (2018), and finite element simulation approaches by Kim et al. (2020), individually investigate coil configurations or simulation methodologies. Nevertheless, these references fail to provide an integrated framework capable of evaluating magnetic flux asymmetry using multiple magnetic paths together with multi-tool electromagnetic validation under varying misalignment conditions.
Accordingly, there exists a need for an improved wireless charging system capable of accurately evaluating magnetic coupling degradation caused by misalignment while providing a practical, reliable, and computationally efficient analysis framework suitable for future adaptive charging systems.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides a system and corresponding method for performing misalignment-aware wireless charging analysis for electric vehicles using a Double-D coil architecture and magnetic flux asymmetry evaluation. The invention is configured to improve the understanding of magnetic coupling behavior when lateral displacement occurs between transmitting and receiving coils during wireless charging. Rather than merely measuring charging efficiency degradation, the invention performs detailed magnetic flux distribution analysis over multiple predefined magnetic paths, thereby enabling accurate characterization of asymmetric magnetic field behavior responsible for reduced power transfer efficiency.
The proposed system comprises a Double-D transmitting coil, a corresponding Double-D receiving coil, ferrite backing structures, an alternating current excitation module, a finite element magnetic modeling engine, an electromagnetic validation engine, a magnetic flux extraction module, a data processing engine, and an analytical comparison module. The transmitter generates an alternating magnetic field that is coupled to the receiver through inductive power transfer. The system is configured to simulate multiple receiver positions corresponding to aligned and laterally displaced conditions, including predefined offsets of 0 mm, 50 mm, 100 mm, and 150 mm. During each operating condition, magnetic flux density is measured independently along left-side, right-side, and central magnetic paths for evaluating magnetic coupling asymmetry.
The invention further introduces a hybrid electromagnetic validation framework in which preliminary magnetic field calculations are performed using FEMM software while high-fidelity verification is carried out using ANSYS Maxwell simulations. This dual-platform validation significantly improves confidence in the obtained magnetic field characteristics while simultaneously reducing overall computational effort during the design stage. Simulation outputs from both environments are subsequently processed through a graphical analysis module that normalizes magnetic flux values, generates comparative plots, determines coupling variation, and quantifies magnetic asymmetry characteristics across different displacement conditions.
Unlike conventional wireless charging systems that primarily analyze global efficiency or mutual inductance, the present invention continuously evaluates spatial magnetic flux imbalance along multiple observation paths. Such analysis enables early identification of asymmetric magnetic behavior that precedes severe charging degradation. The analyzed information can further serve as an input for adaptive compensation mechanisms, intelligent alignment assistance, and predictive charging control algorithms.
The present invention may further incorporate an AI-based predictive misalignment compensation engine configured to learn historical magnetic flux asymmetry patterns under different environmental and vehicle operating conditions. The predictive engine estimates impending misalignment before significant efficiency degradation occurs and dynamically recommends transmitter excitation adjustment, operating frequency tuning, or vehicle repositioning guidance. By combining real-time magnetic flux asymmetry analysis with machine learning-based predictive compensation, the system transforms conventional passive monitoring into an intelligent self-optimizing wireless charging platform capable of maintaining high charging efficiency even under dynamic parking conditions. This feature substantially enhances charging robustness, reduces energy loss, minimizes electromagnetic leakage, and provides a scalable foundation for next-generation autonomous electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
Overall, the invention provides an integrated system and method that combines electromagnetic modeling, multi-path magnetic flux analysis, hybrid simulation validation, and intelligent predictive control into a unified wireless charging platform offering superior reliability, improved charging efficiency, enhanced diagnostic capability, and reduced computational cost compared to existing technologies.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
Figure 1 illustrates a block diagram of the proposed misalignment-aware wireless electric vehicle charging system. The figure depicts an AC power source (10), a high-frequency inverter (20), a Double-D transmitter coil assembly (30), a Double-D receiver coil assembly (40), a rectifier and power conditioning unit (50), a battery charging controller (60), ferrite backing structures (70), a misalignment detection module (80), a magnetic flux analysis module (90), a finite element magnetic modelling module (100), an electromagnetic validation module (110), a data processing module (120), and an intelligent predictive compensation controller (130). The arrangement illustrates the interaction among the electrical hardware, magnetic coupling path, simulation-assisted analysis modules, and intelligent control mechanism for maintaining efficient wireless charging under aligned as well as laterally misaligned operating conditions.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to a system and method for misalignment-aware wireless charging of electric vehicles using a Double-D coil architecture integrated with magnetic flux asymmetry analysis and intelligent compensation. More particularly, the invention provides a complete hardware and analytical platform capable of evaluating, monitoring, validating, and compensating for magnetic coupling degradation occurring due to lateral displacement between a transmitting charging pad and a receiving vehicle-mounted charging pad. The invention is especially suitable for static wireless charging stations installed in residential garages, commercial parking facilities, public charging stations, fleet depots, and autonomous vehicle charging infrastructures where perfect alignment between the transmitter and receiver cannot always be guaranteed.
Referring to Figure 1, the system receives electrical energy from an alternating current power source (10). The AC power source may be a conventional single-phase or three-phase utility supply capable of delivering electrical energy to the wireless charging platform. The incoming electrical power is supplied to a high-frequency inverter (20). The high-frequency inverter converts the input utility frequency into a high-frequency alternating waveform suitable for inductive wireless power transfer. The inverter may include insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), silicon carbide switching devices, gallium nitride semiconductor switches, gate driver circuits, resonant capacitors, voltage sensing circuits, current sensing circuits, protection circuitry, switching controllers, and associated power electronic components required for efficient high-frequency excitation.
The output of the inverter (20) energizes the Double-D transmitter coil assembly (30). The transmitter coil is fabricated using high-conductivity copper windings arranged in a Double-D configuration. The geometry provides improved magnetic field uniformity and enhanced coupling compared to conventional circular coils. The transmitter coil is mounted above ferrite backing structures (70) which guide, concentrate, and confine magnetic flux toward the receiver side while simultaneously minimizing magnetic leakage into surrounding regions. The ferrite backing may consist of segmented ferrite tiles, ferrite plates, ferrite laminations, or equivalent magnetic materials possessing high permeability and low core losses at the selected operating frequency.
Positioned above the transmitter assembly is the Double-D receiver coil assembly (40), which is mounted beneath the electric vehicle chassis. Similar to the transmitter, the receiver comprises copper windings arranged in a complementary Double-D geometry that maximizes magnetic coupling during wireless charging. The receiver coil converts the alternating magnetic field into induced electrical energy through electromagnetic induction. The induced alternating voltage is delivered to the rectifier and power conditioning unit (50), where the received power is converted into regulated direct current suitable for battery charging.
The rectifier and power conditioning unit (50) may include bridge rectifiers, synchronous rectification circuits, smoothing capacitors, inductors, voltage regulators, DC-DC converters, filtering circuits, protection devices, current limiters, thermal sensors, and isolation components. The regulated output is subsequently delivered to the battery charging controller (60). The charging controller supervises battery charging according to the battery management system requirements, monitors charging voltage, charging current, battery temperature, state-of-charge, charging profiles, safety thresholds, and communication with the vehicle battery management system. The controller may employ constant-current charging, constant-voltage charging, adaptive charging algorithms, or programmable charging protocols depending upon battery chemistry and manufacturer specifications.
Unlike conventional wireless charging systems, the present invention continuously evaluates magnetic field behaviour during charging. The magnetic interaction region existing between the transmitter coil (30) and receiver coil (40) is monitored by the misalignment detection module (80). The misalignment detection module determines the relative positional relationship between the transmitting and receiving coils. The module may receive position information from magnetic field sensors, Hall-effect sensors, flux sensors, displacement sensors, optical sensors, proximity sensors, inductive sensors, ultrasonic ranging devices, infrared distance sensors, camera-based position estimation systems, or combinations thereof. In certain embodiments, the module derives misalignment directly from measured magnetic field asymmetry without requiring additional physical position sensors.
The detected positional information is forwarded to the magnetic flux analysis module (90). The magnetic flux analysis module constitutes one of the principal innovations of the present invention. Rather than merely calculating total transferred power, the module separately evaluates magnetic flux density along multiple predefined observation paths including a central magnetic path, a left-side magnetic path, and a right-side magnetic path. Independent evaluation of these magnetic paths enables the system to identify asymmetric magnetic field behaviour that develops as lateral displacement increases between the transmitter and receiver. By continuously calculating left-path flux density, right-path flux density, centre-path magnetic intensity, flux imbalance ratio, coupling coefficient variation, and field distribution characteristics, the module accurately identifies degradation in magnetic coupling before substantial charging efficiency loss occurs.
The magnetic flux analysis module communicates with the finite element magnetic modelling module (100). This module performs rapid electromagnetic analysis using finite element magnetic modelling techniques. The modelling engine generates magnetic field contours, magnetic vector distributions, magnetic flux density plots, leakage flux distributions, and coupling coefficient estimates under various alignment conditions. Finite element analysis enables fast preliminary evaluation of electromagnetic behaviour while reducing computational complexity during system design and optimisation.
Outputs from the finite element magnetic modelling module are validated using the electromagnetic validation module (110). The validation module performs high-fidelity electromagnetic simulations using a three-dimensional electromagnetic solver. The validation process confirms magnetic flux density values, coupling coefficients, leakage fields, eddy current effects, field distribution uniformity, and power transfer characteristics predicted by the preliminary finite element model. Dual-stage electromagnetic verification substantially improves reliability of the calculated results and provides confidence in the analysed magnetic behaviour before deployment into commercial charging systems. This hybrid evaluation methodology combines computational efficiency with highly accurate electromagnetic validation, thereby overcoming limitations associated with using only a single simulation environment. The invention disclosure itself describes combining FEMM-based preliminary analysis with ANSYS Maxwell validation for multi-condition magnetic flux assessment.
Validated simulation results together with experimentally acquired magnetic field measurements are transferred to the data processing module (120). The data processing module performs numerical processing, normalization, statistical comparison, graphical interpretation, feature extraction, trend identification, coupling analysis, magnetic asymmetry quantification, efficiency estimation, and storage of historical operating parameters. The module may include one or more microprocessors, digital signal processors, field programmable gate arrays, embedded controllers, industrial computers, memory devices, communication interfaces, and software routines configured to execute mathematical algorithms for electromagnetic analysis. Data collected over multiple charging cycles are archived to establish historical charging behaviour under varying parking positions.
An intelligent predictive compensation controller (130) receives processed data from the data processing module. The predictive compensation controller represents an advanced enhancement incorporated into the present invention. The controller executes artificial intelligence or machine learning algorithms trained using historical charging data, magnetic flux distributions, coupling coefficients, environmental conditions, and parking position variations. The controller predicts impending efficiency degradation before significant power loss occurs and dynamically determines corrective actions. Such corrective actions may include adjusting inverter switching frequency, modifying resonant operating conditions, altering compensation capacitor tuning, recommending vehicle repositioning, issuing alignment guidance to the vehicle operator, or communicating alignment instructions to an autonomous parking controller. Consequently, the charging process remains highly efficient despite unavoidable parking inaccuracies encountered during practical operation.
During actual operation, an electric vehicle enters a designated wireless charging bay and parks above the embedded charging pad. The transmitter coil (30) remains inactive until communication between the charging controller (60) and vehicle battery management system confirms charging authorization. After authorization, the inverter (20) begins producing high-frequency alternating current that energizes the transmitter coil. The resulting alternating magnetic field couples inductively with the receiver coil (40), inducing electrical energy that is subsequently rectified and supplied to the vehicle battery.
If the vehicle is perfectly centred above the charging pad, magnetic flux distribution remains substantially symmetrical. The magnetic flux analysis module (90) measures nearly identical magnetic field intensities along the left, centre, and right observation paths. Consequently, the predictive compensation controller maintains nominal operating parameters because coupling efficiency remains close to optimum.
However, if the vehicle is parked with a lateral offset, for example approximately one hundred millimetres toward the driver's side, the magnetic field distribution changes significantly. The left observation path experiences higher magnetic flux density while the right observation path exhibits reduced magnetic intensity. The magnetic asymmetry module immediately identifies this imbalance and determines that coupling efficiency is decreasing. The finite element module (100) rapidly estimates the new magnetic field distribution while the validation module (110) confirms expected electromagnetic behaviour. Processed results are delivered to the predictive compensation controller (130), which automatically adjusts inverter operating frequency and recommends slight vehicle repositioning through the charging interface. In autonomous vehicles, the controller may communicate directly with the parking control system to reposition the vehicle until optimum alignment is achieved. Once repositioning occurs, magnetic symmetry is restored, coupling coefficient increases, leakage magnetic field decreases, and charging efficiency returns to its optimum operating condition.
As another practical example, consider a public parking facility where electric taxis repeatedly occupy charging stations throughout the day. Different drivers consistently park their vehicles with varying positional accuracy. Conventional wireless charging stations experience inconsistent charging efficiency because transmitter and receiver coils rarely remain perfectly aligned. In contrast, the present invention continuously evaluates magnetic flux asymmetry during every charging session. Historical parking data stored within the data processing module enable the predictive controller to anticipate common parking patterns for each charging location. Consequently, the controller proactively adjusts operating parameters even before significant efficiency degradation develops, thereby maintaining substantially uniform charging performance across thousands of charging cycles without requiring expensive mechanical alignment mechanisms.
The invention further supports remote monitoring, cloud-based diagnostic analysis, fleet management integration, predictive maintenance, and software-based performance optimisation. Communication interfaces incorporated within the charging controller permit exchange of charging statistics, magnetic field measurements, operational status, fault information, maintenance alerts, and predictive analytics with external supervisory control systems. Such capabilities make the invention particularly suitable for intelligent transportation infrastructure, smart cities, automated parking facilities, commercial fleet charging networks, logistics centres, airport parking systems, bus depots, and future autonomous electric mobility ecosystems.
Accordingly, the disclosed system integrates electrical hardware, magnetic components, electromagnetic modelling, simulation validation, intelligent signal processing, predictive control, and adaptive charging strategies into a unified wireless charging platform capable of delivering stable, reliable, efficient, and intelligent wireless energy transfer even under significant lateral misalignment conditions. The invention therefore provides substantial improvements in charging efficiency, magnetic coupling stability, operational reliability, scalability, computational accuracy, and real-world applicability compared with conventional wireless charging technologies that merely rely upon passive inductive coupling without comprehensive magnetic flux asymmetry evaluation or predictive compensation.:::
ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
1.	The invention provides improved wireless power transfer efficiency by continuously detecting magnetic flux asymmetry and maintaining stable magnetic coupling between the Double-D transmitter coil and the Double-D receiver coil under lateral misalignment conditions.
2.	The invention reduces electromagnetic leakage and minimizes charging efficiency degradation by combining finite element magnetic modelling with high-fidelity electromagnetic validation for accurate analysis of magnetic field distribution.
3.	The invention enables intelligent predictive compensation by automatically identifying misalignment conditions and adjusting charging parameters, thereby improving charging reliability, operational safety, and battery charging performance.
4.	The invention provides a scalable wireless charging platform suitable for residential, commercial, and public electric vehicle charging infrastructures while reducing computational cost through hybrid electromagnetic analysis and validation.

title: Smart Sensorized Pen for Adaptive Handwriting Rehabilitation
abstract:
ABSTRACT
Smart Sensorized Pen for Adaptive Handwriting Rehabilitation
A smart assistive writing pen system (100) for handwriting rehabilitation is disclosed. The system comprises a motion sensing unit (102), a grip force sensor (104), an embedded microcontroller (106), an adaptive handwriting analysis engine (108), a user profile memory (110), a haptic driver (112), a vibration actuator (114), a wireless communication module (116) and a rechargeable power management unit (118). The system continuously acquires handwriting movement and grip behaviour, analyses handwriting characteristics using personalized rehabilitation profiles, detects handwriting abnormalities and generates real-time tactile corrective feedback to improve handwriting quality and motor coordination. The adaptive handwriting analysis engine dynamically updates rehabilitation parameters based on historical handwriting performance and further predicts rehabilitation progress for automatically adjusting correction sensitivity. The wireless communication module enables remote monitoring and long-term rehabilitation assessment.
