title: AN IOT-INTEGRATED WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORK SYSTEM FOR REAL-TIME ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND PREDICTIVE ALERT GENERATION
abstract: An internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network system for real-time environmental monitoring and predictive alert generation is disclosed. A wireless sensor network of plural sensor nodes is distributed over an environment, each node sensing environmental parameters, temperature, humidity, air quality, gas or pollutant concentration, water level or quality, soil condition, sound, or radiation, and communicating the data wirelessly, the nodes being inexpensive and energy-efficient. An internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement, comprising a low-power wide-area, mesh, or cellular network with routing and optional edge processing, conveys the data to a processing platform and aggregates it. The platform monitors the parameters in real time and applies a predictive model, comprising a machine learning model trained on historical data that captures the spatiotemporal patterns by which conditions develop, to predict a future environmental condition, an approaching hazardous condition, a threshold exceedance, or an event, with its location, time, and confidence, in advance and with a lead time sufficient for an anticipatory response. An alert generation arrangement then delivers a predictive alert by notification, dashboard, or actuation before the condition occurs, enabling anticipatory action to prevent, mitigate, or prepare, where conventional monitoring is sparse, delayed, and reactive.
specification:
The present invention relates generally to the field of environmental monitoring and internet-of-things sensing systems, and more particularly to an internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network system for real-time environmental monitoring and predictive alert generation. The invention lies at the confluence of wireless sensor network design, internet-of-things data aggregation and communication, real-time environmental parameter sensing, and the machine-learning-based prediction of environmental conditions and the generation of anticipatory alerts. Specifically, the invention pertains to a system comprising a wireless sensor network of a plurality of sensor nodes distributed over an environment to be monitored, each node sensing one or more environmental parameters comprising a temperature, a humidity, an air quality, a gas or pollutant concentration, a water level or quality, a soil condition, a sound, a radiation, or another environmental parameter, and communicating the sensed data wirelessly; an internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement that conveys the sensed data from the nodes to a processing platform and aggregates it; a processing platform that monitors the environmental parameters in real time and applies a predictive model to the aggregated and historical data to predict a future environmental condition, comprising an approaching hazardous condition, an exceedance of a threshold, or an environmental event; and an alert generation arrangement that generates and delivers, upon the prediction of such a condition, a predictive alert in advance of the condition, to a user or a system, so that anticipatory action may be taken; whereby the environment is monitored pervasively and in real time by the wireless sensor network integrated with the internet-of-things, and the hazardous or significant environmental conditions are predicted before they occur and alerted in advance, affording the anticipatory response that a mere real-time monitoring, alerting only upon the occurrence of a condition, does not.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The monitoring of the environment, comprising the sensing of the environmental parameters of a region, a facility, a habitat, or a process, is of great and growing importance for a wide range of purposes, comprising the protection of health and safety against environmental hazards, comprising the pollution, the toxic gases, the fires, the floods, and the extreme conditions; the management of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure that depend upon the environmental conditions; the protection of the environment and the monitoring of its quality; and the scientific study of the environment. The effective monitoring requires the pervasive sensing of the parameters over the environment, in real time, and, for the anticipation of the hazards and events, the prediction of the future conditions; and it is to such pervasive, real-time, and predictive environmental monitoring, by an internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network, that the present invention is directed, the deficiencies of the prior art, set forth hereinafter, constituting the problems it overcomes.
The conventional monitoring of the environment has relied upon means of limited coverage, limited timeliness, and no prediction, which the present invention overcomes. The conventional monitoring has employed sparse, fixed monitoring stations, comprising the few instrumented stations that monitor the environment of a region at their few locations; these stations are few and widely spaced, so that they sense the environment only at their few points, leaving the great extent of the environment between them unsensed, and do not afford the pervasive coverage that the monitoring of a spatially varying environment requires; and they are costly and cumbersome, limiting their number. The conventional monitoring has employed manual sampling and measurement, in which samples are collected and measured periodically; this is laborious, infrequent, and delayed, sensing the environment only at the times of sampling and affording no real-time or continuous monitoring. And the conventional monitoring is, in the main, reactive, sensing and reporting the environmental conditions as they are and alerting upon the occurrence of a hazardous condition, but not predicting the future conditions and alerting in advance; so that the hazard is alerted only when it has occurred, when it may be too late for the effective anticipatory response, rather than predicted and alerted before it occurs.
The advent of the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things offers the means to the pervasive and real-time monitoring that the conventional means lack, for a wireless sensor network of numerous, inexpensive, wirelessly communicating sensor nodes may be distributed pervasively over the environment to sense it at many points and in detail, and the internet-of-things may convey and aggregate the data of the nodes in real time; affording the pervasive, detailed, real-time sensing of the environment that the sparse stations and the manual sampling do not. The mere pervasive real-time sensing, however, does not by itself afford the prediction of the future conditions and the anticipatory alerting, which require, beyond the sensing, the application of a predictive model to the sensed and historical data to predict the future conditions and the generation of the alerts in advance; and the prior art has not, in the main, provided the specific integrated system, sensing pervasively by the wireless sensor network, aggregating by the internet-of-things, and predicting the future conditions and generating the predictive alerts, that the present invention provides. The prior art comprises the wireless sensor networks and internet-of-things systems that monitor the environment in real time but do not predict and alert in advance, alerting only reactively upon the occurrence of a condition; and the environmental prediction methods that predict conditions but are not integrated with the pervasive real-time sensing network and the alerting. The integration of the pervasive real-time wireless sensor sensing, the internet-of-things aggregation, and the predictive modelling and anticipatory alerting, into a single system, is the specific advance the prior art lacks and the present invention provides.
The technical challenges to such a system are several and interlocking. The environmental parameters must be sensed pervasively over the environment by the plurality of sensor nodes, each sensing its parameters accurately and reliably, and communicating the data wirelessly, at the scale of the network and within the constraints of the sensor nodes, comprising their limited power, which requires the energy-efficient sensing and communication, and their limited cost, which requires the inexpensive nodes. The sensed data must be conveyed from the nodes to the processing platform and aggregated, by the internet-of-things communication arrangement, reliably and in real time, over the wireless network, which requires the appropriate network architecture and protocols suited to the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things, comprising the routing of the data through the network to the platform. The processing platform must monitor the parameters in real time and apply the predictive model to predict the future conditions, the model predicting, from the current, recent, and historical data of the parameters, the approaching hazardous conditions, the exceedances, and the events, with a lead time sufficient for the anticipatory response, which requires the appropriate predictive modelling of the environmental data, comprising the spatiotemporal modelling of the parameters that vary over the environment and over time. And the alerts must be generated and delivered in advance of the predicted conditions, to the users or systems that must respond, effectively and in time. The prior art has not met these challenges in the integrated combination that a pervasive, real-time, and predictive environmental monitoring system requires, and that the present invention provides.
The need for the invention is accordingly clear. The monitoring of the environment is of great importance for safety, management, and protection; the conventional sparse stations and manual sampling do not afford the pervasive and real-time monitoring, and the conventional monitoring is reactive, alerting only upon the occurrence of a hazard; the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things afford the pervasive real-time sensing, but their mere sensing does not afford the prediction and the anticipatory alerting; and there is a pressing need for a system that senses the environment pervasively and in real time by a wireless sensor network integrated with the internet-of-things, and predicts the future conditions and generates predictive alerts in advance. There exists, therefore, a long-felt and unmet need for an internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network system for real-time environmental monitoring and predictive alert generation, sensing the environment pervasively, aggregating by the internet-of-things, monitoring in real time, predicting the future conditions, and generating anticipatory alerts; and the present invention fulfills this need.
It is to be observed that the invention resides not in wireless sensor networks, the internet-of-things, or environmental sensing individually, all of which are known, but in the specific integrated system wherein a wireless sensor network of a plurality of nodes senses the environmental parameters pervasively and in real time, an internet-of-things arrangement conveys and aggregates the sensed data, and a processing platform monitors the parameters in real time and applies a predictive model to predict a future environmental condition and generates a predictive alert in advance of the condition; and in the integration and cooperation of the pervasive real-time sensing, the aggregation, and the prediction and anticipatory alerting, so that the hazardous conditions are predicted and alerted before they occur, which a mere real-time monitoring does not. It is this specific integrated combination, uniting the pervasive real-time wireless sensing with the predictive anticipatory alerting, and directed to the concrete technical problem of monitoring and anticipating the conditions of a physical environment and producing a concrete result in the anticipatory response thereto, that the prior art neither discloses nor renders obvious.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present invention overcomes the aforementioned deficiencies of the prior art by providing an internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network system for real-time environmental monitoring and predictive alert generation. It is a principal object of the invention to monitor an environment pervasively and in real time by a wireless sensor network integrated with the internet-of-things, and to predict a future environmental condition and generate a predictive alert in advance of the condition, so that anticipatory action may be taken.
In accordance with a first aspect of the invention, there is provided a system comprising a wireless sensor network of a plurality of sensor nodes distributed over an environment, each node configured to sense an environmental parameter comprising one or more of a temperature, a humidity, an air quality, a gas or pollutant concentration, a water level or quality, a soil condition, a sound, and a radiation, and to communicate the sensed data wirelessly; an internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement configured to convey the sensed data from the nodes to a processing platform and to aggregate the sensed data; a processing platform configured to monitor the environmental parameters in real time and to apply a predictive model to the aggregated and historical data to predict a future environmental condition; and an alert generation arrangement configured to generate and deliver, upon the prediction of the future environmental condition, a predictive alert in advance of the condition.
In accordance with a second aspect of the invention, and constituting a principal feature, the predictive model is configured to predict the future environmental condition comprising an approaching hazardous condition, an exceedance of a threshold by an environmental parameter, or an environmental event, from a current, a recent, and a historical data of the environmental parameters, with a lead time sufficient for an anticipatory response, whereby the hazardous or significant condition is predicted before it occurs and the predictive alert is generated in advance, in contrast to a reactive alert generated only upon an occurrence of the condition.
In accordance with a third aspect of the invention, the predictive model comprises a machine learning model trained upon historical data of the environmental parameters and the conditions or events, configured to capture a spatiotemporal pattern by which a condition develops over the environment and over time, and to predict the future condition and its location and time from the pattern of the sensed parameters; and the model is retrainable upon accumulating data so that the prediction adapts to the environment.
In accordance with a fourth aspect of the invention, each sensor node comprises a sensing means, a wireless communication means, and a power means, and is configured for an energy-efficient operation, and the internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement comprises a network architecture and protocol suited to the wireless sensor network, comprising a routing of the sensed data through the network to the processing platform, and in embodiments an edge processing at or near the nodes; and the alert generation arrangement delivers the predictive alert to a user or a system through a notification, a dashboard, or an actuation.
In accordance with further aspects of the invention, the processing platform comprises a cloud or an edge platform, and the system is applied to a monitoring of an environment comprising an urban, an industrial, an agricultural, a natural, or a domestic environment; and there is provided a method of operating the system. The invention thereby provides substantial advantages over the prior art, comprising the pervasive and real-time monitoring of the environment by the wireless sensor network, where the conventional stations are sparse and the sampling delayed; the aggregation and processing by the internet-of-things at the scale of the network; the prediction of the future hazardous and significant conditions before they occur, and the generation of predictive alerts in advance, enabling the anticipatory response, where the conventional monitoring is reactive; the spatiotemporal predictive modelling capturing the development of the conditions over the environment and time; and the consequent effective anticipatory monitoring and protection against environmental hazards and events.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The present invention provides an internet-of-things-integrated wireless sensor network system comprising, in an exemplary embodiment, a wireless sensor network of a plurality of sensor nodes, an internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement, a processing platform with a real-time monitoring and a predictive model, and an alert generation arrangement, together with a method of operation.
The wireless sensor network comprises the plurality of sensor nodes distributed over the environment to be monitored, disposed so as to sense the environment pervasively, at many points over its extent. Each node senses one or more environmental parameters, comprising the temperature, the humidity, the air quality, the gas or pollutant concentration, the water level or quality, the soil condition, the sound, the radiation, or another parameter relevant to the monitoring, by the sensing means of the node; and communicates the sensed data wirelessly, by the wireless communication means, toward the processing platform. The nodes are inexpensive and energy-efficient, so that they may be deployed in the numbers required for the pervasive coverage and operate on their limited power.
The internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement conveys the sensed data from the nodes to the processing platform and aggregates it. The data of the many nodes is conveyed, by the wireless network, comprising the routing of the data through the network of nodes and gateways to the platform, reliably and in real time; and it is aggregated at the platform into the picture of the environment across the network. The arrangement employs the network architecture and protocols suited to the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things, and in embodiments an edge processing at or near the nodes, reducing the data conveyed and the latency.
The processing platform monitors the environmental parameters in real time and predicts the future conditions. It monitors the parameters, aggregated from the nodes, in real time, affording the real-time picture of the environment; and it applies a predictive model to the aggregated and historical data to predict a future environmental condition, comprising an approaching hazardous condition, an exceedance of a threshold, or an environmental event. The predictive model, in embodiments a machine learning model trained upon the historical data, has learned the spatiotemporal patterns by which the conditions develop over the environment and over time, and predicts, from the pattern of the sensed parameters, the future condition, its location, and its time, with a lead time sufficient for the anticipatory response; so that the hazardous or significant condition is predicted before it occurs.
The alert generation arrangement generates and delivers, upon the prediction of a future condition, a predictive alert in advance of the condition, to the user or the system that must respond, by a notification, a dashboard, an actuation, or another means; so that the user or system is warned of the approaching condition before it occurs and may take the anticipatory action to prevent, mitigate, or prepare for it, which the reactive alerting, warning only upon the occurrence, does not afford. The system thereby monitors the environment pervasively and in real time and predicts and alerts the hazardous and significant conditions in advance, affording the anticipatory monitoring and protection that the conventional sparse, delayed, and reactive monitoring does not; applied, in embodiments, to the urban, industrial, agricultural, natural, and domestic environments and their hazards and events.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The following detailed description sets forth exemplary and preferred embodiments of the invention. It is to be understood that the embodiments described are illustrative and not restrictive, and that the invention may be practiced with variations, substitutions, and combinations of the features described, with such nodes, networks, platforms, models, and applications as a person skilled in the art may select in accordance with the principles herein set forth.
The wireless sensor network, in a preferred embodiment, comprises the plurality of sensor nodes distributed over the environment to be monitored, the nodes being disposed at the points and in the density required to sense the environment pervasively and with the spatial resolution the monitoring requires, over the extent of the environment, whether a region, a facility, a field, a habitat, or a building. Each sensor node, in a preferred embodiment, comprises a sensing means, comprising one or more sensors that sense the environmental parameters the node is to monitor, comprising a temperature sensor, a humidity sensor, an air-quality or gas sensor sensing a pollutant or gas concentration comprising a carbon monoxide, a carbon dioxide, a methane, a particulate matter, or another, a water-level or water-quality sensor, a soil-moisture or soil-condition sensor, a sound sensor, a radiation sensor, or another environmental sensor, according to the parameters to be monitored; a processing means that acquires and processes the sensed signals; a wireless communication means that communicates the sensed data wirelessly; and a power means, comprising a battery and, in embodiments, an energy-harvesting means, comprising a solar cell, that powers the node. The node is, in a preferred embodiment, configured for the energy-efficient operation that its limited power requires, comprising the low-power sensing, processing, and communication and the duty-cycling of the node, so that the node operates for a long period on its power; and it is inexpensive, so that the numbers required for the pervasive coverage may be deployed.
The internet-of-things communication and aggregation arrangement, in a preferred embodiment, conveys the sensed data from the nodes to the processing platform and aggregates it. The nodes communicate their sensed data wirelessly, in a preferred embodiment by a wireless communication technology suited to the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things, comprising a low-power wide-area network technology, comprising LoRa or a narrowband internet-of-things, suited to the long range and low power of the distributed nodes, a mesh network technology, comprising Zigbee or a like technology, in which the nodes relay one another's data through the network, a cellular technology, or another suited technology; the data being conveyed from the nodes, in embodiments through the gateways that connect the sensor network to the wider network and the platform, and in embodiments routed through the mesh of nodes to the gateways, to the processing platform. The arrangement employs the network architecture and protocols suited to the wireless sensor network and the internet-of-things, comprising the routing, the addressing, and the management of the network of many nodes; and in embodiments it performs an edge processing at or near the nodes or the gateways, comprising the pre-processing, filtering, or summarizing of the data, reducing the data conveyed and the latency and the power. The arrangement aggregates the data of the many nodes at the platform into the aggregated representation of the environment across the network, associating the data with the nodes and the locations and times to which it pertains.
The processing platform, in a preferred embodiment, receives and aggregates the sensed data and monitors the parameters in real time and applies the predictive model. The platform comprises, in embodiments, a cloud platform, an edge platform, or a combination, providing the ingestion, storage, and computation for the data of the network. It monitors the environmental parameters, aggregated from the nodes, in real time, comprising the tracking of the current values of the parameters across the environment, the detection of the current exceedances and conditions, and the presentation of the real-time picture of the environment; affording the real-time monitoring. And it applies the predictive model to the aggregated and historical data to predict the future conditions, as described.
The predictive model, in a preferred embodiment and as a principal feature of the invention, predicts the future environmental condition from the data. The model, in a preferred embodiment, is a machine learning model trained upon the historical data of the environmental parameters and the conditions or events that occurred, from which it has learned the spatiotemporal patterns by which the conditions develop, how the parameters, evolving over the environment and over time, lead to the hazardous conditions, the exceedances, and the events; and it applies this learning to the current, recent, and historical data of the sensed parameters to predict the future condition, comprising the prediction of an approaching hazardous condition, comprising a dangerous concentration of a pollutant or gas, a fire, a flood, or an extreme condition; an exceedance of a threshold by a parameter, comprising the prediction that a parameter will exceed a safe or a significant threshold; or an environmental event; together with, in embodiments, the location and the time of the predicted condition, and a measure of confidence. The model is, in embodiments, of a kind suited to the spatiotemporal prediction of the environmental data, comprising a time-series model, a recurrent or long short-term memory network capturing the temporal evolution, a spatial or graph model capturing the spatial structure of the network and the environment, a combination capturing both, or another model; and it predicts with a lead time sufficient for the anticipatory response, comprising a lead time of minutes, hours, or longer according to the condition and the application, so that the response may be taken before the condition occurs. The model is retrained, in a preferred embodiment, upon the accumulating data, so that it adapts to the environment and improves its prediction over time.
The alert generation arrangement, in a preferred embodiment and as the feature by which the prediction produces its effect, generates and delivers, upon the prediction of a future condition, a predictive alert in advance of the condition. Upon the model's prediction of a future hazardous or significant condition, the arrangement generates an alert, comprising the identification of the predicted condition, its predicted location and time, and its confidence, and delivers it, in advance of the condition, to the user or the system that must respond, by a notification, comprising a message, an alarm, or a signal to the responsible persons; a dashboard, presenting the prediction and the alert to the monitoring operators; or an actuation, comprising the automatic initiation of a response system, comprising a ventilation, a barrier, a suppression, or a shutdown, according to the condition and the application; so that the user or system is warned of the approaching condition before it occurs and takes, or the system effects, the anticipatory action to prevent, mitigate, or prepare for the condition. The predictive alert, in advance of the condition, affords the anticipatory response that the reactive alert, warning only upon the occurrence of the condition, does not; the difference being decisive where the anticipatory response can prevent or greatly mitigate the harm that the condition, once occurred, would cause.
The system operates, in a preferred embodiment, as a continuous real-time loop: the nodes sense the environment and communicate the data; the internet-of-things arrangement conveys and aggregates it; the platform monitors the parameters in real time and predicts the future conditions; and the alert generation arrangement alerts the predicted conditions in advance; the loop repeating continuously as the environment evolves, the monitoring, prediction, and alerting being continual. In an exemplary operation according to a preferred embodiment, the system monitors the air quality of an industrial or urban area: the nodes, distributed over the area, sense the concentrations of the pollutants and gases and the meteorological parameters, and communicate the data through the low-power network to the platform; the platform monitors the air quality in real time and applies the predictive model, which, from the pattern of the rising concentrations and the meteorological conditions, predicts that a dangerous concentration of a pollutant will develop at a location within the coming period; and the alert generation arrangement, upon the prediction, alerts the authorities and the affected persons in advance, and in embodiments actuates a mitigation, so that the anticipatory action is taken before the dangerous concentration occurs, protecting the persons, which a reactive monitoring, alerting only upon the occurrence of the dangerous concentration, would not have afforded in time. In further embodiments the system monitors and predicts other environmental parameters and conditions, comprising the floods from the water levels and rainfall, the fires from the temperature and gases, the agricultural conditions from the soil and weather, and others, in the urban, industrial, agricultural, natural, and domestic environments.
It will be appreciated by persons skilled in the art that numerous variations and modifications may be made to the described embodiments without departing from the scope of the invention. The particular sensor nodes and parameters, wireless and internet-of-things communication and aggregation, processing platform, predictive model, and alert generation described are illustrative, and equivalents and alternatives thereto may be substituted, and the specific nodes, network, model, and alerts are to be selected and configured for a given environment and application. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features of another. The invention accordingly is not limited to the specific embodiments described, but embraces all such variations, modifications, and equivalents as fall within the spirit and scope of the appended claims.

title: AUTOMATIC PREMISES STATE DETERMINATION SYSTEM FOR COORDINATED PUBLIC STATUS AND PRIVATE SECURITY OPERATIONS
abstract:
A system (100) for premises monitoring determines a governing operative premises state from predetermined conditions, alone or with sensor data from premises sensors (110) or premises-associated input data through an interface (112). A state exclusivity core (116) maintains exactly one governing condition of a defined set including accessible and secured conditions, and a state continuity core (118) preserves continuity. A state-integrity arrangement confines establishment or modification of a controlled state representation to a validated automatic state-determination pathway. The same governing state controls a public-status output, comprising a human-perceptible indication through a public status indicator (126) or a machine-readable representation for downstream rendering, and a security operation performed by a module (128), reducing divergence between public and security states. Human-associated input does not directly establish a transition outside evaluation according to the predetermined conditions.

specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention generally relates to premises monitoring and security coordination systems, and more particularly relates to a system, a method, a controller, and a kit of parts for automatically determining a governing operative premises state of a premises from evaluation of one or more predetermined conditions, and for coordinating a public-status output and a private-security operation from that single governing operative premises state, in accordance with an aspect of the present disclosure.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Conventional premises monitoring and security arrangements generally employ separate systems for indicating whether a premises is open or closed and for performing security-related operations. Public-facing status information is commonly provided through manually operated signs, fixed electronic displays, websites, or mobile applications, while security functions are independently controlled through alarm panels, access-control systems, surveillance systems, or manually operated arming and disarming interfaces.
Manual signs require an authorised person to physically change the displayed status whenever the operating condition of the premises changes. Such arrangements are dependent on human intervention and may remain unchanged due to oversight, delay, absence of personnel, or operational error. Consequently, a premises may be displayed as accessible even after closure, or may be displayed as secured despite being operational.
Fixed timer-based and schedule-based systems may automatically change a public status indication according to a stored schedule. However, such systems are generally unable to account for unscheduled closures, extended working hours, public holidays, emergency shutdowns, staff absence, equipment failure, power interruptions, or other real-time operating conditions unless the stored schedule is manually updated. A transition generated merely by execution of a stored target-state instruction upon expiry of an elapsed duration or occurrence of a stored clock value may therefore reflect an assumption about the premises rather than a determination from contemporaneous evaluation of its actual operating condition.
Existing security systems commonly rely on human-originated commands, such as keypad entries, access cards, key fobs, physical switches, or mobile-application commands, to arm or disarm the security system. Such a command directly establishes the security state without evaluating whether the actual operational condition of the premises corresponds to the selected state. Certain systems additionally permit an authorised security-system user to activate an automatic or scheduled mode, after which the system executes a previously stored operator-selected target state at a specified time. In each case the state adopted by the system originates in a human selection of that state, and the machine acts as an executor of that selection rather than as a determiner of the condition of the premises. This may result in incorrect arming or disarming caused by accidental input, delayed action, unauthorised operation, stale stored selections, or inconsistent operator practices.
Certain premises monitoring systems employ sensors to infer occupancy, activity, or operational status. However, individual sensor signals may be affected by noise, transient environmental changes, false detections, sensor failure, communication delay, or incomplete data. For example, a temporary loss of motion, a fluctuation in lighting, or an isolated door-opening event may incorrectly cause a change in the inferred premises status.
Further, in conventional installations, a public-status subsystem and a private-security subsystem may maintain separate state values and independently determine their respective operating conditions. Differences in configuration, asynchronous updates, network latency, sensor processing, or software execution may cause the public-status subsystem and the security subsystem to represent conflicting premises conditions.
Such conflicting representations may create a shadow-state condition in which an independently determined security state remains inconsistent with the public-facing condition, for example by responding as a secured state while the public-facing condition is accessible. Conversely, the public-facing system may indicate that the premises is secured while the security system operates in an accessible or disarmed mode. These inconsistencies may lead to false alarms, missed security events, unauthorised access, incorrect information being communicated to the public, and inefficient utilisation of security resources.
In addition, sensor-processing components, data-input interfaces, communication modules, and software services in conventional systems may have direct or indirect access to stored state information. An erroneous signal, compromised device, software fault, unauthorised write operation, or malformed message may therefore modify a premises-state value without passing through a controlled state-validation process.
Distributed and cloud-based premises systems may further maintain replicated or locally cached state values across multiple devices or services. Where such values are not consistently coordinated, communication failures, delayed synchronisation, service interruptions, or conflicting updates may cause different components to act according to different premises states.
Additionally, where public-facing status information is provided at all, it is commonly presented to an operator, administrator, or authorised security-system user through a monitoring console, an administrative dashboard, or an authenticated operator or administrative application session. Such presentation does not inform a member of the public who is seeking access to, or services from, the premises and who has no operator credentials.
Accordingly, there remains a need to address the problems associated with human-dependent status updates, execution of stored human-selected target states according to a schedule without contemporaneous state determination, sensor-induced false transitions, human-originated commands that establish a state without evaluation of the actual operating condition, independently maintained public and security states, unauthorised state modification, inconsistent state representations across local or distributed premises-monitoring systems, and the absence of reliable premises-status information addressed to persons seeking access to the premises.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
In an aspect of the present disclosure, a system (100) is provided for automatically determining an operative state or operative condition of a premises and for coordinating public-status and private-security operations based on that state or condition. The system (100) automatically determines a governing operative premises state from evaluation of one or more predetermined conditions, alone or in combination with sensor data or premises-associated input data, and uses that single governing operative premises state as a common causal control input for both a public-status output and at least one security operation.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the governing operative premises state is selected from a defined set comprising at least an accessible-associated condition, being an accessible state, and a secured-associated condition, being a secured state, and exactly one condition of the defined set is governing at a given time. The defined set is not limited to two members, and may further comprise an additional, intermediate, transitional, partial-access, restricted-access, maintenance-associated, availability-associated, or other operative condition.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, each automatically determined transition of the governing operative premises state during normal automatic operation is generated by contemporaneous evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions, without requiring, as a prerequisite for that transition, any human-originated authoritative state command or any human-originated authority-mode activation, whether occurring once or repeatedly. No such transition is caused by a human-originated authoritative state command that is sufficient, by itself and without outcome-determinative contemporaneous evaluation, to establish the resulting condition; a human-originated or human-associated input that identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set does not, by itself, cause such a transition where adoption of the candidate condition remains subject to such evaluation.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the system (100) may additionally provide one or more human-authority, manual-override, commissioning, installation, setup, activation, configuration, maintenance, diagnostic, or other operating modes. Assembly, installation, commissioning, activation, and setup are used herein interchangeably to denote actions or procedures performed to bring the system (100), or a kit of parts forming the system (100), into normal automatic operation. The presence, availability, or use of such a mode does not alter the characterisation of a transition occurring during normal automatic operation. Whether a particular transition is an automatically determined transition is determined by the causal mechanism producing that transition and not by the name or label assigned to the operating mode in which it occurs. A system that performs some transitions in response to human-originated authoritative state commands and performs other transitions by contemporaneous evaluation as described herein remains within the automatic architecture described herein with respect to the latter transitions, and the presence of the former does not remove the system from that architecture or exempt its automatically determined transitions from the requirements described herein.
For avoidance of doubt, possession by a person of authority, permission, ownership, administrative privilege, authentication credentials, or a capability to establish or transition the governing operative premises state in a human-authority or manual-override mode does not cause every input originating from or associated with that person to constitute a human-originated authoritative state command. For a particular automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, an input from such a person remains non-authoritative for that transition where the resulting governing operative premises state is determined by outcome-determinative evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions rather than by adoption of a state merely because the person selected, requested, identified, nominated, or indicated that state.
This principle applies irrespective of whether the human-associated input comprises an operational act, a configuration input, a rule, a threshold, a schedule, a calendar value, a parameter, a physical-control actuation, equipment operation, lighting operation, ventilation or appliance operation, shutter or door operation, point-of-sale or till activity, an access-control event, booking or reservation information, communication or network activity, a status-related input, or an input identifying, encoding, requesting, recommending, or otherwise being associated with a candidate condition of the defined set.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, during normal automatic operation, a human-associated input used in generating an automatically determined transition, whether received through an input acquisition subsystem (108) or through any other input, interface, channel, port, or communication pathway of the system (100), constitutes non-authoritative input data for that transition irrespective of the identity, role, ownership, authorisation status, authentication status, privilege, or labelling of a person from whom the input originates, and is incapable, by itself and without evaluation according to the one or more predetermined conditions, of directly transitioning the governing operative premises state. Such an input is not required to participate in every determination; where it does participate, it participates only in a non-authoritative capacity, including as input data or evidence evaluated against the predetermined conditions, or as a predetermined condition or constituent parameter thereof, and does not by itself compel the resulting governing operative premises state. Human-related inputs, including button presses, switch operations, access-control events, equipment operation, lighting or appliance operation, point-of-sale or till activity, booking information, calendar information, occupancy activity, presence indications, and other premises-associated indications, are treated as input evidence rather than as direct state-changing commands.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the system (100) comprises functional elements including a state exclusivity core (116), a state continuity core (118), and a state-integrity arrangement comprising a controlled operative-state representation. A protected operative-state store (120) may be provided as an embodiment of the state-integrity arrangement but is not required in every embodiment. The state exclusivity core (116) maintains exactly one governing condition of the defined set at a given time. The state continuity core (118) preserves continuity of the governing operative premises state, whether by retaining the governing operative premises state, by re-determining it from the one or more predetermined conditions, or by a combination thereof, and permits an automatic transition only upon satisfaction of at least one corresponding predetermined condition. The state-integrity arrangement permits modification of a controlled state representation, resulting from an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, only through a validated automatic state-determination pathway. In an aspect of the present disclosure, the one or more predetermined conditions may comprise a corresponding predetermined condition for the secured-associated condition whose satisfaction is determined, upon evaluation, from a human-absence indication, an inactivity period, or a non-occurrence of activity, alone or in combination with other evaluation data. During normal automatic operation, while the secured-associated condition is governing, mere occurrence of a human-presence indication, human-activity indication, motion indication, activity event, or other activity-related indication is insufficient, outside evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions, to cause the accessible-associated condition to become governing, whether directly or through one or more intermediate conditions of the defined set. The accessible-associated condition becomes governing only where evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions determines that a corresponding predetermined condition for the accessible-associated condition is satisfied.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, said functional elements may be separately implemented or collectively implemented by one or more processors (104) executing instructions stored in one or more memories (106), by firmware executable by physical processing hardware, by the central controller (102), by programmable logic circuitry, electronic control circuitry, hardware logic circuitry, distributed computing hardware, or a combination thereof, without requiring each functional element or constituent module to be embodied as a separately identifiable physical component, and without requiring the state determination logic or any core to be embodied separately from any other. The state determination logic is likewise a functional element and may be implemented separately from, or collectively with, the state exclusivity core (116), the state continuity core (118), and the state-integrity arrangement, by any of the foregoing hardware, firmware, or combination thereof. Where the system (100) comprises state determination logic without a separately identified core, that logic alone may perform the corresponding functions.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the complexity of the instructions, logic, or circuitry by which a functional element performs its corresponding function, when embodied by the electronic-control arrangement, one or more processors (104) executing instructions, firmware, programmable logic circuitry, electronic control circuitry, hardware logic circuitry, distributed computing hardware, or a combination thereof, is not limited. A functional element so embodied may perform its function through an arbitrarily simple or an arbitrarily complex implementation, including a single conditional operation, a sequence of conditional operations, a lookup or table-based operation, a state-machine implementation, or any other logical or circuit-based implementation capable of performing the corresponding function, as described elsewhere herein.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the state-integrity arrangement and the validated automatic state-determination pathway may be implemented functionally by the electronic-control arrangement and the state determination logic themselves, without requiring a separately identifiable state-protection, write-control, validation, or hardware-enforcement component, provided that establishment or transition of the governing operative premises state during normal automatic operation results from evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions rather than from direct state-setting by received data outside such evaluation.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, the public-status output is configured, directly or through downstream human-perceptible rendering, for presentation through a publicly accessible output channel to a person seeking access to, or services from, the premises, including a customer, visitor, client, patient, or delivery agent, without requiring that person to act as, or to authenticate as, a security-system operator, administrator, or authorised security-system user.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, any additional condition, state, mode, value, control parameter, computed result, rule-evaluation output, internal representation, or combination thereof that, alone or in combination, independently determines or governs the public-status output or the at least one security operation constitutes the governing operative premises state or a constituent thereof, irrespective of terminology, labelling, volatility, persistence, storage method, physical location, processing topology, hardware abstraction, virtualisation layer, or hosting environment.
In an aspect of the present disclosure, a method (200), a controller, server, or computing platform, and a kit of parts are further provided, each operating in accordance with the foregoing principles.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
Disclosed is a system for automatically determining an operative state of a premises and coordinating public-status and private-security operations based on the operative state (hereinafter referred to and denoted as “the system 100”), in accordance with an aspect of the present disclosure.
The system (100) includes a central controller (102), a processor (104), a memory (106), an input acquisition subsystem (108), one or more premises sensors (110), a premises-associated data-input interface (112), a state exclusivity core (116), a state continuity core (118), a protected operative-state store (120), a public status indicator (126), a private security action and alert module (128), a communication interface (130), a memory protection unit (132), write-control circuitry (134), a unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136), an evidence acquisition module (138), a non-authoritative classification layer (140), an authority-command rejection gate (142), a tamper detection module (144), a real-time clock and calendar module (146), an audit-log module (148), and an electronic coordination arrangement (150), in accordance with an aspect of the present disclosure. Not every element listed above is required in every embodiment. An embodiment may comprise a subset of the listed elements together with such further elements as the corresponding functions require, and several of the listed elements are described below as embodiments of a more general functional requirement rather than as elements essential to every embodiment.
Definitions
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “governing operative premises state” means the state or condition, howsoever stored, computed, derived, labelled, or distributed, that governs both the public-status output and the at least one security operation of the premises at a given time. The expressions “governing operative premises state”, “governing operative premises condition”, and “governing state or condition” are used interchangeably, and a reference to one includes the others where the context so admits.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “predetermined condition” means a rule, threshold, criterion, pattern, schedule value, operating-hours value, calendar value, sensor-state combination, temporal window, statistical criterion, or logical expression established before the determination to which it is applied and evaluated, alone or against then-current time, calendar data, sensor data, premises-associated input data, or any combination thereof, in order to determine the governing operative premises state. A predetermined condition specifies the circumstances in which a condition of the defined set becomes governing, and may itself identify, encode, or be associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, including a schedule-associated candidate condition, a threshold-associated candidate condition, or a human-established rule associating a time, a calendar value, or a sensor-state combination with a candidate condition, provided that adoption of the identified candidate condition remains subject to contemporaneous evaluation according to the one or more predetermined conditions and is not compelled by the identification, encoding, or association alone.
For the purposes of this disclosure, the term “predetermined conditions” includes any condition, rule, policy, criterion, threshold, schedule, mapping, configuration, or other determination basis that is stored, encoded, configured, or otherwise represented in or accessible to the electronic-control arrangement before an automatic determination. A human-originated input that supplies, creates, modifies, updates, or selects one or more such conditions is treated as configuring the predetermined conditions, and not as directly setting an operative premises state. Such conditions may be supplied once, periodically, or before each determination, provided that the actual operative premises state is determined by evaluation of the conditions and not by direct human state-setting.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “human-originated authoritative state command” means an input by which a human-selected condition of the defined set is adopted by reason of the human selection, without outcome-determinative contemporaneous evaluation capable of preventing, deferring, or substituting the selected condition. An arming command, a disarming command, a security-mode selection, and an open or closed selection, in each case adopted without such outcome-determinative evaluation, are human-originated authoritative state commands for the purposes of this disclosure. A stored human-originated value that identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set does not constitute a human-originated authoritative state command merely by reason of so identifying, encoding, or being associated with that candidate condition, where adoption of that candidate condition remains subject to outcome-determinative contemporaneous evaluation according to the one or more predetermined conditions; such a stored value constitutes a human-originated authoritative state command only where the system adopts the identified candidate condition by reason of the selection and without such evaluation, for example where the system writes the identified candidate condition at the nominated time without evaluation of any further outcome-determinative condition or datum capable of preventing, deferring, or replacing that candidate condition.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “human-originated authority-mode activation” means an input by which a person enables, activates, authorises, or permits a mode in which the system thereafter changes the governing operative premises state, where the change so made is attributable to that enabling act rather than to contemporaneous evaluation. Mere enabling, starting, unlocking, powering, authorising operation of, or permitting execution of an automatic state-determination function does not constitute a human-originated authority-mode activation for a resulting transition where the human action does not select or compel the resulting condition and the resulting condition is determined by outcome-determinative evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “human-associated input” means any input arising from, generated by, caused by, or associated with human activity at or in relation to the premises, whether arising from a deliberate act, an operational act, an incidental act, or an act performed for the purpose of indicating a condition of the premises. During normal automatic operation, a human-associated input used in generating an automatically determined transition is non-authoritative input data for that transition, and is insufficient, by itself and without contemporaneous evaluation according to the one or more predetermined conditions, to establish, select, or transition the governing operative premises state, regardless of its form, modality, subject matter, authentication, or labelling, and regardless of whether the input identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set. A human-associated input that is not used in generating an automatically determined transition, and by which a person selects, specifies, identifies, nominates, or directs the adoption of a particular condition of the defined set such that the system adopts that condition by reason of the selection and without outcome-determinative contemporaneous evaluation capable of preventing, deferring, or substituting the selected condition, is a human-originated authoritative state command as defined above and is not addressed by the automatic-determination aspects of the present disclosure.
For the purposes of this disclosure, “contemporaneous evaluation” means evaluation performed at or about the time of the transition concerned, using the data and conditions then obtaining, as distinct from execution at that time of a selection made earlier.
For the purposes of this disclosure, “outcome-determinative evaluation” means evaluation of one or more predetermined conditions by which the electronic-control arrangement determines whether a candidate condition of the defined set is to become governing, remain non-governing, be deferred, or be replaced by another condition, based on one or more evaluated conditions or data. Mere authentication of a person, verification of authorisation, privilege, credential, command integrity, message validity, receipt, or format, or permission to issue a command, does not, by itself, constitute outcome-determinative evaluation. Where a human-associated input identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition, outcome-determinative evaluation additionally requires evaluation of at least one evaluated condition or datum distinct from validating or executing that input, such that, with the candidate condition held unchanged, a variation in that evaluated condition or datum is capable of causing the candidate condition to be adopted, rejected, deferred, or replaced. Where a human-associated input associates a nominated time with a candidate condition of the defined set, comparison with or satisfaction of the nominated time does not, by itself, constitute the distinct evaluated condition or datum; at least one further condition or datum, distinct from both the human-associated input and the then-current time, is required to be capable of changing whether the candidate condition is adopted, rejected, deferred, or replaced.
For the purposes of this disclosure, the following defined terms apply: “Evaluation data” means any one or more of then-current time, calendar data, sensor data, and premises-associated input data. “Authority status” means any identity, role, ownership, authorisation status, authentication status, privilege, or labelling associated with a person or an input. “Input pathway” means any input, interface, channel, port, or communication pathway, whether physical or logical, through which data is provided to the system, including the input acquisition subsystem (108). “Candidate-condition input” means a human-associated input that identifies, encodes, requests, recommends, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set. “State-related representation” means any condition, state, mode, value, control parameter, computed result, rule-evaluation output, internal representation, or combination thereof, whether additional, alternative, intermediate, transitional, partial-access, restricted-access, composite, derived, probabilistic, or scalar. “Safety overlay” means any safety-related or emergency-related public indication, message, overlay, or notification. A human-originated input is a species of human-associated input as defined above. Unless the context expressly requires otherwise, a reference herein to a human-associated input includes a human-originated input. For the purposes of this disclosure, an "activity-related indication" means an indication, datum, event, or signal indicative of or associated with human activity, premises activity, operation of equipment or an electronic device associated with the premises, access-control activity, transaction activity, lighting or appliance operation, communication or network activity, or another occurrence indicative of activity or operation at or associated with the premises. For the purposes of this disclosure, a "transition" of the governing operative premises state or condition includes a change in which condition of the defined set is governing between successive determinations, re-determinations, or recomputations, whether the change is effected by modification of a persistently stored state representation, by modification of a transient representation, or by recomputation without persistent storage.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “state-integrity arrangement” means the functional arrangement by which establishment, modification, or replacement of a controlled operative-state representation resulting from an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation occurs as a result of evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions through the automatic state-determination architecture, while received data may participate in that evaluation but does not, outside that evaluation, directly establish, transition, modify, override, replace, or corrupt the controlled operative-state representation. The state-integrity arrangement may be implemented by the electronic-control arrangement through the state exclusivity core (116) and the state continuity core (118) themselves, alone or together with one or more additional hardware, firmware, or software protection mechanisms, and does not require a separately identifiable state-protection component, protected operative-state store (120), memory protection unit (132), write-control circuitry (134), protected execution domain, or hardware-enforced write pathway. Accordingly, an implementation in which processor-executed state-determination logic evaluates the one or more predetermined conditions and establishes or modifies the controlled operative-state representation according to the result of that evaluation may constitute the state-integrity arrangement even where no separately identifiable state-protection or write-control module is provided, provided that received sensor data, premises-associated input data, communication data, or other input does not directly establish or transition the controlled operative-state representation outside such evaluation. A write to the controlled operative-state representation that occurs through such evaluation, and only through such evaluation, is referred to herein as occurring through the validated automatic state-determination pathway, regardless of whether that pathway traverses local interconnects of the premises equipment or remote network interfaces.
For the purposes of this disclosure, a “validated automatic state-determination pathway” does not require a separately identifiable validator, validation module, hardware gate, cryptographic mechanism, protected execution environment, or other dedicated validation component. A pathway is validated where an automatically determined transition is established as a result of evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions by the automatic state-determination architecture, and an input participating in that evaluation does not, outside such evaluation, directly establish or transition the controlled operative-state representation. Validation may therefore be inherent in execution of the state determination logic itself. The hardware, firmware, software, cryptographic, access-control, write-control, isolation, and protected-memory mechanisms described herein are particular implementations of such validation and are not required in every embodiment.
For the purposes of this disclosure, the term “personal human status”, also referred to herein as “human status”, includes any status associated with one or more persons, including presence, absence, movement, activity, occupancy, identity, authorisation, location, health-related state, or other person-related condition. It is not limited to status uniquely identifying a particular individual, and includes aggregate or group status. Such status may be indicated by sensor data, premises-associated input data, or data derived therefrom. Use of personal human status as evaluation data does not, by itself, make the input authoritative; the governing operative premises state remains determined by evaluation of the predetermined conditions.
For the purposes of this disclosure, “normal automatic operation” means operation of the system (100) in which the governing operative premises state is determined automatically by evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions, whether alone or together with received data. The system (100) is in normal automatic operation whenever it is so operating, and the presence, availability, or use of any additional mode, including a commissioning mode, a configuration mode, a maintenance mode, a diagnostic mode, a test mode, or a manual override mode, neither removes the system (100) from normal automatic operation at times when it is automatically determining the governing operative premises state, nor exempts such automatic determination from the requirements described herein.
The premises and the system (100)
The premises may comprise a retail shop, showroom, restaurant, cafe, clinic, consulting room, pharmacy, bank branch, service centre, workshop, warehouse, office, educational establishment, place of worship, community facility, storage facility, industrial facility, residential building, or any other defined physical space in respect of which an accessibility condition and a security condition are both relevant. The premises may comprise one or more zones, floors, units, or sections.
The system (100) is adapted to determine automatically whether the premises is accessible or secured, or is in another condition of the defined set, and to cause the public-status output and the at least one security operation to be governed by that single determination. The system (100) may be embodied within a single device, distributed across a plurality of devices at the premises, distributed between premises devices and remote or cloud-based computing resources, or embodied wholly in remote or cloud-based computing resources with only input and output elements located at the premises. Where the premises comprises one or more zones, floors, units, or sections, the governing operative premises state for the governed elements is a premises-level governing state, and both the public-status output and the at least one security operation are governed by that same, premises-level governing state. One or more additional zone-, floor-, unit-, or section-specific states or conditions may be maintained for subordinate functions, provided that no such additional state or condition independently governs either governed element in place of, inconsistently with, or as a competing operative premises state relative to the premises-level governing state. An architecture in which a value aggregated across zones, floors, units, or sections drives one governed element while a value or set of values determined independently for individual zones, floors, units, or sections drives the other governed element does not correspond to a single premises-level governing state and does not embody the technical solution described herein.
Central controller (102), processor (104), and memory (106)
The central controller (102) is adapted to coordinate the operation of the system (100). The central controller (102) comprises at least one of a processor (104) operatively coupled to a memory (106), programmable logic circuitry, electronic control circuitry, and hardware logic circuitry.
The processor (104) may comprise a microprocessor, a microcontroller, a digital signal processor, an applications processor, a system-on-chip, a multi-core processor, a virtual processor instantiated upon a hypervisor, a processor of a cloud computing instance, or any combination thereof. The processor (104) is adapted to execute machine-readable instructions stored in the memory (106).
The memory (106) may comprise volatile memory, non-volatile memory, or a combination thereof, including random access memory, read-only memory, flash memory, electrically erasable programmable read-only memory, ferroelectric random access memory, magnetoresistive random access memory, battery-backed static random access memory, a solid-state storage device, a magnetic storage device, an optical storage device, or a storage volume of a remote or cloud-based storage service.
In an embodiment, the central controller (102) comprises programmable logic circuitry such as a field-programmable gate array or a complex programmable logic device, in which the functions described herein are realised in configurable logic without execution of stored instructions. In a further embodiment, the central controller (102) comprises hardware logic circuitry such as an application-specific integrated circuit, discrete logic, or a state machine realised in gates, in which the functions described herein are realised without a stored instruction sequence and without a memory (106) for holding such a sequence. Accordingly, the presence of a memory (106) holding executable instructions is not essential to the operation of the system (100).
Input acquisition subsystem (108), premises sensors (110), and premises-associated data-input interface (112)
The input acquisition subsystem (108) is adapted to receive at least one of sensor data from one or more premises sensors (110) and premises-associated input data through a premises-associated data-input interface (112). The received data is indicative of at least one of human presence, human absence, human activity, occupancy, operation of the premises, non-operation of the premises, accessibility of the premises, and a condition associated with the premises.
The one or more premises sensors (110) may comprise at least one of a motion sensor, an occupancy sensor, a passive infrared sensor, a microwave sensor, an ultrasonic sensor, a door contact sensor, a window contact sensor, a shutter position sensor, a gate position sensor, a lock state sensor, a light sensor, an ambient illumination sensor, an electrical current sensor, a power consumption sensor, a load sensor, a vibration sensor, an acoustic sensor, a sound level sensor, a temperature sensor, a humidity sensor, a gas sensor, a smoke sensor, a pressure sensor, a weight sensor, a floor mat sensor, a beam-break sensor, an image sensor, a video camera, a thermal imaging sensor, a lidar sensor, a radar sensor, a capacitive sensor, an inductive sensor, a magnetic sensor, a biometric sensor, a proximity sensor, a wireless signal presence sensor, a network association sensor, and a geolocation sensor. One or more selected sensors capable of indicating location or proximity may produce proximity-derived data. Such sensors may detect activity of a human, an object, or both, including movement, placement, removal, or handling of an object associated with the premises.
The premises-associated data-input interface (112) is adapted to receive premises-associated input data from a source other than a premises sensor (110). Such premises-associated input data may comprise at least one of point-of-sale transaction data, till or cash-drawer activity data, payment terminal activity data, booking or appointment data, reservation data, queue or token data, staff rostering data, attendance or clock-in data, access-control event data, badge or credential read data, equipment operation data, lighting circuit state data, appliance operation data, heating, ventilation or air-conditioning operation data, network device association data, application session data, dispatch or delivery data, inventory movement data, utility supply data, calendar data, operating-hours schedule data, public holiday data, and data received from a remote or cloud-based service. Point-of-sale transaction data, till or cash-drawer activity data, and payment terminal activity data are examples of data indicating or recording a financial transaction at or associated with the premises.
In an embodiment, the input acquisition subsystem (108) is adapted to accept a human-associated input without requiring authentication, identity verification, credential presentation, or authorisation of the person from whom the input arises, since the input is treated as evidence and is not permitted to establish the governing operative premises state by itself. A human-associated input may comprise a human-originated or human-associated status-related input, being an input provided by a person for the purpose of indicating the condition of the premises, such as actuation of a control provided for that purpose. Such a status-related input is received as data and is evaluated in the same manner as an operational input; it does not acquire authoritative character by reason of having been produced for the purpose of indicating the condition of the premises.
By way of a first illustrative example, a shopkeeper switches on the shop lighting circuit and the ceiling fan upon arriving at the premises. The resulting change in electrical load is received as sensor data from an electrical current sensor of the one or more premises sensors (110). By way of a second illustrative example, the shopkeeper opens the till at the commencement of trading, and till activity data is received through the premises-associated data-input interface (112). By way of a third illustrative example, the shopkeeper actuates a control provided at the premises for the purpose of indicating that the premises is being opened, and the resulting signal is received through the input acquisition subsystem (108). In each example the received data is human-associated input data. In no case does the received data by itself transition the governing operative premises state. In each case the received data is evaluated against the one or more predetermined conditions, and the governing operative premises state is determined from that evaluation. Accordingly, a signal arising from the third example is evaluated in the same manner as a signal arising from the first or the second, and does not acquire authoritative character by reason of having been produced for the purpose of indicating the condition of the premises.
The one or more predetermined conditions may comprise a human-established schedule value, an operating-hours value, a calendar value, a public-holiday value, a threshold value, a sensor-state combination, a temporal window, a persistence or dwell requirement, a confirmation requirement across a plurality of inputs, a statistical or probabilistic criterion, a pattern derived from historical operation, a machine-learning model parameter set, a rule expression, or a combination thereof.
Where a predetermined condition comprises a human-established schedule value, operating-hours value, or calendar value, that value identifies one or more operating-time intervals. Such a value does not constitute, and is not executed as, a target-state instruction: it does not nominate a condition of the defined set to be written at a nominated time. The governing operative premises state is in every case the condition yielded by contemporaneous evaluation at the time of determination. In a further embodiment, a predetermined condition comprises a human-established schedule value that identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, for example a schedule value associating a nominated time with a candidate secured-associated condition. Such a value does not, by itself, cause adoption of the identified candidate condition; adoption of the candidate condition remains subject to contemporaneous evaluation, at or after the nominated time, of the one or more predetermined conditions together with then-current sensor data or premises-associated input data, such that the candidate condition may be adopted, rejected, deferred, or replaced depending on the result of that evaluation. By way of illustration, a schedule value associates 22:00 with a candidate secured condition; at 22:00 the system evaluates then-current occupancy data, and adopts the secured condition where the premises is unoccupied and defers or rejects adoption where occupancy is detected. In this embodiment the governing operative premises state remains, in every case, the condition yielded by contemporaneous evaluation, and is not established by the schedule value alone.
In a first embodiment, such a value is evaluated as one input among others, together with the sensor data or the premises-associated input data. In that embodiment a transition is not generated solely from the expiry or commencement of an operating-time interval, and where the premises remains in operation beyond a scheduled closing time, or does not open at a scheduled opening time by reason of a holiday, an absence, or an unscheduled closure, the governing operative premises state reflects the condition determined from evaluation of the premises-derived evidence and not the condition implied by the schedule.
In an embodiment, where a predetermined condition comprises a machine-learning model parameter set, the parameters are fixed before commencement of normal automatic operation and are not modified by online learning during normal automatic operation, so that the determination remains reproducible from the conditions then stored.
