In a second embodiment, where such a value identifies one or more operating-time intervals without identifying, encoding, or being associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, such a value is evaluated contemporaneously against a then-current time value without requiring the sensor data or the premises-associated input data; where such a value identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, adoption of that candidate condition remains subject to evaluation of at least one further evaluated condition or datum distinct from both the value and the then-current time. The determination remains automatic and contemporaneous, and remains a determination made by the state exclusivity core (116) upon evaluation of the predetermined conditions then stored, rather than the writing of a condition previously selected by a person. The distinction is one of causation: in an arrangement outside the present invention an operator selects a target condition and nominates a time for its adoption, and the machine writes the condition the operator selected; in the present embodiment the schedule data is a datum evaluated among the predetermined conditions, and the condition that results is the condition the evaluation yields. This embodiment is described further below under the heading Operating-hours schedule data as evidence. For purposes of the schedule embodiments, schedule data defining one or more operating-time intervals does not identify, encode, or become associated with a candidate condition merely because application of a predetermined classification rule to the then-current temporal relationship yields a condition of the defined set. In such an embodiment no state-specific target value or scheduled state-write instruction is stored for execution at the boundary time; the governing condition is computed by contemporaneous evaluation of the predetermined condition against the then-current time. By contrast, a candidate-state schedule stores, specifies, or associates a state-specific candidate condition with a nominated time for possible adoption, and adoption of that candidate condition remains subject to the outcome-determinative evaluation described herein. A schedule value, operating-hours value, calendar value, or threshold value that directly establishes, transitions, or overrides the governing operative premises state without evaluation by the state exclusivity core (116), or that constitutes a direct state-setting cause independently of such evaluation, is a different, non-evaluative species outside the scope of the automatic, evaluation-based determination described herein.
State exclusivity core (116)
The state exclusivity core (116) is implemented by the central controller (102) and is adapted to determine automatically, based on evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions alone or in combination with at least one of the sensor data and the premises-associated input data, an operative premises state selected from a defined set comprising at least an accessible-associated condition, being an accessible state, and a secured-associated condition, being a secured state, and to maintain the operative premises state such that exactly one condition of the defined set constitutes a governing operative premises state at a given time.
The defined set is not limited to two members. In an embodiment the defined set comprises, in addition to the accessible state and the secured state, one or more further conditions such as a partially accessible condition, a restricted-access condition, a staff-only condition, an appointment-only condition, a maintenance condition, a transitional or closing condition, a standby condition, or an operational-availability condition representing availability or unavailability of a resource, a service capability, or an infrastructure function of the premises. Where such a further condition is comprised in the defined set, exactly one condition of the defined set remains governing at a given time, and the further condition governs the public-status output and the at least one security operation in the same manner as the accessible state and the secured state.
The governing operative premises state may be represented as a binary value, a discrete enumerated value, a discrete value, a continuous value, a scalar value, a vector of coordinated values, or a coordinated combination of values, provided that any plurality of such representations collectively corresponds to the same single governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, the state exclusivity core (116) maintains a controlled state representation in or using at least one of an atomic memory value, a single memory location subject to atomic write, a register, a latch, a flip-flop, a hardware state element, a mutually exclusive encoding, a transactional database record, and a single-writer data structure, such that a partially completed transition is not observable by the public status indicator (126) or the private security action and alert module (128). In such an embodiment, modification of the controlled state representation is performed exclusively through an atomic read-modify-write operation carried out through the validated automatic state-determination pathway, such that no partially updated or intermediate operative premises state is observable by either the public status indicator (126) or the private security action and alert module (128).
In an embodiment, the state exclusivity core (116) requires sensor data generated at the premises, or premises-associated input data indicative of an operation performed at the premises, to be evaluated in the determination, such that a transition is not generated in the absence of any indication arising from the premises.
In an embodiment, the state exclusivity core (116) is adapted such that, under at least one pair of operating conditions in which a schedule value is identical and the received data differs, the determined governing operative premises state differs, whereby the determination is demonstrably a function of the received data and not of the schedule value alone.
State continuity core (118)
The state continuity core (118) is adapted to retain the governing operative premises state until at least one corresponding predetermined condition is satisfied, and to permit an automatic transition between conditions of the defined set only upon satisfaction of the at least one corresponding predetermined condition.
Retention of the governing operative premises state is the default behaviour of the system (100). The governing operative premises state does not lapse, decay, expire, revert, or default merely by passage of time independently of satisfaction of a corresponding predetermined condition, nor by the absence of received data, a communication interruption, a session termination, a device restart, or a service restart. Where the system (100) is restarted or power is restored, the governing operative premises state last determined is retained or is re-determined by evaluation, and is not set to a default condition of the defined set in the absence of evaluation. For avoidance of doubt, absence of received data resulting from unavailability, failure, or communication interruption of an input source or input path is distinct from a human-absence indication, inactivity period, or non-occurrence-of-activity indication produced by evaluation of an observation interval. An event-based input source may establish a non-occurrence-of-activity indication from absence of qualifying activity events over such interval where the source or input path has not been determined to be unavailable or failed. In a narrower embodiment, validity of the observation interval is confirmed by a heartbeat, freshness indication, source-health indication, acknowledgement, availability indication, or other evidence that the source or input path remained operative during the interval.
In an embodiment, the state continuity core (118) is adapted to prohibit an automatic transition based solely on an inactivity interval, such that an inactivity-period condition, when used, is evaluated in combination with at least one further predetermined condition. An elapsed duration, timer expiry, countdown, or grace period may be evaluated alone or in combination with other predetermined conditions and may itself function as a predetermined condition or as an input to the evaluation.
In an embodiment, where a candidate transition is rejected, fails validation, or is not verified as satisfying a corresponding predetermined condition, the governing operative premises state then obtaining is retained, and the public-status output and the at least one security operation continue to be governed by the retained state.
Protected operative-state store (120)
The protected operative-state store (120), which is one embodiment of the state-integrity arrangement described below and is not essential to every embodiment, is adapted to maintain a controlled state representation corresponding to the governing operative premises state. The store is protected by restriction of modification of the controlled state representation to a validated automatic state-determination pathway comprising the state exclusivity core (116) and the state continuity core (118), whether such restriction is implemented in hardware, firmware, software, or a combination thereof.
In a hardware implementation, the restriction may be effected by a memory protection unit (132), by write-control circuitry (134), by a protected memory region defined in a memory management unit, by a write-protected register, by a hardware-enforced privilege level, or by a secure execution domain or trusted execution environment. In a firmware implementation, the restriction may be effected by a supervisory routine holding the sole write capability for the controlled state representation, by a firmware-enforced privilege separation, or by a secure boot chain that establishes the write path before application code executes. In a software implementation, the restriction may be effected by an operating-system access-control policy, by process or container isolation, by a capability or token required for the write operation, by a single-writer service holding exclusive write access, by a database transaction constraint permitting the write only from the determination pathway, or by an application architecture in which no code path other than the determination pathway is capable of writing the controlled state representation.
The protected operative-state store (120) may maintain the controlled state representation as an atomic memory value, as a value recomputed at each determination without persistent storage, as a latched or register-held hardware representation, as a derived condition, or as a distributed representation. In an embodiment the protected operative-state store (120) comprises a non-volatile storage element adapted to retain the controlled state representation across a power interruption or a restart.
The protected operative-state store (120) need not be embodied as a separately identifiable physical component, and its function may be performed collectively with the function of one or more other functional elements of the system (100).
State-Integrity Arrangement
The state-integrity arrangement is adapted to permit the sensor data and the premises-associated input data to be evaluated for determining the governing operative premises state, to permit modification of the controlled state representation, resulting from an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, only through the validated automatic state-determination pathway, and to prevent the sensor data and the premises-associated input data from directly establishing, transitioning, modifying, overriding, or corrupting the controlled state representation outside the validated automatic state-determination pathway.
It is to be noted that the state-integrity arrangement does not exclude sensor data or premises-associated input data from the determination. Where used in a determination, such sensor data or premises-associated input data forms part of the evidential basis of that determination. What is prevented, for an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, is the direct writing of the controlled state representation by a sensor-processing component, a data-input component, a communication component, an application service, or any other component otherwise than through the validated automatic state-determination pathway.
In an embodiment, the state-integrity arrangement comprises at least one of a memory protection unit (132) adapted to restrict write access to the protected operative-state store (120), write-control circuitry (134) adapted to gate a write operation to the protected operative-state store (120), a unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136) adapted to convey sensor-domain information towards the determination pathway while excluding a return path capable of writing the controlled state representation, access-control logic, a protected memory region, execution-control circuitry, rule-isolation logic, a protected execution domain, a trusted execution environment, a secure enclave, and a cryptographic validation mechanism.
In an embodiment, the state-integrity arrangement is adapted to operate irrespective of whether the system (100) is embodied within a single device, distributed across premises devices, or distributed between premises devices and remote or cloud-based computing resources, and the restriction upon modification of the controlled state representation applies equally to a write attempted across a local interconnect and to a write attempted across a network interface.
The public-status output and the at least one security operation are governed by the same controlled state representation, directly or through one or more intermediate control outputs. Accordingly, the governing operative premises state constitutes a common causal control input for both the public-status output and the at least one security operation, and neither is governed by an independently determined or maintained competing operative premises state.
Where an additional security-specific state, mode, trigger condition, or control value is present in the system (100), one or both of the following apply. First, no separately computed output-control value independently governs either the public-status output or the at least one security operation. Second, notwithstanding the additional value, the governing operative premises state remains a necessary causal control input for the public-status output and for at least one security operation, alert, resource-control action, or security-operation attribute.
Public status indicator (126)
The public status indicator (126) is adapted to provide, based on the governing operative premises state directly or through a public-status control output, a human-perceptible indication representing whether the premises are accessible or secured, or are in another condition of the defined set. The public status indicator (126), the electronic transmission interface, and the public-output interface generally, when providing or presenting the public-status output, operate as an outbound conveyance pathway and do not themselves constitute a pathway through which the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition is directly established, modified, replaced, or transitioned. A signal, message, selection, or interaction received via the public status indicator (126), the electronic transmission interface, or an application, website, or other electronic or digital medium through which the public-status output is presented, does not thereby directly write to, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition; this is distinct from, and does not preclude, a separately provided control, configuration, or authority pathway that may exist for other purposes.
The public status indicator (126) may comprise at least one of an electronic sign, an illuminated sign, a light-emitting diode display, a liquid crystal display, an electronic paper display, a segment display, an indicator lamp, a coloured lamp, a projector, an audible annunciator, a kiosk display, a window-mounted display, a door-mounted display, a shutter-mounted indicator, a display of a mobile application, a page of a website, an entry of an online directory or map service, a messaging output, a voice-assistant response, and a display of a third-party application receiving a machine-readable public-status representation.
The indication provided by the public status indicator (126) constitutes a public-status output. Any machine-readable representation provided through an electronic transmission interface for downstream human-perceptible rendering likewise constitutes a public-status output. The public-status output is derived from the controlled operative-state representation or from the governing operative premises state, whether directly or through an intermediate control value generated from that representation.
The human-perceptible indication is configured, directly or through downstream human-perceptible rendering, for presentation through a publicly accessible output channel to a person seeking access to, or services from, the premises, including a customer, visitor, client, patient, or delivery agent, without requiring that person to act as, or to authenticate as, a security-system operator, administrator, or authorised security-system user, and to communicate whether or to what extent the premises are accessible or secured for entry, use, or the provision of services.
It is to be noted that the indication is addressed to a person who is not an operator of the system (100) and who is not required to hold credentials as a security-system operator, administrator, or authorised security-system user. A person standing before the premises, or consulting a public listing of the premises from a remote location, is thereby informed of the condition of the premises. This is to be distinguished from the presentation of a system status to an operator, administrator, or authorised security-system user through a monitoring console, an administrative dashboard, or an authenticated operator or administrative application session, which does not inform such a person.
In an embodiment, the public-status output is provided solely as a machine-readable public-status representation through an electronic transmission interface, and the human-perceptible rendering is performed downstream by a receiving application, service, directory, map service, or third-party platform. In such an embodiment the system (100) need not comprise a display element at the premises.
In an embodiment, when the governing operative premises state is the accessible state, the public status indicator (126) or an electronic transmission interface provides an indication of accessibility together with an associated indication of availability, service capability, operating capacity, or expected duration, each such associated indication being derived from and subordinate to the governing operative premises state.
Private security action and alert module (128)
The private security action and alert module (128) is adapted to perform at least one security operation responsive to the governing operative premises state alone, or responsive to the governing operative premises state in combination with satisfaction of at least one security-trigger condition.
Accordingly, a security operation may be performed by reason of the governing operative premises state alone. By way of example, upon determination of the secured state the system (100) arms an intrusion detection function, locks an access-control device, enables a recording resource, or alters an alert-routing configuration, in each case without any separate trigger condition being satisfied and without any human-originated arming command. Separately, a security operation may be performed upon satisfaction of a security-trigger condition while the governing operative premises state is the secured state, in which case the state governs whether the operation is performed at all and the trigger governs when.
The at least one security operation may comprise at least one of arming or disarming an intrusion detection function, enabling or disabling a monitoring function, enabling or disabling a recording function, commencing or ceasing video recording, altering a recording frame rate or retention period, enabling or disabling a motion detection zone, generating an alert, generating an alarm, actuating a siren or strobe, transmitting a notification to an operator device, transmitting a notification to a monitoring centre, transmitting a notification to an emergency service, locking or unlocking an access-control device, altering an access-control permission set, altering a lighting state, altering a heating, ventilation or air-conditioning state, altering an energy or resource allocation, and recording an event in an audit record.
Where the at least one security operation is performed in response to satisfaction of a security-trigger condition, satisfaction of that condition does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state. A detected intrusion, a detected motion event, a detected door opening, a detected glass break, a detected smoke condition, or any other trigger causes the security operation to be performed or not performed according to the governing operative premises state then obtaining, and does not itself change that state. Accordingly, the public status indicator (126) continues to represent the governing operative premises state during and after performance of the security operation.
In an embodiment, an armed state, disarmed state, security-mode value, arming command, or disarming command associated with the at least one security operation is derived from, subordinate to, and governed by the governing operative premises state, and does not constitute an independent determinant of the public-status output or of the at least one security operation.
A safety function of the system (100), including detection of a smoke condition, a fire condition, a gas condition, a flood condition, or a medical emergency condition, and generation of a corresponding safety alert, may operate irrespective of the governing operative premises state. Such a safety function does not determine, modify, override, replace, bypass, or transition the governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, a safety-related or emergency-related indication is additionally presented publicly, for example an evacuation notice, a do-not-enter notice, or an emergency service notification displayed at the premises or transmitted for downstream rendering. Such an indication is an overlay presented in addition to, or in place of, the ordinary presentation of the public-status output for the duration of the safety condition. It does not constitute an independently determined or maintained competing operative premises state or condition, and its presence, generation, or display neither prevents nor displaces the governing operative premises state as the common causal control input for the public status indicator (126) and the private security action and alert module (128), the public-status and private-security operations continuing to be based thereon.
Upon cessation of the safety condition the overlay is withdrawn and the ordinary presentation of the public-status output resumes, corresponding to the governing operative premises state then obtaining. The governing operative premises state during and after the safety condition is that determined by evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions, and is unaffected by the presentation or withdrawal of the overlay.
Communication interface (130)
The communication interface (130) is adapted to convey data between elements of the system (100) and between the system (100) and a remote or cloud-based computing resource, a mobile application, a directory service, a map service, a monitoring centre, or a third-party platform. The communication interface (130) may comprise a wired interface, a wireless interface, a local area network interface, a wide area network interface, a cellular interface, a low-power wide-area network interface, a short-range radio interface, a serial interface, a bus interface, or a combination thereof.
No transmission, message receipt, communication event, session establishment, session termination, connectivity loss, or connectivity restoration by itself determines, modifies, or transitions the governing operative premises state. Where a message received through the communication interface (130) participates in an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, it is treated as received data and is evaluated in the same manner as other received data; a message conveying a genuine human-authority or manual-override command associated with a non-automatic transition, conveyed through a separately validated human-authority pathway, is not thereby excluded.
Memory protection unit (132), write-control circuitry (134), and unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136)
The memory protection unit (132) is adapted to restrict write access to the protected operative-state store (120) such that a write originating otherwise than from the validated automatic state-determination pathway is refused at the hardware level. The memory protection unit (132) may be integrated within the processor (104), provided as a discrete component, or realised within programmable logic circuitry.
The write-control circuitry (134) is adapted to gate a write operation to the protected operative-state store (120) by means of a hardware-level enable signal, an access flag, a privilege control signal, or a combination thereof, such that the write operation is completed only when the gating condition established by the validated automatic state-determination pathway is present. A write attempt originating from a sensor-processing component, a data-input component, a communication component, or an application service is refused and may be recorded.
The unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136) is adapted to permit sensor-domain information to be supplied to the state exclusivity core (116) while physically or logically excluding a return path by which the sensor domain could write the controlled state representation. In a physical embodiment, the data channel (136) comprises an optical coupler, a diode-configured logic element, a driver without a corresponding receiver on the sensor-domain side, or a conductor arrangement in which a back-propagation line is absent or severed, such that no direct write-capable electrical path exists from the sensor domain to the controlled state representation, the permitted sensor-domain path terminating at an evidence-receiving input of the state-determination domain. In a logical embodiment, the data channel (136) comprises a filtering element, a protocol adapter, a message broker subscription, or an interface definition that admits only evidential data and admits no state-setting message.
Each of the memory protection unit (132), the write-control circuitry (134), and the unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136) is optional, and the state-integrity arrangement may comprise one, some, or all of them, or may be realised by the firmware or software mechanisms described above.
Evidence acquisition module (138), non-authoritative classification layer (140), and authority-command rejection gate (142)
In an embodiment, the classification of a human-associated input as non-authoritative evidence, and the prevention of acceptance of that input as a direct authoritative state-setting input, are performed by an automatic determination core comprising an evidence acquisition module (138), a non-authoritative classification layer (140), and an authority-command rejection gate (142), the non-authoritative classification layer (140) being operatively coupled between the evidence acquisition module (138) and the authority-command rejection gate (142).
The evidence acquisition module (138) is adapted to receive an input record comprising the received data and any associated metadata. The non-authoritative classification layer (140) is adapted to classify each human-associated input contained in the input record as non-authoritative evidence, regardless of authentication or labelling, and to identify within the input record any target-state selection field, instruction, command value, or signal configured, encoded, or mapped to identify or direct adoption of a target operative premises state.
The authority-command rejection gate (142) is adapted to prevent the use of any such target-state selection field, instruction, command value, or signal as a direct state-setting value or as an operative premises state value, whether by discarding, masking, or invalidating it, or, in a further embodiment, by retaining it and routing it, stripped of direct state-setting authority, as non-authoritative candidate-condition data for outcome-determinative evaluation against the one or more predetermined conditions, together with the remaining informational content, which is likewise routed for evaluation against the one or more predetermined conditions. Where an input record contains no such field, instruction, command value, or signal, the gate passes the informational content unaltered.
By way of illustration, where an input record received from a mobile application contains both a field indicating that a user has actuated a control at the premises and a field purporting to set the premises state to secured, the latter field is discarded by the authority-command rejection gate (142) and the former is routed for evaluation. The governing operative premises state that results, if any, is determined by evaluation of the predetermined conditions and not by the discarded field.
The automatic determination core is optional. In an embodiment the classification and prevention functions are performed without a separately identifiable evidence acquisition module (138), non-authoritative classification layer (140), or authority-command rejection gate (142), by an input processing arrangement that admits no state-setting field at all, in which case no such field arrives to be discarded and the functions are satisfied by construction of the input interface.
Tamper detection module (144)
In an embodiment, the system (100) further comprises a tamper detection module (144) adapted to detect an unauthorised attempt to modify the controlled state representation, an unauthorised attempt to access the protected operative-state store (120), an unauthorised modification of a predetermined condition, a physical intrusion into an enclosure of the system (100), a disconnection or substitution of a premises sensor (110), or a compromise of the communication interface (130). Upon such detection the tamper detection module (144) is adapted to generate an alert, to record the event, or both. Detection of a tamper condition does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, the tamper detection module (144) is operatively coupled to hardware integrity monitoring circuitry adapted to monitor the physical and logical integrity of the protected operative-state store (120), the write-control circuitry (134), the unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136), and the representation of the one or more predetermined conditions. The hardware integrity monitoring circuitry may comprise a checksum or cyclic-redundancy engine operating upon the stored representation, a parity or error-correcting-code checker, a duplicate-register comparator, a voltage, clock, or temperature glitch detector, an enclosure or mesh intrusion sensor, a bus monitor, or a combination thereof.
The hardware integrity monitoring circuitry is adapted to detect unauthorised access to the controlled state representation, alteration of a predetermined condition, an integrity violation of the controlled state representation, and an attempted bypass of the validated automatic state-determination pathway, including an attempted write to the controlled state representation originating otherwise than through that pathway. Upon such detection the tamper detection module (144) is adapted to generate a tamper signal, to record the event in the audit-log module (148), to restrict access to the protected operative-state store (120) or to a configuration interface, or any combination thereof. Generation of a tamper signal, recording of the event, and restriction of access do not determine, modify, override, replace, bypass, or transition the governing operative premises state.
Real-time clock and calendar module (146) and audit-log module (148)
The real-time clock and calendar module (146) is adapted to provide a then-current time value, a date value, a day-of-week value, and a calendar value to the state exclusivity core (116) for use in evaluation. A time or calendar value so provided is evaluated according to the one or more predetermined conditions and does not, outside such evaluation, directly determine or transition the governing operative premises state. In an embodiment the system (100) operates without a real-time clock, and an operating-period condition is inferred from a recurring pattern of received data.
The audit-log module (148) is adapted to store, in a separate record retained independently of the controlled state representation, a record of each determination, each transition, each rejected candidate transition, each discarded target-state field, each reclassified or routed candidate-condition field, each refused write attempt, and each tamper event, together with the received data and predetermined conditions upon which the determination was based. The audit record is retained for a configured period and is available for retrieval, review, and verification. The audit record is not consumed by the determination pathway and does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
Electronic coordination arrangement (150) and prevention of shadow-state conditions
In an embodiment, the system (100) further comprises an electronic coordination arrangement (150) adapted to cause the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, as applicable, to constitute a necessary causal control input for the public-status output and for at least one attribute of the at least one security operation selected from enablement, operating mode, priority, recipient, content, type, timing, routing, resource, and response, and to prevent the public-status output and the at least one security operation from being governed by independently determined competing operative premises states or operative premises conditions.
In a distributed embodiment, a first subsystem or determination pathway may generate a public-accessibility candidate value and a second subsystem or determination pathway may generate a private-security candidate value. In such an embodiment the electronic coordination arrangement (150) comprises at least one of rule-isolation logic, a deterministic orchestration pipeline, message-bus filtering, database-transaction control, consensus validation, a shared controlling-state service, a message-broker ordering protocol, and an application-programming-interface gateway state-control service, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) being adapted to validate, order, normalise, synchronise, or reconcile the public-accessibility candidate value and the private-security candidate value against the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, as applicable, before either candidate value governs the public-status output or the at least one security operation.
In a further embodiment, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) is adapted to enforce a transactional state-transition barrier operating as a staged-commit barrier. Upon initiation of a candidate transition of the governing operative premises state, incoming or newly applicable evaluation data capable of initiating or altering a state transition is temporarily queued for state-transition processing so that a further transition is not commenced while the pending transition is in progress. Such queuing relates only to the state-transition operation, and does not prevent, delay, or suspend independent processing of a safety condition or generation of a state-independent safety alert or safety response, which continue irrespective of the governing operative premises state and irrespective of any transition then in progress.
In a first phase, following determination of a candidate updated operative premises state or operative premises condition, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) derives an updated public-status control value and an updated private-security control signal from a pending representation of that candidate updated state or condition, writes each control value to a pending or staging store, and delivers the pending control values to the public-output interface or public status indicator (126) and to the private security action and alert module (128) respectively. The pending values are held by the respective recipient in a pending region distinct from the region governing its current operation. Transmission or presentation of a public-status output corresponding to the updated public-status control value is prevented, and application of the updated private-security control signal is prevented, so that neither recipient acts upon the pending value during this phase. The public-status output presented, and the security operation performed, continue to correspond to the governing operative premises state obtaining before the transition.
Each recipient, upon receiving and validating the pending value and confirming that it is able to act upon that value, generates a readiness-acknowledgement signal and returns it to the electronic coordination arrangement (150). A readiness-acknowledgement signal may be conveyed as a hardware handshake or strobe on a physical interface, an electronic acknowledgement frame, a protocol-level response, a message-bus or publish-subscribe acknowledgement, an application-programming-interface response, a database transaction acknowledgement, or any equivalent endpoint-ready indication, and may accordingly be returned by a locally mounted public status indicator (126) or by a public-output interface that conveys a machine-readable public-status representation to a remote or third-party renderer. A readiness-acknowledgement signal is generated without transmitting or presenting a public-status output corresponding to the pending public-status control value and without applying the pending private-security control signal, and therefore does not itself alter what is transmitted, presented, or performed.
Until receipt of both readiness-acknowledgement signals and authorisation of the commit, the pre-transition governing operative premises state remains the governing operative premises state, and the updated state and the corresponding control values remain pending. Upon authorisation of the commit, the updated state becomes the governing operative premises state, and the corresponding public-status output and private-security control signal become operative with respect to it.
In a second phase, upon receipt of the readiness-acknowledgement signals from both recipients, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) revalidates the pending candidate state by re-evaluating the one or more predetermined conditions against evaluation data then current or changed, received, or newly applicable after determination of the pending candidate and before commit, where such evaluation data is relevant under the one or more predetermined conditions. Where such re-evaluation would cause a different condition of the defined set to become governing, or would cause the pending candidate no longer to satisfy its corresponding predetermined condition, the pending transition is cancelled or superseded and a new determination is performed. Where re-evaluation confirms that the pending candidate remains the condition to become governing and continues to satisfy its corresponding predetermined condition, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) authorises transmission or presentation of the public-status output corresponding to the updated public-status control value and application of the updated private-security control signal. Both are thereby committed with respect to the same governing operative premises state. For the purposes of this embodiment, such commitment denotes logical consistency with the same governing operative premises state and does not require simultaneous physical actuation, transmission, reception, or human-perceptible rendering at the respective endpoints. Differences arising solely from propagation, rendering, processing, or actuator latency do not constitute independently governed competing operative premises states, provided that neither endpoint acts according to a different governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, where a readiness-acknowledgement signal is not received from a recipient within a configured interval, or where a recipient returns a failure indication, the electronic coordination arrangement (150) does not authorise transmission, presentation, or application, discards or retains the pending values, and the public-status output and the at least one security operation continue to be governed by the governing operative premises state obtaining before the transition. The failed transition is recorded in the audit-log module (148), and the transition may be retried. Queued evaluation data is thereafter released for evaluation.
Any additional, alternative, intermediate, transitional, partial-access, restricted-access, composite, derived, probabilistic, scalar, or otherwise represented condition, state, mode, value, control parameter, system variable, computed result, rule-evaluation output, internal representation, or combination thereof that, alone or in combination, independently determines or governs the public-status output or the at least one security operation constitutes the governing operative premises state or a constituent thereof, and any plurality of such is treated as a single such governing state. When two or more such representations, variables, or evaluations independently govern different respective governed elements, they must correspond to the same condition of the defined set to constitute the governing state; correspondence to different conditions of the defined set fails to satisfy the requirement that exactly one condition of the defined set constitutes the governing state at a given time.
Any other such condition, value, or representation is permitted to affect the public-status output or the at least one security operation only in combination with the governing operative premises state, and without substituting for, bypassing, overriding, replacing, or independently governing in place of it. A security-trigger condition or a safety condition is permitted to arise independently and to affect whether or how a security operation or a safety operation is performed, without determining, modifying, overriding, replacing, bypassing, or transitioning the governing operative premises state.
The foregoing applies irrespective of terminology, labelling, volatility, persistence, or storage method, whether the state is maintained as a stored variable, an atomic memory value, a value recomputed at each determination without persistent storage, a latched or register-held hardware representation, a derived condition, or a distributed representation. It applies further irrespective of physical location, processing topology, hardware abstraction, virtualisation layer, or hosting environment, including device-resident, distributed, edge, virtualised, containerised, serverless, cloud-based, and remote implementations, and irrespective of whether the relevant components are implemented within a single device or across physically separate devices, subsystems, applications, services, network domains, or administrative domains.
Where the system (100) is distributed across a plurality of subsystems, services, devices, or cloud components, components that determine, maintain, receive, or use the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition for governing the public-status output or the at least one security operation are coordinated to that same governing state or condition. Any locally cached or replicated representation, when maintained by such a component for governing either output, is reconciled to the governing state or condition before being permitted to govern that output.
Absence of a human-originated authoritative state command
During normal automatic operation, a human-associated input received by the system (100) and used in generating an automatically determined transition, whether through the input acquisition subsystem (108) or through any other input, interface, channel, port, or communication pathway of the system (100), constitutes non-authoritative input data for that transition, regardless of authentication or labelling, and is incapable, by itself and without evaluation according to the one or more predetermined conditions, of directly transitioning the governing operative premises state. This applies irrespective of the form, modality, or subject matter of the input, and irrespective of whether the input arises from an operational act at the premises, from an act performed for the purpose of indicating the condition of the premises, from a schedule or calendar entry created or modified by a person, from a presence indication, or from a confirmation, and irrespective of whether the input identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, provided that adoption of the identified candidate condition remains subject to such evaluation.
Each automatically determined transition of the governing operative premises state during normal automatic operation is generated by contemporaneous evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions alone, or against then-current time, calendar data, sensor data, premises-associated input data, or any combination thereof, without requiring, as a prerequisite for that transition, any human-originated authoritative state command or any human-originated authority-mode activation, whether occurring once or repeatedly.
No such transition is caused by a human-originated authoritative state command that is sufficient, by itself and without outcome-determinative contemporaneous evaluation, to establish the resulting condition. No human-originated authoritative state command directly establishes, transitions, or overrides the governing operative premises state for that transition. Any human-associated input used for generating that transition is treated, for that transition, as non-authoritative input data regardless of authentication or labelling, regardless of whether the input identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, and regardless of whether adoption of that candidate condition is subsequently confirmed by the evaluation.
This is to be distinguished from an arrangement in which an operator selects a target state and the system adopts it, and equally from an arrangement in which an operator activates an automatic or scheduled mode and the system thereafter executes a previously stored operator-selected target state at a nominated time. In each of those arrangements the state adopted originates in a human selection of that state. In the present invention the state adopted originates in contemporaneous evaluation of the predetermined conditions and of any then-current data used for the determination, rather than from execution of a previously selected target state. A prior human selection of a candidate condition of the defined set may participate in that evaluation as non-authoritative evidence, but is neither sufficient by itself nor an authoritative prerequisite for adoption of the resulting governing state.
In embodiments employing premises-derived evidence, it follows that the system (100) determines the governing operative premises state on a public holiday, during an unscheduled closure, during an extended working period, during an unplanned absence, and following an equipment failure or power interruption, in each case from the condition of the premises then obtaining, without a person having selected the state and without a person having enabled a mode in which the state would be selected.
Method (200)
In an aspect of the present disclosure, a method (200) is provided, performed by a centralised or distributed electronic-control arrangement including physical processing hardware, for automatically determining an operative condition of a premises and coordinating public-status and private-security operations based on that condition.
The method (200) comprises accessing one or more predetermined conditions; receiving, when used, at least one of sensor data from one or more premises sensors (110) and premises-associated input data through a premises-associated data-input interface (112); automatically determining, from evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions alone or together with the received data, a governing operative premises condition selected from a defined set of two or more operative conditions, the defined set comprising at least an accessible-associated condition, being an accessible state, and a secured-associated condition, being a secured state; providing a public-status output; and performing at least one security operation, the governing operative premises condition constituting a common causal control input for both.
With reference to Fig. 2, in an illustrated embodiment, the method (200) comprises the steps of accessing one or more predetermined conditions (202); receiving sensor data and premises-associated input data, when used (204); classifying each human-associated input used in the automatic determination as non-authoritative evidence for that determination (206); preventing a target-state selection field, instruction, or command value from use as a direct authoritative state-setting value, including by discarding, masking, or invalidating the field, or by retaining and routing the field without authoritative effect as candidate-condition data for evaluation (208); evaluating the one or more predetermined conditions alone or, when received data is used, together with the received data (210); determining the governing operative premises condition (212); writing the controlled state representation exclusively via the validated automatic state-determination pathway (214); retaining the governing condition until a corresponding predetermined condition is satisfied (216); providing the public-status output (218); and performing the at least one security operation (220). The steps (202) to (220), as applicable, are repeated during continuous automatic operation.
The steps of the method (200) may be performed wholly by one or more premises-resident computing resources, wholly by one or more cloud servers or cloud-based computing platforms accessed via a communication interface (130), or by a combination of premises-resident, gateway, edge, and remote computing resources. Where the method (200) is performed by a cloud-based computing platform, the receiving, determining, and output-governing steps are performed upon the infrastructure of that platform.
Controller, server, or computing platform embodiment
In an aspect of the present disclosure, a controller, server, or computing platform is provided, comprising physical processing hardware comprising one or both of a processor (104) operatively coupled to a memory (106) and logic circuitry adapted to operate without execution of stored instructions.
The controller, server, or computing platform is adapted to access or receive determination information comprising one or more of a predetermined condition, sensor data, premises-associated input data, and a determination result generated elsewhere; and to perform one or both of: determining the governing state or condition; and participating in or operating downstream of a distributed determination of the governing state or condition.
The governing state or condition is selected from a defined set comprising at least an accessible-associated condition, being an accessible state, and a secured-associated condition, being a secured state, or is mapped, according to a predetermined mapping, to a condition of that defined set. Accordingly, where a controller, server, or computing platform maintains a state under a different designation, and that state is mapped to a condition of the defined set for the purpose of governing the public-status output and the at least one security operation, the condition resulting from that mapping is the governing state or condition.

In an embodiment, the controller, server, or computing platform generates, provides, relays, or transmits only one of the public-status output and a control signal governing the at least one security operation, the other being generated by another physical component, device, subsystem, application, service, computing platform, or vendor-supplied component, including one situated within a separate network or administrative domain. In such an embodiment the controller, server, or computing platform participates in a distributed coordination mechanism by which the other output is governed by the same governing state or condition. Such participation may comprise publishing the governing state or condition to a shared controlling-state service subscribed to by the other component; holding or observing a lease in respect of the governing state or condition; transmitting the governing state or condition together with a sequence identifier or version token that the other component validates before acting; participating in a commit protocol of the kind described above; or receiving and honouring the governing state or condition determined and published by the other component. In each case a single governing state or condition governs both outputs, notwithstanding that the two outputs are produced by different components, by different vendors, or in different administrative domains.
In a further embodiment, the controller, server, or computing platform determines, receives, or obtains the governing state or condition but does not itself generate, provide, relay, or transmit either the public-status output or the control signal governing the private security action and alert module (128). The controller, server, or computing platform makes said governing state or condition, or a control representation derived therefrom, available to one or more downstream components and participates in a distributed coordination mechanism by which both outputs remain governed by the same governing state or condition, without either downstream component independently determining or maintaining a competing operative premises state or condition. The distributed coordination mechanism may comprise any coordination mechanism described herein, including a shared controlling-state service, an application-programming-interface or message-bus mechanism, a shared state store, a publish-subscribe mechanism, lease-based coordination, sequence or version validation, a commit mechanism, or a reconciliation mechanism. Accordingly, direct generation, provision, relay, or transmission of either output by the controller, server, or computing platform itself is not required where the governing state or condition determined, received, or obtained by that controller, server, or computing platform causally governs both outputs through one or more downstream components.

In a further embodiment, the state-determination unit comprises a non-volatile storage element adapted to retain the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition across a power interruption.
Further forms of premises sensor (110) and premises-associated input
In an embodiment, the one or more premises sensors (110) comprise at least one of an occupancy-related sensor, a door-contact sensor, a window-contact sensor, a shutter or roller-shutter position sensor, a mechanical switch, a toggle switch, a rocker switch, a pull-cord switch, a push-button, a rotary control, a lighting circuit sensor, an equipment-status sensor, an equipment-operational-state sensor, a utility-monitoring sensor, a utility-consumption meter, an electrical current transformer, a wireless-signal presence detector, a network association detector, an actuator position sensor, and a detector of a human-caused physical event at the premises.
In an embodiment, the premises-associated data-input interface (112) receives premises-associated input data from at least one of a point-of-sale system, a payment terminal, a booking or reservation platform, a staff-attendance or clock-in system, a rostering system, an access-control system, a building-management system, an enterprise resource system, an inventory system, a utility-monitoring system, an equipment-status reporting system, a calendar service, a scheduling service, and a remote or cloud-based service.
In an embodiment, received data is conditioned before evaluation by at least one of debouncing, time-windowed aggregation, buffering, averaging, filtering, and combination of a plurality of recent samples, such that a transient, isolated, or spurious signal does not by itself satisfy a predetermined condition. A debounced, time-windowed, buffered, or aggregated value so produced remains non-authoritative input data and is evaluated in the same manner as an unconditioned value.
In an embodiment, the state exclusivity core (116) determines a human-presence indication and a human-absence indication from the received data, and evaluates each against a corresponding predetermined condition, the human-presence indication tending towards the accessible state and the human-absence indication tending towards the secured state, in each case according to the applicable predetermined condition or conditions.
Further forms of public status indicator (126) and of the indication provided
In an embodiment, the public status indicator (126) comprises at least one of a screen, a monitor, a display panel, a tablet, a smartphone, a smartwatch, a wearable device, a personal device of a person seeking access, a web browser, a browser widget, a mobile application widget, a chatbot or conversational agent, a voice assistant, an audio-output device, a networked endpoint, a digital signage player, and a display of a third-party application, directory, or map service.
In an embodiment, the indication provided comprises at least one of a textual indication, a symbol, an icon, a colour, a numerical indication, a graphical indication, an audible indication, a confidence indication, and an omission-based indication in which the absence of a displayed element itself conveys the governing operative premises state. An omission-based indication is a derived representation of the governing operative premises state and does not constitute a separate state. Such an omission-based indication, and any corresponding machine-readable representation in which the absence of an element or value itself conveys the governing operative premises state, are each referred to herein as an omission-based representation.
In an embodiment, the public-status output comprises a confidence representation or numerical score mapped to the governing operative premises state, including an accessibility-confidence value when an accessible-associated condition is governing. Each score or score range used as premises-status information is mapped to and subordinate to a condition of the defined set and does not independently determine, modify, override, replace, bypass, or transition the governing operative premises state. For example, an accessible-associated public-status output may indicate "Accessible - 92% confidence" without the confidence value constituting a separate operative premises state.
In an embodiment, the public-status output is transmitted as a structured payload through a webhook, an application-programming-interface call, a message queue, a publish-subscribe topic, or a data feed, for downstream rendering by a receiving application, service, directory, map service, or third-party platform.
In an embodiment, the public status indicator (126) or public-output interface generates, encodes, validates, and suppresses an outgoing conveyance according to the governing operative premises state, such that a status-indicating symbol, message, or representation inconsistent with the governing operative premises state is suppressed and is not conveyed. A diagnostic output, a safety-event output, and a security-event output are distinguished from the public-status output and are conveyed to their respective recipients without replacing or contradicting the public-status output.
Further forms of security operation and of alert recipient
In an embodiment, the at least one security operation comprises at least one of activating or deactivating a security function, initiating or terminating a recording function, initiating an escalation sequence, altering an alert priority, altering an alert recipient set, altering a security-resource allocation, altering an access-control configuration, and performing a security-only operation that produces no public-facing indication.
In an embodiment, a security-trigger condition comprises detection of a theft, a burglary, an intrusion, a forced entry, motion within a monitored zone, an unauthorised-access event, opening of a door, window, or shutter, breakage of glass, or tampering with a component of the system (100). Where the governing operative premises state is the secured state, satisfaction of such a condition causes the at least one security operation to be performed. In one embodiment, where the governing operative premises state is the accessible state, satisfaction of such a condition does not cause the at least one security operation to be performed. In a further embodiment, one or more security operations remain active while the governing operative premises state is the accessible state, as described elsewhere herein. In none of these embodiments does satisfaction of the condition determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, one or more security operations remain active while the governing operative premises state is an accessible-associated condition. Such operations may comprise monitoring, recording, restricted-zone protection, access-control operation, a local alert, a lower-priority or non-escalated alert, or another security operation. Determination of an accessible-associated condition does not require deactivation of security functionality. The governing operative premises state may govern whether the security operation is performed or one or more attributes thereof, including enablement, sensitivity, operating mode, priority, recipient, content, type, timing, routing, resource, response, or escalation. In different embodiments, the at least one security operation may be performed only while the secured-associated condition is governing, or may remain active both while the accessible-associated condition is governing and while the secured-associated condition is governing. Performance of a security operation while the premises are accessible does not, by itself, establish or constitute a secured-associated condition or a separately determined competing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, an alert generated by the private security action and alert module (128) is transmitted to at least one of an operator device, a designated recipient, a designated responder, a monitoring centre, a security agency, a police department, a fire department, an emergency medical service, and a neighbour or keyholder designated in a configuration of the system (100). An alert relating to an unauthorised-access event may be transmitted concurrently to a plurality of such recipients according to an escalation configuration.
A single signal, event, or datum may serve two distinct roles, and the two roles are to be distinguished. In its first role it is received data evaluated against the one or more predetermined conditions, and the determination made upon that evaluation may result in a transition of the governing operative premises state. In its second role it is, or contributes to, a security-trigger condition, satisfaction of which causes the at least one security operation to be performed. Satisfaction of the security-trigger condition does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state, and this remains so where the same underlying signal is also evaluated in the first role. By way of illustration, a signal from an intrusion sensor may be evaluated against a predetermined condition, and the resulting determination may establish the secured state; the same signal may separately satisfy a security-trigger condition causing an alert to be generated. The transition, where one occurs, is attributable to the determination and not to satisfaction of the security-trigger condition. The two roles are causally distinct. Satisfaction of the security-trigger condition does not itself determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state, and performance of the security operation is not a prerequisite for evaluation of the indication against the one or more predetermined conditions or for a transition resulting from that evaluation. Conversely, completion of such evaluation or transition is not, merely by reason of the indication serving both roles, a prerequisite for satisfaction of the security-trigger condition. Whether and how the security operation is performed remains governed by the governing operative premises state then obtaining, including any state-dependent enablement or security-operation attribute.
In an embodiment, a safety function of the system (100) is state-independent and operates irrespective of the governing operative premises state, whereas a security function is state-dependent and operates according to the governing operative premises state. A trigger-responsive transmission arising from either function does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
Machine-learning and inferential evaluation
In an embodiment, evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions comprises processor-executed inferential evaluation using a trained model. The model may comprise a decision tree, a random forest, a gradient-boosted ensemble, a support vector machine, a logistic regression model, a Bayesian classifier, a hidden Markov model, a recurrent neural network, a long short-term memory network, a convolutional neural network, a transformer network, or a combination thereof. The model produces a likelihood, confidence, or semantic classification indicative of whether the premises is in operation, and that output is evaluated against a corresponding predetermined condition.
Training data for such a model comprises historical records of the received data described herein, namely time-stamped sensor observations from the one or more premises sensors (110) and premises-associated input records received through the premises-associated data-input interface (112), each associated with a label indicating the condition of the premises then obtaining. Labels may be obtained from historical operating records of the premises, from retrospective annotation, or from a period of supervised commissioning operation. Training methodology comprises partitioning the labelled records into training, validation, and test partitions, fitting model weights by supervised optimisation of a loss function upon the training partition, selecting hyperparameters upon the validation partition, and verifying generalisation upon the test partition.
The resulting model weights and hyperparameters constitute a parameter set that is written to a parameter store before commencement of normal automatic operation. The parameter set may be established at manufacture, at installation, at commissioning, or by a subsequent parameter-update operation performed outside normal automatic operation. In this embodiment, during normal automatic operation the parameter set is not adjusted, adapted, or modified by self-training, online learning, runtime adaptation, reinforcement from outcomes, or federated learning across installations. Accordingly, the determination made at a given time is reproducible from the received data and the parameter set then stored.
In embodiments in which inferential evaluation discriminates transient or spurious patterns more effectively than a fixed threshold applied to a single sensor signal, the inferential evaluation may reduce false transitions and correspondingly reduce false alarms and unnecessary transmissions to a monitoring resource.
It is to be noted that an artificial-intelligence or machine-learning component of the system (100) does not exercise autonomous authority over the governing operative premises state. Its output is an evaluated input, and the governing operative premises state is established by the state exclusivity core (116) upon evaluation of the predetermined conditions.
Analytic output and the subordinate non-authoritative output pathway
An analytic output produced by inferential evaluation, pattern recognition, or statistical processing may be employed in three ways. First, it may be used within the determination itself, as a value evaluated against a corresponding predetermined condition by the state exclusivity core (116) or the state determination logic. Second, it may be supplied as an input to the determination, in the same manner as sensor data or premises-associated input data. Third, it may be supplied through a separate subordinate non-authoritative output pathway.
The subordinate non-authoritative output pathway is distinct from, and forms no part of, the validated automatic state-determination pathway. It conveys the analytic output to a display, a dashboard, a logging service, an operator device, an analytics store, or a remote service, and is subject to access-control logic which prevents the analytic output so conveyed from governing the public-status output or the at least one security operation independently of the governing operative premises state. Where an analytic output is required both for determination and for reporting, the value supplied through the subordinate pathway is a copy, and the copy is not a determinant.
The analytic output may comprise a likelihood or confidence value, a classification, an anomaly score, a digital twin representation of the premises maintained as a computational model of its physical layout, occupancy, and equipment state, a semantic environment model expressing relationships between observed conditions in machine-interpretable form, or an output of autonomous processor-executed logic operating without contemporaneous human involvement. In each case the analytic output is non-authoritative: it does not establish, transition, or override the governing operative premises state. Insofar as the analytic output affects determination of, or governance by, the governing operative premises state, it does so only through evaluation against the predetermined conditions; provision of the analytic output through the subordinate non-authoritative output pathway for reporting, display, logging, or analytics does not constitute a state-setting effect.
A safety analytic remains permitted to cause a state-independent safety action. Detection by an analytic process of a smoke, fire, gas, flood, or medical emergency condition may cause generation of a safety alert or performance of a safety operation irrespective of the governing operative premises state, without determining, modifying, or transitioning that state.
Particular coordination and isolation implementations
In an embodiment, coordination between distributed components is effected by one or more of coordinated application-programming-interface payloads, synchronised command sequences, distributed service states, distributed flags, a consensus state agreed between components, a cloud atomic state store, database locking, an atomic compare-and-swap operation, and a distributed lock manager. Each such mechanism operates upon, or resolves to, the single governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, the unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136) comprises an optical coupler array, physical diode logic gates, or a hardware-implemented first-in-first-out buffer having physically severed back-propagation lines, in each case such that no write-capable electrical path exists from a sensor bus to the protected operative-state store (120).
Distributed operation, failover, and reconciliation
In an embodiment, the system (100) comprises components distributed across separate devices, subsystems, services, or cloud components, and comprises a primary determination resource and a backup determination resource. Upon failure, unavailability, or communication loss affecting the primary resource, a failover or handover to the backup resource occurs, and the backup resource continues determination from the governing operative premises state last established. Upon restoration of the primary resource, control returns and any divergence is reconciled.
In an embodiment, coordination between distributed components is effected by at least one of a lease-based ownership protocol in which exactly one component holds a time-bounded lease to write the controlled state representation, an idempotent update protocol in which a repeated update produces no additional effect, a sequential ordering protocol, an event-sourcing arrangement in which the controlled state representation is derived from an ordered event log, a periodic refresh, and a reconciliation procedure applied upon reconnection.
In an embodiment, where a component is offline or intermittently connected, received data is queued or buffered locally and is supplied for evaluation upon restoration of connectivity. During such a period the component does not adopt a fallback or default condition, and may continue to act upon the governing operative premises state last established only while that state remains consistent with the governing operative premises state then obtaining. In one embodiment, a transition affecting a governed element governed by such a component is not committed while that component is unavailable, and the pre-transition governing operative premises state remains governing for both governed elements until reconciliation is completed. In another embodiment, where a newer governing operative premises state is established while the component remains unavailable, a public-status output provided by that component is suppressed, withheld, or designated unavailable, or a security operation governed through that component is disabled, suppressed, or withheld, until reconciliation. An unreconciled local representation is not permitted to govern the public-status output or the at least one security operation until it has been reconciled to the governing operative premises state. Suppression or withholding during loss of connectivity need not depend upon receipt of a suppression command after connectivity has been lost. In an embodiment, authority of an intermittently connected component to present or apply a state-dependent output is subject to a locally enforceable validity interval, lease, freshness token, heartbeat, expiry time, or time-to-live value that expires unless renewed while connectivity is available, upon expiry of which the component locally suppresses the stale output or presents an unavailable or stale-status indication. In an embodiment in which a locally enforceable validity interval, lease, freshness token, expiry time, or time-to-live value is relied upon to prevent stale governance, commitment of a conflicting newer governing operative premises state for a governed element associated with the intermittently connected component is coordinated with expiration, revocation, fencing, or other invalidation of the authority associated with the earlier representation. Accordingly, the conflicting newer governing state is not permitted to become operative for that governed element while an unreconciled component remains authorised to govern that element according to the earlier state. Such coordination may comprise deferring commitment until the earlier authority expires, obtaining acknowledgement of revocation where communication remains available, preventing use of the earlier representation through an upstream fencing mechanism, or another mechanism that prevents the earlier and newer conditions from independently governing respective governed elements. In another embodiment, suppression is performed by a still-connected upstream gateway, service, application, or rendering platform that ceases delivery or rendering of the stale representation. Where omission of an indication is itself mapped to a condition of the defined set, an outage, stale-data condition, or loss-of-freshness suppression is represented by a distinguishable unavailable, stale, indeterminate, or communication-failure indication and is not interpreted as that omission-based premises condition.
In an embodiment, an inactive, standby, or secondary component maintains a preserved copy of the governing operative premises state for the purpose of continuity, and that preserved copy does not independently govern either output while the component is inactive.
In an embodiment, the state-integrity arrangement operates in a premises-resident hardware implementation, in a distributed implementation across premises equipment and cloud resources, or in a virtualised implementation utilising hardware-assisted virtualisation extensions of a host processor to enforce isolation between an input-processing domain and a state-determination domain, and a write operation to the controlled state representation is permitted exclusively via a validated pathway irrespective of whether that pathway traverses a local interconnect of the premises equipment or a remote network interface.
In an embodiment, the state-integrity arrangement detects an integrity violation, an unauthorised alteration of the controlled state representation, or an unauthorised alteration of a predetermined condition, and generates a corresponding alert and record. Detection of such a violation does not determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
Write path, buffering, and hardware gating
In an embodiment, sensor-domain information is conveyed towards the state-determination domain through a hardware-implemented first-in-first-out buffer, the buffer being write-capable from the sensor domain and read-only from the state-determination domain, such that no write-capable path exists from the sensor domain to the controlled state representation.
