The buffer decouples the timing of the two domains without creating a return path.
In an embodiment, the write-control circuitry (134) performs a read-modify-write operation upon the controlled state representation exclusively under the gating condition established by the validated automatic state-determination pathway, such that a partially completed write is not observable and a concurrent or simultaneous write from another source is refused.
Initialisation, restart, and resumption
In an embodiment, upon initialisation, power-on, restart, or resumption of operation, the system (100) does not adopt a preconfigured fallback or default condition of the defined set. The governing operative premises state last established is retained from a non-volatile storage element, or is re-established by evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions alone or together with then-current time, calendar data, sensor data, premises-associated input data, or any combination thereof. No initialisation event, restart event, resumption trigger, session establishment, session termination, connectivity loss, or connectivity restoration by itself determines, modifies, or transitions the governing operative premises state.
In an embodiment, upon assembly and initial power-on of a kit of parts, the central controller (102) automatically recognises one or more connected premises sensors (110), one or more connected data-input interfaces (112), and one or more connected output elements, by means of a preconfigured device profile, an identification exchange, or an enumeration of a connection bus, and commences automatic determination, either automatically or upon a one-time activation action of the kind described above, and thereafter operates without requiring further user programming for state determination.
Audit record
In an embodiment, an audit memory, event log, audit trail, or sequential record is provided, retained separately from and independently of the controlled state representation. Each record comprises a timestamp, a record identifier, an identification of the received data and the predetermined conditions evaluated, the determination made, and where applicable an identification of a rejected candidate transition, a discarded target-state field, a reclassified or routed candidate-condition field, a refused write attempt, an integrity violation, or a tamper event. The records are sequential and retrievable for review, verification, troubleshooting, and compliance purposes. Writing to or reading from the audit record does not affect, determine, modify, or transition the governing operative premises state.
Collective and unified implementation of the common causal control input
In an embodiment, the common causal control input is collectively implemented by a plurality of control inputs, switches, devices, subsystems, applications, or services that are separately selectable, simultaneously activatable, sequentially evaluated, unified in a single control element, or interfaced across a plurality of components. Where the combined effect of such a plurality determines or governs both the public-status output and the at least one security operation, that plurality constitutes the governing operative premises state, whether the determination is implemented as an explicit stored value, a unified control mechanism, distributed logic, or multiple interacting components, and irrespective of whether the components are supplied by separate vendors. An unreconciled value arising within such a plurality is not permitted to govern either output.
Structural enforcement of the validated pathway
In an embodiment, modification of the governing operative premises state or condition is confined to the validated automatic state-determination pathway by a structural enforcement mechanism comprising at least one of a memory protection unit (132), write-control circuitry (134), a unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136), access-control logic, a protected execution domain, and hardware logic circuitry, such that no pathway outside the validated automatic state-determination pathway is capable of establishing or transitioning the state or condition. The structural enforcement mechanism operates by construction of the pathway rather than by a policy applied to a pathway that would otherwise exist, and therefore, with respect to direct establishment or transition of the controlled state representation outside the validated automatic state-determination pathway, is not bypassed merely by a fault, compromise, or error in a component situated outside that pathway. Such structural restriction prevents an outside component from directly writing or establishing the controlled state representation outside the validated pathway; it does not imply that erroneous or malicious evidential data cannot affect the result of an otherwise authorised evaluation where that data satisfies the applicable predetermined conditions.
Elapsed-time values as evaluated inputs
An elapsed duration, grace period, countdown period, or delay may be measured from a preceding sensor event, a preceding premises-associated input event, a preceding state transition, a preceding communication event, or the absence of an event over an interval, and may be evaluated alone or in combination with at least one other predetermined condition, including a condition derived from the sensor data, the premises-associated input data, a calendar value, a day-of-week value, an equipment-mode value indicating an operating mode of equipment at the premises, a configured logical condition, or any combination thereof. In one embodiment, an inactivity period is evaluated in combination with at least one further predetermined condition, and no transition occurs on the basis of inactivity alone. In another embodiment, the one or more predetermined conditions may comprise a corresponding predetermined condition for the secured-associated condition whose satisfaction is determined, upon evaluation, from a human-absence indication, an inactivity period, or a non-occurrence of activity, alone or in combination with other evaluation data, causing an automatic transition from the accessible-associated condition to the secured-associated condition. Accordingly, activity, inactivity, presence, or absence does not inherently require either transition or retention of the governing operative premises state; the result is determined by evaluation of the applicable predetermined condition or conditions. For avoidance of doubt, an "inactivity period" as used herein may comprise an inactivity-derived indication representing absence or non-occurrence of detected activity over an interval. Depending upon the applicable predetermined condition or conditions, such inactivity period may itself constitute a predetermined condition and may be evaluated alone, or may be evaluated in combination with one or more further predetermined conditions. An elapsed-duration, timer-expiry, countdown, grace-period, or delay condition may likewise be evaluated alone or in combination with one or more other predetermined conditions. During normal automatic operation, while the secured-associated condition is governing, mere occurrence of a human-presence indication, human-activity indication, motion indication, activity event, or other activity-related indication is insufficient, outside evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions, to cause the accessible-associated condition to become governing, whether directly or through one or more intermediate, transitional, partial-access, restricted-access, or other conditions of the defined set. The accessible-associated condition becomes governing only where evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions determines that a corresponding predetermined condition for the accessible-associated condition is satisfied. In a narrower embodiment, where a change from the accessible-associated condition to the secured-associated condition is based on a human-absence indication, an inactivity period, or a non-occurrence of activity, the change further requires satisfaction of at least one additional predetermined condition distinct from, and not satisfied solely by, said indication, inactivity period, or non-occurrence of activity. The additional predetermined condition may comprise at least one of a time-of-day condition, an operating-hours condition, a day-of-week condition, a schedule condition, a calendar condition, and a temporal-window condition.
Operational availability information
In an embodiment, the public status indicator (126) or an electronic transmission interface further provides operational availability information indicating availability or unavailability of at least one of a physical resource associated with the premises, a service capability provided at the premises, an infrastructure function of the premises, and a specific person identified by name, role, or other designator. In a subordinate-output embodiment, the operational availability information described in this subsection is distinct from an operational-availability condition included as a governing member of the defined set. In this subordinate-output embodiment, the underlying availability or unavailability may be determined from sensor data or premises-associated input data, while presentation of the resulting information remains subordinate to the governing operative premises state and does not itself constitute, determine, modify, override, replace, bypass, or independently govern as a separate governing operative premises state. In a distinct embodiment, an operational-availability condition itself forms a condition of the defined set. In that embodiment, when the operational-availability condition is governing, it constitutes the governing operative premises state and governs both governed elements in accordance with the principles described herein.
In the subordinate-output embodiment described above, by way of illustration, the operational availability information may indicate that cash is available at an automated teller machine at the premises, that a particular consulting room is free, that a vehicle is available for rental or use, that a parking space is available, that an equipment unit is available, that a charging bay is available, that a laboratory service is operating, or that a named practitioner, technician, or officer is present and available. Such information may be provided regardless of whether the governing operative premises state is the accessible state or the secured state; for example, a hotel or similar premises operating in the secured state outside walk-in hours may nonetheless provide room-availability information for advance reservation or booking purposes. Such information is determined automatically from the sensor data or the premises-associated input data, and is subordinate to the governing operative premises state. It is an additional derived output that is subordinate to the governing operative premises state and does not constitute, determine, modify, override, replace, bypass, or independently govern as a separate governing operative premises state.
Operating-hours schedule data as evidence
In an embodiment, human-created or human-modified operating-hours schedule data, identifying one or more operating-time intervals, is maintained separately from the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition. Such schedule data does not constitute an executable target-state instruction. It identifies intervals during which the premises is expected to operate; it does not nominate a condition of the defined set to be written at a nominated time, and the system does not execute it as such. In a further embodiment, such schedule data identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set. Adoption of the identified candidate condition remains subject to contemporaneous evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions together with then-current sensor data or premises-associated input data, and the schedule data does not, by itself, compel adoption of the candidate condition it identifies.
Where such schedule data identifies one or more operating-time intervals without identifying, encoding, or being associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, the governing operative premises state or condition is automatically determined by contemporaneous machine evaluation of the operating-hours schedule data against a then-current time value, either without requiring sensor data or premises-associated input data or together with an event-derived temporal value or at least one of the sensor data and the premises-associated input data. Where such schedule data identifies, encodes, or is associated with a candidate condition of the defined set, adoption of that candidate condition remains subject to evaluation of at least one further evaluated condition or datum distinct from both the schedule data and the then-current time, such that variation in the further evaluated condition or datum is capable of causing the candidate condition to be adopted, rejected, deferred, or replaced.
The distinction is one of causation rather than of appearance. In an arrangement in which an operator selects a target condition and nominates a time for its adoption, the condition adopted at that time is the condition the operator selected, and the machine writes it. In the present embodiment the schedule data is one datum evaluated among the predetermined conditions at the time of determination, and the condition that results is the condition the evaluation yields. Accordingly, where further evaluation data is available and applicable under the one or more predetermined conditions, the evaluation may yield a condition differing from that implied by the schedule; where such evaluation data indicates that the schedule is stale, incorrect, or overtaken by events, the determination is not bound by the schedule.
Upon determination of the secured state or secured-associated condition, the private security action and alert module (128) performs the at least one security operation and the public status indicator (126) indicates that the premises is secured, each being governed by the same determination.
Coordination of a plurality of control inputs into a single governing control representation
In an embodiment, where the common causal control input is collectively implemented by a plurality of control inputs, switches, devices, subsystems, services, rules, processing elements, or distributed components, implemented within or across one or more of the input acquisition subsystem (108), the premises sensors (110), the premises-associated data-input interface (112), and the central controller (102) or electronic-control arrangement, or by control inputs received from an external system interfaced with the system (100), the state exclusivity core (116) or the state determination logic coordinates that plurality to form a single governing control representation corresponding to the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition.
The single governing control representation so formed governs both the public-status output and the at least one security operation. No member of the plurality, and no combination of members short of the coordinated whole, independently governs either output. This applies irrespective of whether the members are separately selectable, simultaneously activatable, sequentially evaluated, unified within a single control element, or supplied by separate vendors, and irrespective of whether the plurality is implemented within one device or across several.
Generation, validation, and suppression of an outgoing premises-status representation
In an embodiment, the public status indicator (126) or public-output interface generates, exclusively from the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, each status-indicating field, value, symbol, code, or content element of an outgoing premises-status representation that is configured or encoded, according to a predetermined status mapping, to indicate the governing state or condition current at the respective transmission or presentation.
The predetermined status mapping associates each condition of the defined set with the corresponding field values, symbols, codes, or content elements to be used in the outgoing representation. A representation intended for a directory service, a map service, a mobile application, or a third-party platform may employ a mapping specific to that recipient, and the several mappings all derive from the same governing state or condition.
As part of transmitting or presenting the outgoing premises-status representation, the public status indicator (126), the public-output interface, or an electronic transmission interface forming part of or operatively coupled thereto validates each status-indicating field, value, symbol, code, or content element against the governing state or condition then current. Where a field, value, symbol, code, or content element is detected as inconsistent with the governing state or condition, it is replaced with the value corresponding to that state or condition according to the predetermined status mapping, or the outgoing representation is suppressed and is not transmitted or presented. A stale, cached, queued, or previously composed representation is thereby prevented from conveying a condition other than the governing one.
A diagnostic message, a safety-event message, and a security-event message are not status-indicating fields of the premises-status representation, and are conveyed to their respective recipients according to their own conditions without being replaced or suppressed by the foregoing validation.
Forms of predetermined condition
A predetermined condition evaluated by the state exclusivity core (116) or the state determination logic, or by the state continuity core (118), may comprise at least one of a real-time-clock condition, a time-of-day schedule, a calendar condition, a sensor-derived condition, a premises-associated-input-derived condition, a financial-transaction-derived condition, an occupancy condition, an equipment-operation condition, an event-derived condition, a threshold condition, a logical condition, and any combination thereof. A sensor-derived condition is a condition expressed in terms of data received from the one or more premises sensors (110); a premises-associated-input-derived condition is a condition expressed in terms of data received through the premises-associated data-input interface (112); a financial-transaction-derived condition is a condition expressed in terms of a financial transaction associated with the premises.
Parameter storage and the validated parameter-update pathway
Where a parameter, weight, threshold, decision logic, or model logic used in determining the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition is maintained as stored or updateable data, it may be held in a protected parameter-storage region having controlled write access. In that embodiment, the protected parameter-storage region is maintained separately from any storage location or representation maintaining the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, including the protected operative-state store (120). Accordingly, application of a parameter update does not, by itself, write to or transition the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition.
In a first embodiment, the parameter, weight, threshold, decision logic, or model logic is fixed before commencement of normal automatic operation and is not modified by online learning, runtime adaptation, federated learning, or self-training during normal automatic operation. In a second embodiment, the one or more predetermined conditions are fixed at manufacture or during an initial configuration phase and require no configuration during normal automatic operation, or are adjusted from historical data only during that initial configuration phase.
In a third embodiment, the system (100) is adapted to update at least one predetermined condition, or at least one constituent parameter, weight, threshold, decision logic, or model logic thereof, through online learning, runtime adaptation, federated learning, self-training, or an administrative update. Any such update is performed or controlled only by the state exclusivity core (116) or the state determination logic, or through a validated parameter-update pathway. The validated parameter-update pathway is distinct from the validated automatic state-determination pathway, and writes only to the protected parameter-storage region.
Receipt, validation, or storage of a parameter update does not by itself cause a transition of the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition. An updated parameter takes effect upon the next determination performed by evaluation of the predetermined conditions, and the condition then determined is the condition that evaluation yields. A parameter update is therefore an update to the criteria of evaluation and not an instruction as to the outcome of evaluation.
In a fourth embodiment, a human-provided adjustment of a predetermined condition or of a constituent parameter thereof is performed in a configuration, maintenance, or administrative mode distinct from normal automatic operation. Such an adjustment does not constitute online learning or runtime adaptation. It does not directly establish, select, or transition the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, and determination subsequent to the adjustment remains automatic.
By way of illustration, an operator may raise a threshold at which a change in electrical load is treated as indicative of operation of the premises. That adjustment alters the criterion against which the received data is evaluated. It does not tell the system that the premises is accessible or secured, and the condition determined after the adjustment is that yielded by evaluating the received data against the adjusted criterion.
Further aspects of distributed operation
A primary-backup arrangement may be employed, in which a primary determination resource performs determination during normal operation and a backup determination resource assumes that function upon failure, unavailability, or communication loss. Interaction between the primary and backup resources is effected by a lease, a heartbeat, a quorum, or an equivalent coordination protocol, and upon restoration the two are reconciled to a single governing operative premises state.
Transmittable representations
A representation of the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition may be rendered transmittable by encoding it into a structured payload, a message, a datagram, a record, or a document suitable for conveyance through the communication interface (130). A transmittable representation so produced is a derived representation of the governing state or condition, is generated exclusively from it, and does not constitute a separate governing state or condition.
Instruction storage in the controller, server, or computing platform
Where the controller, server, or computing platform comprises one or more processors operatively coupled to one or more memories, the one or more memories store processor-executable instructions which, when executed, cause the controller, server, or computing platform to perform the functions described herein. Where the controller, server, or computing platform comprises programmable logic circuitry, electronic control circuitry, or hardware logic circuitry, that circuitry is configured to perform those functions without requiring execution of instructions by a programmed processor, and no memory storing processor-executable instructions is required for that purpose.
Electronic-control arrangement
The functions described herein are performed by an electronic-control arrangement, implemented centrally or in a distributed manner, comprising physical processing hardware. The electronic-control arrangement comprises one or more of the central controller (102), a processor (104) operatively coupled to a memory (106), firmware executable by physical processing hardware, programmable logic circuitry, electronic control circuitry, hardware logic circuitry, and distributed computing hardware. Accordingly, the central controller (102) is one embodiment of the electronic-control arrangement, and a reference herein to the central controller (102) performing a function is to be understood as a reference to that function being performed by the electronic-control arrangement, whether the arrangement is embodied as a single controller at the premises, as a plurality of cooperating controllers, or as a combination of premises-resident and remote or cloud-based computing resources.
In an embodiment the electronic-control arrangement comprises no processor executing stored instructions, the functions being realised in programmable logic circuitry or hardware logic circuitry. In a further embodiment the electronic-control arrangement is wholly remote from the premises, only input and output elements being located at the premises.
Predetermined conditions and their representation
The one or more predetermined conditions are stored, encoded, configured, or otherwise represented in or accessible to the electronic-control arrangement. They may be held as a memory region of the memory (106), a dedicated storage element, a configuration store, a register or register file, a look-up table, a database, a file, a firmware-resident representation, a hard-coded representation embodied within programmable logic circuitry or hardware logic circuitry, a representation held by a remote or cloud-based service, or as logic whose structure embodies the condition without a separately retrievable stored value. Accordingly, a separately identifiable store for the one or more predetermined conditions is not essential, and the requirement is satisfied wherever the one or more predetermined conditions are available to the determination for evaluation.
State continuity core (118)
The state continuity core (118) is adapted to preserve continuity of the governing operative premises state. Continuity may be preserved by retaining the governing operative premises state, by re-determining the governing operative premises state from the one or more predetermined conditions, or by a combination thereof; and the state continuity core (118) permits an automatic transition from the governing operative premises state only upon satisfaction of at least one corresponding predetermined condition.
The retention-based implementation described above is one embodiment of the state continuity core (118). In a further embodiment, continuity is preserved without persistent storage of the governing operative premises state itself, the governing operative premises state being recomputed at each determination from the one or more predetermined conditions together with any then-current, retained, recoverable, or otherwise available evaluation data or state-determination history required by those conditions, such that the same condition of the defined set continues to be governing so long as the conditions yielding it continue to be satisfied. Where information required by the applicable predetermined conditions is temporarily unavailable, unavailability of that information does not by itself cause adoption of another condition of the defined set; in an embodiment, re-determination or a state-dependent output may be deferred, withheld, or designated unavailable until sufficient information becomes available. In each case the governing operative premises state does not lapse, decay, expire, revert, or default merely by passage of time independently of satisfaction of a corresponding predetermined condition, nor by the absence of received data, a communication interruption, a session termination, a device restart, or a service restart.
In a narrower embodiment, neither a human-presence indication, a human-absence indication, nor an inactivity period, by itself, causes a transition of the governing operative premises state. In each case the indication is one input among others, evaluated together with at least one further predetermined condition.
State-integrity arrangement and the controlled operative-state representation
The system (100) comprises a state-integrity arrangement comprising a controlled operative-state representation corresponding to the governing operative premises state. The expressions controlled operative-state representation and controlled state representation are used interchangeably herein, and a reference to one includes the other.
The controlled operative-state representation is maintained physically or logically, and persistently or transiently, by one or more physical or logical components implemented separately or collectively. It may be maintained as a stored variable, an atomic memory value, a register or latch, a value recomputed at each determination without persistent storage, a derived condition, or a distributed representation across a plurality of components. Accordingly, a separately identifiable store is not essential, and the requirement is satisfied wherever the governing operative premises state is represented in a form upon which the system acts.
Establishment, modification, or replacement of the controlled operative-state representation, resulting from an automatically determined transition during normal automatic operation, is permitted only as a result of a validated automatic state-determination pathway comprising the state exclusivity core (116) and the state continuity core (118); a separately validated human-authority pathway may exist for a non-automatic transition, while the sensor data and the premises-associated input data are permitted to participate in determination of the governing operative premises state but do not, outside the validated automatic state-determination pathway, directly establish, transition, modify, override, replace, or corrupt that representation.
The protected operative-state store (120) is an embodiment of the representation-providing aspect of the state-integrity arrangement, the state-integrity arrangement additionally providing the restriction. In a further embodiment the representation and restriction functions are performed by a single component, or collectively by the electronic-control arrangement, without a separately identifiable store or restriction mechanism. The mechanisms described above in relation to the state-integrity arrangement, including the memory protection unit (132), the write-control circuitry (134), the unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136), access-control logic, a protected memory region, a protected execution domain, and cryptographic state-transition validation logic, are each embodiments of the restriction so imposed.
The governed elements and their coupling
The public-status output and the at least one security operation are together referred to herein as the governed elements. The governing operative premises state constitutes a common causal control input for both governed elements, such that neither governed element is independently governed by a separately determined or maintained competing operative premises state or condition.
In an embodiment the controlled operative-state representation is used to generate a public-status control output governing the public status indicator (126) and a private-security control output governing the private security action and alert module (128), such generation being performed by the electronic-control arrangement without requiring a separately identifiable component for that purpose. In a further embodiment no intermediate control output is generated, and the public status indicator (126) and the private security action and alert module (128) are each governed directly by the controlled operative-state representation, whether by program code reading that representation and driving both output paths, by hardware logic fanning out a state signal, or by a state message published once and consumed by both output paths. In each case a single governing operative premises state governs both governed elements. For avoidance of doubt, correspondence of two representations to the same condition of the defined set does not, merely by coincidental equality of independently governing results, establish the common causal control relationship described herein. Where a plurality of representations, variables, services, or distributed evaluations collectively constitutes the governing operative premises state, the members of that plurality derive from, map to, are validated against, are reconciled to, or are otherwise coordinated as one logical governing state or condition before independently governing respective governed elements.
In a redundant-determination embodiment, coordination as one logical governing operative premises state or operative premises condition may be established by construction through deterministic evaluations performed by separate processing elements using a common identified input snapshot or a common ordered input sequence, consistent versions of the applicable predetermined conditions and parameters, and, where relevant, a consistent initial state, evaluation history, and temporal reference, for example by the deterministic orchestration pipeline or message-broker ordering protocol described herein. The arrangement controls the applicability of the resulting determinations to the respective governed elements so that inconsistent results, or results belonging to unreconciled evaluation epochs (that is, determinations derived from different input snapshots, input sequences, or rule or parameter versions and not reconciled before governing), do not independently govern those elements. Such an arrangement need not require direct communication between the evaluating processing elements or a separately stored common-state variable. The evaluations collectively implement determination of one logical governing operative premises state or operative premises condition, and their separate execution does not, by itself, make their results independently governing competing conditions. Mere equality of results, without the foregoing common determination relationship or another coordination mechanism described herein, is insufficient. Evaluations using different predetermined conditions or different evaluation data may nevertheless contribute to the same governing operative premises state or operative premises condition where their results are validated or reconciled before governing the respective governed elements.
Where the term public-status control output is used herein, it denotes the value by which the public-status output is governed; where no separately identifiable coordination module is present, that value is the controlled operative-state representation itself or a value derived exclusively from it. The same applies to the private-security control output in relation to the at least one security operation.
In a scope-correlated coordination embodiment, each public-accessibility candidate value and private-security candidate value is associated with a common premises-scope identifier and an evaluation epoch identifier. The electronic coordination arrangement validates that the candidate values are derived from, map to, or are reconciled to the same governing operative premises state or operative premises condition for that premises scope and evaluation epoch before either value is permitted to govern its respective governed element. Where a candidate value is scope-mismatched or epoch-mismatched, that is, where it has a mismatched scope identifier or a mismatched evaluation epoch, or where it is unreconciled in that it cannot be so validated or reconciled, the arrangement prevents transmission or presentation of the corresponding public-status output and prevents application of the corresponding private-security control signal until reconciliation is completed; the prior governing operative premises state or operative premises condition remains operative, or a distinguishable unavailable, indeterminate, or communication-failure condition of the defined set is provided.
In a composite-zone embodiment, where the premises comprises zones, floors, units, or sections, the governing operative premises state or operative premises condition comprises a composite representation having respective zone-associated constituents determined and reconciled as one logical governing state or condition. A public-status output applicable to the premises is generated by a predetermined aggregation mapping of that composite representation, and each zone-associated private-security control signal is generated by a predetermined mapping of that same composite representation. Neither the aggregation value nor a zone-associated security value is permitted to govern its respective governed element from an independently determined, unreconciled, or scope-mismatched representation.
Presentation of the public-status output
The public-status output is configured for presentation through a publicly accessible output channel, whether at the premises or remotely rendered, in any human-perceptible form, including an electronic or digital presentation through an application, a website, a directory or map service, a messaging output, a voice-assistant response, or any other electronic or digital medium.
A channel is publicly accessible where the public-status output conveyed through it is available to a person seeking access to, or services from, the premises, including a customer, visitor, client, patient, or delivery agent, and is not confined to an authorised security-system user. Presentation through such a channel remains publicly accessible whether access to the particular presentation is authenticated or unauthenticated; accordingly, a customer signing in to a retail application, a patient signing in to a clinic booking service, or a delivery agent signing in to a logistics application each receives the public-status output through a publicly accessible channel. A monitoring console, an administrative dashboard, or an authenticated operator session provided for the purpose of administering the system (100) is not a publicly accessible output channel.
Independent safety and emergency operation
Any security-trigger condition or safety condition may arise independently of the governing operative premises state and may affect whether or how a security operation or a safety operation is performed, without determining, modifying, overriding, replacing, bypassing, or transitioning the governing operative premises state. Accordingly, a smoke, fire, gas, flood, or medical emergency detection function required by applicable safety codes to operate independently may be provided in the system (100) and may act irrespective of the governing operative premises state, and its independent operation does not remove the system (100) from the architecture described herein.
Any safety-related or emergency-related public indication, message, overlay, or notification neither constitutes an independently determined or maintained competing operative premises state or condition, nor prevents the governing operative premises state from constituting the common causal control input for the governed elements. Such an indication is presented in addition to, or in place of, the ordinary presentation of the public-status output for the duration of the condition concerned, and upon cessation of that condition the ordinary presentation resumes, corresponding to the governing operative premises state then obtaining.
Spectrum of embodiments
The system (100) may be embodied at a range of scales and topologies. In a first embodiment, all functional elements are contained within a single premises-resident device coupled to one or more premises sensors (110) and to a public status indicator (126) mounted at the entrance of the premises. In a second embodiment, the input acquisition subsystem (108) and the public status indicator (126) are premises-resident and the determination is performed by a remote or cloud-based computing resource accessed through the communication interface (130). In a third embodiment, the determination is performed by an edge gateway at the premises and the public-status output is transmitted to a directory or map service for downstream rendering. In a fourth embodiment, the functional elements are distributed across a plurality of services of a cloud platform, including a serverless or containerised execution environment, and the controlled state representation is maintained by a shared controlling-state service. In a fifth embodiment, the system (100) is supplied as a kit of parts for assembly at the premises.
The public-status output may be embodied as a physical indication at the premises, as a machine-readable representation transmitted for downstream rendering, or as both. The at least one security operation may be embodied as an on-premises actuation, as a message to a remote monitoring resource, or as both. Each combination of the foregoing is contemplated.
TECHNICAL PROBLEM, TECHNICAL SOLUTION AND TECHNICAL EFFECT
The technical problem addressed by the present invention is a problem of electronic premises control systems, arising from physical sensors, electronic control circuits, memory-resident state values, and distributed communication paths. It comprises, first, the maintenance of two independently determined state values, one governing a public-facing indication and one governing a security function, with the consequence that the two may diverge and a shadow-state condition arise; second, the direct writing of a stored state value by a sensor-processing component, a data-input component, a communication component, or an application service without passage through a controlled determination path, with the consequence that an erroneous, delayed, or malformed signal may corrupt the state; third, the execution at a nominated time of a stored human-selected target-state instruction, with the consequence that the condition adopted is the condition a person selected earlier rather than the condition yielded by evaluation at the time of adoption, and ceases to correspond to the premises where circumstances have changed; and fourth, in a distributed or cloud-hosted deployment, the maintenance of replicated or cached state values that may be updated asynchronously, with the consequence that different components act upon different states.
The technical solution, in its broadest form, comprises automatic determination of a single governing operative premises state or operative premises condition from one or more predetermined conditions, and use of that governing state or condition as a common causal control input for the public-status output and for at least one private-security operation, while preventing an independently governed competing operative premises state or condition from governing either.
In one hardware-enforced embodiment, the technical solution further comprises an architecture in which a single controlled state representation is maintained within a protected operative-state store (120); in which modification of that representation is confined by the state-integrity arrangement to a validated automatic state-determination pathway comprising a state exclusivity core (116) and a state continuity core (118); in which a memory protection unit (132), write-control circuitry (134), and a unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136) restrict, at the hardware level, the paths by which the representation may be written; in which both the public-status control output and the private-security control output are derived from that same representation; and in which an electronic coordination arrangement (150) reconciles candidate values and enforces a transactional state-transition barrier before either output is released.
This configuration produces technical effects that are not achieved by a general-purpose computer executing software alone in the conventional manner. The unidirectional or logically filtered data channel (136), in its physical embodiment comprising an optical coupler, a diode-configured logic element, or a conductor arrangement in which a back-propagation line is absent or severed, physically eliminates the electrical path by which a sensor-domain component could write the controlled state representation; no arrangement of program instructions can eliminate a path that exists in the circuit. The write-control circuitry (134) gates the write operation by a hardware enable signal, so that a write attempt originating outside the determination pathway is refused by the circuit and not merely declined by a program that could itself be subverted. The memory protection unit (132) enforces the restriction at a privilege level below that at which application software executes. In the physical unidirectional embodiment, the sensor-domain connection terminates at an evidence-receiving buffer or input of the state-determination domain and exposes no address, data-write, write-enable, memory-mapped write, or equivalent control connection from the sensor domain to the controlled state representation. The state-determination logic obtains sensor-domain information only as evidence from that buffer or input, and modification of the controlled state representation is performed by the state-determination domain, or by the write-control circuitry (134) acting under its gating condition, after evaluation of the one or more predetermined conditions.
The technical effects so produced comprise the following. The common-state architecture prevents divergence between the public-facing indication and the security function arising from independently determined competing operative premises states or conditions, in a single-device embodiment by construction and in a distributed embodiment by the coordination, reconciliation, and, where implemented, staged-commit mechanisms described herein. Where non-volatile retention is employed, the state is deterministically retained across power interruption, communication loss, session termination, and restart; where the state is recomputed at each determination without persistent storage, continuity is preserved by re-determination from the predetermined conditions together with any then-current, retained, recoverable, or otherwise available input data or state-determination history required by those conditions. In a hardware-enforced embodiment, direct state corruption by an erroneous, delayed, malformed, or malicious signal attempting to establish, modify, or write the controlled state representation from the sensor or communication domain outside the validated automatic state-determination pathway is prevented at circuit level; in a firmware- or software-enforced embodiment the equivalent restriction is enforced by the privilege or access-control mechanisms described. In an embodiment employing premises-derived evidence, the state corresponds to the operating condition of the premises rather than to a stored assumption about it; in a schedule-evaluating embodiment the state is the result of contemporaneous evaluation rather than of executing a previously selected target state. In embodiments employing input conditioning, inferential evaluation, or state-dependent alert routing, false alarms and unnecessary transmissions to a monitoring resource may be reduced, with a corresponding reduction in network and processing load, and distributed components operate upon a single reconciled state.
Accordingly, the invention improves the reliability, security, and deterministic operation of premises control systems beyond the normal functioning of a programmed computer, and is not a scheme, rule, or method for performing a mental act, nor a presentation of information as such, nor a computer program as such.
RESERVATION
The embodiments described herein are illustrative and are not exhaustive of the invention. The invention is limited only by the claims. No statement, example, embodiment, drawing, or description contained in this specification shall be construed to narrow the claims unless the narrowing is expressly stated. Where an element is described as comprising a plurality of alternatives, each alternative is disclosed independently and, where technically compatible, in combination with one or more other alternatives. Where a function is described as performed by a named element, performance of that function by a differently named element, by a combination of elements, or by a distributed arrangement of elements is contemplated.
Terms such as “comprising”, “including”, and “having” are used in an open sense and do not exclude further elements or steps. The expression “at least one of” followed by a list denotes any one of the listed items and any combination of them. Reference numerals in the claims are for convenience of reference and do not limit the claims. ,

title:
“HASTRA” – A PNEUMATIC-BASED PROSTHETIC ARM 
WITH HUMAN–COMPUTER INTERACTION (HCI) INTEGRATION
abstract:
Assistive healthcare technology has gained significant importance in improving the quality of life for individuals with limb loss. Prosthetic arms are designed to replicate human hand functions such as grasping, holding, and manipulating objects. However, conventional prosthetic systems rely on rigid motor-driven mechanisms, which make them heavy, expensive, and less adaptable to natural human movement. 
This invention proposes a pneumatic-based prosthetic arm that utilizes soft robotic actuators to mimic natural muscle movement. The system integrates Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) through lectromyography (EMG) signals, enabling intuitive control of the prosthetic device based on user muscle activity. The EMG signals are acquired from the user’s forearm and undergo preprocessing, feature extraction, and lassification using machine learning techniques to identify gestures such as open, close, and relax. The classified signals are processed using an embedded Arduino-based control system, which regulates airflow through solenoid valves connected to a pneumatic actuation system. The pneumatic actuators expand and contract using compressed air, resulting in smooth and natural finger movements. The proposed system is designed to be lightweight, cost-effective, and modular compared 
to existing prosthetic solutions. It eliminates the need for complex mechanical components while maintaining functional efficiency. The prototype demonstrates improved user interaction, reduced cost, and enhanced adaptability, making it a scalable and practical solution for assistive prosthetic technology.
specification:
Limb loss is a critical global health challenge affecting millions of individuals, with a profound impact on independence, productivity, and quality of life. Statistical data indicates that access to functional prosthetic devices remains severely limited in low- and middle-income countries due to the prohibitive cost and complexity of commercially available myoelectric prosthetics. HASTRA proposes a cost-effective and technically viable alternative to address this unmet need. 
The invention presents a pneumatic-based prosthetic arm that uses soft actuators to replicate natural finger motion. The user’s muscle activity is captured through surface EMG sensors on the forearm. These signals undergo noise filtering and feature extraction, after which a trained machine learning model classifies the intended gesture in real time. The classified command is transmitted to an Arduino microcontroller, which drives solenoid valves to regulate compressed air flow into the pneumatic finger actuators, causing bending or relaxation of the rosthetic fingers. The hand structure is fabricated using 3D-printed lightweight materials (PLA), with finger segments designed to ccommodate soft pneumatic actuator channels. This approach liminates 
the need for heavy rigid motors and complex mechanical transmissions, resulting in a lightweight and compliant prosthetic structure. In terms of performance, the system targets successful classification of three basic gestures (open, close, relax) with high accuracy, demonstrating smooth and natural finger movements through pneumatic actuation. The prototype achieves this at an estimated cost of ₹20,000–₹25,000, 
representing a significant cost reduction compared to commercially available myoelectric prosthetics (₹16 lakhs–₹58 lakhs). Looking ahead, the system can be extended to include a wider vocabulary of hand gestures, wireless control interfaces, tactile feedback sensors, and miniaturized portable air supply systems. The modular design of ASTRA ensures that individual components can be upgraded independently, providing a scalable foundation for future advancements in intelligent and accessible prosthetic technology.  , C , C , C
claims:
1. A pneumatic-based prosthetic arm system comprising: (a) a 3D-printed modular hand skeleton with integrated soft pneumatic actuator channels for each finger; (b) an EMG signal acquisition module comprising surface electrodes placed on the residual forearm; (c) a signal conditioning circuit for noise filtering and feature extraction 
from raw EMG signals; (d) a machine learning classification module trained to classify basic hand gestures including open, close, and relax; (e) an Arduino-based embedded microcontroller that receives classified gesture commands and generates corresponding actuator control signals; and (f) a pneumatic actuation assembly comprising an air pump, solenoid valves, and a driver circuit, which regulates compressed air flow to produce finger bending and relaxation motion 
2. A method for controlling a prosthetic arm using myoelectric signals, wherein a user’s muscle activity is captured by surface EMG sensors on the forearm, preprocessed through filtering and feature extraction, classified into a gesture command by a trained machine learning model, and used to drive pneumatic actuators via an Arduino microcontroller and solenoid valve assembly. 
3. The system of claim 1, wherein the soft pneumatic actuators are fabricated from flexible silicone or elastomeric materials, and are embedded within the 3D-printed finger structure to produce compliant, muscle-like bending motion through pneumatic inflation and deflation. 
4. The system of claim 1, wherein the machine learning classification module uses features including Root Mean Square (RMS), Mean Absolute Value (MAV), and Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR) extracted from windowed EMG signal segments to classify gestures in real time with high accuracy.
 5. The system of claim 1, wherein the entire prosthetic system is designed to be lightweight, modular, and cost-effective, with a target manufacturing cost of ₹20,000–₹25,000 INR, making it accessible to a broader population compared to commercially available myoelectric prosthetics.
6. The method of claim 2, wherein the EMG signal processing pipeline includes bandpass filtering to remove noise, envelope detection for signal smoothing, and sliding window feature extraction for real-time gesture prediction.

title: A SYSTEM FOR A COMPANION ROBOT
abstract: A system 100 for a robot 200 includes a pan-tilt head 202 including a pair of cameras 204, a microphone array 206, and a speaker 208; a driving mechanism 132 including motion controller 138 to move the robot 200 automatically; and a controller 110 leverages accelerated graphic processing unit (GPU). The controller 110 including at least one database, one or more processors coupled with memory 108, and the one or more processors to receive real-time images, audio, and motion data to fuse employing single embedded edge AI platform; pre-processing captured images for object detection and recognition employing machine learning model; form episodic and semantic memory 128 representations from perceptual data for recall-based reasoning; communicate with user via voice assistant and screen to control the robot 200 using wireless transceiver; and perform localization and 3-D mapping along with compensating head motion to navigate the robot 200 marinating low-latency privacy preserving local inference.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD	
[0001]	The present disclosure relates generally to the technical field of robotics. In particular, it pertains to a system for a companion robot to perceive, memorise and make decisions and provide low-latency, context aware conversation, and navigational behaviour in indoor environments.

BACKGROUND
[0002]	Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present disclosure. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed disclosure, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art.
[0003]	In recent years, field of robotics has expanded significantly covering a wide array of applications starting from industrial robotics to social robotics.  Social robots are designed for human interaction, which have gained increasing attention due to their potential roles in different field such as healthcare, elderly care, and various service industries includes education, museum and finance. 
[0004]	This surge in interest has led to extensive research endeavours aimed at enhancing the quality of human-robot interaction by refining robot systems to mimic human-like behaviours and exploring the impact of social attributes on robot dynamics. Existing solutions include smart speakers’ excellent language, vision-language models, and classical navigation systems mapping without semantic/episodic memory. 
[0005]	Recent advancements in this field have focused on improving the multi-model perception, episodic memory, and context-aware reasoning by addressing above issues. One such Patent Document US11151992B2 discloses a context aware interactive robot comprising a camera to capture a plurality of images. A spatial image is generated using a sensor in the system, and a semantic location map is generated using analysed captured images. A natural language input referencing a desired product item is received from a user and the speech recognition result is sent to a reasoning engine to receive one or more commands for the robotic system for performing and feedback to the user is provided based on at least one of the one or more commands.
[0006]	While cited reference generates a spatial map and a semantic location map for navigation and provides feedback to the user, but does not disclose persistent episodic memory across sessions and based explicitly user commands, there is a possibility to provide better robot solution that can address the abovementioned problem.
[0007]	There is, therefore, a need to provide an efficient, talkative, low-latency system architecture for a robotic device that can directly address the shortcomings.

OBJECTS OF THE DISCLOSURE
[0008]	A general object of the present disclosure is to provide a robotic system unifies multimodal perception, spatial memory, and behavioural reasoning deployed entirely on an edge AI platform. 
[0009]	An object of the present disclosure is to provide an efficient, self-driven, cost-effective system and apparatus for self-cleaning of air filter.
[0010]	Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a system for robot with persistent memory, contextual adaptation, and real-time embodied intelligence.
[0011]	Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a robot that can be used for elder care, domestic assistance, hospitality, retail, etc.
[0012]	Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a system for robot where a separate microcontroller governs motor control with emergency stop logic independent of high level AI compute model.

SUMMARY
[0013]	Aspects of the present disclosure relate to the technical field of robotics. In particular, it pertains to a system for a companion robot to perceive, memorise and make decisions and provide low-latency, context aware conversation, and navigational behaviour in indoor environments. More particular, a compact, wheel-based companion robot run primarily on an edge platform with a ROS2 middleware integration enabling stereo depth, object recognition for real-time perception, context-aware memory, audio front end, integrated decision/reasoning to combine speech, vision and map/memory to produce adaptive behaviours for real-time interactions.
[0014]	In an aspect, the disclosure is about a system for a robot includes a pan-tilt head including a pair of cameras to capture real-time images, a microphone array, and a speaker 28 for two-way voice interaction; a driving mechanism including motion controller to move the robot automatically; and a controller leverages accelerated graphic processing unit to perceive and act as decision nodes. The controller including at least one database, one or more processors coupled with a memory, and the memory stores one or more instructions executable by the one or more processors to receive real-time images, audio, and motion data to fuse employing single embedded edge AI platform; pre-processing captured images for object detection and recognition employing machine learning model; form episodic and semantic memory representations from perceptual data for recall-based reasoning; communicate with user via voice assistant and screen to control the robot using wireless transceiver; and perform localization and 3-D mapping along with compensating head motion to navigate the robot marinating low-latency privacy preserving local inference.
[0015]	In an embodiment, the controller is embedded system-on-module working on edge AI computer having Jetson Orin Nano ensures all components interact over ROS2 middleware to have modularity, data synchronization and safety integrity.
[0016]	In an embodiment, the edge AI computer integrates perception, spatial mapping, simultaneous localization and mapping, episodic and semantic memory formation, navigation planning, and context-aware interaction for safe, autonomous operation of the robot. 
[0017]	In an embodiment, the system includes an Arduino UNO microcontroller working long with the controller for real-time motor control, servo synchronization, and safety interlocks which executes a PID control loop using encoder feedback to generate motor PWM signals. 
[0018]	In an embodiment, the simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) module provides coordinates to control movement of the robot employing an inertial measurement unit for continuous estimation of the robot in map. 
[0019]	In an embodiment, the controller processes image and speech data for real-time object detection employing YOLO V8 and convert audio to text, compensating for head or camera motion to maintain accurate perception.	
[0020]	In an embodiment, the each perceptual event includes object detection, personal and speech recognition and converted to a persistent episodic memory.
[0021]	In an embodiment, the persistent episodic memory includes unique identifier, entry type like person/object/utterance, canonical label, timestamp, confidence score, map coordinate, sensor reference, and auxiliary attributes such as colour, approximate size.
[0022]	In an embodiment, the system includes a behavior manager registered on ROS 2 to receive transcribed user utterances, faults, and perception events to explain user intents.
[0023]	In an embodiment, the system compensates head motion for navigating robot by controlling servo angles through re-projected head angles received from the camera ensuring accuracy in depth estimates and map anchoring when the head angle change.

The camera pair is RGB or RGB-D.
[0044]	In an embodiment, the simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) module 134 provides coordinates to control movement of the robot 200 employing an inertial measurement unit (IMU) for continuous estimate of the robot 200 in the map. 
[0045]	In an embodiment, the controller 110 processes image 106 and speech data 104 for real-time object detection employing YOLO V8 and convert audio to text, compensating for head 202 or camera motion to maintain accurate perception.	
[0046]	In an embodiment, the each perceptual event includes object detection, personal and speech recognition and converted to a persistent episodic memory.
[0047]	In an embodiment, the persistent episodic memory 128 includes unique identifier, entry type like person/object/utterance, canonical label, timestamp, confidence score, map coordinate, sensor reference, and auxiliary attributes such as colour, approximate size. The robot 200 differs from prior art in regards of active components reinforced each other. The system 100 operates under a memory first control paradigm where the cognitive controller decides whether incoming perception should become a memory trigger and action or prompt clarification. Visual identity is maintained through embedding based representations rather than relying only on class labels. Retrieved memories can directly generate navigation goals. When perpetual confidence falls below a threshold, the system 100 enters a confirmation state instead of committing uncertain data. This straight coupling enables adaptive behaviour over time rather than isolated module execution.
[0048]	In an embodiment, when the system 100 is energised, it starts the robot 200. The robot 200 executes a boot/initialization sequence in which the microcontroller initializes motor drivers and annunciates odometer; the camera (s) 204 and microphone(s) 206 are brought online and streamed to the compute module, and software nodes for perception, SLAM, memory and behaviour manager register on the middleware bus, for example, ROS2 topics and services. The robot 200 loads stored calibration parameters including camera intrinsic, stereo rectification maps, servo zero positions, and verifies camera sensor 204 alignment. If head angle or sensor offsets exceed defined tolerances, a calibration compensation routine is carried out that updates re-projection parameters for subsequent depth fusion.
[0049]	In an embodiment, during normal operation the robot repeatedly executes a runtime pipeline composed of multiple steps. Initially the system 100 performs sensing and pre-processing. The synchronized stereo frames and microphone-array samples are continuously acquired 112 in perception layer. Audio pre-processing includes voice-activity detection, noise reduction and beam forming to produce an enhanced audio stream and an estimated direction-of-arrival. Video pre-processing includes image demosaicing, rectification using stored stereo parameters and current head angles, and optional temporal smoothing.
[0050]	In an embodiment, for perception and vision, each pre-processed image is submitted to an on-board object detection and recognition module for example, a CNN such as YOLO-class model 114 optimized for edge inference. Each detection the module output include class label, bounding box, detection confidence and image centroid coordinate. Depth at the centroid is computed by fusing stereo disparity or depth sensor output with re-projection corrected for current head pan/tilt angles. A 3-D world coordinate for the detection is computed by transforming the camera-frame coordinates into map/world coordinates using the latest pose estimate from the SLAM subsystem.
[0051]	In an embodiment, for perception and audio, when the robot detects voice activity, beam formed audio is sent to an on-device speech-to-text (STT) module for example, a quantized or small-footprint transformer model. The STT output is time stamped and forwarded to the behaviour/dialog manager. The direction-of-arrival (DoA) output is used concurrently to orient the pan/tilt head toward the speaker to facilitate face/object alignment and to cue gaze behaviour.
[0052]	In an embodiment, the localisation and mapping, a SLAM module fuses wheel odometer, inertial measurements and visual odometer to maintain a metric map and a continuous estimate of the Robot’s pose in the map. The SLAM map provides persistent coordinates that are used to spatially anchor perception outputs.
[0053]	In an embodiment, the system 100 forms memory and perform indexing for each perceptual event including object detection, person recognition, or speech event, is converted to a persistent episodic memory entry having fields including unique identifier, entry type such as person/object/utterance, canonical label, timestamp, confidence score, map coordinate, sensor reference link to stored image/audio snippet, and auxiliary attributes like colour, approximate size. The memory service layer 118 maintains two complementary structures. First, a chronological episodic log and second, a semantic index mapping canonical labels to one or more episodic entries. 
[0054]	In an embodiment, the memory entries are persisted in a lightweight data store (for example, SQLite or JSON-backed store and are subject to retention and pruning policies for example, maximum number of entries or time-based expiration configurable per deployment. The system 100 uses fine-tuned vision language joint embedding predictive architecture (VL JEPA2) model as its core vision backbone. The model generates stable visual embedding that remains consistent across time lighting changes and viewpoint variations. Instead of predicting raw pixels or generating text tokens word-by-word like standard models, it predicts abstract semantic meaning directly in a continuous latent space. These embedding enable reliable memory indexing re-identification and long term visual recall.
[0055]	In an embodiment, the behaviour/dialog manager receives transcribed user utterances and perception events. It parses user intents via rule-based parsing or a small intent classification model and issues queries to the memory service and to live perception feeds. For example intent Recall Location (object_name) triggers a ranked query of the semantic index for object_name, retrieving episodic entries ordered by a composite score computed from recency, detection confidence and spatial relevance. 
[0056]	In an embodiment, the manager applies configurable thresholds, and if the top entry exceeds a confidence threshold, the manager composes a natural language response referencing the retrieved location for example- “I last saw your red mug on the kitchen table at 10:15 AM”. If confidence is low the manager selects a conservative fall back response like- “I’m not sure, would you like me to search the kitchen?”
[0057]	In an embodiment, if the behaviour manager decides to navigate for example, after user confirmation, it issues a navigation goal in map coordinates to the path planner 136 such as example, Nav2. High-level velocity or waypoint commands from the planner are sent to the microcontroller which executes a PID control loop using encoder feedback to generate motor PWM signals for motion control. The microcontroller monitors current, temperature and an emergency stop input, and in case of a fault it halts the robot and notifies the behaviour manager.
[0058]	In an embodiment, as the cameras are mounted on a movable head, the system compensates for head motion by calculating depth and 3-D world coordinates. Servo angles are polled and provided to the re-projection module, bounding box centroids are re-projected using the current camera extrinsic derived from head angles, ensuring depth estimates and map anchoring remain accurate while the head moves.
[0059]	In an embodiment, the system 100 performs memory-anchored query for example- on detecting and recognizing a person labelled “Mr. X” the manager retrieves recent interaction entries for “Mr. X” and selects a greeting appropriate to the time of day and prior interactions.
[0060]	In an embodiment, the system 100 performs confidence handling and failure modes by applying confidence thresholds at multiple stages such as detection, recognition, memory retrieval. When SLAM pose uncertainty exceeds a threshold or lost tracking, the robot suspends navigation commands and initiates a re-localization routine. When STT confidence is low, the manager requests clarification. Safety interlocks on the microcontroller provide emergency stop functionality independent of the edge compute.
[0061]	In an embodiment, the system 100 supports alternative embodiments and heavy language understanding may be optionally offloaded to a cloud LLM interface 130 while retaining local memory and safety-critical loops on-device.
