title: WEARABLE SENSOR-BASED SYSTEM FOR KNEE RANGE-OF-MOTION MONITORING AND VOICE-GUIDED REHABILITATION
abstract:
The present invention discloses a wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system (100) for monitoring knee movement and providing real-time rehabilitation guidance. The system (100) comprises a wearable support assembly (102), a knee movement sensing arrangement (104), and a processing/control unit (106) configured to process sensor data and determine knee range of motion through a range-of-motion determination module (108). An exercise evaluation module (110) evaluates the determined range of motion relative to predefined exercise criteria, while a repetition counting module (112) detects completed exercise repetitions. A voice guidance module (114) generates movement-responsive instructions output through an audio output device (116). A wireless communication module (118) transmits rehabilitation information to an external monitoring device (120), while a memory/storage unit (122) stores rehabilitation data. A power supply (124) powers the system (100) for clinical and home-based rehabilitation.
Figure 1 will be the reference.
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD
[001]	The present disclosure relates to the field of wearable rehabilitation and sensor-based healthcare systems. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to a wearable sensor-based system for knee range-of-motion monitoring and voice-guided rehabilitation.
BACKGROUND
[002]	Conventional knee rehabilitation and range-of-motion assessment techniques commonly rely on devices such as universal goniometers, digital goniometers, smartphone-based applications, and wearable sensor systems for evaluating knee flexion and extension. In many rehabilitation settings, a physiotherapist or other trained professional is required to position the measuring instrument, observe the joint movement, and manually record the range-of-motion values. Such manual assessment can be time-consuming, operator-dependent, and inconvenient when repeated measurements are required during a rehabilitation session.
[003]	Universal and digital goniometers are widely used for measuring joint angles; however, their use generally requires proper alignment of the instrument with anatomical landmarks and direct involvement of a trained person. Repeated manual measurements may increase therapist workload and may not provide continuous monitoring of the knee throughout an exercise session. Conventional approaches may therefore be less suitable for independent or unsupervised rehabilitation, particularly in a home environment.
[004]	Smartphone-based rehabilitation applications provide a degree of portability and digital interaction, but such applications may depend on proper device positioning, manual user interaction, or external sensing arrangements for acquiring reliable knee-motion information. Further, conventional smartphone-based approaches may not provide an integrated mechanism for continuously measuring knee range of motion, automatically identifying completed exercise repetitions, and delivering immediate exercise-specific voice feedback during rehabilitation.
[005]	Wearable sensor-based rehabilitation systems have also been developed for monitoring joint movement. Such systems may provide motion-related or angular information and may reduce the dependence on conventional manual instruments. However, existing wearable systems may primarily focus on movement sensing or data collection without integrating real-time voice guidance, automatic repetition counting, and wireless monitoring in a coordinated rehabilitation platform. The invention disclosure specifically identifies the absence of integrated voice guidance and automatic repetition counting as drawbacks of several existing approaches.
[006]	Furthermore, existing rehabilitation techniques may require frequent supervision by a physiotherapist, making continuous home-based rehabilitation difficult. Lack of immediate feedback may also result in exercises being performed without real-time correction or guidance. Accordingly, conventional knee rehabilitation technologies exhibit limitations relating to manual assessment, dependence on trained personnel, lack of integrated real-time guidance, limited automated exercise tracking, and reduced suitability for continuous home-based or remote rehabilitation.
OBJECTIVES 
[007]	An object of the present invention is to provide a wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system capable of monitoring knee range of motion during rehabilitation exercises.
[008]	Another object of the present invention is to provide real-time and objective measurement of knee flexion and extension for improving knee movement assessment and extension accuracy.
[009]	Another object of the present invention is to provide real-time voice-guided exercise feedback and automatic repetition counting based on monitored knee movement.
[010]	A further object of the present invention is to provide wireless transmission of rehabilitation data for facilitating clinical, home-based, and remote rehabilitation monitoring.
SUMMARY
[011]	The present invention relates to a wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system configured to monitor knee movement during rehabilitation exercises and provide real-time guidance to a user. The system is designed to facilitate objective assessment of knee range of motion while reducing dependence on repeated manual measurement and continuous supervision by a physiotherapist.
[012]	The system comprises a wearable support assembly configured to be positioned relative to a knee of the user and a knee movement sensing arrangement supported by the wearable support assembly. The sensing arrangement acquires movement-related information during flexion, extension, or other prescribed rehabilitation movements and generates corresponding sensor data. A processing and control unit receives and processes the sensor data to determine a range-of-motion value representative of movement of the knee.
[013]	The determined range-of-motion value is evaluated relative to one or more predefined exercise criteria to determine whether the user has achieved a prescribed movement range, requires further movement, or has completed an intended exercise movement. Based on the evaluated knee movement, the system determines whether a valid rehabilitation exercise repetition has been completed and automatically updates a repetition count.
[014]	The system further provides a voice-guidance functionality configured to generate spoken exercise instructions based on the evaluated movement of the knee. The generated instructions may guide the user to continue movement, increase extension or flexion, return toward an initial position, or indicate completion of a prescribed movement or exercise repetition. The voice guidance is provided through an audio output device during performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[015]	Rehabilitation-related information, including range-of-motion information, exercise-performance information, and repetition-count information, may be stored in a memory and transmitted through a wireless communication interface to an external monitoring device for review or evaluation.
[016]	The present invention further provides a method for sensor-based knee rehabilitation monitoring comprising acquiring knee movement information, processing the acquired information to determine knee range of motion, evaluating the determined range of motion against an exercise criterion, generating movement-responsive voice guidance, detecting completion of exercise repetitions, updating a repetition count, and storing or wirelessly transmitting rehabilitation information.
[017]	Accordingly, the invention provides a coordinated closed-loop rehabilitation platform in which sensed knee movement is utilized for exercise assessment, repetition validation, voice-guided feedback, and remote rehabilitation monitoring.

[030]	Wearable Support Assembly
[031]	The wearable support assembly may be configured to be positioned around, above, or below the knee of the user during performance of a rehabilitation exercise. The wearable support assembly may include one or more straps, bands, supports, or fastening arrangements for maintaining the system at a desired position relative to the knee.
[032]	The sensing arrangement may be mounted on or supported by the wearable support assembly. Depending upon the implementation, the sensing arrangement may include one sensor or a plurality of sensors positioned relative to the upper leg, lower leg, or knee region.
[033]	Knee Movement Sensing Arrangement
[034]	The knee movement sensing arrangement is configured to acquire movement-related information associated with movement of the knee during rehabilitation exercises.
[035]	The sensing arrangement may include at least one motion sensor. Depending upon the actual implementation, the motion sensor may include an accelerometer, gyroscope, inertial measurement unit, flex sensor, angular-position sensor, potentiometric sensor, magnetometer, or a combination thereof.
[036]	Range-of-Motion Determination
[037]	During operation, the sensing arrangement acquires sensor signals corresponding to movement of the knee. The processing unit receives and processes the sensor signals to determine orientation, angular displacement, or another movement parameter associated with flexion or extension of the knee.
[038]	An initial or reference knee position may be established before commencement of the rehabilitation exercise. The processing unit may thereafter determine a current knee position based on the acquired sensor information. A difference between the reference position and the current position may be used to determine the knee range of motion.
[039]	The determined range-of-motion value may further be compared with an exercise requirement, prescribed movement range, or predetermined target associated with the rehabilitation exercise.
[040]	Calibration
[041]	The system may further perform a calibration operation before commencement of the rehabilitation exercise. The calibration operation may include zero-angle calibration, initial posture calibration, sensor-offset calibration, user-specific calibration, or calibration relative to a full-extension position of the knee.
[042]	Calibration may be used to establish a reference condition for subsequent determination of knee movement and extension accuracy.
[043]	Exercise Evaluation
[044]	The processing unit may evaluate the determined knee range of motion with respect to one or more predetermined exercise criteria.
[045]	The exercise criteria may define whether a desired movement range has been achieved, whether the knee has been sufficiently extended or flexed, whether a prescribed position has been maintained for a required duration, or whether the exercise movement has been completed in accordance with a predefined rehabilitation requirement.
[046]	Based on the evaluation, the processing unit may determine an exercise condition indicative of correct movement, incomplete movement, insufficient extension, insufficient flexion, or completion of a prescribed movement.
[047]	Voice Feedback Mechanism
[048]	The voice guidance functionality may operate based on a sequence comprising acquisition of sensor data, determination of knee range of motion, evaluation of the determined range of motion relative to an exercise criterion, identification of a feedback condition, and generation of a corresponding voice instruction.
[049]	The voice guidance module may provide audible instructions or feedback through an audio output device during performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[050]	By way of example, the voice feedback may indicate that the user should continue extending the knee, that a required movement range has been achieved, that the user should return to an initial position, or that an exercise repetition has been completed.
[051]	Such voice instructions should be treated as exemplary and should not unnecessarily restrict the scope of the invention.
[052]	Automatic Repetition Counting
[053]	The system may automatically detect and count repetitions of a knee rehabilitation exercise based on detected movement of the knee.
[054]	A repetition may be registered after detection of a first movement condition corresponding to movement of the knee beyond a predetermined angular or range-of-motion threshold followed by detection of a return movement satisfying a second movement condition.
[055]	The processing unit may distinguish a completed repetition from an incomplete movement by evaluating movement direction, angular position, return movement, timing information, or one or more predefined exercise conditions.
[056]	The repetition count may be incremented only after satisfaction of the predefined completion criteria.
[057]	Wireless Monitoring
[058]	The system may include a wireless communication interface configured to transmit rehabilitation-related information to an external device for monitoring or evaluation.
[059]	The rehabilitation information may include knee range-of-motion information, exercise repetition information, exercise completion information, or other movement-related data.
[060]	The wireless communication interface may employ a suitable wireless communication technology. Where supported by the actual prototype, the wireless communication technology may include Bluetooth, Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi, radio-frequency communication, or another short-range or remote communication protocol.
[061]	The external device may include a smartphone, computing device, rehabilitation-monitoring terminal, or other suitable receiving device, subject to confirmation of the actual implementation.
[062]	Experimental Validation
[063]	The developed prototype was evaluated on sixty participants by measuring knee-extension range of motion and comparing the measurements with those obtained using a universal goniometer. The disclosure indicates that the prototype demonstrated excellent agreement with the universal goniometer and that the experimental results supported validity and reliability of the developed system.
[064]	Method of Sensor-Based Knee Rehabilitation Monitoring
[065]	A method for sensor-based monitoring and guidance of a knee rehabilitation exercise may include acquiring movement information from a sensing arrangement positioned relative to the knee of a user.
[066]	Based on the evaluation, voice-guided feedback may be generated and communicated to the user during performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[067]	FIG. 1 illustrates a block diagram of a wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. Referring to FIG. 1, a wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system (100) is illustrated, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The system (100) is configured to monitor movement of a knee of a user during a rehabilitation exercise, determine a range of motion of the knee, evaluate performance of the rehabilitation exercise, automatically count exercise repetitions, provide voice-guided feedback, and communicate rehabilitation-related information for monitoring purposes.
[068]	The system (100) comprises a wearable support assembly (102) configured to be positioned relative to a knee region of the user. The wearable support assembly (102) provides mechanical support for retaining one or more components of the system (100) at a desired position during performance of the rehabilitation exercise. The wearable support assembly (102) may be configured to extend around, above, below, or adjacent to the knee and may include one or more straps, bands, fastening portions, supporting members, or combinations thereof for maintaining the system (100) in operative association with the knee. The wearable support assembly (102) is configured to permit movement of the knee while maintaining the sensing components in a substantially stable position relative to the user's leg.
[069]	A knee movement sensing arrangement (104) is operatively associated with the wearable support assembly (102). The knee movement sensing arrangement (104) is configured to acquire movement information representative of movement of the knee during flexion, extension, or another prescribed rehabilitation movement. The knee movement sensing arrangement (104) generates sensor data corresponding to movement of the user's knee and communicates the sensor data to a processing/control unit (106). The particular sensing technology is not specified by FIG. 1; accordingly, the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) may broadly comprise one or more sensors capable of generating information representative of knee movement.
[070]	The processing/control unit (106) is communicatively coupled to the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) and is configured to receive and process the sensor data generated by the knee movement sensing arrangement (104). The processing/control unit (106) coordinates operation of the system (100) and facilitates determination, evaluation, storage, feedback generation, repetition counting, and communication of rehabilitation-related information.
[071]	A range-of-motion determination module (108) is operatively coupled to the processing/control unit (106). The range-of-motion determination module (108) is configured to process movement information obtained from the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) to determine a range of motion of the knee. In an embodiment, the processing/control unit (106) receives movement data corresponding to an initial knee position and movement data corresponding to a subsequent knee position. The range-of-motion determination module (108) determines a change in knee position from the received movement data and generates a range-of-motion value representative of flexion, extension, or a combination thereof.
[072]	The range-of-motion determination module (108) may determine the knee range of motion relative to an initial or reference position established before or during commencement of a rehabilitation exercise. The determined range-of-motion information may thereby provide an objective indication of movement of the knee instead of relying solely upon visual observation or repeated manual measurement by a physiotherapist.
[073]	An exercise evaluation module (110) is operatively associated with the range-of-motion determination module (108) and the processing/control unit (106). The exercise evaluation module (110) is configured to evaluate the determined knee range of motion with respect to one or more exercise criteria associated with a rehabilitation exercise. The exercise evaluation module (110) may determine whether a prescribed knee movement has been performed, whether a desired range of motion has been achieved, whether a movement remains incomplete, or whether a user is required to continue or modify the movement.
[074]	The exercise evaluation module (110) may compare the knee range-of-motion information generated by the range-of-motion determination module (108) with a predetermined or prescribed exercise parameter. Based on the comparison, the exercise evaluation module (110) generates exercise-evaluation information indicative of the performance of the user during the rehabilitation exercise. Such exercise-evaluation information may subsequently be utilized for repetition determination and voice-guided feedback.
[075]	A repetition counting module (112) is operatively coupled to the exercise evaluation module (110). The repetition counting module (112) is configured to automatically detect completion of individual repetitions of the rehabilitation exercise and maintain a count of completed repetitions. The repetition counting module (112) may determine completion of a repetition based on movement information, range-of-motion information, exercise-evaluation information, or a combination thereof.
[076]	In an embodiment, a repetition may be registered when the system (100) detects completion of a prescribed knee movement followed by return of the knee toward an initial or predetermined position. Accordingly, incomplete or partial movement may be distinguished from a completed rehabilitation movement before the repetition count is incremented. The exact repetition-detection criteria may be configured according to the particular rehabilitation exercise being performed.
[077]	A voice guidance module (114) is operatively coupled to the exercise evaluation module (110) and is configured to generate voice-guidance information based on the evaluated performance of the rehabilitation exercise. The voice guidance module (114) enables real-time feedback to be provided to the user while the rehabilitation exercise is being performed.
[078]	The voice guidance module (114) may generate an instruction corresponding to a detected exercise condition. By way of example, the instruction may indicate that the user is required to continue movement, increase extension, return the knee toward an initial position, or that a required movement or repetition has been completed. Such voice instructions are exemplary and may vary depending upon the prescribed rehabilitation exercise and the evaluated movement of the knee.
[079]	An audio output device (116) is operatively coupled to the voice guidance module (114) and is configured to output the voice-guidance information in an audible form to the user. Accordingly, the system (100) provides feedback during performance of the exercise without requiring the user to continuously observe a display. The audio output device (116) thereby facilitates guided rehabilitation in clinical as well as home-based environments.
[080]	A wireless communication module (118) is communicatively coupled to the processing/control unit (106). The wireless communication module (118) is configured to communicate rehabilitation-related information generated by the system (100) to an external monitoring device (120). The rehabilitation-related information may comprise one or more of knee range-of-motion information, exercise-evaluation information, repetition-count information, and other information associated with performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[081]	The external monitoring device (120) may receive the rehabilitation-related information transmitted by the wireless communication module (118) for monitoring, review, recording, or evaluation. The external monitoring device (120) may thereby enable rehabilitation information generated by the wearable system (100) to be made available outside the wearable system (100). Such communication facilitates remote monitoring and may enable rehabilitation exercises performed outside a clinical environment to be subsequently reviewed or monitored.
[082]	A memory/storage unit (122) is operatively coupled to the processing/control unit (106). The memory/storage unit (122) is configured to store information associated with operation of the system (100). The stored information may include sensor information, determined knee range-of-motion values, exercise-evaluation information, repetition counts, rehabilitation-session information, or combinations thereof. The stored rehabilitation information may be subsequently retrieved by the processing/control unit (106) or transmitted through the wireless communication module (118).
[083]	A power supply (124) is electrically coupled to one or more components of the system (100) and provides electrical power required for operation of the wearable knee rehabilitation system (100). As illustrated in FIG. 1, the power supply (124) may supply power to the knee movement sensing arrangement (104), processing/control unit (106), memory/storage unit (122), wireless communication module (118), audio output device (116), and other electrically operated components of the system (100).
[084]	During operation, the wearable support assembly (102) is positioned relative to the knee of the user. The knee movement sensing arrangement (104) detects movement of the knee as the user performs a prescribed rehabilitation exercise and generates corresponding sensor data. The sensor data is communicated to the processing/control unit (106), which causes the range-of-motion determination module (108) to determine the knee range of motion.
[085]	The exercise evaluation module (110) evaluates the determined range of motion with respect to the applicable exercise criteria. Based on the evaluation, the repetition counting module (112) determines whether a prescribed movement constitutes a completed repetition and updates the repetition count accordingly. Concurrently or subsequently, the voice guidance module (114) generates feedback corresponding to the evaluated exercise performance, and the audio output device (116) communicates the feedback audibly to the user.
[086]	The processing/control unit (106) may further cause rehabilitation-related information to be stored in the memory/storage unit (122) and/or communicated through the wireless communication module (118) to the external monitoring device (120). The sensing, processing, evaluation, repetition-counting, feedback, storage, and communication functions may be repeatedly performed during the rehabilitation session to provide continuous or periodic monitoring of knee movement.
[087]	Accordingly, the wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system (100) integrates the wearable support assembly (102), knee movement sensing arrangement (104), processing/control unit (106), range-of-motion determination module (108), exercise evaluation module (110), repetition counting module (112), voice guidance module (114), audio output device (116), wireless communication module (118), external monitoring device (120), memory/storage unit (122), and power supply (124) to provide sensor-based monitoring and guidance during knee rehabilitation exercises.
[088]	FIG. 2 illustrates an exemplary arrangement of the wearable knee rehabilitation system positioned relative to a knee of a user, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. Referring to FIG. 2, an exemplary arrangement of the wearable sensor-based knee rehabilitation system (100) positioned relative to a knee region of a user is illustrated, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The system (100) is configured to be worn by the user during performance of a knee rehabilitation exercise so that movement of the knee can be sensed, processed, and monitored while providing real-time guidance to the user.
[089]	The system (100) comprises the wearable support assembly (102) configured to be positioned around the knee region of the user. As illustrated in FIG. 2, the wearable support assembly (102) extends around the leg adjacent to the knee and is configured to support one or more functional components of the system (100) in an operative position relative to the knee. The wearable support assembly (102) may comprise one or more flexible straps, bands, fastening portions, or support members configured to retain the system (100) on the leg while permitting natural flexion and extension of the knee during the rehabilitation exercise.
[090]	The wearable support assembly (102) may be positioned such that at least a portion thereof lies above the knee joint and at least another portion lies below or adjacent to the knee joint. Such positioning enables the wearable support assembly (102) to maintain the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) substantially in alignment with the knee region while minimizing displacement of the sensing arrangement (104) during repeated movement.
[091]	The knee movement sensing arrangement (104) is mounted on or operatively associated with the wearable support assembly (102) and is positioned adjacent to the user's knee region. The knee movement sensing arrangement (104) is configured to detect movement associated with flexion and extension of the knee and to generate sensor data representative of the detected movement. The sensor data may include information representative of angular displacement, movement direction, orientation, acceleration, rotational movement, or another movement-related parameter associated with the knee.
[092]	In an embodiment, the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) may comprise at least one motion-sensing device configured to detect changes occurring during movement of the upper and lower portions of the leg relative to the knee joint. The generated movement data is communicated to the processing/control unit (106) for further processing. The particular sensor configuration may be selected according to the intended rehabilitation application and may comprise a single sensor or a plurality of sensors positioned at selected locations relative to the knee.
[093]	The processing/control unit (106) is positioned on or supported by the wearable support assembly (102) and is communicatively coupled to the knee movement sensing arrangement (104). The processing/control unit (106) receives the sensor data generated by the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) and processes the sensor data to obtain information indicative of knee movement during the rehabilitation exercise.
[094]	The processing/control unit (106) may determine or facilitate determination of a knee range of motion based on the sensor data received from the knee movement sensing arrangement (104). In particular, the processing/control unit (106) may process movement information corresponding to an initial knee position and a subsequent knee position to determine an angular or positional change associated with flexion or extension of the knee.
[095]	The processing/control unit (106) may further evaluate the determined knee movement relative to a predefined rehabilitation requirement. Based on such evaluation, the processing/control unit (106) may determine whether the user has achieved a desired movement range, whether additional extension or flexion is required, whether a prescribed exercise movement has been completed, or whether another exercise-related condition has been satisfied.
[096]	The system (100) further comprises an audio output device (116) operatively coupled to the processing/control unit (106). As illustrated in FIG. 2, the audio output device (116) may be configured as an earphone, earpiece, speaker, or another audible-output arrangement capable of communicating voice-guided instructions to the user during the rehabilitation exercise.
[097]	The audio output device (116) is configured to output audible feedback generated in response to the monitored knee movement. The audible feedback may guide the user during performance of the rehabilitation exercise without requiring continuous visual observation of a display or continuous intervention by a physiotherapist. For example, the audio output device (116) may provide instructions indicating that the user should continue extending the knee, return the knee toward an initial position, maintain a selected movement, or that an exercise repetition has been completed.
[098]	The voice-guided feedback may be generated dynamically based on the sensor data acquired by the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) and the corresponding exercise evaluation performed by the processing/control unit (106). Thus, the audible output is linked to the detected movement of the knee rather than being limited to a predetermined sequence of instructions.
[099]	The processing/control unit (106) may further automatically determine and maintain a count of completed rehabilitation exercise repetitions. A repetition may be identified based on detection of a prescribed movement pattern, achievement of a required range of motion, return toward an initial knee position, or satisfaction of another predefined exercise-completion condition.
[100]	The system (100) is further configured to communicate rehabilitation-related information to an external monitoring device (120). As illustrated in FIG. 2, communication between the wearable system (100) and the external monitoring device (120) may be established wirelessly. The external monitoring device (120) may receive rehabilitation information generated during performance of the exercise.
[101]	The rehabilitation information communicated to the external monitoring device (120) may include knee range-of-motion information, exercise-performance information, repetition-count information, or other data representative of the rehabilitation session. Such information may be utilized for monitoring, reviewing, recording, or evaluating the rehabilitation activity of the user.
[102]	In the illustrated embodiment, the external monitoring device (120) is represented as a portable electronic device. However, the external monitoring device (120) is not limited to the illustrated configuration and may comprise any suitable electronic device capable of receiving rehabilitation information from the system (100).
[103]	During use, the wearable support assembly (102) is positioned around the knee of the user such that the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) is maintained adjacent to the knee region. The user thereafter performs a prescribed knee rehabilitation exercise involving flexion, extension, or repeated movement of the knee.
[104]	As the knee moves, the knee movement sensing arrangement (104) continuously or periodically detects the movement and generates corresponding sensor data. The sensor data is supplied to the processing/control unit (106), which processes the sensor data to determine the movement of the knee and evaluate the performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[105]	Based on the evaluated movement, the processing/control unit (106) causes corresponding voice-guided information to be delivered through the audio output device (116). The processing/control unit (106) may concurrently determine whether individual exercise repetitions have been completed and maintain a corresponding repetition count.
[106]	The rehabilitation information generated during the exercise may further be transmitted to the external monitoring device (120), thereby enabling information relating to the user's exercise performance to be monitored or reviewed outside the wearable system (100).
[107]	Accordingly, the arrangement illustrated in FIG. 2 enables the wearable support assembly (102), knee movement sensing arrangement (104), processing/control unit (106), audio output device (116), and external monitoring device (120) to operate cooperatively for sensor-based knee movement monitoring, real-time rehabilitation guidance, automatic exercise tracking, and remote monitoring of rehabilitation-related information.
[108]	FIG. 3 illustrates a functional flow of sensor-data acquisition, knee range-of-motion determination, exercise evaluation, repetition detection, and voice-feedback generation, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. Referring to FIG. 3, a functional flow for knee rehabilitation monitoring is illustrated, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The functional flow represents processing of movement information associated with a knee of a user during performance of a rehabilitation exercise, beginning with acquisition of sensor data and proceeding through signal processing, range-of-motion determination, exercise evaluation, repetition detection, voice-feedback generation, and storage or wireless transmission of rehabilitation information.
[109]	During performance of the rehabilitation exercise, movement of the knee is detected and corresponding sensor information is supplied to a sensor-data acquisition module (302). The sensor-data acquisition module (302) is configured to receive sensor signals representative of movement of the knee during flexion, extension, or another prescribed rehabilitation movement. The acquired sensor data may include one or more movement-related parameters generated by the knee movement sensing arrangement associated with the wearable rehabilitation system.
[110]	The sensor-data acquisition module (302) communicates the acquired sensor signals to a signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304). The signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304) is configured to process the acquired sensor signals before determination of knee range of motion. The processing may include conditioning, filtering, normalization, removal or reduction of unwanted signal variations, or other preprocessing operations suitable for obtaining movement information usable for subsequent analysis.
[111]	The signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304) thereby generates processed sensor information corresponding to movement of the knee. The processed sensor information is supplied to a range-of-motion determination module (306). The signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304) may further provide processed rehabilitation-related information to a data storage/wireless transmission module (316) for storage, recording, or subsequent transmission.
[112]	The range-of-motion determination module (306) is configured to determine a knee range of motion based on the processed sensor information received from the signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304). In an embodiment, the range-of-motion determination module (306) determines movement of the knee relative to an initial, reference, or previously determined knee position and obtains a range-of-motion value corresponding to knee flexion, knee extension, or a combination thereof.
[113]	The range-of-motion determination module (306) may determine an angular or positional change associated with the knee during movement. The determined knee range-of-motion information provides an objective representation of the movement performed by the user during the rehabilitation exercise and is communicated to an exercise evaluation module (308).
[114]	The exercise evaluation module (308) is configured to evaluate the determined knee range of motion with respect to one or more exercise conditions or criteria associated with the rehabilitation exercise. The exercise evaluation module (308) may determine whether a prescribed target has been achieved, whether the knee has been sufficiently extended or flexed, whether further movement is required, or whether another predefined exercise condition has been satisfied.
[115]	By way of example, the exercise evaluation module (308) may compare the determined range of motion with a target range associated with the prescribed rehabilitation exercise. Based on such comparison, the exercise evaluation module (308) may identify a condition such as achievement of the target range or insufficient extension. These conditions are illustrated in FIG. 3 merely as exemplary exercise-evaluation conditions and are not intended to limit the system to those particular conditions.
[116]	The exercise evaluation module (308) is functionally coupled to a repetition detection module (310). The repetition detection module (310) is configured to determine whether an exercise repetition has been completed based on the evaluated knee movement. The repetition detection module (310) may process information received from the exercise evaluation module (308) to identify completion of a prescribed movement cycle.
[117]	In an embodiment, the repetition detection module (310) may identify completion of a repetition after the knee reaches a required movement condition and subsequently returns toward an initial or predetermined position. The repetition detection module (310) may therefore distinguish between partial movement and a completed exercise repetition before updating or recording a repetition count.
[118]	The repetition information generated by the repetition detection module (310) is communicated to the data storage/wireless transmission module (316). The data storage/wireless transmission module (316) is configured to store rehabilitation-related information locally and/or transmit the rehabilitation-related information to an external monitoring device.
[119]	The rehabilitation-related information handled by the data storage/wireless transmission module (316) may include acquired sensor information, processed movement information, determined range-of-motion information, exercise-evaluation information, repetition information, or combinations thereof. Accordingly, rehabilitation progress may be recorded for subsequent review or communicated for remote monitoring.
[120]	The exercise evaluation module (308) is further functionally coupled to a voice-feedback generation module (312). The voice-feedback generation module (312) is configured to generate voice-guidance information based on the exercise condition determined by the exercise evaluation module (308).
[121]	For example, when the exercise evaluation module (308) determines that a target range has not yet been achieved, the voice-feedback generation module (312) may generate an instruction requesting continued movement or additional extension. When the exercise evaluation module (308) determines that the required movement has been achieved, the voice-feedback generation module (312) may generate feedback indicating successful completion of the movement or directing the user to return toward an initial position.
[122]	The voice-feedback generation module (312) communicates the generated voice-guidance information to an audio output device (314). The audio output device (314) is configured to provide the voice-guidance information to the user in an audible form during performance of the rehabilitation exercise.
[123]	The audio output device (314) may thereby provide real-time or substantially real-time guidance based on the actual movement of the knee. Accordingly, the voice feedback is generated in response to sensed and evaluated knee movement rather than merely according to a fixed sequence of prerecorded instructions.
[124]	During operation, the sensor-data acquisition module (302) acquires knee movement data while the user performs the prescribed rehabilitation exercise. The acquired data is processed by the signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304), and the processed data is supplied to the range-of-motion determination module (306).
[125]	The range-of-motion determination module (306) determines the knee range of motion, and the exercise evaluation module (308) evaluates the determined range of motion relative to the applicable exercise condition. Based on the evaluation, the repetition detection module (310) determines whether a repetition has been completed, while the voice-feedback generation module (312) generates appropriate exercise guidance.
[126]	The generated voice feedback is output through the audio output device (314), while rehabilitation-related information is stored and/or wirelessly communicated through the data storage/wireless transmission module (316).
[127]	Accordingly, the functional flow illustrated in FIG. 3 enables the sensor-data acquisition module (302), signal conditioning/preprocessing module (304), range-of-motion determination module (306), exercise evaluation module (308), repetition detection module (310), voice-feedback generation module (312), audio output device (314), and data storage/wireless transmission module (316) to cooperate for objective monitoring, evaluation, exercise tracking, real-time voice guidance, and recording or transmission of knee rehabilitation information.
[128]	FIG. 4 illustrates a flow chart of a method for sensor-based monitoring and guidance of a knee rehabilitation exercise, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. Referring to FIG. 4, a flow chart of a method (400) for sensor-based monitoring and guidance of a knee rehabilitation exercise is illustrated, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The method (400) is configured to monitor movement of a knee of a user during performance of a rehabilitation exercise, determine a knee range of motion, evaluate the exercise performance, provide voice-based guidance, detect completed exercise repetitions, and store and/or transmit rehabilitation-related information.
[129]	At step (402), the wearable knee rehabilitation system is positioned on a knee of the user. The wearable system may be secured around or adjacent to the knee region such that the sensing arrangement remains operatively positioned relative to the knee during performance of the rehabilitation exercise. Proper positioning facilitates acquisition of movement information representative of knee flexion, knee extension, or another prescribed knee movement.
[130]	At step (404), knee movement data is acquired from one or more sensors associated with the wearable knee rehabilitation system. The sensor or sensors detect movement of the knee as the user performs the prescribed rehabilitation exercise and generate corresponding sensor signals. The acquired knee movement data may represent one or more movement-related parameters associated with motion of the knee during the exercise.
[131]	At step (406), the acquired sensor data is processed to determine a knee range of motion (ROM). The sensor data may be processed to determine a change in position associated with flexion or extension of the knee. In an embodiment, the range of motion may be determined with reference to an initial or reference knee position and a subsequent knee position detected during the exercise. The resulting ROM information provides an objective indication of movement performed by the user.
[132]	At step (408), the determined knee range of motion is evaluated with respect to a predefined target range associated with the rehabilitation exercise. The predefined target range may represent a desired degree or extent of movement to be achieved during performance of the exercise. The determined ROM is compared with the predefined target range to determine whether the user's knee movement satisfies an applicable exercise requirement.
[133]	The evaluation at step (408) may indicate whether the user has reached the target range, whether additional knee movement is required, or whether the performed movement is insufficient with respect to the prescribed rehabilitation exercise. The evaluation thereby provides an exercise-performance condition that may be used for generating real-time guidance to the user.
[134]	At step (410), voice-based feedback is generated and provided to guide the user's exercise performance. The voice-based feedback is generated based on the evaluation of the determined knee range of motion. The feedback may therefore correspond to the actual movement performed by the user rather than merely providing a predetermined sequence of instructions.
[135]	By way of example, the voice-based feedback generated at step (410) may instruct the user to continue movement, increase extension, return the knee toward an initial position, or indicate that the desired movement has been achieved. The particular voice instruction may depend upon the exercise condition identified during the evaluation at step (408).
[136]	At step (412), the method (400) determines whether an exercise repetition has been completed. Completion of an exercise repetition may be determined based on the movement data, the determined knee ROM, satisfaction of the predefined target range, return of the knee toward an initial or predetermined position, or a combination thereof.
[137]	At decision step (414), a determination is made as to whether the repetition has been completed. When the repetition is determined not to have been completed, the method (400) returns to step (404), and additional knee movement data is acquired. The system therefore continues monitoring the knee until movement satisfying the applicable repetition-completion condition is detected.
[138]	When the repetition is determined to have been completed at decision step (414), the method (400) proceeds to step (416). At step (416), a repetition count is updated to represent the completed exercise repetition. The repetition count may be incremented each time the method detects satisfaction of the repetition-completion condition.
[139]	At step (418), rehabilitation information is stored and/or transmitted to an external device. The rehabilitation information may include the determined knee range of motion, repetition count, exercise-performance information, or combinations thereof. The information may be stored locally for subsequent review and/or communicated to an external monitoring device for remote monitoring or evaluation.
[140]	At decision step (420), a determination is made as to whether the rehabilitation exercise is to be continued. When the exercise is to be continued, the method (400) returns to step (404) for acquisition of further knee movement data. Accordingly, subsequent knee movements may be monitored, evaluated, and counted in substantially the same manner for additional repetitions.
[141]	When the determination at decision step (420) indicates that the exercise is not to be continued, the method (400) proceeds to step (422), at which the monitoring and guidance operation is terminated.
[142]	Accordingly, the method (400) provides a closed-loop rehabilitation-monitoring process in which knee movement data is acquired at step (404), processed for determination of knee ROM at step (406), evaluated relative to a predefined target range at step (408), and used to generate voice-based guidance at step (410). Completion of an exercise repetition is determined at steps (412) and (414), the repetition count is updated at step (416), and rehabilitation information is stored and/or transmitted at step (418). The method may thereafter repeat based on the determination at step (420) until termination at step (422).
Advantages:
•	The present disclosure enables real-time and objective monitoring of knee range of motion during rehabilitation exercises, thereby reducing dependence on repeated manual measurement.
•	The present disclosure provides voice-guided exercise feedback based on monitored knee movement, thereby assisting the user in performing prescribed rehabilitation exercises with improved guidance.
•	The present disclosure supports automatic detection and counting of completed rehabilitation exercise repetitions, thereby reducing manual tracking by the user or physiotherapist.
•	The present disclosure enables storage and wireless transmission of rehabilitation-related information, including range-of-motion and repetition data, for remote monitoring and evaluation.
•	The present disclosure facilitates use of the wearable knee rehabilitation system in clinical, home-based, and tele-rehabilitation environments, thereby improving accessibility and reducing continuous therapist supervision.

title: METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR SPATIAL CROP YIELD ESTIMATION
abstract:
A computer-implemented method (700) for spatial crop yield estimation includes acquiring (702), from a plurality of data sources, multi-source agricultural data associated with an agricultural region. The method includes preprocessing (704) the acquired multi-source agricultural data to generate a plurality of features associated with the multi-source agricultural data, integrating (706) the plurality of features to generate a unified geospatial dataset, and preprocessing (708) the unified geospatial dataset to generate a machine-learning ready dataset. The method includes generating (710) a plurality of feature combinations from the machine-learning ready dataset and determining (712) an optimal feature combination from the plurality of feature combinations based on one or more performance metrics. The method includes generating (714) a spatial crop yield estimation map for the agricultural region based on the optimal feature combination and rendering (716) the spatial crop yield estimation map on an electronic device.
 >
specification:
TECHNICAL FIELD
	The present disclosure relates to agricultural data processing and crop yield prediction, and more particularly to a method and system for spatial crop yield estimation using multi-source agricultural data comprising optical remote sensing data, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, and agricultural datasets to generate a spatial crop yield estimation map for an agricultural region.
BACKGROUND
	Crop yield estimation involves predicting the quantity of agricultural produce expected from a given region. Accurate crop yield estimation supports food security planning, resource allocation, and agricultural policy development. Spatial crop yield estimation extends this concept by generating yield predictions across geographic areas, enabling identification of high-productivity and low-productivity zones within agricultural regions. Remote sensing technologies and machine learning (ML) approaches have emerged as tools for crop yield estimation due to the ability of remote sensing technologies and ML approaches to process large volumes of heterogeneous data.
	Empirical models represent one approach to crop yield estimation. Empirical models rely on statistical relationships between yield and factors such as weather conditions or vegetation indices. Empirical models are straightforward to implement and interpret. However, empirical models assume fixed relationships that may not hold under varying environmental conditions. Empirical models often fail to generalize across different regions or growing seasons.
	Crop simulation models represent another approach to yield estimation. Crop simulation models, such as Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT) and Agricultural Production Systems Simulator (APSIM), simulate plant growth processes based on environmental inputs and management practices. Crop simulation models are grounded in plant physiology. However, crop simulation models require extensive input data and calibration. The data requirements of crop simulation models limit the applicability of crop simulation models at larger scales or in data-scarce regions.
	Semi-physical models have been developed to balance the complexity of crop simulation models with the simplicity of empirical models. Semi-physical models use remote sensing inputs within simplified growth models. Semi-physical models are less demanding than full simulation models. However, semi-physical models still rely on assumptions about plant behavior that may not align with real-world variability.
	Remote sensing-based approaches have enhanced the ability to estimate crop yields with improved accuracy and spatial detail. Optical remote sensing data provides vegetation indices that correlate with crop health and productivity. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data provides observations under all weather conditions, which is advantageous in tropical regions where persistent cloud cover limits the usability of optical data. However, existing remote sensing methods frequently operate at coarse spatial scales. Coarse-scale approaches ignore fine-scale variability that is relevant for localized decision-making. Many existing methods rely on a single type of input data, such as optical indices alone or SAR parameters alone. Single-source approaches fail to capture the full range of biophysical interactions that influence crop productivity.
	Ground-based surveys represent a traditional approach to crop yield estimation. Ground-based surveys involve field observations and crop cutting experiments to measure actual yield. Ground-based surveys are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Ground-based surveys are difficult to scale across large agricultural regions.
	Accordingly, there exists a need for a method and system for spatial crop yield estimation that overcomes one or more of the above-mentioned problems.

	As used herein, the term "agricultural region" refers to a geographic area in which crops are cultivated, such as a taluk, district, or other administrative or agronomic zone. The term "multi-source agricultural data" refers to data acquired from a plurality of data sources and Including optical remote sensing data, SAR data, and one or more agricultural datasets. The term "optical remote sensing data" refers to imagery acquired by sensors operating in visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared wavelengths, such as data from a Sentinel-2 platform carrying a Multispectral Instrument (MSI) sensor. The term "SAR data" refers to radar imagery acquired by a synthetic aperture radar sensor, such as data from a Sentinel-1 platform operating in C-band with dual polarization. The term "agricultural datasets" refers to datasets Including meteorological data, soil data, and field-observed crop yield data. The term "features" refers to derived variables extracted from the multi-source agricultural data, including optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, and soil features. The term "unified geospatial dataset" refers to an integrated dataset in which the plurality of features are spatially and temporally aligned to a common reference frame. The term "machine-learning ready dataset" refers to a dataset prepared from the unified geospatial dataset by extraction at field-observation locations, exploratory data analysis, and normalization. The term "feature combination" refers to a subset of the plurality of features selected for evaluation by a machine-learning model. The term "performance metric" refers to a quantitative measure of prediction accuracy, such as a coefficient of determination (R²), a root mean square error (RMSE), or a mean absolute error (MAE). The term "crop yield prediction model" refers to a machine-learning model trained to predict crop yield values from predictor variables. The term "crop cultivation mask" refers to a binary spatial layer identifying crop cultivation areas within the agricultural region. The term "feature matrix" refers to a structured array of predictor values extracted at locations associated with field-observed crop yield data. The term "field-observed crop yield data" refers to yield measurements obtained through crop cutting experiments or agricultural records. The term "spatial crop yield estimation map" refers to a georeferenced map depicting predicted crop yield values across the agricultural region.

	In an embodiment, the plurality of optical vegetation features may include one or more vegetation, canopy, chlorophyll, biomass, productivity, moisture, or crop-condition indicators, at least one of a normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), an enhanced vegetation index (EVI), a soil adjusted vegetation index (SAVI), a normalized difference red edge index (NDRE), a leaf area index (LAI), and a fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (FAPAR).
	In an embodiment, the NDVI may be computed according to: 
NDVI=(NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red),
where NIR is the reflectance in the near-infrared band and Red is the reflectance in the red band. NDVI values may range from −1 to +1, with values near zero indicating barren or non-vegetated surfaces and values approaching one indicating dense healthy vegetation.
	In an embodiment, the EVI may be computed according to:
EVI=G×(NIR-Red)/(NIR+(C_1×Red)-(C_2×Blue)+L),
where G is a gain factor, C1 and C2 are atmospheric resistance coefficients of 6 and 7.5 respectively, L is a canopy background adjustment of 1, and Blue is the blue band reflectance. In an example, EVI values may range from −1 to 1.
	In an embodiment, the NDRE may be computed according to:
NDRE=(NIR-Re)/(NIR+Re),
where Re is the red-edge band. In an example, NDRE values may range from −1 to 0.81.
	In an embodiment, the SAVI may be computed according to:
SAVI=(NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red+L)×(1+L),
where L is a soil brightness correction factor typically set at 0.5. In an example, SAVI values may range from 0.04 to 1.5.
	In an embodiment, the LAI may be computed according to:
LAI=3.318×EVI-0.118. In an example, LAI values may range from 0 to 2.6.
	In an embodiment, the FAPAR may be derived from MODIS data and represents the fraction of incoming solar radiation in the photosynthetically active wavelengths absorbed by the vegetation canopy. In an example, FAPAR values may range from 0.29 to 0.56.
	In an embodiment, the plurality of optical vegetation features collectively characterize crop vigor, canopy development, vegetation density, chlorophyll content, biomass conditions, and other crop-related characteristics across one or more crop growth stages.
