	In an embodiment, the plurality of SAR-derived features may include one or more radar backscatter features, polarimetric features, decomposition features, texture features, coherence features, vegetation-related radar indices, or combinations thereof, including but not limited to vertical transmit-vertical receive (VV) backscatter, a vertical transmit-horizontal receive (VH) backscatter, a Radar Vegetation Index (RVI), an entropy, and an alpha angle.
	In an embodiment, the backscatter coefficient may be computed as 
σ^0 (dB)=10〖log⁡〗_10 (DN),
where DN is the digital number, VV backscatter is sensitive to surface scattering and dielectric characteristics at the soil-plant interface, VH backscatter responds to volume scattering from canopy structure.
	In an embodiment, the RVI may be computed as 
RVI=(4×σ_VH^0)/(σ_VH^0+σ_VV^0 ).
	In a non-limiting example, the RVI values may range from 0 to 1, with higher values in areas of dense isotropic vegetation scattering.
	In an embodiment, the entropy H may be computed as 
H=-∑_(i=1)^n▒ P_i 〖log⁡〗_n P_i, where P_i=λ_i/(∑_(j=1)^n▒ λ_j ) and
λi are eigenvalues of the coherency matrix [T]. Entropy values may range from 0 to 1, with low values indicating dominant surface scattering and higher values indicating complex or multiple scattering.
	In an embodiment, the alpha angle α may be computed as 
α=∑_(i=1)^n▒ α_i P_i, where α_i=〖cos⁡〗^(-1) ("∣" ν_1i "∣").
	In a non-limiting example, the Alpha angle values may range from 0° to 90°, with lower values indicating surface scattering and increased values indicating volume scattering. 
	In an embodiment, the plurality of SAR-derived features may provide structural, geometric, moisture-related, and scattering-characteristic information that complements information obtained from optical remote sensing data.
	In an embodiment, the meteorological extraction unit 422 and the temporal harmonization unit 424 may be configured to extract and temporally harmonize one or more meteorological, climatic, environmental, or agro-meteorological variables associated with the agricultural region 120 including rainfall, growing degree days (GDD), humidity, solar radiation, temperature, evapotranspiration, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, the GDD may be computed as 
GDD=(T_min+T_max)/2-T_b,
where Tmin is daily minimum temperature in °C, Tmax is daily maximum temperature in °C, and Tb is base temperature in °C. The GDD represents the accumulated thermal time experienced by the crop from planting to maturity and provides insight into crop phenology.
	In an embodiment, the soil property extraction unit 426 and the standardization unit 428 may be configured to extract and standardize one or more physical, chemical, biological, hydrological, environmental, or agronomic soil properties associated with the agricultural region 120, including but not limited to organic carbon, pH, clay content, nitrogen content, soil texture, moisture retention capacity, or combinations thereof. The soil data may be spatially interpolated using geostatistical techniques to create raster layers at the target spatial resolution.
	In an embodiment, the optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, and soil features so generated are integrated by the feature integration module 306 into the unified geospatial dataset and then evaluated as described with reference to FIG. 5.
	FIG. 5 illustrates a feature evaluation and selection module 312, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. In an embodiment, the feature evaluation and selection module 312 may include a combination generator 502, a machine-learning evaluator 504, a performance metric comparator 506, a ranking unit 508, and an optimal combination selector 510.
	In an embodiment, the feature evaluation and selection module 312 may be configured to identify a feature subset that provides improved crop-yield prediction performance from among a plurality of candidate feature combinations generated from the machine-learning ready dataset.
	In an embodiment, the feature evaluation and selection module 312 may be configured to identify a feature subset that provides improved crop-yield prediction performance from among a plurality of candidate feature combinations generated from the machine-learning ready dataset.
	In an embodiment, the combination generator 502 may be configured to form the plurality of feature combinations. The plurality of feature combinations may be generated by combining different subsets of optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, soil features, agricultural information features, field-observation features, or combinations thereof. The plurality of feature combinations may be generated by combining different subsets of optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, soil features, agricultural information features, field-observation features, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, the machine-learning evaluator 504 may be configured to evaluate each of the plurality of feature combinations using at least one machine-learning model to determine one or more performance metrics corresponding to each feature combination. The performance metric comparator 506 may be configured to compare the one or more performance metrics corresponding to the plurality of feature combinations. The ranking unit 508 may be configured to rank the plurality of feature combinations based on the comparison of the one or more performance metrics. The optimal combination selector 510 may be configured to determine the optimal feature combination based on the one or more performance metrics. In some embodiments, the optimal feature combination may correspond to a feature combination exhibiting a desired balance between prediction accuracy, robustness, computational efficiency, model interpretability, reliability, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, the at least one machine-learning model may be implemented using one or more machine-learning techniques, including but not limited to regression models, decision-tree models, ensemble-learning models, boosting algorithms, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, deep-learning models, probabilistic models, or combinations thereof.
	In some embodiments, the at least one machine-learning model may be implemented using a Random Forest algorithm. The Random Forest algorithm may be an ensemble-learning method configured to construct multiple decision trees during training and output an aggregate prediction for regression tasks.
	In alternate embodiments, the at least one machine-learning model may be implemented using an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm. The Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm may be configured to sequentially generate boosted decision trees and iteratively reduce prediction errors to improve model performance.
	In an embodiment, hyperparameter tuning may be performed to optimize operation of the at least one machine-learning model. The hyperparameter tuning may be performed using one or more optimization techniques including randomized search, grid search, Bayesian optimization, evolutionary optimization, adaptive search techniques, or combinations thereof.
	In a non-limiting example, the hyperparameter tuning may be performed using RandomizedSearchCV with stochastic sampling of the parameter space. In a non-limiting example, the hyperparameter tuning may be configured with 10 iterations and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. The parameters tuned may include number of estimators, learning rate, tree depth, subsample ratio, and column sampling ratio. The parameters tuned may include, without limitation, a number of estimators, learning rate, tree depth, subsample ratio, column sampling ratio, regularization parameters, feature-selection parameters, or other model-specific parameters.
	In an embodiment, the one or more performance metrics may include one or more prediction-performance measures including, but not limited to, a coefficient of determination (R²), a root mean square error (RMSE), and a mean absolute error (MAE). The coefficient of determination may be computed as:
R^2=1-(∑_(i=1)^n▒( O_i-P_i )^2)/(∑_(i=1)^n▒( O_i-O_avg )^2 ) 		….(a)
	In an embodiment, the root mean square error may be computed as: 
RMSE=√(1/n ∑_(i=1)^n▒( O_i-P_i )^2 ) 	….(b)
	In an embodiment, the mean absolute error may be computed as: 
MAE=1/n ∑_(i=1)^n▒"∣"  O_i-P_i "∣"  		…(c)
Where, Oi is observed yield, Pi is predicted yield, and Oavg is the mean observed yield. Higher coefficient-of-determination values and lower prediction-error values may indicate improved prediction performance for a corresponding feature combination.
	In an embodiment, the machine-learning evaluator sub-module 504 may be configured to perform feature importance analysis to determine the relative contribution of individual variables may be configured to perform feature importance analysis to determine the relative contribution of individual variables to crop-yield prediction performance.
	The feature-importance analysis may be performed using model-derived importance scores, permutation-based importance measures, sensitivity analyses, explainable artificial intelligence techniques, statistical analyses, or combinations thereof.
	The machine-learning evaluator 504 may be further configured to generate one or more diagnostic outputs for evaluating prediction performance.
	The diagnostic outputs may include one or more of Taylor diagrams, correlation analyses, residual analyses, scatter plots of observed versus predicted crop-yield values, feature-importance visualizations, comparative-performance charts, validation reports, or combinations thereof. In some embodiments, scatter plots may include a reference line corresponding to ideal agreement between predicted and observed values.
	In an embodiment, the performance metric comparator 506, and the ranking unit 508 may be automated to perform comparison and ranking of feature combinations. The automated evaluation process may reduce reliance on predefined assumptions regarding feature relevance and may facilitate identification of feature combinations exhibiting improved predictive capability for the agricultural region 120.
	In some embodiments, the feature evaluation and selection module 312 may iteratively evaluate multiple feature combinations and corresponding machine-learning model configurations until one or more selection criteria are satisfied.
	The generation of the spatial crop yield estimation map from the optimal feature combination is described with reference to FIG. 6.
	FIG. 6 illustrates a map generation module 316, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. In an embodiment, the map generation module 316 may include a feature matrix generator 602, a model training unit 604, a prediction unit 606, a crop cultivation mask unit 608, a filtering unit 610, and a map rendering unit 612.
	In an embodiment, the feature matrix generator 602 may be configured to extract, using the selected optimal feature combination determined as described with reference to FIG. 5, one or more predictor values corresponding to locations associated with the field-observed crop yield data to generate a feature matrix. The feature matrix may include predictor values corresponding to the selected optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, soil features and other selected agricultural features extracted at the locations associated with the filed observed crop yield data.
	In some embodiments, the feature matrix generator 602 may further organize, transform, encode, normalize, or otherwise prepare the predictor values for training and execution of the crop yield prediction model.
	In an embodiment, the model training unit 604 may be configured to train a crop yield prediction model using the feature matrix and the field-observed crop yield data. The prediction unit 606 may be configured to generate one or more predicted crop yield values for a plurality of geographic locations within the agricultural region 120 using the trained crop yield prediction model. In some embodiments, the predicted crop yield values may be generated at a pixel level, grid level, field level, management-zone level, or any other geographic unit associated with the agricultural region 120.
	In some embodiments, the crop yield prediction model may include one or more machine-learning models, ensemble-learning models, statistical models, regression models, deep-learning models, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, the crop cultivation mask unit 608 may be configured to apply a crop cultivation mask to identify crop cultivation areas within the plurality of geographic locations. The crop cultivation mask may be generated using one or more land-cover classification techniques, crop-identification techniques, vegetation-classification techniques, remote-sensing analyses, machine-learning techniques, image-processing techniques, or combinations thereof. In some embodiments, the crop cultivation mask may identify cultivated crop areas within the agricultural region 120. The filtering unit 610 may be configured to filter the one or more predicted crop yield values to retain one or more predicted crop yield values corresponding to the identified crop cultivation areas.
	In an embodiment, the map rendering unit 612 may be configured to generate the spatial crop yield estimation map for the agricultural region 120 based on the retained predicted crop yield values. The spatial crop yield estimation map generated by the map rendering unit 612 may be communicated to the rendering module 318, which may be configured to output the spatial crop yield estimation map to the electronic device 118 for visualization. The spatial crop yield estimation map may represent spatial variation of estimated crop yield across the agricultural region 120 and may be rendered using one or more visual representations including color gradients, thematic layers, geospatial overlays, field boundaries, dashboards, analytical reports, or combinations thereof. In a non-limiting example, the spatial crop yield estimation map may be generated at a spatial resolution of 10 meters so that intra-field productivity variation is resolved.
	In an embodiment, masking and filtering may confine predictions to cultivated agricultural areas and reduce generation of predictions for non-agricultural locations. Training on locations of the field-observed crop yield data may facilitate calibration and validation of the crop yield prediction model using ground-observed crop-yield measurements. The successive operations performed by the feature matrix generator 602, model training unit 604, prediction unit 606, crop cultivation mask unit 608, filtering unit 610, and map rendering unit 612 may transform the optimal feature combination into a geospatially resolved crop-yield estimation output for the agricultural region 120.
	FIG. 7 illustrates a method 700 for spatial crop yield estimation, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The method 700 may be a computer-implemented method executed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 116 or the processor 202.
	At step 702, the data acquisition module 302 may acquire the multi-source agricultural data from the plurality of data sources. At step 704, the data preprocessing module 304 may preprocess the acquired multi-source agricultural data to generate the plurality of features. At step 706, the feature integration module 306 may integrate the plurality of features into the unified geospatial dataset. At step 708, the dataset preparation module 308 may preprocess the unified geospatial dataset into the machine-learning ready dataset.
	At step 710, the feature combination generation module 310 may generate the feature combinations from the machine-learning ready dataset. At step 712, the feature evaluation and selection module 312 may determine the optimal feature combination based on the one or more performance metrics. At step 714, the map generation module 316 may generate the spatial crop yield estimation map for the agricultural region 120. At step 716, the rendering module 318 may render the spatial crop yield estimation map on the electronic device 118.
	The method 700 may improve crop-yield prediction accuracy through fusion of multi-source agricultural data, provide geospatially resolved yield estimates suitable for localized decision-making, and reduce dependence on extensive field-based surveys. The preprocessing of step 704 is described in greater detail with reference to FIG. 8.
	FIG. 8 illustrates a method 800 of preprocessing multi-source agricultural data, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The method 800 is a detailed implementation of step 704 of the method 700. The method 800 may be a computer-implemented method executed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 116 or the processors 202.
	At step 802, the data preprocessing module 304 may be configured to receive the multi-source agricultural data. At step 804, the optical preprocessing unit 402 may preprocess the optical remote sensing data to generate the plurality of optical vegetation features. The preprocessing the optical remote sensing data includes performing one or more of cloud removal, shadow removal, geometric correction, temporal alignment, spatial harmonization, clipping to the agricultural region 120, atmospheric correction, radiometric correction, reprojection, masking, image enhancement, normalization, or combinations thereof.
	At step 806, the SAR preprocessing unit 404 may preprocess the SAR data to generate the plurality of SAR-derived features. The preprocessing the SAR data includes performing one or more of orbit correction, TOPS splitting, calibration, deburst processing, terrain correction, speckle removal, covariance matrix generation, multilooking, polarimetric decomposition or combinations thereof.
	At step 808, the meteorological preprocessing unit 406 may preprocess the meteorological data to generate the plurality of meteorological features by extracting and temporally harmonizing one or more meteorological, climatic, environmental, or agro-meteorological properties associated with the agricultural region 120, including rainfall, growing degree days (GDD), humidity, solar radiation, temperature, evapotranspiration, or combinations thereof.
	At step 810, the soil preprocessing unit 408 may preprocess the soil data to generate the plurality of soil features by extracting and standardizing one or more physical, chemical, biological, hydrological, environmental, or agronomic soil properties associated with the agricultural region 120, including organic carbon, pH, clay content, nitrogen content, soil texture, moisture retention capacity, or combinations thereof. At step 812, the plurality of features is output for integration by the feature integration module 306.
	In an embodiment, preprocessing operations associated with optical remote sensing data, SAR data, meteorological data, and soil data may be performed sequentially, in parallel, iteratively, or in any suitable combination.
	Domain-specific preprocessing of the multi-source agricultural data may preserve information associated with each data source while transforming heterogeneous datasets into a form suitable for integration, feature engineering, machine-learning operations, and crop-yield prediction. The preprocessing of the unified geospatial dataset is described with reference to FIG. 9.
	FIG. 9 illustrates a method 900 of preprocessing the unified geospatial dataset, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The method 900 is a detailed implementation of step 708 of the method 700. The method 900 may be a computer-implemented method executed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 116 or the processor 202.
	At step 902, the dataset preparation module 308 may receive the unified geospatial dataset. At step 904, the dataset preparation module 308 may extract data associated with locations corresponding to the field-observed crop yield data from the unified geospatial dataset. In some embodiments, the extraction may establish associations between predictor variables and corresponding field-observed crop yield values for subsequent machine-learning operations.
	At step 906, the dataset preparation module 308 may perform exploratory data analysis on the extracted data. The exploratory data analysis may assess the distribution of and relationships among variables, including one or more of correlation analysis, feature-distribution analysis, outlier analysis, data-quality assessment, statistical analysis, and visualization of variable relationships. In some embodiments, the correlation analysis may be represented as a correlation heatmap or other graphical representation.
	At step 908, the dataset preparation module 308 may normalize the extracted data prior to generation of the plurality of feature combinations. The normalization may include one or more scaling, transformation, standardization, normalization, encoding, or data-conditioning operations suitable for machine-learning processing. The normalization ensures consistency and comparability across inputs having different units and dynamic ranges. At step 910, the dataset preparation module 308 outputs the machine-learning ready dataset.
	In an embodiment, extraction of data associated with the field-observation locations may facilitate pairing of predictor variables with corresponding measured crop-yield values for supervised training of one or more crop-yield prediction models.
	The machine-learning ready dataset may include normalized predictor variables and associated crop-yield observations suitable for feature-combination generation, feature evaluation, feature selection, model training, and crop-yield prediction.
	The determination of the optimal feature combination is described with reference to FIG. 10.
	FIG. 10 illustrates a method 1000 of determining the optimal feature combination, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The method 1000 is a detailed implementation of steps 710 and 712 of the method 700. The method 1000 may be a computer-implemented method executed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 116 or the processor 202.
	At step 1002, the combination generator 502 may generate the plurality of feature combinations from the machine-learning ready dataset. The plurality of feature combinations may include different combinations of optical vegetation features, SAR-derived features, meteorological features, soil features, agricultural information features, field-observation features, or combinations thereof.
	At step 1004, the machine-learning evaluator 504 may evaluate each feature combination using at least one machine-learning model. At step 1006, the machine-learning evaluator 504 may determine the one or more performance metrics for each feature combination. The one or more performance metrics may include at least one of the coefficient of determination R², the root mean square error RMSE, and the mean absolute error MAE, computed using the expressions described with reference to FIG. 5. In some embodiments, additional performance metrics may be utilized for evaluation of the feature combinations.
	At step 1008, the performance metric comparator 506 may compare the one or more performance metrics corresponding to the plurality of feature combinations. At step 1010, the ranking unit 508 may rank the plurality of feature combinations based on the comparison of the one or more performance metrics. At step 1012, the optimal combination selector 510 may determine the optimal feature combination based on the one or more performance metrics. In some embodiments, determination of the optimal feature combination may be based on one or more selection criteria including prediction accuracy, prediction error, robustness, computational efficiency, model interpretability, reliability, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, automated evaluation, comparison, and ranking of the plurality of feature combinations may facilitate identification of a feature combination exhibiting improved predictive capability for the agricultural region 120.
	The determination of the optimal feature combination may reduce reliance on predefined assumptions regarding feature relevance and may enable data-driven selection of predictor variables for crop-yield prediction.
	The generation of the spatial crop yield estimation map from the selected combination is described with reference to FIG. 11.
	FIG. 11 illustrates a method 1100 of generating the spatial crop yield estimation map. The method 1200 is a detailed implementation of steps 714 and 716 of the method 700. The method 1100 may be a computer-implemented method executed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 116 or the processor 202.
	At step 1102, the feature matrix generator 602 may extract predictor values at field-observation locations to generate the feature matrix. The feature matrix may comprise predictor values corresponding to the optimal feature combination and associated field-observed crop yield values.
	At step 1104, the model training unit 604 may train the crop yield prediction model using the feature matrix and the field-observed crop yield data. n some embodiments, the crop yield prediction model may comprise one or more machine-learning models, ensemble-learning models, statistical models, regression models, deep-learning models, or combinations thereof.
	At step 1106, the prediction unit 606 may generate predicted crop yield values for a plurality of geographic locations within the agricultural region 120 using the trained crop yield prediction model. In some embodiments, the predicted crop yield values may be generated at pixel level, grid level, field level, management-zone level, or other geographic scales within the agricultural region 120.
	At step 1108, the crop cultivation mask unit 608 may apply the crop cultivation mask to identify crop cultivation areas within the plurality of geographic locations. The crop cultivation mask may be generated using one or more land-cover classification techniques, crop-identification techniques, vegetation-classification techniques, remote-sensing analyses, machine-learning techniques, image-processing techniques, or combinations thereof.
	At step 1110, the filtering unit 610 may filter the predicted crop yield values to retain values corresponding to the identified crop cultivation areas. At step 1112, the map rendering unit 612 may generate the spatial crop yield estimation map for the agricultural region 120 based on the retained predicted crop yield values. At step 1114, the rendering module 318 may render the spatial crop yield estimation map on the electronic device 118. In some embodiments, the spatial crop yield estimation map may be presented using one or more visual representations including color gradients, thematic layers, geospatial overlays, field boundaries, dashboards, reports, or combinations thereof.
	In an embodiment, the spatial crop yield estimation map may facilitate visualization of spatial variability in crop-yield estimates within the agricultural region 120.
	The rendered map may present low, moderate, and high productivity zones for resource allocation, procurement planning, and risk management. Filtering by the cultivation mask suppresses predictions over non-cultivated surfaces and retain predictions associated with cultivated crop areas. The operations performed at steps 1102 through 1114 may transform the optimal feature combination into a geospatially resolved crop-yield estimation output for the agricultural region 120.
	The interaction between the data sources, the system, and the electronic device is described with reference to FIG. 12.
	FIG. 12 illustrates a flow diagram 1200 of sequence of data exchanges between data sources 1202, a spatial crop yield estimation system 1204, and an electronic device 1206. In an embodiment, the data sources 1202 may correspond to the data sources of FIG. 1. The spatial crop yield estimation system 1204 may correspond to the spatial crop yield estimation system 116. The electronic device 1206 may correspond to the electronic device 118.
	At step S1208, the multi-source agricultural data may be transferred from the data sources 1202 to the spatial crop yield estimation system 1204 over the network 114. At step S1210, the spatial crop yield estimation system 1204 may preprocess and integrate the data into the unified geospatial dataset. At step S1212, the spatial crop yield estimation system 1204 may prepare the machine-learning ready dataset from the unified geospatial dataset. At step S1214, the spatial crop yield estimation system 1304 may evaluate the feature combinations and determine the optimal feature combination. At step S1216, the spatial crop yield estimation system 1204 may generate the spatial crop yield estimation map using the optimal feature combination.
	At step S1218, the spatial crop yield estimation map may be transmitted from the spatial crop estimation system 1204 to the electronic device 1206. At step S1220, the electronic device 1206 may render the spatial crop yield estimation map for presentation to the user.
	In an embodiment, a majority of the data-processing, feature-engineering, model-training, feature-selection, crop-yield prediction, and map-generation operations may be performed by the spatial crop yield estimation system 1204, while the electronic device 1206 may receive and present the generated spatial crop yield estimation map.
	The data flow diagram 1200 illustrates end-to-end generation and delivery of crop-yield estimation outputs from acquisition of multi-source agricultural data through presentation of the spatial crop yield estimation map on the electronic device 1206.
	The technical advantages of the disclosed method and system include metric-driven feature combination selection that removes reliance on fixed assumed relationships. Fusion of optical, SAR, meteorological, and soil domains provides complementary information on crop biophysical state and environmental conditions. All-weather observation capability under persistent cloud cover is provided by the SAR data. Fine spatial resolution output at 10 meters enables localized decision-making. Reduced dependence on extensive calibration data and on labor-intensive ground surveys is achieved through machine-learning-based prediction. Interpretability through feature importance analysis supports understanding of variable contributions. The framework is transferable to other crops, seasons, and agro-climatic zones with appropriate calibration.

title: OIL MIST SEPARATOR
abstract:
The object is to reduce or prevent the ejection of oil in an oil mist separator. 
[Solution] 
The present invention relates to an oil mist separator for a PCV system of an internal combustion engine. The oil mist separator includes an inlet opening for allowing blow-by gas to flow in, a discharge opening for discharging the blow-by gas, a bottom plate forming a flow path for circulating the blow-by gas between the inlet opening and the discharge opening, an impactor for separating oil from the blow-by gas, provided on the bottom plate, and an oil drain part disposed below the bottom plate and having an oil drain port area for receiving the separated oil, in which a cover structure part for preventing oil from scattering is disposed above the oil drain port area.

title: A POLE MODULE FOR A CIRCUIT BREAKER ARRANGEMENT
abstract: A pole module for a circuit breaker arrangement is disclosed. The pole module (1A) comprises a housing (2A) having a top end and a bottom end (5A), two or more contact arms (6A, 8A), and an interrupter (10A) comprising a stationary member (11A) and a movable member (13A). The pole module (1A) is characterized by one or more vertical creepage ribs (14A) provided on an inner surface of the housing (2A).

title: ENHANCED BEAM MANAGEMENT IN CELLULAR COMMUNICATION NETWORKS
abstract: According to an example aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a method, comprising receiving, by a user equipment, a downlink control message, the downlink control message comprising a time domain configuration for Transmission Configuration Indicator, TCI, state switching and performing by the user equipment, based on the time domain configuration, said TCI state switching.

title: A METHOD OF A USER EQUIPMENT MANAGING CELL BARRING IN A TELECOMMUNICATIONS NETWORK DURING CELL SELECTION AND/OR RESELECTION, A USER EQUIPMENT AND A COMPUTER PROGRAM
abstract: A method of a User Equipment, UE, managing cell barring in a telecommunications network during cell selection and/or reselection is provided. The method comprises receiving a Signal Synchronisation Block, SSB, from a cell in the telecommunications network. The method further comprises based on the SSB, determining that the cell is in a Network Energy Saving, NES, mode. The method further comprises modifying a behaviour of the UE for barring the cell in response to determining that the cell is in NES mode.

title: HIGH PURITY TIN COMPOUNDS AND RELATED COMPOSITIONS AND RELATED METHODS
abstract: Compositions comprising tin (IV) alkoxide compounds useful for extreme ultraviolet lithography are provided. The compositions comprise a highly pure tin (IV) alkoxide compound, with low levels of impurities, including, for example and without limitation, at least one of halide impurities, ammonium impurities, or any combination thereof. Halide-free methods for synthesizing the tin (IV) alkoxide compounds are also provided. Various other compositions and methods are provided.

title: HYBRID BIOELECTRONIC DEVICES AND METHODS OF MANUFACTURE AND USE THEREOF
abstract: Nanoelectronic devices and bioelectronic hybrids thereof are described herein. Methods of making and using such devices and hybrids are also described. The nanoelectronic devices and bioelectronic hybrids can be used, for example, in medical applications. For example, the bioelectronic hybrids can be non-surgically implanted to provide stimulation or modulation to a target site or region in a subject.

title: GRAPHITE PARTICLES, CARBON MATERIAL, AND SECONDARY BATTERY
abstract: The present invention relates to graphite particles coated with amorphous carbon, wherein, when the particles are pressurized to a pressure of 9.81 mN and then decompressed to 0.05 mN, a value derived by dividing the particle size displacement amount observed when the pressure is released so as to reach 0.05 mN after reaching 9.81 mN by the particle size displacement amount at the time at which 9.81 mN is reached is 0.5 or greater.

title: MOBILE BIOPROCESSING MODULE, BIOPROCESSING UNIT AND BIOPROCESSING SYSTEM FOR PERFORMING A BIOPROCESS
abstract: A mobile bioprocessing module (1) for performing a bioprocess, comprising a bioreactor vessel support section (2) configured for supporting a, preferably expandable, bioreactor vessel (3) for containing a culture medium and/or cell culture, an agitation device (4) for agitating the bioreactor vessel (3), and a control device (5) for controlling the mobile bioprocessing module (1), preferably for controlling the bioprocess performed by the mobile bioprocessing module (1), is presented and described. In order to provide a mobile bioprocessing module (1) with improved handling and/or design it is proposed that the mobile bioprocessing module (1) comprises at least one module interface section (22) for detachably connecting the bioprocessing module (1) to a bioprocessing unit (34) and in that the module interface section (22) comprises, preferably consists of, at least one module power interface (23) for receiving power for the mobile bioprocessing module (1), at least one module data interface (24) for receiving data for and/or transmitting data from the mobile bioprocessing module (1) and/or at least one module gas interface (25) for receiving gas for and/or transferring gas from the mobile bioprocessing module (1). Also presented and described are a bioprocessing unit (34) and bioprocessing system (36) for performing a bioprocess.

title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR TREATING OPHTHALMIC DISEASE
abstract: Therapeutic methods and ophthalmic compositions for reducing ocular mast cell degranulation and/or ocular mast cell cytokine production in a human subject, inhibiting ocular mast cell activation in a human subject, treating dry eye disease (DED) or allergic conjunctivitis (AC) in a human subject, inhibiting mast cell activation in a human subject, and reducing or alleviating a sign or symptom of dry eye disease in a human subject using a BTK inhibitor are described. The disclosure also includes therapeutic methods and ophthalmic compositions for reducing or alleviating a sign or symptom of allergic conjunctivitis in a human subject and treating allergic conjunctivitis in a human subject using a BTK inhibitor.

title: PROCESSING MULTIMODAL PROMPTS USING TEXT-ONLY LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
abstract: A multimodal system (150) includes a multimodal encoder (160), a vector quantization model (170), and a text-only large language model (LLM) (180). The multimodal encoder is configured to receive, as input, a multimodal input (106) for a prompt (184), and generate, based on the multimodal input, a sequence of embeddings (162). The vector quantization model is configured to receive, as input, the sequence of embeddings generated by the multimodal encoder, and generate, based on the sequence of embeddings, a sequence of textual tokens (172). The text-only LLM is configured to receive, as input text, a natural language command (104) for the prompt and the sequence of textual tokens generated by the vector quantization model, and generate, based on the natural language command and the sequence of textual tokens, a corresponding textual output (182).

title: BACKLIGHT MODULE AND DISPLAY DEVICE
abstract: Provided is a backlight module, comprising: a backplane; a light guide plate located on the backplane, wherein the light guide plate comprises a first light-incident surface, a second light-incident surface and a light-emergent surface; light sources including a first light source and a second light source, wherein the first light source and the second light source are respectively located on two sides of the light guide plate in a first direction, a light-emergent surface of the first light source is arranged facing the first light-incident surface, and a light-emergent surface of the second light source is arranged facing the second light-incident surface; a first side frame extending in a second direction and located on the side of the first light source facing away from the light guide plate, wherein the first side frame is connected to the side of the backplane facing away from the first light source; and a second side frame extending in the second direction and located on the side of the second light source facing away from the light guide plate, wherein the second side frame is connected to the side of the backplane facing away from the second light source; and the orthographic projection of the first side frame on the backplane is spaced apart from the orthographic projection of the first light source on the backplane, and the orthographic projection of the second side frame on the backplane covers at least a portion of the orthographic projection of the second light source on the backplane.

title: WINDING, TRANSFORMER, METHOD OF MANUFACTURING A WINDING OF A TRANSFORMER, AND METHOD OF OPERATING A DRY-TYPE TRANSFORMER
abstract: The present invention relates to winding (10) of a dry-type transformer (80) configured to be arranged to surround a core (82) of the transformer (80). The winding (10) includes a first winding portion (16A), a second winding portion (16B), and at least one third winding portion (16C) which each include an electrically conductive material. The winding includes a first gap (20A) which is arranged between the first winding portion (16A) and the second winding portion (16B) and which is filled with electrically insulating material (22), at least a second gap (20B) which is arranged between the second winding portion (16B) and the third winding portion (16C) and which is filled with electrically insulating material (22), and a plurality of cooling channels (24) configured to guide a cooling medium therethrough to transfer heat from the transformer (80) to the cooling medium. The plurality of cooling channels (24) include a first cooling channel (24A) arranged within the first gap (20A) and a second cooling channel (24B) arranged within the second gap (20B). The first cooling channel (24A) and the second cooling channel (24B) each include a medium inlet (28) for introducing the cooling medium into the respective cooling channel (24) and a cooling medium outlet (30) for allowing the cooling medium to exit from the respective cooling channel (24). The cooling medium inlets (28) and the cooling medium outlets (30) are arranged in a side wall (34) of the transformer (80) and/or a side wall (34) of the winding (10). The present invention further relates to a transformer (80), a method of manufacturing a winding (10) of a transformer (80), and a method of operating a transformer (80).

title: BIOPROCESSING BASE, BIOPROCESSING STATION AND BIOPROCESSING SYSTEM
abstract: Shown and described is a bioprocessing base (1) for performing a bioprocess, comprising: a base body (2) comprising: base alignment means (3), one or more interface elements (4) adapted to support and preferably accommodate a bioprocess component (18), and pumping means (8), preferably a peristaltic pump head; an adapter module (9) comprising: one or more fluidic valve actuators (10); and optionally at least one electrical connector (11). In order to perform different and/or multiple operations for a bioprocess, preferably cell and/or gene therapy, while providing an improved handling, the described bioprocessing base (1) is proposed. In addition a bioprocessing station (17), a bioprocessing system (27), a use of a bioprocess component (18) in combination with a bioprocessing base (1) and a method of processing a biological sample in a bioprocessing system (27) are also described and shown intended for performing different and/or multiple operations for a bioprocess, preferably cell and/or gene therapy, while providing an improved handling.

title: TIMING OFFSET MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING
abstract: Example embodiments of the disclosure relate to methods, apparatuses and a computer readable medium for timing offset measurement and reporting. In a method, a first apparatus receives, from a second apparatus, a configuration of a time offset report indicating the first apparatus to measure and report respective one or more time offsets of at least one transmission reception point (TRP) relative to a reference TRP; determines, based on the configuration, the respective one or more time offsets based on measurements on respective reference signal transmitted by the at least one TRP and a further reference signal transmitted by the reference TRP; and transmits, to the second apparatus, the time offset report indicating a set of time offset indices associated with at least one time interval within which respective one or more time offsets fall.

title: INFORMATION PROCESSING METHOD, INFORMATION PROCESSING DEVICE, AND COMPUTER PROGRAM
abstract: The present invention provides an information processing method for using a plurality of AIs to provide services. The information processing method comprises: a reception step for receiving an input that includes a purpose of a task and a constraint condition; an identification step for identifying a delegation destination model and delegation content on the basis of the input; a transmission step for transmitting the delegation content to the identified delegation destination model; a result reception step for receiving an execution result of the delegation content from the delegation destination model; and a presentation step for presenting information based on the execution result. In the identification step, the delegation destination model is identified from among the plurality of AI models on the basis of execution history data together with the delegation content.
